# BADAN Repo Audit

> Full-repository audit of `badan` @ `main` (audited 2026-07-11, HEAD `ab1aa47`). 1,500 structured recommendations across five categories, grounded in the actual code. Generated by a lead auditor plus 15 scoped audit agents; every cited path is real.

## 1. Repository inventory

### 1.1 Top-level map

| Path | What it actually is | State |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/` | Shared language-neutral contracts: `metric-ontology/registry.json` (44 metrics, 8 families: activity, body, heart, sleep, respiratory, nutrition, subjective, symptoms), `contracts/insights/templates.json` (13 wellness-safe templates en+ar), `contracts/dictionaries/symptoms.json` (47 symptoms), `export-schemas/csv_columns.json` (24-column CSV contract) | Real source of truth, consumed by both apps via copy scripts |
| `apps/ios/` | The flagship: runnable SwiftUI app, single module, XcodeGen (`project.yml`), iOS 17+, ~13.7k lines Swift, 79 files | Runnable, seeded demo data only |
| `apps/android/` | Kotlin/Compose parity port, ~80 Kotlin files, framework SQLite (ADR-0007), Gradle 8.11/AGP 8.9 | Builds; Health Connect reads are real |
| `docs/` | PRD, architecture.md, data-model.md, 7 ADRs, execution plan, parity status, design tokens/screens JSON, screenshots | Rich, some drift (see §2.7) |
| `backend/`, `infra/` | READMEs only — dormant by design (ADR-0002, local-first no-backend MVP) | Intentionally empty |
| `scripts/` | `run_ios.sh`, `run_android.sh`, `sync_ios_resources.sh`, `sync_android_assets.sh`, `next_steps.md`, `tree.txt` | Dev helpers |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Two jobs: JSON contract/mirror validation (iOS mirrors only) + full iOS simulator build+test on macos-15 | Works; slow, no Android job |

### 1.2 iOS app anatomy (`apps/ios/`)

- **Entry/shell:** `App/BADANApp.swift` → `RootView.swift`: splash → onboarding → five-tab shell (Today, Body, Log, Insights, Settings), each tab its own `NavigationStack`. Portrait-only, iPhone-only (`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY: "1"`).
- **Composition root:** `Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift` — a single `@Observable @MainActor` class owning the `Database`, 8 repositories, 4 services (`IngestionPipeline`, `BaselineEngine`, `InsightEngine`, `ExportRunner`), and the live `CustomizationProfile`. Mutating the profile re-renders the entire app. First-run seeding via `SeedController` in `Task.detached`.
- **Storage:** `Sources/Storage/SQLite/SQLiteConnection.swift` — hand-rolled SQLite3 C wrapper (WAL, FULLMUTEX, `NSRecursiveLock`, `busy_timeout 3000`); no prepared-statement cache; `query()` materializes every row into a `[String: SQLValue]` dictionary. `Database.swift` opens **two files** — `badan.db` and `badan_sensitive.db` (meds/symptoms/conditions) — so disabling sensitive modules is a literal file deletion (`purgeSensitiveNamespace()`). `Migrations.swift` holds migration 001: the entire schema, with embedded provenance columns on every measurement table, sync-ready convention columns (`updated_at`, `origin_device_id`, `deleted_at`), named + partial unique identity indexes for idempotent re-ingest, and three **reserved-but-unused** tables (`read_anchors`, `import_batches`, `sync_cursors`).
- **Domain:** canonical entities under `Sources/Domain/` (RawSample / IntervalRecord / Session+stages / DerivedValue append-only / Baseline median+MAD / Insight / ReconciliationDecision / logging entities / `Goal` — which has a table and a domain type but **no UI anywhere**). Engines: `Ingestion/IngestionPipeline.swift` (normalize → provenance → idempotent upsert → per-night `DedupLite` ≥70% overlap sleep dedup with reversible journal → daily sleep rollup rebuild), `Derivation/BaselineEngine.swift` (14-day rolling median/MAD + composite readiness/sleep-efficiency `DerivedValue`s with input manifests), `Derivation/InsightEngine.swift` (deterministic template selection, en+ar).
- **Health seam:** `Platform/Health/HealthStorePort.swift` with two conformers. `FakeHealthStore.swift` — deterministic 90-day two-source seed generator — is the **only data source the app actually uses**. `HealthKitAdapter.swift` requests authorization for 4 types but its `readSamples/readIntervals/readSessions` **return `[]` (explicit post-MVP TODOs)**. The iOS flagship therefore never ingests a real health datum.
- **Export:** `Sources/Export/` — `ExportRunner` (scope-honoring, raw/derived routed to separate files, SHA-256 checksums, versioned manifest), `CSVWriter` (24-column contract), `JSONBundleWriter`. Fully offline.
- **Features (15 screens):** Home (716 lines, dual-altitude), Body + Sources, MetricDetail + AnatomySheet, Timeline (+ query-time `TimelineAssembler`), LogHub, Symptom (646), Medication (883 — the largest file in the app), Workout (426), Nutrition (371), ExportCenter (705), Settings (497), Insights (425), Onboarding (405).
- **Design system:** `Tokens.swift` / `Theme.swift` + components (`MetricChart` incl. sparkline, `StatBox`, `StatusChip`, `Pills`, `ProvenanceRow`, `StatefulContainer` with a `LoadState` loading/loaded/empty/error enum). One calm amber for out-of-band; no red/green moralizing.
- **Localization:** hand-rolled `LocalizedString(en:ar:)` pairs in `Core/Localization/Strings.swift` (no String Catalogs); language is a runtime switch that flips `layoutDirection`, so RTL is structural.
- **Tests:** exactly 3 files (`PipelineTests`, `UnitTests`, `SmokeTests`) — domain/pipeline coverage only. No UI tests, no snapshot tests, no performance tests.

### 1.3 Android app anatomy (`apps/android/`)

Deliberate mirror of the iOS architecture (same layer names, same DDL, same enum codes; `Long` epoch-millis instead of `Date`, kotlinx.serialization instead of Codable; ADR-0007). Notable divergences from iOS:

- **Health Connect is real** — `platform/health/HealthConnectAdapter.kt` maps 9 record types via paged `readRecords`, with availability states, staged permission requests, denial retry, and a `HealthConnectCard` UI in Sources. Android is *ahead* of iOS on real data.
- **Hand-rolled navigation** (`app/Navigation.kt`) and Compose-state DI (`app/Composition.kt`) — no NavHost, no ViewModel/SavedStateHandle layer.
- **Tests:** 10 pure-JVM parity tests (`FoundationTest.kt`); the DB-backed pipeline is only "validated at runtime" per `docs/android-parity-status.md` — no instrumented/Robolectric suite.
- **No CI at all** for Android: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` neither builds the APK nor checks `apps/android/app/src/main/assets/*` mirrors against `packages/` (it checks only the iOS mirrors).

### 1.4 Feature surface today (what a user can actually do)

Onboard → view seeded demo data on Home (casual or power altitude) → drill into Body → metric detail with baseline band, sparkline, provenance, anatomy sheet → Timeline → log symptoms/medications/workouts/nutrition/notes → view template insights → export CSV/JSON+manifest → customize depth/units/language/theme/modules → purge sensitive namespace / reset demo data. **Not possible today:** getting real health data in on iOS, widgets, notifications/reminders, search, goals UI, backup/restore, any background work.

### 1.5 Performance-sensitive areas identified

Startup seed (90 days × multiple metrics, first launch), every screen's ViewModel `load()` running synchronous SQL on the `@MainActor`, per-render `DateFormatter` allocations (e.g. `HomeScreen.swift` `HomeHeader.dateText`, `TimelinePreviewCard.timeText`), N+1 query patterns per metric on Home, `SQLiteConnection.query()` full materialization with per-row column-name dictionaries, whole-app re-render on any `profile` mutation, chart/sparkline path building, `ExportRunner` building full files in memory, CI re-running the entire xcodebuild on xcpretty failure, no perf instrumentation anywhere (no signposts, no MetricKit, no Macrobenchmark).

## 2. Architecture assessment

### 2.1 What is genuinely strong

1. **The domain model is the best part of the repo.** Embedded denormalized provenance on every measurement row, append-only derived values, reversible dedup journal, idempotent identity indexes, and the two-file sensitive namespace are all real implementations of the stated invariants (I1–I8) — not aspirations. `Migrations.swift` reads like the data-model doc because it is the data-model doc.
2. **Contracts-first sharing works.** `packages/` → mirrored assets → typed loaders on both platforms is a sane native-first sharing model (ADR-0001), and CI actually enforces the iOS half of it.
3. **Dual altitude is honestly one model.** `DepthPolicy` gates presentation only; the numbers are provably identical between casual and power (`HomeScreen.swift` branches on `env.depth.showsPowerDetail` around the same `HomeData`).
4. **RTL/Arabic is structural**, not bolted on: runtime `layoutDirection` flip, en+ar pairs at every string site, Arabic numerals/durations in `ValueFormatter`.
5. **ADR discipline is real** (7 ADRs, referenced from code comments), and the parity-status doc tracks truth rather than hope — it even confesses the missing instrumented tests.

### 2.2 The flagship risk: a demo heart in a real body

The iOS app's entire data path runs off `FakeHealthStore`. `HealthKitAdapter` exists to "nail the seam" but reads nothing. Meanwhile the schema carries `read_anchors`, `import_batches`, `sync_cursors` — infrastructure for a future that has no iOS producer. **Android shipped real Health Connect reads first**, inverting the "iOS-first flagship" premise (ADR-0006). Until HealthKit reads land, every iOS screen, baseline, insight, and export is a demo of seeded data, and none of the hard problems (permission UX, incremental anchored sync, real-world dirty data, DST/timezone edge cases at scale) have been exercised on the flagship platform. This single gap dominates the audit's priority analysis (§8).

### 2.3 Concurrency and data-access architecture will not survive real data volumes

Everything below the view layer is synchronous, lock-serialized, and mostly invoked from the `@MainActor`: view models call repositories directly in `.task {}` closures; `SQLiteConnection` serializes all access behind an `NSRecursiveLock`; there is no read/write split, no statement caching, no pagination anywhere (Timeline loads what the assembler returns; Body loads all metrics). With 90 seeded days this is fine; with 3+ years of real HealthKit history (10⁵–10⁶ rows) the main thread will pay for every query. The fix direction is clear and incremental — background query executor + async repository façade + paged reads — and is fully itemized in PERF-101…200.

### 2.4 State management is one big knob

`AppEnvironment` is a god object: DI container, live profile, lifecycle, formatters. Because it is one `@Observable` and every view reads it, a single profile mutation (theme, language, even a module toggle) invalidates the world. That is *by design* for language/theme ("re-skins instantly") but it means there is no granular invalidation story, and screen view models re-query on every `.task` with no caching or shared per-day snapshot. A `HomeData`-style read-model service with day-keyed caching would cut most redundant SQL (itemized in PERF-A/OPT-A).

### 2.5 Testing posture is inverted relative to risk

The most test-worthy logic (DST transitions in `DayAttribution`, MAD=0 degenerate baselines, dedup tie-breaks, export manifest checksums, migration idempotency, repository SQL) has *some* coverage in 3 iOS test files and 10 Android JVM tests, but: no cross-platform conformance fixtures actually run in CI (the architecture doc promises them), no UI/snapshot tests despite RTL being first-order, no instrumented Android DB tests, and CI runs iOS tests only. The parity claim ("same numbers as iOS") is enforced by hand-checking, not by a shared golden-fixture suite — the single highest-leverage QA investment available (OPT-C).

### 2.6 Tension scorecard (the blueprint's own tensions)

| Tension | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Casual simplicity vs power depth | **Succeeding** — one model, two presentations, honest numbers. Weakness: depth switch discoverability and power-only affordances hidden rather than progressive. |
| Privacy vs convenience | **Succeeding architecturally** (local-first, two-file namespace, offline export), but unfinished: no iCloud-backup exclusion decision, no SQLCipher (ADR-0004 deferred), no app lock, and the privacy story is invisible to the user in-app. |
| Broad capability vs calm UX | **Holding** — but only because capability is small. The 44-metric registry outstrips what screens surface (~6 metrics on Home, hardcoded list in `HomeViewModel.loadMetrics`). |
| Customization vs chaos | **Under-built** — `CustomizationProfile` exists (depth/units/language/theme/modules) but no layout editor, no per-metric preferences; low chaos risk today. |
| Local-first ambition vs implementation complexity | **Well-judged** — raw SQLite + no backend was the right MVP cut; sync-ready columns keep the door open cheaply. |
| Cross-platform parity vs platform-native quality | **Mostly well-handled** (ADR-0007 divergences are principled), but Android skips platform idioms it shouldn't (no Material You, no predictive back, hand-rolled nav) and parity is asserted, not fixture-verified. |
| Fast iteration vs architectural durability | **Leaning durable** — the domain layer is over-engineered relative to the data actually flowing through it (fake), which is the inverse of the usual failure but still a scheduling smell: the hard integration risk was deferred, the easy modeling was polished. |

### 2.7 Cross-cutting hygiene gaps

No lint/format config on either platform (no SwiftLint/SwiftFormat/ktlint/detekt); no crash reporting or local logging framework (errors are swallowed with `try?` in `AppEnvironment.bootstrap`, `resetDemoData`, `HomeViewModel.loadEvents` and surfaced as raw `String(describing:)` in `LoadState.error`); doc drift (blueprint exists in two copies — root `BADAN_MASTER_BLUEPRINT.md` and `docs/BADAN_MASTER_BLUEPRINT_OLD_DONT_USE.md` — plus an archived execution plan); `scripts/tree.txt` is a stale snapshot; the fallback path in `AppEnvironment.makeDefault()` silently boots into a **temporary-directory database**, which for a "your data is safe here" product is a data-loss trap wearing a resilience costume.

Each item carries ROI/Importance/Effort (1–5), approval requirement, affected files/systems, owner, dependencies, risk, and implementation notes; items with ROI ≥ 4 and Effort ≤ 3 include a first-patch sketch.*

## 3. Performance recommendations (300)

Scope: `apps/ios/Sources/Features/**`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/**`, `apps/ios/App/**` + `apps/ios/Sources/App/**`, `Core/Localization`, `Core/Units.swift`. Storage/Domain internals are out of scope; repositories are cited only as call sites from view models.

---

### PERF-001 — AppEnvironment.init blocks the first frame with synchronous construction

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `AppEnvironment.init` (called from `BADANApp.swift:5` via `@State private var env = AppEnvironment.makeDefault()`, evaluated on the main thread before `WindowGroup` renders) synchronously opens two SQLite databases and constructs 8 repositories + 4 services before `SplashView` ever appears.
- **Recommendation:** Move DB open + repository wiring off the critical path — construct a lightweight placeholder environment first, then hydrate it asynchronously and swap in, or at minimum profile whether this exceeds a frame budget on older devices.
- **Why it matters:** Every millisecond here delays the very first pixel, before the "calm splash" the app is designed to show.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster time-to-first-frame on cold launch, especially on older iPhones.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/App/BADANApp.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift`
- **Affected systems:** App startup
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Cold-launch time keeps growing as more repositories/services are added to the composition root.
- **Implementation notes:** Consider a two-phase `AppEnvironment` (infra-only, then services attached after first frame) or explicitly measure with `os_signpost` before optimizing further.

### PERF-002 — Ontology singletons synchronously decode JSON on the main thread during init

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `MetricRegistry.shared`, `SymptomDictionary.shared`, and `InsightTemplateStore.shared` (`apps/ios/Sources/Ontology/MetricRegistry.swift`, `SymptomDictionary.swift`, `InsightTemplateStore.swift`, loaded via `BundleJSON.swift`) each do blocking `Data(contentsOf:)` + `JSONDecoder().decode` and are called directly and synchronously inside `AppEnvironment.init` (`AppEnvironment.swift:51-53`), on the main actor, before `bootstrap()` even starts.
- **Recommendation:** Kick off the three decodes in parallel (`Task` group) or memoize them behind a background-warmed cache so `AppEnvironment.init` doesn't pay for ~39KB of synchronous file I/O + decode serially on the main thread.
- **Why it matters:** Three separate synchronous disk reads plus decode passes, done serially, add up before the splash screen can even draw.
- **Expected user impact:** Slightly snappier app launch, most noticeable on first-install cold starts.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Ontology/MetricRegistry.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Ontology/SymptomDictionary.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Ontology/InsightTemplateStore.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift`
- **Affected systems:** App startup, ontology loading
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low today (39KB total) but grows as the metric ontology/symptom dictionary expand.
- **Implementation notes:** Simplest fix: wrap the three `.shared` accesses in a `Task.detached` group awaited once, or precompute during `Task.detached` seeding rather than at `init`.

### PERF-003 — First-run 90-day seed blocks `isReady` with no progress feedback

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `AppEnvironment.bootstrap()` awaits `SeedController.seedIfNeeded(asOf:)` (`apps/ios/Sources/App/SeedController.swift`), which ingests 90 days of `FakeHealthStore` data, seeds medications/symptoms/workouts/nutrition, then runs `baselines.recomputeAll` and 4 days of `insightEngine.generate` — all before `RootView` leaves `SplashView`.
- **Recommendation:** Show incremental progress (or at least a determinate/looping animation keyed to seed phase) instead of a static spinner, and consider deferring `insightEngine.generate` for days 1-3 until after first paint of the tab shell.
- **Why it matters:** First-run users stare at an indeterminate `ProgressView` for the single longest synchronous operation in the app with zero visibility into progress.
- **Expected user impact:** Less perceived-dead-time on first launch, which is the app's most important first impression.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/App/SeedController.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift`, `apps/ios/App/RootView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** First-run onboarding, splash
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** No regression risk today, but as seed volume grows this becomes a worse first impression.
- **Implementation notes:** Publish a `SeedController` progress enum through `AppEnvironment` and bind `SplashView` to it.

### PERF-004 — No os_signpost instrumentation around AppEnvironment.bootstrap()

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `AppEnvironment.bootstrap()` (`apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift:110`) is the single longest-running startup operation in the app and has zero `os_signpost`/`os_log` instrumentation, so there is no way to measure real-device cold-launch or reseed latency outside of manual profiling.
- **Recommendation:** Wrap `bootstrap()` and `SeedController.seed(asOf:)` in `os_signpost` begin/end intervals under a dedicated "BADAN.Startup" category.
- **Why it matters:** The repo has zero performance instrumentation anywhere (per repo facts); startup is the highest-value place to start.
- **Expected user impact:** No direct user-facing change, but unlocks measuring and defending future startup optimizations.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/App/SeedController.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Observability, startup
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Any future startup regression ships silently with no telemetry to catch it.
- **Implementation notes:** Add `OSLog`/`OSSignposter` around `bootstrap()`, `seedIfNeeded`, and `seed(asOf:)`; visible immediately in Instruments' os_signpost track.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `static let signposter = OSSignposter(subsystem: "com.badan.app", category: "Startup")` in `AppEnvironment.swift`, wrap the `Task.detached` body in `bootstrap()` with `signposter.beginInterval`/`endInterval`.

### PERF-005 — No MetricKit integration for production launch/hang telemetry

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** The app has no `MXMetricManager` subscriber anywhere in `apps/ios/App/` or `apps/ios/Sources/App/`, so there is no way to learn about real-world launch time, hang rate, or disk-write metrics from TestFlight/App Store users (confirmed absent per repo facts: "No: analytics/observability... performance instrumentation").
- **Recommendation:** Add a minimal `MXMetricManagerSubscriber` in `BADANApp.swift` that logs `MXMetric` payloads (or writes them to a local debug log) so launch/hang data is at least inspectable during beta testing.
- **Why it matters:** Without this, every perceived-performance claim in this audit is based on code reading, not field data.
- **Expected user impact:** No direct UI change; enables catching real regressions before broad rollout.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/App/BADANApp.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Observability
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Startup/hang regressions in later features go undetected until user complaints.
- **Implementation notes:** `MXMetricManager.shared.add(subscriber)` in `BADANApp.init`; keep the subscriber local-first (no network) to respect the local-only guardrail.

### PERF-006 — RootView's Splash→Onboarding→MainTabView swap fully discards/rebuilds the tree

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `RootView.body` (`apps/ios/App/RootView.swift:9-21`) uses a plain `Group { if ... }` over three mutually-exclusive views; each state transition (`isReady` flip, `onboardingComplete` flip) destroys the entire previous subtree and constructs the next one from scratch with no transition/preserved identity.
- **Recommendation:** This is likely fine given the transitions happen once each, but confirm there's no unnecessary re-render churn from `env.profile` reads inside `badanChrome` firing between these transitions during startup.
- **Why it matters:** Two full-tree constructions happen back-to-back on cold launch, compounding whatever else is happening during `bootstrap()`.
- **Expected user impact:** Minor smoother launch transition.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/App/RootView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** App startup
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** None material; noted for completeness only.
- **Implementation notes:** Low priority; only worth touching if profiling shows a visible glitch at the isReady/onboardingComplete boundary.

### PERF-007 — `env.format` allocates a fresh ValueFormatter on every access

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `AppEnvironment.format` (`apps/ios/Sources/App/UISupport.swift:11`) is a computed property that constructs `ValueFormatter(profile: profile, registry: registry)` fresh every time it's read; a single screen body (e.g. `HomeScreen`) reads `env.format` 5+ times per render pass.
- **Recommendation:** Cache the `ValueFormatter` as a computed-once-per-profile-change value (e.g. store it as a real `@Observable` property recomputed only when `profile` changes) instead of a plain computed property.
- **Why it matters:** `ValueFormatter` is a lightweight struct so each individual allocation is cheap, but it multiplies the deeper `Numerals.format`/`NumberFormatter` cost (see PERF-011) across every call site with no shared instance.
- **Expected user impact:** Marginally lower CPU/allocations during scroll-heavy screens (Home, Body, MetricDetail).
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/App/UISupport.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/App/ValueFormatter.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Value formatting (app-wide)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low on its own; compounds with PERF-011/012.
- **Implementation notes:** Store `private var _format: ValueFormatter?` on `AppEnvironment`, invalidate in `update(_:)`.

### PERF-008 — AppEnvironment.resolveDeviceId() does synchronous UserDefaults I/O during init

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `AppEnvironment.resolveDeviceId()` (`apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift:152-157`) reads/writes `UserDefaults.standard` synchronously as part of `init`, on the main thread, alongside the DB/repository construction already flagged in PERF-001.
- **Recommendation:** Fold this into the same startup-latency review as PERF-001; `UserDefaults` access is typically fast but is one more synchronous call stacked before first paint.
- **Why it matters:** Small individually, but it's one more item on the pre-first-frame critical path.
- **Expected user impact:** Negligible alone; contributes to overall startup latency reduction effort.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift`
- **Affected systems:** App startup
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** PERF-001
- **Risk if skipped:** Negligible in isolation.
- **Implementation notes:** No action needed unless profiling under PERF-001 shows it matters.

### PERF-009 — CustomizationProfile as a single Observable property causes whole-app re-render on any settings mutation

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `AppEnvironment.profile` (`apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift:39`) is one stored property holding language, theme, depth, units, home-module visibility, notification prefs, and sensitive/nutrition toggles combined; `env.update { }` reassigns the whole struct, so mutating an unrelated field (e.g. a notification toggle in Settings) invalidates every view anywhere in the tab tree that reads any `env.profile.*`/`env.language`/`env.depth` — which is nearly every screen in the app.
- **Recommendation:** Split `CustomizationProfile` into narrower `@Observable` slices (e.g. separate presentation-affecting fields like language/theme/depth from purely-persisted fields like notification prefs) so Swift's Observation tracking can skip re-rendering views that don't read the changed slice.
- **Why it matters:** This is the single biggest architectural performance lever in the presentation layer — it's the difference between a notification toggle repainting one row versus the entire mounted tab tree.
- **Expected user impact:** Snappier, more localized UI updates when changing any single setting.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Observation/state architecture (app-wide)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every future screen added to the app inherits this over-invalidation by default; gets more expensive as the view tree grows.
- **Implementation notes:** Requires care since `profiles.save(p)` currently persists the whole struct atomically; a split needs to preserve one atomic persistence write while exposing finer-grained observable reads. Marked "Approval needed: Yes" because it's an architecture-direction change, not a drop-in fix.

### PERF-010 — BadanThemeModifier reapplies at the app root on every profile mutation, not just theme/language ones

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `badanChrome(_:)` (`apps/ios/Sources/App/UISupport.swift:35-42`) and `badanTheme(_:language:)` (`apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Theme.swift:78-83`) are applied once at `RootView`'s root but read `env.profile.theme`/`env.language`, both of which live inside the same single `profile` property flagged in PERF-009 — so any settings change re-evaluates `preferredColorScheme`/`layoutDirection`/`Locale(identifier:)` at the root, invalidating environment values for the whole mounted tree even when theme/language didn't change.
- **Recommendation:** Same root cause as PERF-009; once `profile` is split, gate this modifier specifically on theme/language fields.
- **Why it matters:** The root-level environment modifier is the single most expensive place for over-invalidation to occur, since it cascades to every descendant.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer full-tree layout passes when changing unrelated settings.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/App/UISupport.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Theme.swift`, `apps/ios/App/RootView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Theming/RTL chrome (app-wide)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** PERF-009
- **Risk if skipped:** Continues to amplify every settings-page interaction into a full-tree environment invalidation.
- **Implementation notes:** Once `profile` is decomposed, bind `badanChrome` to a narrower `ThemeLanguageState` object.

### PERF-011 — Numerals.format allocates a new NumberFormatter on every single call, app-wide

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `Numerals.format` (`apps/ios/Sources/Core/Localization/AppLanguage.swift:73-93`) constructs a brand-new `NumberFormatter()` on every invocation; it backs `ValueFormatter.number`/`.integer`/`.duration`/`.heroValue`, which are called for essentially every visible number in the app — hero values, deltas, chips, table rows, chart axis labels indirectly.
- **Recommendation:** Cache `NumberFormatter` instances keyed by `(language, arabicDigits, fractionDigits)` in a small static dictionary/pool, since `NumberFormatter` construction (locale resolution, digit symbol tables) is one of the more expensive Foundation object inits.
- **Why it matters:** This is the single highest-frequency formatting hotspot in the entire presentation layer — every screen that shows a number pays this cost on every render.
- **Expected user impact:** Reduced CPU/allocation pressure during scrolling on any number-dense screen (Home, Body, MetricDetail, Export).
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Core/Localization/AppLanguage.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/App/ValueFormatter.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Number formatting (app-wide)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** This scales linearly with the number of visible numeric values on screen; gets worse as denser power-mode screens (grids, tables) are used more.
- **Implementation notes:** A `NSCache`-backed or simple `[FormatterKey: NumberFormatter]` static dictionary in `Numerals` is enough; `NumberFormatter` is not thread-safe for mutation but read-only reuse across the main actor is fine since all call sites are `@MainActor`.
- **First patch sketch:** In `apps/ios/Sources/Core/Localization/AppLanguage.swift`, add a `private static var cache: [String: NumberFormatter] = [:]` inside `Numerals`, key by `"\(language)-\(arabicDigits)-\(fractionDigits)"`, and reuse instead of constructing fresh.

### PERF-012 — Numerals.format reconstructs Locale(identifier:) on every call instead of caching per language

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** Inside the same `Numerals.format` (`apps/ios/Sources/Core/Localization/AppLanguage.swift:83`), `Locale(identifier: language == .ar && arabicDigits ? "ar" : "en_US_POSIX")` is constructed fresh every call rather than reusing one of exactly two possible `Locale` values.
- **Recommendation:** Precompute the two `Locale` instances once (e.g. as `static let` constants) and select between them instead of re-resolving from a string identifier every call.
- **Why it matters:** `Locale(identifier:)` construction involves locale-data lookup; doing it on every formatted number compounds with PERF-011's NumberFormatter cost.
- **Expected user impact:** Same as PERF-011 — lower CPU on number-dense screens.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Core/Localization/AppLanguage.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Number formatting (app-wide)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor on its own; best fixed together with PERF-011 in the same formatter-caching pass.
- **Implementation notes:** `static let arLocale = Locale(identifier: "ar")`, `static let enLocale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")`.
- **First patch sketch:** Add the two static locales next to `Numerals.format` and swap the inline `Locale(identifier:)` call for a ternary over the two constants; ship alongside PERF-011's formatter cache.

### PERF-013 — AppLanguage has no memoized Locale despite 15+ call sites constructing Locale(identifier:) independently

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `AppLanguage.localeIdentifier` (`apps/ios/Sources/Core/Localization/AppLanguage.swift:27-32`) returns a raw string; every DateFormatter site across the codebase (Home, Sources, MetricDetail, Timeline, Medication, Workout, Nutrition, Export, Insights — see PERF-019, 033, 040, 056/057, 065/066, 076, 080, 082/085, 092) independently calls `Locale(identifier: env.language.localeIdentifier)` from scratch.
- **Recommendation:** Add a memoized `AppLanguage.locale: Locale` computed/stored property (two cached values total) so every one of those ~15 call sites shares the same construction instead of re-resolving locale data repeatedly.
- **Why it matters:** This is the root cause shared by nearly every per-row DateFormatter finding in this report; fixing it once here reduces the marginal cost of each of those call sites.
- **Expected user impact:** Broad, small CPU reduction across every list/detail screen with dates.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Core/Localization/AppLanguage.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Date/number formatting (app-wide)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every new screen added will keep copying the same `Locale(identifier:)` pattern.
- **Implementation notes:** Add `public var locale: Locale { Self.cachedLocales[self]! }` backed by a `static let cachedLocales: [AppLanguage: Locale]` built once.
- **First patch sketch:** Add the cached-locale property to `apps/ios/Sources/Core/Localization/AppLanguage.swift`; follow-up PRs can then swap call sites incrementally without behavior change.

- **Risk if skipped:** Redundant with PERF-011; listed separately to flag `duration` as a 2x multiplier on the same root cost.

### PERF-016 — Units.convert dictionary lookups repeated per row instead of pre-converting a series once

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `Units.convert` (`apps/ios/Sources/Core/Units.swift:72-79`) does two dictionary lookups + arithmetic per call; `MetricDetailScreen.valuesTableCard` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift:239-261`) calls `env.format.full(metricId:canonicalValue:)` — which internally calls `Units.convert` — once per row for up to 14 rows, every render, instead of converting the whole series once when `data` loads.

### PERF-017 — HomeViewModel.loadMetrics issues 12 sequential repo calls on the MainActor .task

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `HomeViewModel.loadMetrics` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift:605-630`) loops over 4 metric IDs and, per metric, calls `latestInterval`, `latestBaseline`, and `intervalRecords(from:to:)` (14-day window) — 3 sequential repository round trips × 4 metrics = 12 calls, all synchronous on the main actor inside `HomeScreen`'s `.task { vm.load(env) }`.
- **Recommendation:** Batch these into fewer repository calls (e.g. one multi-metric "latest + baseline + spark" query) or at minimum fetch all 4 metrics' `latestInterval`/`latestBaseline` concurrently via a `TaskGroup` off the main actor, then hop back to publish state.
- **Why it matters:** This N+1 pattern runs on every single visit to the Today tab (the app's primary landing screen) and blocks the main actor for the duration.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, less janky Today-tab loads, especially noticeable when switching back to the tab repeatedly.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Home/Today tab, measurement + derivation repositories (call sites)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** As more key metrics are added to the Home snapshot grid, this N+1 scales linearly and worsens perceived Today-tab responsiveness.
- **Implementation notes:** A repository-level batch API (`latestIntervals(metricIds:)`) would need Storage-layer changes (out of this scope); the presentation-layer fix here is to at least parallelize the existing per-metric calls with `withThrowingTaskGroup`.

### PERF-018 — HomeViewModel.latestReadiness loops up to 4 separate queries instead of one bounded query

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `latestReadiness` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift:568-577`) loops `for offset in 0..<4`, issuing a separate `env.derivation.latestDerived(metricId:periodKey:)` call per day offset until it finds a value, instead of a single "most recent within last 4 days" query.
- **Recommendation:** Replace the loop with a single repository call that accepts a date range and returns the most recent match (repository-layer change, but the call-site pattern here is what forces the current 4x fan-out).
- **Why it matters:** In the common case (no readiness computed yet today), this is 2-4 sequential SQLite round trips just to find the latest readiness score, on every Home load.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster readiness hero card render on Home.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Home/Today tab, derivation repository (call site)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor on its own; compounds with PERF-017's other 12 calls in the same `load()`.
- **Implementation notes:** If a range-based repository query isn't available, at least parallelize the 4 lookups via `TaskGroup` rather than sequential loop-and-return.

### PERF-019 — HomeHeader.dateText allocates a DateFormatter on every render

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `HomeHeader.dateText` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift:57-63`) constructs a new `DateFormatter()` inside a computed property evaluated every time `HomeHeader`'s body runs — which happens on every Home re-render, including ones triggered by unrelated `env.profile` mutations (see PERF-009).
- **Recommendation:** Cache a `DateFormatter` per `(language)` similarly to PERF-013's `Locale` cache, or precompute the date string once in `HomeViewModel.load` and store it on `HomeData`.
- **Why it matters:** `DateFormatter` construction (parsing format templates, locale/calendar setup) is one of the more expensive Foundation object inits, and this fires on every Home body evaluation, not just data reloads.
- **Expected user impact:** Reduced CPU on Home tab, especially during any settings change that ripples into a Home re-render.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Home/Today tab
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low individually; part of a systemic per-row/per-render DateFormatter pattern repeated across ~15 files in this report.
- **Implementation notes:** Move the formatted date into `HomeData` (computed once in `load()`), or add a small shared `DateFormatterCache` keyed by `(language, dateStyle, timeStyle, template)`.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `dateText: String` to `HomeData` in `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`, compute it once inside `HomeViewModel.load`, and have `HomeHeader` read `data.dateText` instead of recomputing.

### PERF-021 — HomeViewModel.loadEvents issues 5 independent 7-day-window repo calls merged in Swift

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `loadEvents` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift:666-699`) makes up to 5 separate `try?` repository calls (workouts, notes, nutrition, symptoms, adherence), each over a 7-day window, then merges and sorts the results in Swift — duplicating logic that `TimelineAssembler` (PERF-054) already implements more completely for the Timeline screen.

### PERF-022 — HomeScreen.task reloads all Home data on every tab reappearance with no staleness check

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `HomeScreen.body` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift:32`) runs `.task { vm.load(env) }` unconditionally on every appearance; switching away to another tab and back re-runs the full N+1 load from PERF-017/018/021 even if nothing changed.
- **Recommendation:** Add a lightweight staleness check (e.g. skip reload if `state` is already `.loaded` and less than N seconds old, or invalidate only on data-mutating events) rather than unconditionally reloading on every tab reappearance.
- **Why it matters:** Today's tab is visited most frequently in typical usage; avoiding redundant full reloads has outsized impact on perceived responsiveness.
- **Expected user impact:** Instant Today-tab redisplay when tab-switching back, instead of a fresh load+possible flash to `.loading`.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Home/Today tab
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every tab switch pays the full N+1 cost from PERF-017 for no reason when nothing changed.
- **Implementation notes:** Track `lastLoadedAt: Date?` on `HomeViewModel`; skip reload if under a small threshold (e.g. 5s) unless a known mutation occurred (new log entry, profile change).

### PERF-025 — HomeViewModel has no signpost instrumentation despite the heaviest N+1 load() in the app

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `HomeViewModel.load` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift:534-564`) — which per PERF-017/018/021 issues up to 20 sequential repository calls — has no `os_signpost` markers, so its real-device latency is invisible in Instruments without manual breakpoint profiling.

- **Expected user impact:** No direct UI change; enables data-driven prioritization of PERF-017/018/021/022.

- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No

### PERF-026 — BodyViewModel.makePillar tries multiple metric candidates, each triggering up to 3 sequential store fallbacks

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `BodyViewModel.makePillar` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift:47-61`) iterates a candidate metric-ID list per family (headline metrics + all baseline-eligible metrics in that family), and for each candidate calls `recentSeries`, which itself tries up to 3 different repository calls in sequence (`derivedSeries` → `intervalRecords` → `rawSamples` → `derivedSeries` fallback again) before finding data — worst case this is family-count × candidate-count × 3 repo round trips just to render 6 pillar cards.
- **Recommendation:** Short-circuit earlier (e.g. try the single most-likely store first based on `MetricDefinition.kind` instead of always probing derived→interval→raw→derived), and cap the candidate probing to the headline list before falling back to the full family list.
- **Why it matters:** Body is one of two primary tab destinations and this fan-out is the worst-case query pattern of any load() in the presentation layer.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster Body tab load, especially for families with sparse data where several candidates are tried before one succeeds.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Body tab, measurement/derivation repositories (call sites)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Gets worse as more metrics are added to each family's candidate list.
- **Implementation notes:** Use `def.kind` (already available via `env.registry.definitionOrFallback`) to pick the correct store directly instead of trying all three speculatively.

### PERF-027 — BodyViewModel.recentSeries rebuilds a dedup dictionary + sorts keys per pillar per load

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `recentSeries` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift:65-93`) builds a `[String: IntervalRecord]` dictionary keyed by local day, then calls `.keys.sorted()` — O(n log n) — for every pillar on every Body screen load, and this work is never shared with `HomeViewModel.loadMetrics` (PERF-017) even though both screens fetch overlapping series for shared metrics (steps, RHR, HRV) within the same session.
- **Recommendation:** Introduce a small session-scoped cache (metricId → recent series) shared between `HomeViewModel` and `BodyViewModel` so switching between the Today and Body tabs doesn't re-fetch and re-process the same 12-14 day windows twice.
- **Why it matters:** Users commonly bounce between Today and Body; today each visit re-does the full query + dedup + sort from scratch with zero cross-screen reuse.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster Body tab load on the (common) second-or-later visit within a session.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Body tab, Home/Today tab
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Duplicate work continues to scale with the number of shared metrics between the two screens.
- **Implementation notes:** A simple `AppEnvironment`-scoped `RecentSeriesCache` with a short TTL (e.g. 60s) would cover the common tab-switching case without needing full reactive invalidation.

### PERF-028 — BodyAllMetricsBrowser.results re-runs uncached registry.search(query) on every keystroke

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `BodyAllMetricsBrowser.results` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift:343-345`) calls `env.registry.search(query)` — an uncached linear scan with per-element string folding (confirmed: `MetricRegistry.search` has no memoized folded strings) — on every character typed into the `.searchable` field, then `groups` re-groups and re-sorts the results again on top.
- **Recommendation:** Precompute folded/normalized labels once when `MetricRegistry` loads (at init, alongside the `byId` dictionary) so `search` doesn't re-fold every metric's label on every keystroke, and consider debouncing the search-triggered recompute.
- **Why it matters:** At n=44 metrics this is cheap in absolute terms, but it's a wasted-computation pattern that will matter more as the ontology grows, and it's evaluated in a computed property (`results`) that also reruns `groups`' `Dictionary(grouping:)` + sort on every keystroke.
- **Expected user impact:** Snappier typing responsiveness in "All metrics" search, particularly noticeable if the ontology grows beyond ~100 metrics.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Ontology/MetricRegistry.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Body tab, metric browsing/search
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low today given n=44; becomes a real typing-lag risk if the ontology registry grows significantly.
- **Implementation notes:** Precompute `foldedLabel` per `MetricDefinition` at registry-load time; have `search` filter against the precomputed field.

### PERF-036 — MetricDetailScreen.chartCard recomputes fullSeries redundantly, duplicating work already done in content(_:)

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `MetricDetailScreen.content(_:)` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift:138-160`) computes `fullSeries` once via `data.fullSeries(tz: tz)`, but then `chartCard(_:days:tz:)` (line 189-190) independently calls `data.fullSeries(tz: tz)` again — re-running the derived-series `map`/`filter`/`sort` chain (`MetricDetailData.fullSeries`, lines 38-43) a second time on every single render.
- **Recommendation:** Pass the already-computed `fullSeries` array into `chartCard` instead of recomputing it from `data`.
- **Why it matters:** This redundant computation fires on every render of the MetricDetail screen — including from period-picker taps and any unrelated `env.profile` mutation — not just on data load.
- **Expected user impact:** Snappier MetricDetail screen, especially when switching the 7/30/90-day period picker.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** MetricDetail screen
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Doubles the derived-series computation cost on every MetricDetail render for composite/derived metrics.
- **Implementation notes:** Change `chartCard`'s signature to accept `fullSeries: [(date: Date, value: Double)]` directly and have `content(_:)` pass the one it already computed.
- **First patch sketch:** In `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`, change `chartCard(_ data:, days:, tz:)` to `chartCard(_ data:, days:, fullSeries:)`, drop the internal `data.fullSeries(tz: tz)` call, and update the one call site in `content(_:)` to pass the already-computed `fullSeries`.

### PERF-037 — MetricDetailScreen filters series(within:from:) twice per render over the same full series

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `content(_:)` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift:145-159`) calls `series(within: chartDays, from: fullSeries)` for `valuesTableCard`, and `chartCard` independently recomputes its own filtered slice from its redundant `fullSeries` call (PERF-036) — meaning the `cutoff`/`.filter` pass over the series runs twice per render for two views that both want the same date-bounded slice.
- **Recommendation:** Compute the filtered slice once per render (after fixing PERF-036) and pass it to both `chartCard` and `valuesTableCard`.
- **Why it matters:** Same root cause and fix path as PERF-036; combined they roughly halve the per-render series-processing cost of the MetricDetail screen.
- **Expected user impact:** Same as PERF-036.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** MetricDetail screen
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** PERF-036
- **Risk if skipped:** Redundant filtering compounds with PERF-036's redundant mapping.
- **Implementation notes:** Compute `let points = series(within: chartDays, from: fullSeries)` once in `content(_:)` and pass to both card builders.

### PERF-038 — MetricDetailViewModel.load always fetches 90 days of intervals even when casual altitude only shows 30

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `MetricDetailViewModel.load` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift:60-99`) unconditionally fetches `intervalRecords(from: now - 90 days, to: now)` regardless of depth; casual mode's `chartDays` is hardcoded to 30 (line 143: `let chartDays = power ? periodDays : 30`), so two-thirds of the fetched data is discarded by the later `series(within:from:)` filter for casual users.
- **Recommendation:** Fetch a smaller window (e.g. 30 days) up front for casual mode, and only fetch the full 90-day window lazily when the user switches to power mode or picks a longer period.
- **Why it matters:** Over-fetching from SQLite (no prepared-statement caching per repo facts, so every query is a fresh prepare+finalize) for data that's immediately discarded wastes both query time and row-materialization cost for the majority of users who stay in casual mode.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster MetricDetail loads for casual-mode users, who are the majority per the app's "casual by default" design.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** MetricDetail screen, measurement repository (call site)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every casual-mode MetricDetail visit over-fetches 60 days of data it will never render.
- **Implementation notes:** Pass `env.depth` into `MetricDetailViewModel.load` and choose the fetch window (`30` vs `90` days) accordingly; re-fetch the wider window only if the user switches period/depth.

### PERF-047 — BadanCard's fixed shadow forces repeated offscreen rasterization app-wide

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `BadanCard` (`apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Theme.swift:14-26`) applies `.shadow(color: Color.black.opacity(0.05), radius: 12, x: 0, y: 6)` to every instance unconditionally; `BadanCard` is the single most-used container in the app (Home, Body, Sources, MetricDetail, Timeline, LogHub, Symptom, Medication, Workout, Nutrition, Export, Settings, Insights, Onboarding all use it), so every scrollable screen pays repeated shadow rasterization cost proportional to card count.
- **Recommendation:** Either apply `.compositingGroup()` + `.drawingGroup()` selectively for screens with many stacked cards, reduce the shadow radius (12pt is a fairly soft/expensive blur for a 0.05-opacity shadow), or precompute a shadow-image asset for static card chrome.
- **Why it matters:** This is the single highest-leverage DesignSystem fix in the report — one change benefits every screen in the app simultaneously.
- **Expected user impact:** Broad scroll-performance improvement across the entire app, most noticeable on card-dense screens (Home, Settings, Medication, Export history).
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Theme.swift`
- **Affected systems:** DesignSystem (app-wide)
- **Suggested owner:** Design, Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every new screen that adopts `BadanCard` inherits the same per-card shadow cost by default.
- **Implementation notes:** Profile with Instruments' Core Animation "Color Offscreen-Rendered" overlay first to confirm the shadow is actually triggering offscreen passes before optimizing; a smaller radius or a `strokeBorder`-only treatment on dense list screens may be sufficient.
- **First patch sketch:** In `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Theme.swift`, reduce `BadanCard`'s shadow radius from 12 to ~6-8 and re-verify visually against `docs/design/design-tokens.json`; measure with Instruments before/after on the Home and Settings screens.

### PERF-048 — MetricChart/MetricSparkline uses the Charts framework for small decorative sparklines

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `MetricSparkline` (`apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/MetricChart.swift:76-97`) wraps a full Swift `Chart { LineMark(...) }` even for tiny 28-76pt decorative trend lines with no axes, legend, or interactivity — used across Home (up to 5 instances), Body (up to 6), and any future card adopting it.
- **Recommendation:** Replace `MetricSparkline`'s backing with a lightweight custom `Shape`/`Path`-based polyline (normalize values to the frame, draw a single `Path` with `.stroke`), reserving the full Charts framework for `MetricChart`'s real interactive detail-screen chart.
- **Why it matters:** Charts' layout engine, animatable data machinery, and per-mark view diffing are disproportionately expensive for a shape that's purely decorative and never interacted with.

- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/MetricChart.swift`
- **Affected systems:** DesignSystem charts, Home, Body
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile, Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Sparkline density will only grow as more metric cards adopt this component.
- **Implementation notes:** A `Path` built from normalized `(index, value)` points via `path.addLine(to:)` in a custom `Shape` replicates the visual (catmull-rom can be approximated with quad curves) at a fraction of the framework overhead; keep `MetricChart` (the real chart) on Charts since it needs axes/bands/interactivity.

### PERF-049 — MetricChart.init remaps tuples into Point structs on every instantiation

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `MetricChart.init(series:style:band:)` (`apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/MetricChart.swift:22-26`) does `self.points = series.map { Point(date: $0.date, value: $0.value) }` — since `MetricChart` is a `struct` re-created on every parent render, this remap runs every time the chart's parent view body re-evaluates, not just when the underlying series data actually changes.
- **Recommendation:** Accept `[Point]` directly from the caller (who can build/cache it once when data loads) instead of accepting raw tuples and remapping on every render.
- **Why it matters:** Combines with PERF-036/037 — on MetricDetail, this remap runs on top of the already-redundant `fullSeries` recomputation.
- **Expected user impact:** Marginal on its own; meaningful once combined with the MetricDetail fixes above.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/MetricChart.swift`
- **Affected systems:** DesignSystem charts, MetricDetail
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** PERF-036
- **Risk if skipped:** Low individually.
- **Implementation notes:** Change `MetricChart`'s public initializer to accept `points: [Point]` directly, pushing the tuple→struct mapping to the one place the series is actually computed.

### PERF-050 — StatefulContainer's full-subtree swap discards and rebuilds all child view state on every load

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `StatefulContainer.body` (`apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatefulContainer.swift:23-47`) switches over `.loading`/`.empty`/`.error`/`.loaded` using a plain `switch`, which gives each case a different view identity — every transition (e.g. `.loading` → `.loaded`) causes SwiftUI to fully discard the previous subtree and construct the new one from scratch, losing any incidental child state (e.g. scroll position) and paying full layout cost.
- **Recommendation:** This is likely acceptable given loads are typically one-shot per screen visit, but for screens that reload frequently (Home via PERF-022, Body via PERF-031, Timeline via PERF-053) this means every reload — even ones that resolve to the same `.loaded` data — pays a full subtree rebuild rather than an in-place content diff.
- **Why it matters:** Compounds directly with the "reload on every tab visit" pattern flagged in PERF-022/031/053 — each of those reloads pays not just the query cost but also a full view-identity discard/rebuild via this shared container.
- **Expected user impact:** Smoother, flash-free tab revisits once combined with the staleness-check fixes above.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatefulContainer.swift`
- **Affected systems:** DesignSystem (app-wide)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** PERF-022, PERF-031, PERF-053
- **Risk if skipped:** Every screen using `StatefulContainer` (nearly all of them) pays this cost on reload.
- **Implementation notes:** Consider keeping the last `.loaded` content visible (with a subtle overlay indicator) while a reload is in flight, rather than transitioning through `.loading` and back, which would both look calmer (matching the "no idle spinners of drama" design intent already documented in the component) and avoid the subtree discard.

### PERF-051 — Color(light:dark:) reparses hex strings inside the dynamic-UIColor resolution closure

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `Color.init(light:dark:)` (`apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift:21-27`) wraps `UIColor { traits in UIColor(traits.userInterfaceStyle == .dark ? Color(hex: dark) : Color(hex: light)) }`; the `Color(hex:)` parsing (`Scanner(string:).scanHexInt64(&value)`, lines 9-16) happens *inside* the trait-resolution closure, so it re-parses the hex string via `Scanner` every time UIKit resolves the dynamic color for a given trait collection (e.g. on appearance changes, some redraw paths), not just once at the `static let` declaration site.
- **Recommendation:** Precompute both the light and dark `UIColor`/`Color` values once outside the closure and simply select between the two pre-built values inside the trait-resolution block, rather than re-parsing hex strings inside it.
- **Why it matters:** Every `BadanColor` token (`background`, `surface`, `primary`, `textPrimary`, etc.) uses this pattern; while individually cheap, trait resolution can be invoked more often than the design assumes (e.g. during interactive dark/light transitions), and hex parsing is pure waste when the two possible outputs are already known constants.
- **Expected user impact:** Marginal CPU reduction during appearance/trait changes.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift`
- **Affected systems:** DesignSystem (app-wide theming)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low; a correctness-neutral micro-optimization.
- **Implementation notes:** `init(light: String, dark: String) { let l = UIColor(Color(hex: light)); let d = UIColor(Color(hex: dark)); self.init(UIColor { $0.userInterfaceStyle == .dark ? d : l }) }`.
- **First patch sketch:** Update `Color.init(light:dark:)` in `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift` to precompute `let l = UIColor(Color(hex: light))` / `let d = UIColor(Color(hex: dark))` before constructing the dynamic `UIColor` closure, then reference `l`/`d` inside it instead of calling `Color(hex:)` per resolution.

### PERF-053 — TimelineScreen reloads the entire 7-store assembly on any profile mutation

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `TimelineScreen.body` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift:41`) uses `.task(id: env.profile) { vm.load(env) }` — since `env.profile` is `Equatable` over the entire `CustomizationProfile` struct (PERF-009), this re-runs the full `TimelineAssembler.assemble()` (PERF-054's 7-store fan-out) on *any* settings change: toggling a notification preference, flipping Arabic digits, changing the unit profile, or toggling home-module visibility all trigger a full Timeline reassembly, even though only language/units/depth actually affect what's rendered.
- **Recommendation:** Narrow the `.task(id:)` key to only the fields that actually affect Timeline's rendered output (e.g. a derived `struct TimelineRelevantState: Equatable { language, arabicDigits, unitProfile, depthPolicy, sensitiveModulesEnabled, nutritionEnabled }`).
- **Why it matters:** This is the most over-eager reload trigger in the app — a user toggling "Weekly digest" notifications in Settings, while nowhere near the Timeline tab, will cause the next Timeline visit to pay the full 21-day/7-store re-assembly for no rendering benefit.
- **Expected user impact:** Timeline stays instantly responsive after unrelated settings changes instead of re-fetching from scratch.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Timeline screen, settings/profile architecture
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** PERF-009
- **Risk if skipped:** Every future field added to `CustomizationProfile` silently expands this over-invalidation further.
- **Implementation notes:** The comment at `TimelineScreen.swift:39-40` explicitly acknowledges wanting reload on "language, digits, units, depth" — the fix is simply to key `.task(id:)` on a narrower derived value containing only those fields instead of the whole profile.
- **First patch sketch:** In `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`, add a small `private var relevantProfileKey: some Equatable { [env.language.rawValue, "\(env.profile.arabicDigits)", "\(env.profile.unitProfile)", "\(env.depth)"].joined() }` (or a proper `Hashable` struct) and key `.task(id:)` on that instead of `env.profile`.

### PERF-054 — TimelineAssembler.assemble() issues 7 sequential unbatched repo calls over a fixed window every load

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `TimelineAssembler.assemble()` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineAssembler.swift:17-61`) issues up to 7 sequential repository calls (sleep sessions, workout sessions, symptoms, regimens, adherence, nutrition, notes, raw weight samples) over a fixed 21-day window, every single time it's called — with no pagination, no incremental loading, and (per PERF-053) triggered far more often than necessary.
- **Recommendation:** Parallelize the independent repository calls via `TaskGroup` (they don't depend on each other except `regimenById` needing `regimens()` first), and consider caching the assembled result keyed by the window + relevant profile fields with a short TTL.
- **Why it matters:** This is explicitly documented in the repo as BADAN's "anti-fragmentation spine" — the widest single-screen repository fan-out in the presentation layer, and per PERF-053 it fires far more often than the data it produces actually changes.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster Timeline loads, especially for users with rich cross-store history (workouts + meds + symptoms + meals + notes all populated).
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineAssembler.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Timeline screen, multiple repositories (call site)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** PERF-053
- **Risk if skipped:** Grows worse as more event types are added to the Timeline spine.
- **Implementation notes:** Since `TimelineAssembler` is a `@MainActor struct`, parallelizing its internal calls requires either moving the calls off-actor (if repos are thread-safe per the SQLite connection's `NSRecursiveLock`) or restructuring as an async function using `async let` for the independent fetches.

### PERF-058 — TimelineScreen.groupByDay recomputes bucketing on every body render

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `loaded(_:)` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift:47-65`) calls `groupByDay(filtered(events))` inline in the view body — this bucketing pass (building a `[String: [TimelineEvent]]` dictionary and sorting keys, lines 226-234) reruns on every render, including renders triggered by unrelated state (e.g. scroll-adjacent SwiftUI diff passes, filter-chip taps that don't change the actual filter set).
- **Recommendation:** Cache the grouped result in `@State`, recomputed only when `events` or `selectedTypes` actually change (e.g. via `.onChange`), rather than inline in the body.
- **Why it matters:** Grouping + sorting a 21-day, potentially-dozens-of-events list is meaningfully more expensive than a plain filter, and doing it unconditionally on every render is wasted work.
- **Expected user impact:** Smoother Timeline interaction, particularly when toggling filter chips.

- **Risk if skipped:** Grows with event history density.

- **Recommendation:** Compute `let descriptor = severityDescriptor(sev)` once per render and reuse it for both the label and the accessibility value.

- **Expected user impact:** Negligible; a clean, essentially free fix.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1

- **Approval needed:** No

### PERF-069 — MedicationLogViewModel.load's due-slot assignment is an O(regimens×times×events) nested scan

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `load(_:)` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift:69-185`) assigns adherence events to schedule slots via a nested loop (`for e in events { for (i, s) in descs.enumerated() where assigned[i] == nil { ... } }`, lines 102-111) with no early exit once every slot is claimed, plus a second independent O(week × regimens) pass for the 7-day adherence strip.
- **Recommendation:** Break out of the inner loop once `assigned.count == descs.count`, and consider indexing events by scheduled-minute up front instead of a linear best-distance scan per event.
- **Why it matters:** Negligible at typical scale (a handful of regimens/times per user) but architecturally unbounded — this runs on every load, and `load()` is called after every single take/skip action (see PERF-072).
- **Expected user impact:** Marginal today; protects against slowdown for power users with many regimens/times.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low at current scale; worth a comment/guard if regimen counts are expected to grow significantly.
- **Implementation notes:** Add an early `if assigned.count == descs.count { break }` inside the outer event loop.

### PERF-072 — MedicationLogViewModel.load rebuilds the full 7-day adherence-count structure from scratch on every take/skip mutation

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `take(_:env:)`, `skip(_:reason:env:)`, and `takeAll(env:)` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift:189-226`) all call `record(...)` followed by a full `load(env)` — re-running the entire due-slot assignment (PERF-069) and 7-day adherence-strip rebuild (lines 137-169) for every single take/skip tap, when only one slot's/day's state actually changed.
- **Recommendation:** After a mutation, update the affected `DueSlot`/adherence-strip entry locally in `state` instead of re-running the full `load(env)` pipeline.
- **Why it matters:** Taking or skipping a medication is likely the single most frequent interaction on this screen, and each tap currently pays the full reload cost (2 repository queries + the nested-loop reconstruction from PERF-069) instead of an O(1) local update.
- **Expected user impact:** Instant visual feedback on Take/Skip taps instead of a reload-driven micro-delay.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** PERF-069
- **Risk if skipped:** Every take/skip tap pays full-reload latency, which is the primary interaction loop on this screen.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a `MedicationLogViewModel.applyLocal(slotId:status:)` that mutates the existing `MedData` in `state` directly after a successful `insertAdherence`, falling back to a full `load(env)` only if local state is stale.

### PERF-078 — WorkoutLogView's flat body re-diffs the entire recent-workouts list on every capture-form interaction

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `WorkoutLogView.body` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift:131-147`) is one flat `VStack` containing both the interactive capture form (`activityCard`, `durationCard`, `effortCard`, `optionalCard`) and the read-only `recentSection` — every `@State` change from the form (RPE slider drag, activity pill tap, text field edit) forces SwiftUI to re-evaluate and diff the entire body, including the recent-workouts list below, even though that list's underlying data hasn't changed.
- **Recommendation:** Extract `recentSection` into its own child view (e.g. `WorkoutRecentList(workouts: vm.recent)`) so SwiftUI's diffing can skip it when only capture-form `@State` changes.
- **Why it matters:** RPE slider dragging in particular can fire many state updates per second, each currently forcing a full-list re-diff; extracting the list into a separate view identity is a standard SwiftUI performance pattern that directly addresses this.
- **Expected user impact:** Smoother slider dragging and form interaction, most noticeable for users with a longer recent-workouts history.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Workout logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every future field added to the capture form (this pattern repeats in Nutrition, PERF-081) makes the recent-list re-diff cost worse.
- **Implementation notes:** Standard SwiftUI technique — a child view with `let workouts: [WorkoutEntry]` (or observing its own slice of state) only re-evaluates when its own inputs change, not when a sibling's `@State` changes.
- **First patch sketch:** In `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, extract `recentSection`'s body into a new `private struct WorkoutRecentSection: View { let vm: WorkoutLogViewModel; ... }` (or pass `workouts`/`loggedToday` directly) so it has independent view identity from the capture-form `VStack`.

### PERF-079 — NutritionLogViewModel.load recomputes totals via full reduce over the day's meals on every save

- **Expected user impact:** Marginally snappier meal logging.

- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No

- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low; small daily entry counts keep this cheap in practice.
- **Implementation notes:** In `save(...)`, append the new `NutritionEntry` to `meals` and add its `energyKcal`/`proteinG` to the running totals directly, skipping the re-fetch.

### PERF-083 — ExportHistoryRow.availableFileURLs performs synchronous disk I/O inside the view body per row per render

- **Category:** Performance
- **Problem:** `ExportHistoryRow.availableFileURLs()` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift:691-704`) calls `FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath:)` synchronously, once per candidate filename, inside the view body — for up to 20 history rows × 2-3 candidate files each, this is 40-60 filesystem stat calls on every render of the export history section.
- **Recommendation:** Resolve and cache `availableFileURLs` once per `ExportJob` when `ExportCenterViewModel.loadHistory` runs, rather than re-checking the filesystem on every SwiftUI body evaluation.
- **Why it matters:** Filesystem I/O inside a view body is one of the more expensive patterns in this report — unlike in-memory formatting costs, `fileExists` involves an actual syscall, and it's re-run on every render including ones triggered by unrelated screen state.
- **Expected user impact:** Meaningfully smoother scrolling of the export history list, especially for users with many past exports.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Export center
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Grows linearly with a user's export history size and directly does syscalls in the render path.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a small presentation wrapper (`ExportHistoryItem { let job: ExportJob; let fileURLs: [URL] }`) computed once in `loadHistory`, and have `ExportHistoryRow` read the precomputed `fileURLs` instead of calling `availableFileURLs()` in its body.
- **First patch sketch:** In `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`, change `ExportCenterViewModel.history: [ExportJob]` to `history: [ExportHistoryItem]`, compute `availableFileURLs()` once per job inside `loadHistory(_:)`, and update `ExportHistoryRow` to take the precomputed array directly.
