## Cluster B — Incremental & background sync

### FEAT-017 — Wire the reserved `read_anchors` table to HKAnchoredObjectQuery for incremental iOS sync

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `read_anchors (store, platform_type) pk, anchor BLOB` exists in both `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Migrations.swift:182` and Android's `Schema.kt:185` but is queried/written by nothing — every sync re-reads the full requested date range from scratch.
- **Recommendation:** Persist `HKQueryAnchor` (serialized) per platform type into `read_anchors` after each `HKAnchoredObjectQuery`, and pass the stored anchor back in on the next sync to fetch only new/changed samples.
- **Why it matters:** `docs/data-model.md` documents this table as the sync-ready seam (ADR-0003) specifically so incremental sync doesn't require a schema retrofit — it's sitting there unused.
- **Expected user impact:** Sync becomes fast and battery-cheap instead of always re-scanning 90 days.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Migrations.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Platform/Health/HealthKitAdapter.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/` (new `ReadAnchorRepository`)
- **Affected systems:** iOS sync
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-001
- **Risk if skipped:** Every sync stays an expensive full re-scan; battery and latency cost scale with account age.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a small `ReadAnchorRepository` (get/set BLOB by store+platformType) alongside the existing repositories in `Sources/Storage/Repositories/`, then have `HealthKitAdapter` accept/return an anchor.

### FEAT-018 — HKObserverQuery + enableBackgroundDelivery for near-real-time updates

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** BADAN has no background delivery at all (per repo facts: "No: ... background sync"); `Info.plist`/`project.yml` declare no background modes, so HealthKit changes are only ever seen if the user happens to open the app.
- **Recommendation:** Register `HKObserverQuery` for the app's core types and call `HKHealthStore.enableBackgroundDelivery(for:frequency:)`, triggering an anchored incremental ingest (FEAT-017) on each callback.
- **Why it matters:** Without this, "Last delivery" timestamps on `SourcesScreen` are stale by definition — data only updates on manual app open.
- **Expected user impact:** Today tab reflects new sleep/steps/HR shortly after the Health app or a paired device records them, not only after next launch.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/App/Info.plist`, `apps/ios/project.yml`, `apps/ios/Sources/Platform/Health/HealthKitAdapter.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS background sync
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-001, FEAT-017
- **Risk if skipped:** Data feels stale; "Sources" screen's "last delivery" concept has no real trigger behind it.
- **Implementation notes:** Requires the `remote-notification` or `processing` background mode; needs care that observer callbacks don't fire ingestion on the main thread (per `SQLiteConnection`'s existing lock-serialized access).

### FEAT-019 — BGAppRefreshTask scheduling for periodic HealthKit ingestion

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** No `BGTaskScheduler` registration exists anywhere in `apps/ios` (confirmed via repo-wide search) — there is no scheduled background refresh path independent of `HKObserverQuery` wake-ups.
- **Recommendation:** Register a `BGAppRefreshTaskRequest` in `App/BADANApp.swift` that periodically triggers `syncHealthKit()` (FEAT-002) even when observer callbacks are throttled by iOS.
- **Why it matters:** `HKObserverQuery` background delivery can be delayed/coalesced by iOS; a periodic refresh task is the standard belt-and-suspenders complement.
- **Expected user impact:** More consistently fresh data across variable background-delivery timing.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/App/BADANApp.swift`, `apps/ios/App/Info.plist`
- **Affected systems:** iOS background scheduling
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-018
- **Risk if skipped:** Sync freshness depends solely on best-effort observer delivery timing.

### FEAT-020 — Use Health Connect's changes API instead of always re-reading the last 90 days

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `AppEnvironment.kt` `syncHealthConnect()` (lines 90-97) always ingests `range = last 90 days` on every manual "Sync now" tap — there is no `getChangesToken`/`getChanges` usage, so every sync re-reads and re-dedupes the full window.
- **Recommendation:** Call `HealthConnectClient.getChangesToken()` once, persist it in the reserved `read_anchors` table, then use `getChanges(token)` on subsequent syncs for incremental reads, falling back to full-range only on first connect or token expiry.
- **Why it matters:** `read_anchors` already exists in `Schema.kt:185` for exactly this purpose and is unused; the current approach means sync cost grows with account age rather than staying O(new records).
- **Expected user impact:** Faster "Sync now" taps, lower battery/CPU cost per sync.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/app/AppEnvironment.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/platform/health/HealthConnectAdapter.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/storage/Schema.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Android sync
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every "Sync now" tap costs the same regardless of how little actually changed; this scales badly.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `ReadAnchorDao`/query pair for `read_anchors`, store the changes token after each successful `syncHealthConnect()`, and branch `HealthConnectAdapter` reads to use `getChanges(token)` when a token is present.

### FEAT-021 — Android background sync via WorkManager (currently manual-button-only)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `HealthConnectCard.kt` only syncs on an explicit "Sync now" tap (`hcSyncNow`); there is no `WorkManager`/`work-runtime` dependency in `apps/android/app/build.gradle.kts` and no periodic work request anywhere — sync only happens while the Sources screen is open and tapped.
- **Recommendation:** Add `androidx.work:work-runtime-ktx`, define a `CoroutineWorker` that calls `AppEnvironment.syncHealthConnect()`, and schedule it as periodic (respecting Health Connect's ~15 min minimum interval doctrine).
- **Why it matters:** This is the largest single foreground/background gap on Android — real Health Connect reads exist, but they're inert unless the user manually opens Sources and taps sync.
- **Expected user impact:** Data freshness without manual intervention, matching what users expect from any health app.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/build.gradle.kts`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/app/AppEnvironment.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
- **Affected systems:** Android background sync
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-020 (to make periodic syncs cheap)
- **Risk if skipped:** Android's real HC integration is functionally manual-only, undercutting the "ahead of iOS" advantage noted in repo facts.

### FEAT-022 — Handle Health Connect changes-token expiry with fallback to full resync

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Once FEAT-020 introduces token-based incremental sync, Health Connect's `getChanges` can throw when a token has expired (data purged or app dormant too long); nothing in `HealthConnectAdapter.kt`'s `readAll` (lines 99-119) currently distinguishes "no data" from "token expired."
- **Recommendation:** Catch the expired-token case explicitly and fall back to a full-range re-ingest (idempotent via the existing partial-unique identity indexes per ADR-0003), then re-establish a fresh token.
- **Why it matters:** Without this, a stale token after a long dormancy silently returns empty/wrong deltas instead of recovering.
- **Expected user impact:** Sync stays correct even after long periods of not opening the app.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/platform/health/HealthConnectAdapter.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Android sync correctness
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-020
- **Risk if skipped:** Long-dormant users could silently stop receiving new data after reopening the app.

### FEAT-023 — Wire the reserved `import_batches` table for resumable/chunked bulk backfill

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `import_batches` (`source_kind, file_name, state, chunk_cursor, counts`) exists identically in `Migrations.swift:183` and `Schema.kt:186` but nothing reads or writes it — a first-time 90-day (or multi-year Apple Health export) backfill has no resumability if interrupted.
- **Recommendation:** On any large initial sync or file import (FEAT-045/046), write progress rows to `import_batches` with a `chunk_cursor`, so an interrupted backfill can resume from the last completed chunk rather than restarting.
- **Why it matters:** This table is explicitly the reserved seam for exactly this purpose per `docs/data-model.md`; large first-sync jobs (e.g., years of Apple Health history) can otherwise be killed by iOS backgrounding mid-import with total loss of progress.
- **Expected user impact:** Interrupted large imports resume instead of restarting from zero.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Migrations.swift`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/storage/Schema.kt`, new `ImportBatchRepository` on both platforms
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android import & first-sync
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-002, FEAT-045
- **Risk if skipped:** Large first-time backfills (common for new installs with years of Health data) have no resilience to interruption.

### FEAT-024 — Populate `Source.lastDeliveryAt` from real ingestion runs

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `sources.last_delivery_at` is displayed in `SourcesScreen.swift`'s `detailLine(Self.lastDeliveryLabel, ...)` but is only ever populated by `SeedController`'s demo seed — no real ingestion path (once FEAT-002 exists) currently updates it.
- **Recommendation:** Have `IngestionPipeline.ingest(from:range:)`'s `upsertSourcesAndDevices` step stamp `last_delivery_at = now` on every successful real sync.
- **Why it matters:** Otherwise this field permanently shows the seed timestamp, misleading users about how current their data connection is.
- **Expected user impact:** "Last delivery" becomes a trustworthy, live indicator.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Ingestion/IngestionPipeline.swift`, `apps/android/.../domain/ingestion/IngestionPipeline.kt`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android source metadata
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-002
- **Risk if skipped:** UI shows a permanently stale, seed-derived timestamp once real syncing exists.
- **First patch sketch:** In `IngestionPipeline.upsertSourcesAndDevices`, set `lastDeliveryAt: now` on the `Source` upsert whenever `port` is not the fake store.

### FEAT-025 — Persist "syncing" state across process death (Android)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `HealthConnectCard.kt`'s `hcSyncing` indicator is held in local `@Composable` `remember`/`mutableStateOf` — if the process is killed mid-sync (backgrounding during a long first pull), the UI has no way to know a sync was in progress or whether it completed.
- **Recommendation:** Back the syncing/last-result state with a persisted flag (e.g., in the `import_batches`/`sync_cursors` seam per FEAT-020/023) instead of purely in-memory Compose state.
- **Why it matters:** Without persisted state, users get no feedback if a sync silently died mid-flight from process death.
- **Expected user impact:** Reliable sync status across app restarts.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/HealthConnectCard.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Android sync UX
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-021
- **Risk if skipped:** Low-frequency but confusing "did my sync work?" moments after backgrounding.

### FEAT-026 — Build an iOS SourcesScreen connect/status component matching HealthConnectCard's state machine

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Android's `HealthConnectCard.kt` models five explicit states (`hcConnect`, `hcSyncNow`, `hcConnected`, `hcSyncing`, `hcNoData`, `hcDenied`, `hcUpdate`); iOS's `SourcesScreen.swift` has no equivalent state machine at all — it's pure read-only display.

- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/SourcesScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Sources screen
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile

- **Risk if skipped:** Cross-platform UX inconsistency; iOS users have no way to know if they're still looking at demo data post-onboarding.

### FEAT-027 — Declare Health Connect's background-read permission

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `AndroidManifest.xml` declares 9 `android.permission.health.READ_*` permissions (lines 5-13) but not `android.permission.health.READ_HEALTH_DATA_IN_BACKGROUND`, which Health Connect requires for any read attempted while the app is not in the foreground.
- **Recommendation:** Add the background-read permission declaration and the corresponding runtime permission request, as a prerequisite for FEAT-021's WorkManager-driven background sync.
- **Why it matters:** Without this manifest entry, FEAT-021's background worker would fail to read any Health Connect data when the app isn't foregrounded, silently defeating the feature.
- **Expected user impact:** Enables true background sync (not just background scheduling with foreground-only reads).
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
- **Affected systems:** Android permissions
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** FEAT-021's background worker would run but read nothing while backgrounded.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.health.READ_HEALTH_DATA_IN_BACKGROUND" />` next to the existing `READ_*` block in `AndroidManifest.xml`.

### FEAT-028 — Retry/backoff policy for transient Health Connect read failures

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `HealthConnectAdapter.kt`'s `readAll` (lines 99-119) wraps each paged read in `runCatching {...}.getOrNull() ?: break` — any transient failure (e.g., a momentary Health Connect provider hiccup) silently truncates the page loop with no retry and no surfaced error, potentially losing part of a sync.
- **Recommendation:** Add a bounded retry with backoff before treating a page failure as terminal, and surface a distinguishable "partial sync" result to the UI instead of silent truncation.
- **Why it matters:** Right now a single flaky read call can silently under-ingest a sync with no user-visible signal that anything went wrong.
- **Expected user impact:** More reliable syncs; honest reporting when something did go wrong instead of silent partial success.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/platform/health/HealthConnectAdapter.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Android sync reliability
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Silent, hard-to-diagnose partial-sync data gaps.

## Cluster C — Device & vendor integrations (BLE, vendor-class, file-based)

### FEAT-029 — BLE integration for blood pressure cuffs (iOS CoreBluetooth)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** No `CoreBluetooth` import exists anywhere in `apps/ios/Sources` or `apps/ios/App` — BADAN has zero direct-device connectivity; blood pressure data (`heart.bp_systolic`/`_diastolic`) can only ever be manually entered or come via HealthKit-linked apps.
- **Recommendation:** Build a `CoreBluetooth`-based adapter implementing the Bluetooth SIG Blood Pressure GATT profile, feeding `SampleDTO` pairs into the same `IngestionPipeline` as HealthKit, with `SourceType.vendor`.
- **Why it matters:** Many BP cuffs (especially non-Apple-ecosystem ones) never reach HealthKit at all; direct BLE is the only path to their data.
- **Expected user impact:** Users with BLE BP cuffs get automatic readings without a third-party bridge app.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** No existing file; new module required under `apps/ios/Sources/Platform/Health/` (e.g., `BLEBloodPressureAdapter.swift`)
- **Affected systems:** iOS device connectivity
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-040
- **Risk if skipped:** Direct-BLE-only devices remain permanently unreachable regardless of HealthKit wiring quality.

### FEAT-030 — BLE integration for blood pressure cuffs (Android)

- **Category:** New Feature

### FEAT-043 — Flag live vendor API integrations (Withings/Garmin/Oura Connect APIs) as an explicit post-M4 backend decision

- **Category:** New Feature

- **Recommendation:** Record a lightweight forward-looking spec (not implementation) distinguishing "vendor file import" (MVP-safe, no network) from "vendor live API" (post-M4, requires backend/network ADR revision), so file-import work isn't conflated with a scope-violating live integration.
- **Why it matters:** Prevents an implementer from accidentally building a live network-calling vendor integration that violates ADR-0002's zero-network-in-MVP guardrail.

- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `docs/adr/ADR-0002-no-backend-mvp.md` (cross-reference), no code changes
- **Affected systems:** Planning/architecture
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Risk of an accidental ADR-0002 violation when someone implements "vendor integration" without checking whether it means file import or live API.

### FEAT-044 — Vendor file import format validation & user-facing error mapping

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** None of the file-import features (FEAT-033/034/035/045/046) have any defined error-handling contract yet for malformed/unsupported files — there's no existing import code at all to check against.

- **Why it matters:** Import is inherently failure-prone (users pick wrong files, partial downloads, format drift across vendor app versions); without a shared error contract each importer would invent its own inconsistent failure UX.
- **Expected user impact:** Clear, calm recovery guidance instead of a silent no-op or a raw exception message.

- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** No existing file; shared import infrastructure to be created alongside FEAT-046
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android import UX
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-046
- **Risk if skipped:** Each importer reinvents its own error handling, likely inconsistently and not wellness-safe by default.

## Cluster D — Manual file import

### FEAT-045 — Apple Health export.zip (XML) parser & importer

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Users who already have years of Apple Health history in an `export.zip` (from Health app's "Export All Health Data") have no way to bring that history into BADAN — there is no XML parser anywhere in the repo, and HealthKit's live API (FEAT-001) typically only surfaces a rolling window efficiently for bulk historical backfill.
- **Recommendation:** Build a streaming XML parser for the Apple Health export format (`export.xml`), mapping `Record`/`Workout`/`Sleep` elements into the same DTOs `HealthKitAdapter` produces, registered as `SourceType.fileImport`.
- **Why it matters:** This is the single most direct way for a new BADAN user to arrive with complete history on day one instead of only forward-looking data.
- **Expected user impact:** New users can import their entire Apple Health archive instead of starting from zero.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** No existing file; new module required (e.g., `Sources/Platform/Import/AppleHealthExportImporter.swift`)
- **Affected systems:** iOS import
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-023 (resumability — these files can be enormous), FEAT-036
- **Risk if skipped:** Users migrating to BADAN start with no history, a major onboarding disadvantage versus competitors that support this import.

### FEAT-046 — Generic CSV metric importer using the existing 24-column export schema as the reciprocal import contract

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `packages/export-schemas/csv_columns.json` defines a complete 24-column contract (including `import_batch_id`, described in-schema as the "One-tap-undo import lineage id (§30.5)") for export, but there is no importer anywhere that reads this same shape back in — the schema is one-directional today.
- **Recommendation:** Build a CSV importer that accepts files in the same 24-column shape (or a subset), enabling round-trip export→edit→reimport and CSV exports from other tools that adopt BADAN's schema.
- **Why it matters:** The schema already documents an import-lineage column (`import_batch_id`) that presumes a reciprocal importer exists — the contract was designed for this and it was never built.
- **Expected user impact:** Power users can bulk-correct or bulk-add historical data via spreadsheet, then reimport.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `packages/export-schemas/csv_columns.json`, no existing importer file — new module required
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android import
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-023
- **Risk if skipped:** The `import_batch_id` column in the export schema stays a documented-but-unrealized promise.

### FEAT-047 — CSV import column-mapping/preview UI before commit

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Once FEAT-046 exists, arbitrary/non-BADAN-shaped CSVs (e.g., a user's own spreadsheet, or a vendor CSV not covered by FEAT-033/034/035) still need a way to map their columns to BADAN metric IDs before committing — no such mapping UI exists anywhere.
- **Recommendation:** Add a preview screen showing detected columns with dropdowns to map each to a `registry.json` metric ID (or "skip"), plus a row-count/date-range summary before the final "Import" commit.
- **Why it matters:** Blind CSV import without preview risks silently importing garbage (wrong units, wrong metric) into a user's permanent health record.
- **Expected user impact:** Confident, reviewable imports instead of a black-box "hope it worked" action.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** No existing file; new screen required in `Sources/Features/Body/` or a new `Import` feature folder
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android import UX
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-046
- **Risk if skipped:** CSV import (FEAT-046) ships as a risky black box for anything beyond BADAN's exact own export shape.

### FEAT-048 — Route imported rows through the existing dedup-lite reconciliation pipeline

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `IngestionPipeline`'s dedup-lite (sleep overlap ≥70%, `ReconciliationRepository`) currently only runs against `HealthStorePort`-sourced sessions; none of the planned importers (FEAT-033/034/035/045/046) have a defined path through the same reconciliation journal.
- **Recommendation:** Ensure every importer feeds through the identical `IngestionPipeline.ingest`-style path (or an explicit import-specific variant that still calls the dedup/reconciliation step), so an imported Apple Health sleep session doesn't duplicate a HealthKit-sourced one.
- **Why it matters:** Without this, a user who both connects HealthKit live (FEAT-001) and imports a historical `export.zip` (FEAT-045) covering an overlapping period would get duplicate rows.
- **Expected user impact:** No duplicate data when live sync and historical import overlap in time range.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Ingestion/IngestionPipeline.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android import correctness
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-045, FEAT-046
- **Risk if skipped:** Overlapping live-sync + import scenarios silently double-count data (e.g., inflated step counts, duplicate sleep sessions).

### FEAT-049 — Import batch undo, realizing the "one-tap-undo import lineage" the schema already documents

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `csv_columns.json` describes `import_batch_id` as enabling "one-tap-undo import lineage" but no undo action exists anywhere in the codebase — once an import commits, there is no way to reverse it short of manual row-by-row deletion.
- **Recommendation:** Add an "Undo import" action (surfaced per `import_batches` row once FEAT-023 exists) that tombstones (`deleted_at`, per ADR-0003) every row carrying that `batch_id`.
- **Why it matters:** This closes the loop on a feature the schema was explicitly designed for but that was never built — a mis-mapped or duplicate import currently has no clean recovery path.
- **Expected user impact:** A bad import (wrong file, wrong mapping) can be cleanly reversed in one action.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `packages/export-schemas/csv_columns.json` (spec reference), `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/` (new undo method)
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android import
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-023, FEAT-046
- **Risk if skipped:** Users have no safety net for a bad import into their permanent local health record.
- **First patch sketch:** Add an `undoImportBatch(batchId:)` method to the measurement repositories that sets `deleted_at = now` on every row with a matching `batch_id`, reusing the existing tombstone convention already used for the reversible dedup journal.

- **Recommendation:** Add a Jetpack Glance-based home-screen widget mirroring FEAT-051's content.
- **Why it matters:** Parity with iOS; Android widgets are historically an even more heavily used surface than iOS ones.
- **Expected user impact:** Same glance value as FEAT-051, on Android.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, `apps/android/app/build.gradle.kts`, no existing widget source
- **Affected systems:** Android widgets
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-021 (needs real synced data to be worth showing)
- **Risk if skipped:** Same as FEAT-051, for Android.

### FEAT-055 — Widget deep link into MetricDetail

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** BADAN has no URL scheme or `App Intents`/deep-link routing declared anywhere (`project.yml` has no `CFBundleURLTypes`); once widgets exist (FEAT-051/054) tapping one would have no way to open the specific relevant metric screen.
- **Recommendation:** Add a custom URL scheme (`badan://metric/{metricId}`) and a router in `App/BADANApp.swift`/`RootView` that navigates directly to `MetricDetail` for that metric.
- **Why it matters:** Without deep linking, a widget tap can only open the app to its default tab, losing the "glance then drill in" value widgets are supposed to provide.
- **Expected user impact:** Tapping a widget takes users straight to the relevant metric, not just the app's home screen.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/App/BADANApp.swift`, `apps/ios/project.yml`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android navigation
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-051, FEAT-054
- **Risk if skipped:** Widgets become read-only glances with no drill-down path.

### FEAT-056 — Widget data provider respects the casual/power CustomizationProfile

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `CustomizationProfile` lives in-process inside `AppEnvironment` (`@Observable @MainActor`); a widget extension runs in a separate process and has no access to it, so a widget built naively would either hardcode one depth or need its own profile read path.
- **Recommendation:** Persist the relevant subset of `CustomizationProfile` (casual/power depth) into the App Group shared container so the widget's timeline provider can render consistently with the main app's current mode.
- **Why it matters:** "Casual and power-user modes are presentation layers over one underlying model" is a stated product guardrail (CLAUDE.md) — a widget that ignores it would silently break that consistency.
- **Expected user impact:** Widget content matches the depth (casual vs. power) the user has chosen in the app.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift` (CustomizationProfile), widget extension target
- **Affected systems:** iOS widgets
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-051
- **Risk if skipped:** Widget could show power-mode density to a casual-mode user or vice versa, violating the stated one-model guardrail.

### FEAT-057 — Widget Arabic/RTL layout support

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Arabic/RTL is a stated first-order concern (CLAUDE.md) with structural support in the main app (`Core/Localization/Strings.swift`, `AppLanguage.swift`), but a WidgetKit extension is a separate SwiftUI environment that needs its own explicit RTL verification — nothing today establishes that widgets will inherit it correctly.
- **Recommendation:** Explicitly verify and test the widget extension's layout mirroring and text direction under `AppLanguage.arabic`, reusing `Strings.swift`'s `Loc` catalog inside the extension target.
- **Why it matters:** A widget that silently breaks RTL would violate a stated first-order product guardrail on the app's most-visible-outside-the-app surface.
- **Expected user impact:** Correct Arabic-language widget rendering for Arabic-locale users.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** Widget extension target (once FEAT-051 exists)
- **Affected systems:** iOS widgets, localization
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-051
- **Risk if skipped:** Silent RTL regression on a highly visible surface, contradicting a stated project guardrail.

### FEAT-058 — Interactive widget button for quick symptom/mood log

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** iOS 17+ (BADAN's deployment target) supports interactive widgets (App Intent buttons directly in the widget), but nothing in the repo has any `AppIntent` code (confirmed via repo-wide search) to back such a button.
- **Recommendation:** Add an interactive widget button that invokes an `AppIntent` to quick-log mood/symptom severity without opening the app, writing directly via the same repositories `LogHub` uses.
- **Why it matters:** This is the highest-friction-reduction possible for subjective check-ins (mood/energy/stress), which currently require a full app launch and navigation to log.
- **Expected user impact:** One-tap mood/symptom logging from the home screen.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** Widget extension target, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/` (shared write path)
- **Affected systems:** iOS widgets, App Intents
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-051, FEAT-083
- **Risk if skipped:** Subjective check-ins remain full-app-launch-only, a meaningful friction tax on the data BADAN most wants frequent entries for.

## Cluster H — Notifications & reminders

### FEAT-068 — Medication adherence reminder notifications (iOS)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/` (883 lines, the largest feature file) models `medication_regimens.schedule(JSON)` and `adherence_events` with `skip_reason`/`skip_note`, but a repo-wide grep for `UNUserNotificationCenter`/notification code returns zero hits — nothing ever reminds a user to take a dose.
- **Recommendation:** Schedule local notifications (`UNUserNotificationCenter`, no network/backend required) at each regimen's scheduled dose times, deep-linking into the Medication log screen on tap.
- **Why it matters:** A medication-tracking feature with schedule data but no reminders only helps users who remember on their own — the highest-value moment (a timely nudge) is entirely missing.
- **Expected user impact:** Users actually get reminded to take medication, not just given a place to log it after the fact.

- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/` (schedule model), no existing notification scheduling file

### FEAT-072 — Notification permission request timing/UX (first-ask moment)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** No notification permission request exists anywhere in the app today (a prerequisite gap for FEAT-068/069/070/071); unlike HealthKit's onboarding moment (however currently broken per FEAT-003), there's no defined "when do we ask for notifications" moment at all.

## Cluster I — Backup & device-to-device transfer

### FEAT-076 — iCloud/Drive encrypted backup using the reserved sync-ready columns

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Repo facts confirm "No: ... iCloud backup exclusion handling" and no backup mechanism exists; every row table already carries `updated_at`/`origin_device_id`/`deleted_at` specifically "for a future multi-device / E2E-sync world" per ADR-0003, but nothing uses them for backup today — a lost/wiped device means total data loss.
- **Recommendation:** Build an iCloud (or user-chosen Drive) backup of `badan.db` (and `badan_sensitive.db` when the user opts in), using the existing `updated_at`/`origin_device_id` columns to support future incremental/multi-device merge, gated behind SQLCipher adoption for the sensitive file (see FEAT-077).
- **Why it matters:** BADAN is explicitly local-first with "no backend" — but that design choice makes device loss catastrophic without an explicit backup story; this is the single highest-stakes data-loss gap in the whole app.
- **Expected user impact:** Users don't permanently lose years of health history to a lost or replaced phone.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Database.swift`, `docs/adr/ADR-0003-sync-ready-not-sync-dependent.md` (design continuity)
- **Affected systems:** iOS backup
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-077 for the sensitive-plus namespace
- **Risk if skipped:** Total, unrecoverable loss of a user's entire local health history on device loss/replacement — the single largest data-loss risk in the product today.

### FEAT-077 — SQLCipher adoption as the explicit prerequisite for encrypted backup/passphrase export

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** ADR-0004 explicitly flags SQLCipher as "not yet adopted" and states it's "needed before sync or passphrase-protected export," tracked for M4 — this is a named, deliberate blocker rather than an oversight.
- **Recommendation:** Treat SQLCipher adoption as its own tracked prerequisite work item ahead of FEAT-076/078/079, since encrypting `badan_sensitive.db` at rest with a user passphrase is required before any off-device backup of sensitive data is responsible to ship.
- **Why it matters:** Backing up `badan_sensitive.db` (medications, symptoms, conditions) to iCloud/Drive without SQLCipher would mean sensitive health data leaves the device protected only by generic OS file encryption, not app-level passphrase protection — a meaningfully weaker posture than the sensitive-namespace design intends.
- **Expected user impact:** Ensures sensitive backup data is properly protected before backup ships, not after.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `docs/adr/ADR-0004-sensitive-namespace-and-encryption.md`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/SQLite/SQLiteConnection.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android storage encryption
- **Suggested owner:** Infra
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Shipping FEAT-076/078 without this would put sensitive-plus data (meds/symptoms/conditions) into cloud backup with a weaker protection posture than the rest of the app's design implies.

### FEAT-078 — Google Drive / local backup (Android parity)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Same gap as FEAT-076 on Android — no backup mechanism exists; `AndroidManifest.xml` even explicitly sets `android:allowBackup="false"`, meaning Android's own auto-backup is deliberately disabled with nothing custom in its place.
- **Recommendation:** Build a Google Drive (or user-chosen storage) backup path for `Schema.kt`'s tables, mirroring FEAT-076.
- **Why it matters:** `allowBackup="false"` means Android's stock backup mechanism is off and nothing replaces it — this is a stronger, more explicit data-loss risk than iOS's default-silent gap.
- **Expected user impact:** Same as FEAT-076, on Android.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/storage/`
- **Affected systems:** Android backup
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-077
- **Risk if skipped:** Same catastrophic-data-loss risk as FEAT-076, and explicitly acknowledged in the manifest's `allowBackup="false"` with no replacement.

### FEAT-079 — Device-to-device transfer via AirDrop of an export bundle, with a matching restore importer

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `ExportRunner`/`CSVWriter`/`JSONBundleWriter` (`Sources/Export/`) can produce a manifest-checksummed export bundle, but there is no corresponding import path anywhere to rehydrate that bundle into a fresh install — export is a one-way door today.
- **Recommendation:** Build a "Restore from BADAN export" importer that reads `ExportRunner`'s own JSON bundle format back in, then surface an AirDrop share/receive flow so a user can move their full history to a new device without cloud backup.
- **Why it matters:** BADAN already produces a complete, checksummed, provenance-preserving export — the missing half is simply reading it back in, which is far less work than a from-scratch backup format.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can move to a new iPhone and restore their full history via AirDrop, no cloud/backend required — consistent with the local-first philosophy.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Export/` (ExportRunner, JSONBundleWriter), no existing import counterpart
- **Affected systems:** iOS export/import
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-048 (dedup on reimport)
- **Risk if skipped:** Export is a dead-end feature that can produce a file but never rehydrate it — a lighter-weight local-first alternative to full cloud backup goes unbuilt despite most of the plumbing already existing.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `restoreFromBundle(url:)` method that parses `JSONBundleWriter`'s own manifest format and calls the standard repository upsert paths — start with the JSON bundle format only since CSV round-trip already has a separate track (FEAT-046).

### FEAT-080 — Restore-from-backup import path (rehydrate a new device from FEAT-076/078)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Same "export without import" asymmetry as FEAT-079, but specifically for the cloud-backup file format from FEAT-076/078 rather than the manual-share export bundle.
- **Recommendation:** Build the restore path as part of FEAT-076/078's initial scope, not as a follow-up — a backup with no tested restore path isn't a real backup.
- **Why it matters:** An untested/nonexistent restore path is the single most common way "backup" features fail silently in production (the backup exists, but nobody can actually recover from it).
- **Expected user impact:** Confidence that backup actually works when needed, not just that it silently uploads.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** Same as FEAT-076/078
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android backup
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-076, FEAT-078
- **Risk if skipped:** A backup feature that's never been exercised as a restore is not meaningfully different from having no backup at all.

### FEAT-081 — iCloud auto-backup exclusion policy review for badan_sensitive.db

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Repo facts list "iCloud backup exclusion handling" as explicitly absent — today, iOS's own automatic iCloud device backup may already be silently including `badan_sensitive.db` (medications/symptoms/conditions) without any deliberate `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` policy decision having been made either way.
- **Recommendation:** Make an explicit, documented decision (via a new mini-ADR) on whether `badan_sensitive.db` should be excluded from the OS's automatic device backup pending FEAT-077's SQLCipher work, or included with today's OS-level-only encryption — right now it's unintentional default behavior, not a decision.
- **Why it matters:** ADR-0004 was deliberate about the sensitive-plus namespace's threat model (module-disable = file deletion) but never addressed what happens to that file inside the OS's own backup mechanism — a silent gap in an otherwise carefully reasoned privacy design.
- **Expected user impact:** No direct UI impact; closes an unreviewed privacy-posture gap.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Database.swift`, `docs/adr/ADR-0004-sensitive-namespace-and-encryption.md`
- **Affected systems:** iOS storage/privacy posture
- **Suggested owner:** Infra
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The carefully designed sensitive-plus namespace's actual behavior inside Apple's own iCloud device backup remains an unreviewed, undocumented default rather than a deliberate choice.

### FEAT-082 — Nearby Share device-to-device transfer (Android counterpart to FEAT-079)

- **Category:** New Feature

- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/` export module, no existing import counterpart
- **Affected systems:** Android export/import

- **Category:** New Feature

- **Effort:** 4

### FEAT-100 — Multi-profile / dependents support

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `user_profile` (`Migrations.swift` lines 59-63: `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, display_name, height_m, birth_year, bio_note...`) and `customization_profile` (`id=1 singleton, json(TEXT)`, per `docs/data-model.md:31`) are both modeled and used throughout `AppEnvironment.swift` as exactly one profile per device — there is no profile-switching UI, no per-profile data partitioning, and `customization_profile` is explicitly a hardcoded singleton row.
- **Recommendation:** Introduce a profile-selection layer above the existing single-profile model — either multiple `user_profile` rows with a `current_profile_id` pointer and per-profile data scoping across every measurement table, or (lower-effort) a documented explicit decision that BADAN is intentionally single-user-per-install and dependents need a separate install.
- **Why it matters:** A common real-world need (a parent tracking a child's growth/medications, or an adult caregiver managing an elderly parent's meds) is entirely unaddressed, and the schema's `customization_profile` singleton assumption (`id=1`) would need a real migration to support it later rather than being sync-ready like the rest of the schema.
- **Expected user impact:** Families/caregivers could manage multiple people's health data from one install, a significant expansion of BADAN's addressable use cases.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 5
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Migrations.swift` (`user_profile`, `customization_profile`), `apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift`, every repository (profile-scoped queries)
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android core data model, DI
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Unlike most other schema decisions in this codebase (which were deliberately made sync-ready/extensible per ADR-0003), the single-profile assumption has no reserved seam at all — retrofitting multi-profile later would be one of the most invasive schema changes possible, touching every measurement table's implicit single-owner assumption.

Scope: LOGGING, REPORTING, EXPORT, SEARCH capabilities materially absent from `apps/ios/Sources/Features/{LogHub,Symptom,Medication,WorkoutNutrition,Export,Timeline,Body}` and `apps/ios/Sources/Export/**` / `packages/export-schemas/`. Grounded by direct reads of these files plus `packages/metric-ontology/registry.json`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Logging.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/LoggingRepository.swift`, and `apps/ios/Sources/Export/ExportRunner.swift`.

### FEAT-101 — Mood logging has no path anywhere in the app

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `packages/metric-ontology/registry.json` defines `subjective.mood`, but a repo-wide grep for it outside `Resources/registry.json` returns zero hits — no LogHub tile, no quick-add sheet, nothing writes a `RawSample` for it.
- **Recommendation:** Add a "Mood" quick-add tile in `LogHubScreen.swift` (alongside water/weight) with a 1–5 calm-face picker, writing a `RawSample` via the same pattern as `LogHubViewModel.logWeight`.
- **Why it matters:** A metric that exists in the canonical ontology but has no capture path is dead weight — Body/Timeline/Insights can never surface it because no data is ever created.
- **Expected user impact:** Users get a first-class, casual-friendly daily mood check-in that feeds baselines/insights like every other metric.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/RawSample.swift` (pattern only, no schema change)
- **Affected systems:** LogHub, MeasurementRepository, Metric ontology
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** `subjective.mood` stays permanently unreachable, making the ontology entry misleading documentation rather than a real capability.
- **Implementation notes:** Reuse `env.registry.definitionOrFallback(MetricID.mood)` + `Units.toCanonical` exactly as `logWeight` does; no new storage plumbing needed.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `MoodQuickSheet` beside `WeightQuickSheet` in `LogHubScreen.swift` and a `logMood(_:env:)` method on `LogHubViewModel` mirroring `logWeight`.

- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`, new `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Notes/NoteLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** LogHub, LoggingRepository, Timeline (already renders notes)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A complete, working backend feature stays permanently unreachable by any user — the highest-ROI single fix in this entire audit slice.
- **Implementation notes:** `NoteLogView` can be a much smaller version of `SymptomLogView` (no dictionary picker step) — just `noteCard` + `whenCard` + save button calling `env.logging.upsertNote(NoteEntry(...))`.
- **First patch sketch:** Create `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Notes/NoteLogView.swift` with a text field + date picker + save button calling `env.logging.upsertNote`; add a `NavigationLink` tile to `LogHubScreen.logTypesSection`.

### FEAT-121 — Symptom entries cannot be edited after saving

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `LoggingRepository` has `insertSymptom` (an `INSERT OR REPLACE`, so technically update-capable by id) but `SymptomLogView.swift` never loads an existing entry back into the capture form — there is no "edit" entry point from Timeline or any symptom history list, only forward-only creation.
- **Recommendation:** Add an edit affordance (e.g. tapping a symptom row in `TimelineScreen.eventRow`, currently a plain `HStack` with no tap target at all) that opens `SymptomLogView` pre-populated with the existing entry's fields.
- **Why it matters:** Mis-logged severity/triggers/notes are common and currently permanently uncorrectable except by deleting (which also has no UI — see FEAT-122) and re-creating.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can fix mistakes without losing history or duplicating entries.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging, Timeline
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-122 (delete) is a natural companion, often shipped together
- **Risk if skipped:** Users accumulate uncorrectable bad data in their most sensitive personal-health records.
- **Implementation notes:** Add an `existingEntry: SymptomEntry?` init parameter to `SymptomLogView` that pre-fills `selection`/`severity`/`triggers`/`note`/`occurredAt` from the passed entry.

### FEAT-122 — Symptom entries have a working delete repository method but no delete UI anywhere

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `LoggingRepository.deleteSymptom(id:at:)` is fully implemented (soft-delete via `deleted_at`), but no view in `apps/ios/Sources/Features/` ever calls it — `TimelineEvent.deletable` is even set to `false` for symptom rows in `TimelineAssembler.symptomEvent` (line 92), and `TimelineScreen.swift` has no swipe/context-menu action wired to `deletable` at all (a repo-wide grep for `swipeActions`/`onDelete`/`contextMenu` across `Features/` returns zero matches).
- **Recommendation:** Wire `TimelineEvent.deletable` into an actual `.swipeActions`/`.contextMenu` in `TimelineScreen.eventRow`, and flip `symptomEvent`'s `deletable` to `true` once a confirm-delete flow exists.
- **Why it matters:** `deletable` is a fully-designed field in the domain model (`Domain/Timeline.swift:47`) that the UI layer never consumes — this is a half-finished feature, not a missing one, making it a very contained, low-risk fix.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can remove mis-logged or duplicate sensitive entries, matching the calm/non-punitive tone already established for medication skips.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineAssembler.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Timeline, Symptom logging (sensitive DB)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Sensitive-data users have no way to remove a mistaken entry short of app-level data deletion.
- **Implementation notes:** Add `.swipeActions { Button(role: .destructive) { delete(event) } }` to `TimelineScreen.eventRow`, routed through a new `TimelineViewModel.delete(_:env:)` that dispatches by `event.type` to the right repository delete call.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `.swipeActions` to `eventRow` in `TimelineScreen.swift` calling a new `TimelineViewModel.delete(event:env:)` that calls `env.logging.deleteSymptom` for `.symptom` events.

### FEAT-123 — Workout entries cannot be edited after saving

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `WorkoutLogView.swift`'s `workoutRow` renders each past entry as a plain `BadanCard` with no tap target, `NavigationLink`, or edit affordance; `LoggingRepository` also has no `updateWorkout`/`deleteWorkout` method at all (only `upsertWorkout` and `workouts(from:to:)`).
- **Recommendation:** Make `workoutRow` tappable, opening a pre-filled edit form; add `updateWorkout`/`deleteWorkout` to `LoggingRepository` (or reuse `upsertWorkout` with the same id for edits).
- **Why it matters:** Every other correctable log type at least has some path to fix mistakes; workouts have none — a wrong duration or RPE is permanent.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can correct workout details without deleting and re-logging (which isn't possible either, per FEAT-124).
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/LoggingRepository.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Workout logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-124
- **Risk if skipped:** Workout history accumulates permanent, uncorrectable errors.
- **Implementation notes:** `upsertWorkout` already does `INSERT OR REPLACE`, so an edit form just needs to re-submit with the same `id`.

### FEAT-124 — Workout entries have no delete path at either the repository or UI layer

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Unlike symptoms and medications (which at least have a repo-layer `deleteRegimen`/`deleteSymptom`), `LoggingRepository` has no `deleteWorkout` method whatsoever — a full grep of the file confirms only `upsertWorkout`/`workouts(from:to:)` exist for the `workout_entries` table.
- **Recommendation:** Add a soft-delete `deleteWorkout(id:at:)` method to `LoggingRepository` (same pattern as `deleteSymptom`) plus a swipe-to-delete action in `WorkoutLogView.workoutRow`.
- **Why it matters:** This is a storage-layer gap, not just a UI gap — deleting a bad workout entry is currently impossible at any level of the stack.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can remove accidental or duplicate workout logs.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/LoggingRepository.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Workout logging, LoggingRepository
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Any manual-entry mistake in workout data is permanent.
- **Implementation notes:** `workout_entries` already has a `deleted_at` column (used in the `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` filter in `workouts(from:to:)`), so the column exists — only the delete method is missing.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `func deleteWorkout(id: String, at date: Date) throws` to `LoggingRepository.swift` mirroring `deleteSymptom`, then wire a swipe action in `WorkoutLogView.workoutRow`.

### FEAT-125 — Nutrition/meal entries cannot be edited after saving

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `NutritionLogView.swift`'s `mealRow` is a static `BadanCard` with no tap target or edit path, matching the workout gap in FEAT-123.
- **Recommendation:** Make `mealRow` tappable to open a pre-filled edit form reusing the existing capture cards.
- **Why it matters:** Meal descriptions/macros are commonly mistyped (e.g. wrong calorie estimate) and currently permanently uncorrectable.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can fix meal entries without duplicating them.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-126
- **Risk if skipped:** Nutrition history accumulates uncorrectable errors, undermining the "today's totals" accuracy shown on the same screen.
- **Implementation notes:** `upsertNutrition` is already an `INSERT OR REPLACE`, so editing is a same-id re-save, matching the workout pattern.

### FEAT-126 — Nutrition entries have no delete path at either the repository or UI layer

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `LoggingRepository` has no `deleteNutrition` method — only `upsertNutrition`/`nutrition(from:to:)` exist for the `nutrition_entries` table, identical to the workout gap in FEAT-124.
- **Recommendation:** Add `deleteNutrition(id:at:)` to `LoggingRepository` and a swipe-to-delete in `NutritionLogView.mealRow`.
- **Why it matters:** A mistakenly logged meal (wrong day, duplicate, wrong food) permanently skews `vm.kcalTotal`/`vm.proteinTotal` for that day with no way to remove it.
- **Expected user impact:** Accurate daily totals; ability to remove bad entries.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/LoggingRepository.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Daily nutrition totals stay permanently corruptible by any single mis-tap.
- **Implementation notes:** Ship together with FEAT-124 as one "add delete to workout+nutrition" PR since the pattern is identical.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `deleteNutrition` to `LoggingRepository.swift` mirroring `deleteSymptom`; wire a swipe action in `NutritionLogView.mealRow`.

### FEAT-127 — Medication regimens cannot be edited after creation

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `AddMedicationSheet` in `MedicationLogView.swift` only supports creating a new regimen; `regimenCard` renders name/strength/schedule with no tap target, so a typo'd name or a schedule change (e.g. dose time shifted) requires deleting (also not exposed, see below) and re-adding, which loses adherence history linkage by regimen id.
- **Recommendation:** Add an edit entry point on `regimenCard` that reopens `AddMedicationSheet` pre-filled, calling `env.logging.upsertRegimen` with the same id (already `INSERT OR REPLACE`).
- **Why it matters:** Medication data is in the sensitive DB and often needs correction as dosages/schedules genuinely change over time; today the only "correction" path destroys history.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can adjust a regimen's schedule or strength without losing its adherence trail.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging (sensitive DB)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Real-world schedule/dose changes force users to fragment adherence history across duplicate regimens.
- **Implementation notes:** Add an `editing: MedicationRegimen?` param to `AddMedicationSheet`, defaulting its `@State` fields from it when present.

### FEAT-128 — No undo affordance after saving a log entry

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Every save action across `SymptomLogView`, `WorkoutLogView`, `NutritionLogView`, and `LogHubScreen`'s quick-add sheets dismisses or resets immediately with no confirmation toast or undo window — a mis-tapped "Save" is immediately committed with no recovery path (compounding FEAT-122/124/126's missing delete UI).
- **Recommendation:** Add a brief (e.g. 4–5s) undo snackbar/toast after each save, calling the relevant delete method if tapped, using a shared `UndoToast` component.
- **Why it matters:** Given how many log flows still lack any delete UI at all (FEAT-122/124/126), a save-time undo window is the cheapest safety net until full edit/delete ships everywhere.
- **Expected user impact:** Immediate mistake recovery without navigating to find (or waiting for) a delete affordance.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Logging UI (cross-cutting)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile + Design
- **Dependencies:** Requires delete methods to exist for all log types first (FEAT-124, FEAT-126)
- **Risk if skipped:** Users remain one mis-tap away from a permanently wrong (or, for symptoms, permanently un-removable) entry.
- **Implementation notes:** Build one shared `UndoToast(message:action:)` `DesignSystem` component and thread it through each save call site.

### FEAT-129 — No photo attachment on symptom entries

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `SymptomEntry` has no image/attachment field, and `SymptomLogView.swift`'s capture form has no camera/photo picker (e.g. for a rash, swelling, or visible injury).
- **Recommendation:** Add an optional photo attachment (stored on-device, path referenced from `SymptomEntry`) to the symptom capture form, respecting the sensitive-DB boundary (photo files should be purged alongside `purgeSensitiveNamespace`).
- **Why it matters:** Visual symptoms (rashes, swelling, bruising) are common and currently can only be described in the free-text note, losing critical visual detail a clinician might want later (export supports "doctor" use cases per the export cockpit's framing).
- **Expected user impact:** Richer, more clinically useful symptom records.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Logging.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/LoggingRepository.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging (sensitive DB), local file storage, Export
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** Must integrate with `purgeSensitiveNamespace`'s file-deletion semantics (D-9) and the export bundle's file inclusion
- **Risk if skipped:** Visual symptom detail is permanently lost to free-text description only.
- **Implementation notes:** Store photos in the sensitive DB's local file directory (not iCloud-backed, consistent with local-first/no-network guardrail); add an `attachmentPaths: [String]` column.

### FEAT-130 — No voice-note attachment for any log type

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** No log entry type (`SymptomEntry`, `WorkoutEntry`, `NutritionEntry`, `NoteEntry`) has an audio-attachment field, and no capture screen offers a record button.
- **Recommendation:** Add an optional voice-memo attachment to the free-text journal entry proposed in FEAT-120 first (lowest-friction entry point), then extend to symptoms if validated.
- **Why it matters:** Voice capture is meaningfully faster than typing for on-the-go logging (e.g. describing a symptom while it's happening) and complements the "under-10-second capture" design goal already stated in `SymptomLogView`'s and `WorkoutLogView`'s doc comments.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, lower-friction logging for users who prefer speaking over typing.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** New `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Notes/NoteLogView.swift` (FEAT-120), `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Logging.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Logging (cross-cutting), local file storage
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-120 (journal entries must exist first)
- **Risk if skipped:** Users limited to typed or structured input only; no accessible speed alternative.
- **Implementation notes:** Requires microphone permission (a new permission-timing consideration for Ease-of-Use) and on-device storage of `.m4a` files.

### FEAT-131 — No photo attachment for meals

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `NutritionEntry` has no image field; `NutritionLogView.swift`'s `descriptionCard` is text-only.
- **Recommendation:** Add an optional meal-photo attachment to `NutritionLogView`, stored locally and referenced by path.
- **Why it matters:** A photo is often faster and more accurate than typing a food description, and is a standard expectation for any nutrition-logging surface.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, richer meal logging; visual meal history in Timeline.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Logging.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging, local file storage
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Nutrition entries remain text-only despite this being a near-universal expectation for food logging apps.

### FEAT-132 — No medication refill/supply tracking

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `MedicationRegimen` (`Logging.swift:24-44`) has `name`, `strength`, `form`, `schedule`, `startedAt`/`endedAt`, `notes` — no `quantityOnHand`, `refillThreshold`, or `lastRefillAt` field at all.
- **Recommendation:** Add supply-count fields to `MedicationRegimen` and a small "pills remaining" stepper/decrement in `MedicationLogView.swift`'s `regimenCard`, auto-decrementing on each "Take" action.
- **Why it matters:** Running out of medication unexpectedly is a real adherence risk; the app tracks whether doses were taken but has no concept of remaining supply at all.
- **Expected user impact:** Users get a low-friction "running low" signal without needing to count pills manually.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Logging.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/LoggingRepository.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging (sensitive DB)
- **Suggested owner:** Product + Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Adherence tracking exists in isolation from the practical constraint (running out) that most often breaks adherence.
- **Implementation notes:** Decrement supply in the same `record(...)` call in `MedicationLogViewModel` that already writes the `AdherenceEvent` on "Take".

### FEAT-133 — No medication interaction / duplicate-ingredient awareness

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `MedicationRegimen` has no ingredient or interaction metadata, and there is no cross-regimen check anywhere in `MedicationLogView.swift` or `LoggingRepository`.
- **Recommendation:** At minimum, add a same-name/near-duplicate check when adding a new regimen (warn, don't block, per wellness-safe/non-alarming tone) using `regimens(activeOnly:)` already available in `LoggingRepository`.
- **Why it matters:** BADAN explicitly avoids prescriptive/alarming language, so this must stay informational — but even a simple duplicate-name warning would catch a common real-world logging mistake (adding a medication twice under slightly different names).
- **Expected user impact:** Reduces accidental duplicate regimens; lays groundwork for a future non-diagnostic interaction awareness feature.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging
- **Suggested owner:** Product + Mobile
- **Dependencies:** Full interaction-database checking is out of scope for a local-first, no-network app (D-8) and would need a bundled, versioned dataset — flag as a larger follow-on
- **Risk if skipped:** Duplicate/near-duplicate regimens accumulate unnoticed, fragmenting adherence history.
- **Implementation notes:** Start with a client-side Levenshtein-distance check against existing `regimens(activeOnly: true)` names in `AddMedicationSheet.save()`.

### FEAT-134 — Medication regimen deletion has a working repository method but no UI trigger

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `LoggingRepository.deleteRegimen(id:at:)` (line ~38) is fully implemented, but `MedicationLogView.swift` never calls it — `regimenCard` has no swipe action, context menu, or delete button.
- **Recommendation:** Add a swipe-to-delete or "End medication" action on `regimenCard` calling the existing `deleteRegimen`.

- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging (sensitive DB)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Discontinued medications permanently clutter the active regimens list with no removal path.
- **Implementation notes:** Distinguish "end medication" (set `endedAt`, keeps history) from "delete" (soft-delete via `deletedAt`) as two distinct actions, since `isActive` already depends on `endedAt == nil`.

### FEAT-135 — Conditions feature has complete domain/storage support but zero UI anywhere in the app

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `Condition` (`Logging.swift`), `LoggingRepository.upsertCondition`/`conditions()` are fully implemented against the sensitive DB, but a repo-wide search for `Condition(` / `upsertCondition` across `apps/ios/Sources/Features/` returns zero matches — there is no screen to create, view, or link a condition to symptoms/medications, despite `Condition.linkedRegimenIds`/`linkedSymptomIds` fields existing specifically for that purpose.
- **Recommendation:** Add a "Conditions" screen (list + add/edit form) reachable from `LogHubScreen.swift` or `SourcesScreen`-adjacent settings, using the existing repository methods as-is.
- **Why it matters:** This is the second-largest "fully built, zero UI" gap found in this audit after journaling (FEAT-120) — the linking fields to symptoms and medications suggest Conditions was designed as the organizing concept for chronic-illness users, but it's entirely unreachable today.
- **Expected user impact:** Chronic-condition users get a way to group symptoms/medications under a named condition (e.g. "Migraine," "IBS"), which the storage layer already anticipates.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** New `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Conditions/ConditionsScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/LoggingRepository.swift` (read-only reuse)
- **Affected systems:** Sensitive DB, Symptom logging, Medication logging
- **Suggested owner:** Product + Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A deliberately-designed, storage-complete feature remains permanently invisible to every user.
- **Implementation notes:** Start read/write on `conditions()`/`upsertCondition` as-is; the linking UI (picking existing symptom/regimen ids into `linkedSymptomIds`/`linkedRegimenIds`) can follow in a v2.
