- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Macro entry remains error-prone for any non-single-serving meal.
- **Implementation notes:** Simplest version: a "servings" stepper that multiplies whatever is typed in the kcal/protein fields before saving.

### FEAT-140 — Workout entries always save "now" with no backdate option

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `WorkoutLogView.swift`'s `save()` hardcodes `startAt: now.addingTimeInterval(-Double(minutes) * 60)` / `endAt: now` — unlike `SymptomLogView`, which has a full `whenCard` with a `DatePicker`, there is no way to log a workout that happened earlier today or yesterday.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `whenCard`-style date/time picker to `WorkoutLogView.swift`, matching the pattern already proven in `SymptomLogView`.
- **Why it matters:** Users very often log a workout after the fact (post-shower, end of day) — forcing "now" as the only option silently mis-attributes every retroactively-logged workout.
- **Expected user impact:** Accurate workout timestamps regardless of when the user actually opens the app to log it.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Workout logging, DayAttribution
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every workout logged after the fact gets silently misattributed to the wrong time (and potentially the wrong day, affecting `DayAttribution`-based aggregates).
- **Implementation notes:** Copy `SymptomLogView.whenCard`'s `DatePicker(..., in: ...maxDate, ...)` pattern directly.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `DatePicker` bound to a new `@State private var startAt: Date` in `WorkoutLogView.swift`, replacing the hardcoded `now` in `vm.save`.

### FEAT-141 — Nutrition entries always save "now" with no backdate option

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `NutritionLogView.swift`'s `save()` hardcodes `occurredAt: now` in `NutritionLogViewModel.save` — identical gap to FEAT-140, no `DatePicker` exists anywhere in the file.
- **Recommendation:** Add the same `whenCard`-style date/time picker as proposed for workouts.
- **Why it matters:** Meals are frequently logged well after eating (e.g. logging breakfast+lunch together in the evening); forcing "now" misattributes the meal's actual time and meal-type auto-suggestion (`mealForHour`).
- **Expected user impact:** Accurate meal timestamps and correct automatic meal-type suggestions even when logging retroactively.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging, DayAttribution
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Retroactively-logged meals get the wrong timestamp and a mismatched meal-type auto-suggestion.
- **Implementation notes:** Ship together with FEAT-140 as one "add backdating to workout+nutrition" PR since the pattern is identical.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `DatePicker` to `NutritionLogView.swift` bound to a new `@State private var occurredAt: Date`, replacing the hardcoded `now` in `vm.save`.

### FEAT-142 — No way to mark an open-ended symptom episode as resolved

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Even if FEAT-116 adds duration capture, there is no "still ongoing" concept — every symptom entry is a single point-in-time record with a fixed severity, so a multi-day symptom (e.g. a week-long cold) must be logged as repeated separate entries rather than one episode with a start and eventual resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Add an optional "ongoing" flag to symptom entries and a "Mark as resolved" action (settable from Timeline or a symptom-history list) that fills in the duration once the episode ends.
- **Why it matters:** Chronic/multi-day symptoms are common in exactly the population most likely to use a dedicated symptom tracker; without episode support, their data becomes a series of disconnected points instead of one coherent episode.
- **Expected user impact:** More accurate representation of real symptom courses, especially for chronic-condition users.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Logging.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging (sensitive DB)
- **Suggested owner:** Product + Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-116 (duration field UI) and FEAT-121 (edit support, to close out an episode)
- **Risk if skipped:** Multi-day symptoms remain modeled as disconnected point events indefinitely.
- **Implementation notes:** Larger effort — sequence after FEAT-116/121 land, since "resolve" is really "edit an existing entry's duration."

### FEAT-143 — No meal templates or favorites

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `NutritionLogView.swift` has no save-as-favorite mechanism — every meal, even an identical daily breakfast, requires re-typing description/kcal/protein from scratch each time.
- **Recommendation:** Add a "Save as favorite" toggle on the save button and a "Favorites" horizontal chip row (styled like `SymptomLogView.recentsSection`) above `descriptionCard` for one-tap re-log.
- **Why it matters:** Nutrition logging is famously abandoned due to entry friction; repeat meals are the highest-leverage place to cut that friction, and `SymptomLogView` already proves the "recents chip" UX pattern works well in this codebase.
- **Expected user impact:** Near-instant logging for the (very common) case of eating the same thing as before.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Nutrition logging remains high-friction for the common repeat-meal case, risking abandonment.
- **Implementation notes:** Reuse `SymptomLogView`'s `recentsSection`/`chip(title:...)` pattern directly, sourced from distinct recent `NutritionEntry.description` values via `env.logging.nutrition`.

### FEAT-144 — No workout templates or saved routines

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `WorkoutLogView.swift` has no save/reuse mechanism for a recurring routine (e.g. "Tuesday leg day: Strength, 45min, RPE 7") — every workout, even a repeated routine, is entered from the same blank defaults (`activity = .run, minutes = 30, rpe = 5`).
- **Recommendation:** Add a lightweight "recent workouts" quick-repeat affordance (tap a past `workoutRow` to pre-fill the form with its activity/duration/RPE), similar to the favorites pattern in FEAT-143.
- **Why it matters:** Users with a consistent routine currently re-enter the same values every session.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster logging for repeat routines.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Workout logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Repeat-routine users face unnecessary re-entry friction every session.
- **Implementation notes:** Make `workoutRow` in `recentSection` tappable to pre-fill `activity`/`minutes`/`rpe` `@State` instead of only displaying history.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a tap gesture to `workoutRow` in `WorkoutLogView.swift` that sets `activity`/`minutes`/`rpe` from the tapped entry, scrolling to the top of the form.

### FEAT-145 — No bulk/batch backfill logging for multiple days at once

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Every capture screen (`SymptomLogView`, `WorkoutLogView`, `NutritionLogView`) logs exactly one entry per save action; there is no "log the same thing for the last 5 days" or multi-day batch-entry flow anywhere.
- **Recommendation:** Add a lightweight batch mode (e.g. "log this for multiple days") to at least the medication adherence flow first, where retroactive multi-day backfill is most common (e.g. after returning from time away from the app).
- **Why it matters:** Users who miss a few days of logging currently have to re-open the same form repeatedly rather than backfilling once; this is a real onboarding/re-engagement friction point.
- **Expected user impact:** Much faster catch-up logging after a gap.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Logging (cross-cutting)
- **Suggested owner:** Product + Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users returning after a data gap face high-friction one-by-one backfill or simply abandon backfilling entirely.
- **Implementation notes:** Start narrow — a "log for the last N days" multi-select date picker on `AddMedicationSheet`'s adherence flow — rather than a fully generic batch system.

### FEAT-146 — No recurring/scheduled log prompts (e.g. daily check-ins)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Nothing in `LogHubScreen.swift` or elsewhere schedules a recurring prompt to log a metric (e.g. daily mood/energy check-in once FEAT-101/102 exist); medication is the only log type with any due-time concept (`MedicationLogViewModel`'s `dueTimes`).
- **Recommendation:** Extend the due-time/adherence pattern already built for medications to optional daily subjective check-ins (mood/energy/sleep quality), surfaced as a due-today card similar to `dueSection` in `MedicationLogView.swift`.
- **Why it matters:** The medication module already proves the "due today" UX pattern works well; reusing it for subjective check-ins would be low-risk since the pattern is battle-tested in this exact codebase.
- **Expected user impact:** Higher-quality longitudinal subjective data via a consistent daily prompt, without needing OS-level notifications (out of this slice's scope).
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift` (pattern reference)
- **Affected systems:** LogHub
- **Suggested owner:** Product + Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-101/102/104 (subjective metrics must exist to schedule)
- **Risk if skipped:** Subjective metrics, once added, will suffer from low, inconsistent logging frequency without a prompt structure.
- **Implementation notes:** In-app only (a due-today card), not a push notification — notifications are explicitly out of this slice's scope (FEAT-A).

### FEAT-147 — "Recent" chips across log types navigate to a blank form instead of pre-filling it

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `LogHubScreen.swift`'s `recentsSection` renders tappable `RecentChip`s for symptoms/workouts, but `destination(for:)` just opens a blank `SymptomLogView()`/`WorkoutLogView()` — the tapped recent item's data is never passed through, so "recent" is purely informational, not a quick-repeat action.
- **Recommendation:** Pass the tapped `RecentItem`'s source id into the destination view so it can pre-fill the form (same underlying need as FEAT-143/144, but for the cross-type LogHub recents specifically).
- **Why it matters:** The UI visually promises "tap to log again" (chip label pattern, `arrow.counterclockwise` icon precedent in `SymptomLogView.recentsSection`) but LogHub's version doesn't deliver on it — a broken affordance is worse than no affordance.
- **Expected user impact:** LogHub recents become an actual one-tap re-log instead of a shortcut to an empty form.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** LogHub
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A visually-promised quick-repeat affordance stays functionally a no-op.
- **Implementation notes:** Thread the source symptom/workout id through `destination(for:)` into `SymptomLogView`/`WorkoutLogView`'s (proposed) pre-fill init parameter from FEAT-121/144.
- **First patch sketch:** Change `LogHubViewModel.RecentItem` destinations in `LogHubScreen.destination(for:)` to pass the underlying entry into the target view for pre-fill.

### FEAT-148 — No support for user-defined custom logged metrics

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `MetricRegistry` is a fixed, 44-entry catalog from `packages/metric-ontology/registry.json`; there is no path anywhere in `apps/ios/Sources/` for a user to define their own tracked metric (e.g. a specific symptom-adjacent number their clinician wants tracked that isn't in the ontology).
- **Recommendation:** Add a "custom metric" creation flow that writes a user-scoped registry entry (separate from the shared ontology file) and reuses the existing `RawSample`/quick-add pattern for capture.
- **Why it matters:** A fixed 44-metric ontology inevitably misses individual needs; without a custom-metric escape hatch, those needs go completely untracked in BADAN.
- **Expected user impact:** Power users can track anything relevant to them, not just what's pre-defined.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 5
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Ontology/MetricRegistry.swift`, new `apps/ios/Sources/Features/CustomMetrics/`
- **Affected systems:** MetricRegistry, LogHub, Export
- **Suggested owner:** Product + Mobile
- **Dependencies:** Must not corrupt the shared, versioned `packages/metric-ontology/registry.json` contract — needs a clearly separated user-metric namespace
- **Risk if skipped:** Users with tracking needs outside the fixed 44 metrics have no path within BADAN at all.
- **Implementation notes:** Largest-effort item in this batch; should be scoped as its own initiative with explicit ontology-versioning implications.

### FEAT-149 — No lab-results/bloodwork logging

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** No metric family, screen, or domain type in `apps/ios/Sources/` covers periodic lab values (e.g. cholesterol, A1C, vitamin D) — the closest concept is the auto-synced HealthKit/Health Connect vitals, which don't cover lab panels.
- **Recommendation:** Add a "Labs" log type (test name, value, unit, reference range, date) reusing the manual `RawSample` capture pattern, likely under the sensitive DB given clinical sensitivity.
- **Why it matters:** Periodic lab results are a core piece of a personal health record that BADAN, as a "personal health repository," currently has no place for at all.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can keep a full longitudinal health record including lab trends, not just device-measured vitals.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `packages/metric-ontology/registry.json`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Logging.swift`, new `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Labs/`
- **Affected systems:** Sensitive DB, Metric ontology, Export
- **Suggested owner:** Product + Mobile
- **Dependencies:** Ontology extension for lab-type metrics (open-ended value+unit+reference-range shape differs from the fixed-catalog metrics)
- **Risk if skipped:** BADAN's "personal health repository" positioning has a conspicuous hole around clinical lab data.
- **Implementation notes:** Reference-range handling needs wellness-safe presentation (no red/green flagging against lab reference ranges, per product guardrails).

### FEAT-150 — No allergy tracking

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** No allergy concept exists anywhere — not in `registry.json`, not in `packages/contracts/dictionaries/symptoms.json`'s categories, not as a `Condition` subtype.
- **Recommendation:** Model allergies as a lightweight extension of the `Condition` type proposed for UI in FEAT-135 (a `kind: .allergy` case) rather than a wholly new table.
- **Why it matters:** Allergies are foundational personal-health-record data (relevant to medication safety in particular) and currently have zero representation.
- **Expected user impact:** Users get a place to record allergies as part of their overall health record.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Logging.swift`, new `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Conditions/ConditionsScreen.swift` (from FEAT-135)
- **Affected systems:** Sensitive DB, Conditions
- **Suggested owner:** Product + Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-135 (Conditions UI must ship first)
- **Risk if skipped:** A standard personal-health-record data point stays entirely unmodeled.
- **Implementation notes:** Sequence strictly after FEAT-135 to avoid building a second, parallel "conditions-like" screen.

### FEAT-151 — No comparative reports (this week vs. last week / period vs. period)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `MetricDetailScreen.swift`'s `periodSelector` (line 222) only lets a power user pick a single window (7/30/90 days) to view in isolation — `InsightEngine`/`BaselineEngine` compute a single rolling baseline (14-day median/MAD) but nothing in the UI ever puts two explicit periods side by side.
- **Recommendation:** Add a "Compare" toggle to `MetricDetailScreen` that overlays the previous equivalent period (e.g. this week vs. last week) on the same chart, computed client-side from data already fetched by `MetricDetailViewModel`.
- **Why it matters:** "Am I doing better or worse than last week" is one of the most natural questions a health-tracking user asks, and the app currently has no direct way to answer it beyond eyeballing a single trend line.
- **Expected user impact:** Users get an immediate, concrete before/after comparison instead of having to remember or manually recompute it.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** MetricDetail, DerivationRepository
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users are left to manually eyeball or mentally compute period-over-period change, a task the app is well positioned to do for them.
- **Implementation notes:** Fetch the prior window's series alongside the current one in `MetricDetailViewModel.load` and add a second series to the existing `MetricChart` component.

### FEAT-152 — No PDF or clinician-oriented report export

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `ExportFormat` (referenced throughout `ExportRunner.swift`/`ExportCenterScreen.swift`) supports only `.csv` and `.json` — there is no visual, printable summary despite `ExportCopy`'s own framing implying doctor-facing use ("Keep the file somewhere private" language and per-metric row counts already computed).
- **Recommendation:** Add a `.pdf` export format that renders a clean, calm one-page-per-family summary (headline value, baseline status, recent trend chart) using the data `ExportRunner` already gathers.
- **Why it matters:** CSV/JSON are excellent for data portability but useless to hand to a physician in an appointment; a PDF is the single most-requested format for "show my doctor" use cases in health apps generally.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can generate a shareable, human-readable summary instead of raw spreadsheets/JSON.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Export/ExportRunner.swift`, new `apps/ios/Sources/Export/PDFReportWriter.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Export
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile + Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** BADAN's export cockpit, despite framing itself as trust/doctor-oriented, can never produce anything a clinician would actually want to read.
- **Implementation notes:** Reuse `MetricChart`'s rendering logic via `ImageRenderer` (iOS 17+, matches the app's minimum deployment target) to snapshot charts into the PDF.

### FEAT-153 — No cross-metric correlation explorer

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** No screen or repository method anywhere computes or displays a relationship between two metrics (e.g. sleep vs. next-day HRV, caffeine vs. symptom severity) — `InsightEngine` only applies deterministic single-metric templates against a baseline.
- **Recommendation:** Add a power-only "Explore" screen letting users pick two metrics and a date range, rendering a scatter/dual-line view computed from data both `MeasurementRepository` and `LoggingRepository` already store.
- **Why it matters:** Correlation-seeking ("does X affect my Y?") is a primary reason people track multiple health metrics simultaneously; today BADAN stores everything needed to answer this but never presents the relationship.
- **Expected user impact:** Power users get genuine analytical value from their combined dataset instead of only per-metric trend lines.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** New `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Insights/CorrelationExplorerScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/DerivationRepository.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Insights, MeasurementRepository, LoggingRepository
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile + Data
- **Dependencies:** Must stay descriptive/correlational only, never causal-sounding language, per wellness-safe guardrail
- **Risk if skipped:** The app's richest analytical opportunity (cross-metric relationships) stays permanently unexplored despite having all the underlying data.
- **Implementation notes:** Start with a simple two-series overlay chart before attempting any statistical correlation coefficient, to keep both effort and misinterpretation risk low.

### FEAT-154 — No custom derived-metric / formula builder

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `DerivationRepository`/`BaselineEngine` compute a fixed set of engine-defined derived values; there is no user-facing way to define a custom formula (e.g. "resting HR / HRV ratio") anywhere in the app.
- **Recommendation:** Add a simple formula builder (pick two metrics + an operator) that produces a new locally-computed derived series, stored the same way as engine-derived values.
- **Why it matters:** Power users frequently want a personally meaningful composite metric; today the only derived values are the ones BADAN's engine chose to compute.
- **Expected user impact:** Power users can create metrics meaningful to their specific situation.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 5
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** New `apps/ios/Sources/Features/CustomMetrics/FormulaBuilderScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/DerivationRepository.swift`
- **Affected systems:** DerivationRepository, MetricRegistry
- **Suggested owner:** Product + Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-148 (custom metric infrastructure is a natural prerequisite)
- **Risk if skipped:** Power users remain limited to BADAN's fixed set of derived metrics.
- **Implementation notes:** Highest-effort reporting item in this batch — sequence last, after FEAT-148 lands.

### FEAT-155 — No general tagging system across log entries

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Only `NoteEntry.tags` exists as a tagging field in the entire domain model (`Logging.swift:247`), and even that field is never surfaced in any UI (compounding FEAT-120's gap) — symptoms have `triggers` (a similar but narrower concept) while workouts/nutrition have no tagging at all.
- **Recommendation:** Once journaling ships (FEAT-120), expose `NoteEntry.tags` in its capture form, then extend the same lightweight tag-chip pattern to workouts/nutrition for filtering/reporting purposes.
- **Why it matters:** A consistent tagging vocabulary is the foundation for the filtering, saved views, and reporting gaps described elsewhere in this section (FEAT-166, FEAT-167).
- **Expected user impact:** Users can create their own organizing categories across log types (e.g. "travel," "period," "work stress").
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Logging.swift`, new `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Notes/NoteLogView.swift` (FEAT-120)
- **Affected systems:** Logging (cross-cutting)
- **Suggested owner:** Product + Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-120
- **Risk if skipped:** Even the one existing tag field (`NoteEntry.tags`) stays permanently unused, and no cross-cutting user-organizing scheme ever emerges.
- **Implementation notes:** Start with just surfacing the already-built `NoteEntry.tags` field before generalizing to other log types.

### FEAT-156 — No annotation support on metric charts

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `MetricChart`/`MetricSparkline` (`DesignSystem/Components`) render pure line/sparkline visuals with no tap-to-annotate interaction — a user can't mark "started new medication" or "travel" directly on their weight or HRV trend.
- **Recommendation:** Add a lightweight date-annotation capability (reusing the note/tag infrastructure from FEAT-120/155) that renders as a marker on `MetricChart` in `MetricDetailScreen`.
- **Why it matters:** Annotating a trend chart with life events is one of the most effective ways users self-derive insight from their own data, and BADAN's chart component has no hook for it at all today.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can visually connect life events to metric changes directly on the chart they're already viewing.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`, DesignSystem `MetricChart` component
- **Affected systems:** MetricDetail, Notes (FEAT-120)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile + Design
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-120 (notes must exist as the underlying annotation data)
- **Risk if skipped:** Charts remain purely passive visualizations with no way to connect trend changes to real-world context.
- **Implementation notes:** Render existing same-day `NoteEntry`s (once FEAT-120 ships) as small markers under the chart's x-axis rather than building a wholly new annotation data type.

### FEAT-157 — No weekly/monthly rollup report screen on Body

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `BodyScreen.swift`'s pillars show only a 7-value sparkline (`values: series.suffix(7)`) and a single "latest" number — there is no dedicated weekly/monthly summary report anywhere (e.g. "average sleep this week," "workouts this month").
- **Recommendation:** Add a "This week" / "This month" summary card per family on `BodyScreen`, aggregating already-fetched `recentSeries` data (avg/min/max/total depending on metric type).

- **Expected user impact:** A quick, casual-friendly weekly/monthly overview without needing to open each metric's detail screen individually.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Body, DerivationRepository
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile + Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users must open each metric individually to get any sense of period-level trends.

### FEAT-158 — No printable/shareable single-metric report card

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `MetricDetailScreen.swift` has no share/export action at all — a user viewing, say, their HRV trend has no way to share or print just that screen; the only export path is the full-repository `ExportCenterScreen`.
- **Recommendation:** Add a "Share this metric" action to `MetricDetailScreen`'s toolbar producing a small shareable image/PDF card (headline value, status, chart) via `ImageRenderer`.
- **Why it matters:** Sharing one specific metric (e.g. "look at my sleep improvement") is a much lower-friction, more common need than running a full data export, and there's currently no path for it at all.
- **Expected user impact:** Fast, targeted sharing of a single insight without navigating to the full Export cockpit.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** MetricDetail, ShareSheet
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users wanting to share one metric are forced through the much heavier full-export flow, or take a manual screenshot instead.
- **Implementation notes:** Reuse `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ShareSheet.swift` (already built, 16 lines, generic `UIActivityViewController` wrapper) with an `ImageRenderer`-produced image.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a toolbar share button to `MetricDetailScreen.swift` that renders the current chart+headline via `ImageRenderer` and presents the existing `ShareSheet`.

### FEAT-159 — No combined multi-metric dashboard/report for a date range

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Every reporting surface (`MetricDetailScreen`, `BodyScreen`) is single-metric; `TimelineScreen` lists raw events but never aggregates. There is no screen that summarizes, say, "sleep + activity + symptoms this week" together.
- **Recommendation:** Add a date-range "Summary" report screen combining headline stats across families for the selected window, reusing `BodyViewModel`'s per-family data-fetching pattern.
- **Why it matters:** Users trying to understand a specific period (e.g. "how was my trip week") currently have to manually cross-reference multiple single-metric screens and Timeline.
- **Expected user impact:** One-screen situational awareness across the whole tracked dataset for a chosen period.
- **ROI:** 2

- **Dependencies:** FEAT-157 (rollup logic is a natural building block)

### FEAT-160 — No data-completeness / logging-gap report

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Nothing in `Body`, `Timeline`, or `Export` ever reports which days have no logged data at all — a user can't see "you didn't log symptoms for 5 days" anywhere.
- **Recommendation:** Add a small completeness indicator (e.g. a calendar heat-strip) to relevant log-history sections showing logged vs. gap days, computed from existing `from`/`to` queries already used by each view model.
- **Why it matters:** Understanding data completeness is essential context for interpreting any derived baseline or trend — right now a user has no way to know if a "flat trend" reflects reality or just missed logging.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can distinguish real trends from logging gaps, improving trust in the data they see elsewhere.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Body, Timeline
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile + Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users may misread gaps in their own logging as genuine health stability/decline.
- **Implementation notes:** A simple 7/30-day dot/heat strip (reusing `MedicationLogView.AdherenceDot`'s visual pattern) is sufficient for v1.

### FEAT-161 — Symptom-frequency derived metrics exist but are never displayed anywhere

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `registry.json` defines `symptoms.severity_avg` and `symptoms.count` as derived metrics, but neither appears in `SymptomLogView.swift`, `BodyScreen.swift`, or any other Feature file — a grep confirms zero references outside the registry file itself.
- **Recommendation:** Surface these two derived metrics as a small "your symptom trend" summary card in `SymptomLogView.swift`'s picker screen or on `BodyScreen`'s `.mental`/relevant family pillar.
- **Why it matters:** Two derived metrics were specifically designed for symptom reporting but, like several LOGGING-side gaps in this audit, were never wired to any presentation surface.
- **Expected user impact:** Users see an at-a-glance symptom-frequency/severity trend instead of having to scroll raw history.

- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging, DerivationRepository
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Two purpose-built derived metrics remain permanently invisible to users.
- **Implementation notes:** Fetch `symptoms.severity_avg`/`symptoms.count` via the same `env.derivation.latestDerivedSeries` call pattern already used in `BodyViewModel.derivedSeries`.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a small trend card to `SymptomLogView.picker(_:)` fetching `env.derivation.latestDerivedSeries(metricId: "symptoms.count")` and `"symptoms.severity_avg"`.

### FEAT-162 — No symptom-medication correlation report

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Symptoms and medication adherence both live in the sensitive DB and both appear in Timeline, but nothing ever cross-references them (e.g. "symptom severity in the days after a missed dose").
- **Recommendation:** Add a report view (or extend FEAT-153's correlation explorer) that overlays adherence events against symptom severity for a chosen regimen/symptom pair.
- **Why it matters:** For chronic-condition users, this is one of the most clinically actionable questions BADAN's own data could answer but currently never does.

- **Risk if skipped:** A high-value, data-already-available insight stays permanently unsurfaced.

### FEAT-163 — No year-in-review / annual summary report

- **Implementation notes:** Sequence after FEAT-152/157 land to reuse both the PDF pipeline and the rollup-aggregation logic.

### FEAT-165 — Timeline is hard-capped at a 21-day window with no way to see further back

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `TimelineAssembler.windowDays = 21` (line 14) is a hardcoded constant — there is no date-range picker or "load more" anywhere in `TimelineScreen.swift`; history beyond 3 weeks is completely inaccessible from the unified spine (only reachable per-metric via `MetricDetailScreen`'s 90-day option).

- **Importance:** 3

- **Approval needed:** Yes

- **First patch sketch:** Parameterize `TimelineAssembler.assemble(from:to:)` (currently hardcoded to `Self.windowDays`) and add a simple range picker to `TimelineScreen.swift` that re-triggers `vm.load`.

### FEAT-176 — CSV export completely omits all logged health data (symptoms, medications, meals, notes)

- **Problem:** `ExportRunner.runCSV` (lines 99–138) builds `rawRows`/`derivedRows` exclusively from `rawSamples`, `intervalRecords`, `sessions`, `derivedValues`, and `baselines` — symptoms, medication adherence, nutrition, and notes are never included in CSV output at all; they only appear in the `.json` bundle path (`runJSON`, lines 142–194).

- **Affected systems:** Export
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile

- **Implementation notes:** Add `rowFor(symptom:)`/`rowFor(adherence:)`/`rowFor(nutrition:)`/`rowFor(note:)` builders mirroring the existing `rowFor(sample:)` pattern, gated by the same `scope.includeSensitive`/`logFamilyIncluded` checks already used in `runJSON`.

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `ExportCenterViewModel.run` (`ExportCenterScreen.swift:101-123`) only fires on an explicit button tap — there is no cadence/schedule concept anywhere in `ExportJob`, `ExportRunner`, or the UI.
- **Recommendation:** Add an optional "Auto-export weekly to Files" toggle that schedules a periodic background export using `BGTaskScheduler`, writing to a user-chosen Files location.
- **Why it matters:** Users who treat exports as a backup mechanism currently must remember to manually run one every time; a scheduled option would make export a true "set and forget" backup strategy consistent with the local-first, "nothing left your device" framing already established.
- **Expected user impact:** Peace-of-mind automatic backups without manual effort.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Export/ExportRunner.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Export, iOS background task scheduling
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** Background task entitlements/configuration (new `project.yml` capability)
- **Risk if skipped:** Export remains a manual, easy-to-forget action rather than a reliable backup mechanism.
- **Implementation notes:** Must respect the no-network guardrail (D-8) — this is local-file scheduling only (e.g. to Files/iCloud Drive folder), never any remote upload.

### FEAT-181 — No export path back into Apple Health (write-back)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `HealthKitAdapter.swift` exists as a read boundary per repo facts, but there is no write path anywhere — manually-logged metrics (weight, subjective ratings once added, etc.) can never flow back out to Apple Health for use by other apps.
- **Recommendation:** Add an opt-in "Also save to Apple Health" toggle on manual-entry quick-add sheets (starting with `WeightQuickSheet` in `LogHubScreen.swift`) that writes via `HKHealthStore.save`.
- **Why it matters:** BADAN currently only consumes from the health ecosystem, never contributes back — for metrics BADAN captures that HealthKit also models (weight, BP once FEAT-105 exists), this is a one-way door that limits interoperability with other apps the user might use.
- **Expected user impact:** Manually-entered BADAN data becomes visible to the user's other HealthKit-integrated apps.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Platform/Health/HealthKitAdapter.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** HealthKit integration
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** New HealthKit write-permission request flow (permission-timing consideration)
- **Risk if skipped:** BADAN stays a one-way data sink relative to the Apple Health ecosystem.
- **Implementation notes:** Must be strictly opt-in per entry, respecting the product's local-first-by-default posture — write-back should never be silently automatic.

### FEAT-182 — No import/restore of a previous BADAN export

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `ExportRunner` is entirely write-only — there is no counterpart `ImportRunner`, no "restore from backup" screen, and no way to read a previously-generated `bundle.json`/`raw.csv` back into the app (e.g. after a reinstall or device switch).
- **Recommendation:** Add an "Import BADAN backup" flow in `ExportCenterScreen.swift` (or Settings) that reads a `.json` bundle and reconciles it against the existing DB by record id, respecting the app's suppress-not-delete dedup policy already described in `ExportRunner.dedupPolicyNote`.
- **Why it matters:** Since BADAN is explicitly local-first with no backend (ADR-0002) and no iCloud backup exclusion handling (per repo facts), a JSON export is currently the *only* possible backup mechanism — but it's a dead end, since there's no way to ever bring that data back in. A reinstall or device change means permanent data loss.
- **Expected user impact:** Genuine backup/restore capability for a local-first app that otherwise risks total data loss on reinstall or device change.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 5
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** New `apps/ios/Sources/Export/ImportRunner.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Export, all repositories (Measurement, Derivation, Logging), Storage
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile + QA
- **Dependencies:** Needs careful ID-collision/merge semantics given the existing suppress-not-delete dedup model
- **Risk if skipped:** Given no backend and no documented iCloud-backup handling, this is the single highest-stakes gap in the Export area — users have no real safety net against data loss from reinstall, device loss, or storage corruption.
- **Implementation notes:** Highest-effort, highest-importance item in this entire batch; should be treated as a dedicated initiative, not a quick add. Start scoping with the JSON bundle format (already schema-versioned via `ExportManifest.schemaVersion`) as the single supported import source.

### FEAT-183 — No progress indicator or cancel control for large exports

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `ExportCenterViewModel.run` shows only an indeterminate `ProgressView()` (`ExportCenterScreen.runButton`, line 329) for the entire duration of a potentially large "all time, raw+derived+sensitive" export — there is no percentage/row-count progress and no cancel button.
- **Recommendation:** Add coarse progress reporting (e.g. per-metric-id completion count, since `ExportRunner.run` already iterates `ids` one metric at a time) and a cancel action that aborts the detached `Task`.
- **Why it matters:** `ExportCenterViewModel.run` already explicitly runs off the main actor specifically to avoid freezing the UI on large exports (per its own doc comment) — but a large export can still take a long time with zero feedback or escape hatch.
- **Expected user impact:** Confidence that a long-running export is actually progressing, and the ability to back out of an accidental "all time" export.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Export/ExportRunner.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Export
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users have no feedback or recourse during a long export beyond waiting or force-quitting the app.
- **Implementation notes:** `ExportRunner.run`'s existing per-metric-id loop (`metricIdsInScope`) is a natural progress-reporting checkpoint via a callback closure.

### FEAT-184 — No direct email/AirDrop export shortcuts beyond the generic ShareSheet

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `ShareSheet.swift` (16 lines) wraps a plain `UIActivityViewController` with no pre-selected/prioritized targets — every export requires the same two extra taps through the full share sheet even for the common "email to my doctor" case.
- **Recommendation:** Add an explicit "Email" quick-action button next to the generic share button on `ExportSuccessCard`, using `MFMailComposeViewController` pre-attaching the export files.
- **Why it matters:** Given the export cockpit's own framing implies clinician-sharing use cases, a one-tap email shortcut removes friction for the single most common sharing destination.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster path to the most common export destination (email).
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ShareSheet.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Export
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor — the generic share sheet still reaches email, just with one extra tap.
- **Implementation notes:** Additive only; keep the existing generic `ShareSheet` as the default, add email as a secondary quick action.

### FEAT-185 — No export encryption/password protection option

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Exported files (`raw.csv`, `derived.csv`, `bundle.json`) are written as plain, unencrypted files to a temp folder — there is no password-protection or encryption option anywhere in `ExportRunner.swift`, even though `sensitiveNote` in `ExportCenterScreen.swift` already warns "Keep the file somewhere private."
- **Recommendation:** Add an optional password-protected ZIP output (using a bundled encryption library, staying fully offline per D-8) when `scope.includeSensitive` is true.
- **Why it matters:** The UI already acknowledges the sensitivity risk in copy ("Keep the file somewhere private") but offers no technical mitigation — this is a real gap between the app's stated privacy stance and what it actually does for sensitive exports.
- **Expected user impact:** Meaningfully reduced risk if an exported file is misplaced, especially for sensitive medication/symptom data.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Export/ExportRunner.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Export
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile + QA
- **Dependencies:** Needs a vetted, offline-capable encryption approach (no network dependency, consistent with D-8)
- **Risk if skipped:** Sensitive exports remain plain-text files with only a copy-level warning as protection.
- **Implementation notes:** Gate behind `scope.includeSensitive` specifically, matching the existing `sensitiveNote` UI trigger in `ExportCenterScreen.swift`.

### FEAT-186 — No way to export both CSV and JSON in one run

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `ExportCenterScreen.swift`'s `formatSection` is a mutually-exclusive single-select (`format: ExportFormat = .csv`) — generating both formats requires running the entire export twice.
- **Recommendation:** Allow multi-select in `formatSection`, running `ExportRunner.run` once per selected format and presenting both result sets together.
- **Why it matters:** Users who want both a human-friendly CSV and a complete JSON backup currently have to manually repeat the entire flow, including re-selecting the same scope/range twice.
- **Expected user impact:** One export action instead of two identical, redundant ones.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Export
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor annoyance — dual-format users repeat the full flow twice.
- **Implementation notes:** `ExportFormatCard`'s `selected` binding just needs to become a `Set<ExportFormat>` instead of a single value; `vm.run` already takes `format` as a parameter and can be called in a loop.
- **First patch sketch:** Change `ExportCenterScreen.format` from `ExportFormat` to `Set<ExportFormat>`, looping `vm.run(scope:format:env:)` once per selected format.

### FEAT-187 — No export template/preset system (e.g. "doctor visit" preset scope)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Every export run starts from the same default `ExportScope()` — there's no way to save a named combination of format/scope/range/units for reuse (e.g. a recurring "quarterly doctor visit" export).
- **Recommendation:** Add a small "Save as preset" action on `ExportCenterScreen` that persists a named `ExportScope`+`format`+`range` combination for one-tap reuse.
- **Why it matters:** Once per-metric/per-source selection (FEAT-173/175) exists, building that precise scope becomes valuable enough to want to repeat without reconfiguring every field each time.
- **Expected user impact:** Recurring export needs (e.g. quarterly appointments) become one tap instead of full reconfiguration.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Export
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-173 (per-metric scope makes presets meaningfully differentiated from each other)
- **Risk if skipped:** Recurring export configurations must be manually rebuilt every time.
- **Implementation notes:** Persist named `ExportScope` snapshots via `Profile` repository or `UserDefaults`.

### FEAT-188 — No per-day or per-event single-record share from Timeline

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `TimelineScreen.swift`'s `eventRow` has no action menu at all (not even a tap target) — sharing a single day's events or one specific event requires running the full Export cockpit and manually narrowing the date range.
- **Recommendation:** Add a context menu on `daySection`/`eventRow` with a "Share this day" action producing a small scoped export (reusing `ExportRunner` with `startDate`/`endDate` pinned to that day).
- **Why it matters:** Sharing "what happened on this specific day" (e.g. for a specific symptom flare) is a much more targeted, common need than the full Export cockpit's broad scope selection.
- **Expected user impact:** Fast, targeted single-day sharing directly from where the user is already looking at that day's events.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Timeline, Export
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Single-day sharing remains a multi-step detour through the full Export cockpit.
- **Implementation notes:** Reuse `ExportRunner.run` with `scope.startDate`/`endDate` both set to the tapped day's bounds; present via the existing `ShareSheet`.

### FEAT-189 — No CSV column customization (all-or-nothing column set)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `CSVWriter`/`ExportRow` (`apps/ios/Sources/Export/CSVWriter.swift`) always emit the full fixed 24-column contract defined in `packages/export-schemas/csv_columns.json` — there is no way for a user to select a subset of columns for a simpler file.
- **Recommendation:** Add an optional "Simplified columns" toggle to `ExportCenterScreen`'s power-only unit section, dropping provenance/quality-flag columns for users who just want value+timestamp+metric.
- **Why it matters:** The full 24-column contract is valuable for power users and is explicitly the shared, versioned contract (`packages/export-schemas/csv_columns.json`) — but casual users opening a CSV in a spreadsheet app may find it overwhelming with no simpler option.
- **Expected user impact:** A lighter-weight CSV option for casual users while preserving the full contract for power users/programmatic consumption.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Export/CSVWriter.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Export
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile + Product
- **Dependencies:** Must not break the versioned `packages/export-schemas/csv_columns.json` contract — should be an additive, opt-in simplified mode, not a schema change
- **Risk if skipped:** Casual users get the full power-user column set with no lighter alternative.
- **Implementation notes:** Implement as a second, clearly-named output shape (not a modification to the canonical contract file), to avoid any versioning ambiguity.

### FEAT-190 — No export of Sources/permissions/audit info for support purposes

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `SourcesScreen.swift` displays connected sources, devices, and permission states, but none of it is ever included in any export — `ExportRunner` never touches `env.catalog.sources()`/`permissions()`.
- **Recommendation:** Add an optional "Include sources & permissions" toggle to the power-only export scope that writes a small `sources.json`/`sources.csv` alongside the main export files.
- **Why it matters:** When troubleshooting a data-quality issue (e.g. "why is my HRV missing for these two weeks"), having the connected-source/permission state alongside the exported data is valuable diagnostic context that currently must be manually screenshotted from `SourcesScreen` separately.
- **Expected user impact:** Self-service and support-assisted debugging of data gaps becomes easier with source/permission context bundled alongside the data itself.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Export/ExportRunner.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Export, Sources
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor — diagnostic context stays available only within the app UI, not in exports.
- **Implementation notes:** `env.catalog.sources()`/`permissions()` (already used by `SourcesViewModel`) are the only queries needed; write as one small extra JSON file in the export folder.

### FEAT-191 — No global search across logged data (symptoms, medications, notes, workouts, meals)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** The only `.searchable()` modifier in the entire codebase is on `BodyAllMetricsBrowser` (`apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift:324`), searching only the static 44-metric ontology; `SymptomLogView.searchResults` (line 213) searches only the symptom *dictionary*, not the user's own logged entries. There is no way to search across a user's actual medication list, symptom history, notes, workouts, or meals anywhere in the app.
- **Recommendation:** Add a global search entry point (e.g. a search tab/toolbar action) that queries across `LoggingRepository`'s symptoms/adherence/workouts/nutrition/notes plus `MeasurementRepository` samples, ranked by recency, jumping into the relevant detail/Timeline position on tap.
- **Why it matters:** This is the single largest SEARCH gap in the app — a personal health repository with months of logged data has no way to find "that thing I logged about my knee in March" except manually scrolling Timeline's 21-day window (itself limited per FEAT-165).
- **Expected user impact:** Users can actually retrieve specific past entries instead of relying on memory of roughly when something happened.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** New `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Search/GlobalSearchScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/LoggingRepository.swift`
- **Affected systems:** LoggingRepository, MeasurementRepository, Timeline
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile + Data
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-165 (widening Timeline's window makes search results more consistently navigable once tapped)
- **Risk if skipped:** A "personal health repository" with growing history has no retrieval mechanism beyond linear scrolling — the app's core value (a complete record) is undermined by an inability to find anything specific within it.
- **Implementation notes:** Start with simple substring matching over already-fetched text fields (symptom labels/notes, medication names, meal descriptions) rather than building full-text search infrastructure; SQLite FTS5 is a natural follow-on if substring search proves too slow at scale.

### FEAT-192 — No keyword search within Timeline

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `TimelineScreen.swift`'s only filtering mechanism is `selectedTypes: Set<TimelineEventType>` (type filter, power-only) — there is no text-search box anywhere on the screen, so finding a specific event within even the current 21-day window requires visually scanning every row.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `.searchable()` modifier to `TimelineScreen` filtering the already-loaded `[TimelineEvent]` array by title/subtitle substring match.
- **Why it matters:** This is a much smaller, faster win than the full global search in FEAT-191 (client-side filtering of already-fetched data, no new repository queries) while directly addressing the most-visited "everything" screen.
- **Expected user impact:** Quick in-place filtering of the current Timeline view by keyword.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Timeline
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Timeline stays scan-only for keyword lookup even within its current limited window.
- **Implementation notes:** Add `.searchable(text: $searchText)` to the existing `ScrollView` in `TimelineScreen.body`, extending `filtered(_:)` to also check `event.title`/`event.subtitle` against `searchText`.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `@State private var searchText = ""` and `.searchable()` modifier to `TimelineScreen.swift`, extending the existing `filtered(_:)` function with a substring check.

### FEAT-193 — No "jump to date" search in Timeline

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `TimelineScreen.swift` has no date-picker/jump-to-date affordance — navigating to a specific date requires either scrolling (bounded by the 21-day window, FEAT-165) or is simply impossible for older dates today.
- **Recommendation:** Add a small calendar/date-jump button to `TimelineScreen`'s toolbar that scrolls (or, once FEAT-165 widens the window, re-queries) to the selected date's section.
- **Why it matters:** "What happened on this specific date" is a fundamentally different, very common need from either keyword search (FEAT-192) or type filtering — currently unaddressed by any existing control.
- **Expected user impact:** Direct navigation to a known date instead of scroll-searching for it.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Timeline
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-165 (widening the window makes older dates actually reachable once jumped to)
- **Risk if skipped:** Known-date navigation remains impossible or scroll-dependent.

### FEAT-199 — No recent-search suggestions/autocomplete for custom symptom or trigger entry

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `SymptomLogView.swift`'s `customResultRow`/`newTrigger` free-text fields (lines 256–276, 418–432) offer no autocomplete against the user's own previously-used custom labels/triggers — every custom entry is typed from scratch even if identical text was used last week.
