- **Risk if skipped:** Worst-case first impression for motion-sensitive users specifically.
- **Implementation notes:** Given FEAT-239's shared helper, this is a one-line application of it to `OnboardingView`'s existing animation call site.

### FEAT-249 — VoiceOver-friendly description of `StatusChip` trend/position beyond color+icon

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `StatusChip` (used throughout `InsightsWeeklyRow`, `MetricDetailScreen`, etc.) communicates within/above/below-band status via color, icon, and short label together, but there's no dedicated `accessibilityValue` confirming the underlying semantic state independent of the label text choice — if a future label wording changes, VoiceOver's understanding of the actual state (in/above/below range) has no separate structured guarantee.
- **Recommendation:** Add an explicit `accessibilityValue` on `StatusChip` derived directly from `Baseline.Position`, decoupled from the display label string, so the semantic meaning is guaranteed even if display copy changes.
- **Why it matters:** This is a small but real robustness gap in the app's most-repeated status-communication component — accessibility currently depends entirely on the label string staying in sync with meaning, not from an explicit semantic binding.
- **Expected user impact:** More robust, consistent VoiceOver announcements of status across every screen using `StatusChip`.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatusChip.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Accessibility, design system
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low immediate impact, but a latent robustness gap in the most-reused status component.
- **Implementation notes:** Straightforward addition given `Baseline.Position` is already a clean three-case enum available at every `StatusChip` call site.

### FEAT-250 — Accessibility Inspector-driven audit pass tracked as a recurring internal tool, not a one-off

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Given the confirmed near-total absence of accessibility coverage (5 files touch any a11y API in ~13.7k lines of Swift), a single one-time fix pass (FEAT-237–249) will not stay fixed without a recurring audit process — there is currently no CI step, lint rule, or scheduled review for accessibility regressions anywhere in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- **Recommendation:** After the initial fix pass, add a recurring (e.g., per-release) Accessibility Inspector run against key screens (Home, Insights, MetricDetail, Settings) as a documented QA step, and consider a minimal automated check (e.g., failing CI if a new SwiftUI `Text`/`Image` is added to a Feature screen with no accessibility modifier nearby) as tooling matures.
- **Why it matters:** Without a recurring process, the app will regress back to today's near-zero coverage as new features ship — this closes the loop on FEAT-237–249 rather than treating them as one-time fixes.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — sustains any accessibility gains made instead of letting them erode over subsequent releases.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, new QA process doc
- **Affected systems:** Accessibility tooling, CI, internal tooling
- **Suggested owner:** QA
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-237–249 should exist first as the baseline to maintain.
- **Risk if skipped:** Today's near-zero accessibility coverage is the predictable outcome of having no process to prevent it — without one, any fix pass simply resets the clock until the next regression.
- **Implementation notes:** Start with a documented manual QA checklist per release; automate the cheapest checks (missing labels on new interactive elements) once the fix passes above land.

## RETENTION LOOPS (FEAT-251 – FEAT-262)

### FEAT-251 — Build the Goals UI (domain, storage, and repository already exist; zero UI consumes them)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `Goal`/`GoalDirection` are fully modeled in `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Customization.swift`, `ProfileRepository.goals()/upsertGoal(_:)/deleteGoal(id:)` are fully implemented against a real `goals` SQL table (`apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Migrations.swift`), yet a repo-wide search finds zero UI anywhere in `apps/ios/Sources/Features/` that creates, edits, lists, or displays progress against a goal — this is a completely dead feature at the presentation layer.
- **Recommendation:** Build a Goals screen (create/edit/list, reachable from Settings or Home) that reads/writes through the existing `ProfileRepository` goal methods — no new domain or storage work required, purely a UI gap.
- **Why it matters:** This is the single most concrete, lowest-risk retention feature available in the entire codebase — the backend is done and tested-by-construction (it's plain SQL CRUD), and only the screen is missing.
- **Expected user impact:** Users get a genuine goal-setting/tracking loop (e.g., "at least 7h sleep," "at most 3 caffeine servings") that today simply doesn't exist anywhere reachable.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/ProfileRepository.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Customization.swift`, new `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Goals/GoalsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Customization, retention, home surface
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None — storage and domain layers are already complete.
- **Risk if skipped:** A fully-built backend capability sits permanently unused, and BADAN ships with zero goal-setting mechanic despite having already paid the engineering cost for one.
- **Implementation notes:** `Goal.direction` (`atLeast`/`atMost`/`around`) plus `target`/`unit` map directly onto a simple form; progress-against-goal can reuse `MeasurementRepository.latestInterval` the same way `InsightsViewModel.weeklyChanges` already does.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `GoalsScreen` list view backed by `env.profileRepo.goals()` with a simple add-goal sheet (metric picker + target + direction) calling `upsertGoal`, and a nav entry point from `SettingsScreen`'s modules or a new Home module card.

### FEAT-252 — Build metric-pinning UI (storage/repository already exist; zero UI consumes them)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `ProfileRepository.pinnedMetrics()`/`setPinned(_:_:at:)` are fully implemented against a real `metric_pins` table (`apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Migrations.swift:180`), but no screen in `apps/ios/Sources/Features/` ever calls either method — there is no pin/unpin affordance on `MetricDetailScreen`, Home, or anywhere else.
- **Recommendation:** Add a pin toggle (star icon) on `MetricDetailScreen` and surface pinned metrics as a prioritized row/module on Home, reading through the existing repository methods.
- **Why it matters:** Like Goals (FEAT-251), this is a fully-built storage capability with zero UI — a second concrete, low-risk retention win sitting unused in the same repository file.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can curate the metrics they personally care most about into quick-access, distinct from the fixed 7-module home layout.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/ProfileRepository.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Customization, retention, home surface
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None — storage layer complete.
- **Risk if skipped:** A second fully-built, zero-cost-to-surface capability stays permanently invisible to users.
- **Implementation notes:** A simple `Set<String>` membership check (`pinnedMetrics()`) plus a toggle button; Home module rendering can filter/sort by pin status the same way it already sorts `homeModules` by `order`.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a star `Button` in `MetricDetailScreen`'s header calling `env.profileRepo.setPinned(metricId, !isPinned, at: env.now())`, and add a "Pinned" row to `HomeScreen` reading `env.profileRepo.pinnedMetrics()`.

### FEAT-253 — Real streak domain object (`StreakEngine`), not just the unused insight template copy

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** The only streak-adjacent code in the entire app is the unwired `within_band_streak` insight template text (FEAT-208); there is no `StreakEngine`, no persisted streak count, and no streak concept anywhere in `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Derivation/` analogous to `BaselineEngine`.
- **Recommendation:** Add a small `StreakEngine` (parallel structure to `BaselineEngine`) that computes and persists consecutive-day streaks per metric/goal (logging streak, in-band streak, goal-met streak), feeding both FEAT-208's insight and a dedicated retention surface.
- **Why it matters:** Streak mechanics are the most well-evidenced retention lever in the competitive research (one case study cited: 45%→68% habit completion, +21% conversion) and BADAN currently has none, in a codebase whose architecture (deterministic engines over repositories) is well-suited to add one cleanly.
- **Expected user impact:** A genuine, wellness-safe (non-shaming) consistency mechanic across logging and goal-adherence.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** New `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Derivation/StreakEngine.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/DerivationRepository.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Migrations.swift` (new table)
- **Affected systems:** Retention, derivation pipeline, storage
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** Shares the day-position lookback groundwork with FEAT-207/FEAT-208.
- **Risk if skipped:** BADAN forgoes the single most evidence-backed retention mechanic in the category despite having template copy already written for it.
- **Implementation notes:** Must strictly follow the wellness rules — no "streak broken, you failed" framing; a lapsed streak should reset silently/calmly, not moralize.

### FEAT-254 — Persistent, revisitable weekly recap (retention framing of FEAT-210)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** As noted in FEAT-210, `InsightsViewModel.weeklyChanges` recomputes the "This week" card fresh every time the Insights tab loads and never persists it — from a retention standpoint, this means there is no "your week in review" moment a user can be drawn back to revisit, share, or compare against a prior week.
- **Recommendation:** Building on FEAT-210's persistence work, add a dedicated "This week vs last week" comparison view once weekly insights are durable, explicitly designed as a return-visit hook.
- **Why it matters:** A revisitable, comparable weekly recap is a standard retention loop in this category (per the competitive research's "Trends tab...rolling averages, date selectors") and currently impossible since the current weekly card has no memory of prior weeks.
- **Expected user impact:** A concrete reason to return to the Insights tab on a weekly cadence beyond daily insight-checking.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Insights/InsightsScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Derivation/InsightEngine.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Retention, insight generation
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** FEAT-210 (persisted weekly insight) must land first.
- **Risk if skipped:** The weekly card stays a stateless snapshot with no comparative or return-visit value.
- **Implementation notes:** Week-over-week delta is a simple diff once two persisted weekly `Insight` rows exist.

### FEAT-255 — First-baseline-unlocked celebratory moment

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `BaselineEngine` computes a metric's first non-provisional baseline once 14 days of coverage exist, but this transition (provisional → real baseline) happens completely silently — no card, animation, or acknowledgment anywhere marks the moment a user's data becomes "calibrated" for the first time.
- **Recommendation:** Add a one-time, dismissible "Your [metric] baseline is ready" moment (Home or Insights) the first time each metric transitions out of `provisional`.
- **Why it matters:** This is a natural, deserved milestone the engine already detects internally (`Baseline.provisional`) but never surfaces as a positive moment — a clear missed retention/reward opportunity using data BADAN already computes.
- **Expected user impact:** Rewards the two-week data-building period with a tangible payoff moment instead of a silent status-badge change.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Derivation/BaselineEngine.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Insights/InsightsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Retention, baselines
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A natural milestone moment the engine already computes goes permanently unused.
- **Implementation notes:** Needs a one-time "seen" flag per metric (small addition to `ProfileRepository` or a new table) to avoid re-showing the celebration on every load.

### FEAT-256 — Surface data-coverage/consistency progress ("your baselines are X% calibrated")

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `Baseline.nPoints`/coverage against `BaselineEngine.windowDays` (14) is already computed and shown as a raw number in `MetricAnatomySheet` ("Days used"), but there is no aggregate, motivating view of overall calibration progress across all tracked metrics — a user has no single place to see "12 of 14 metrics are fully calibrated."
- **Recommendation:** Add a simple aggregate progress indicator (e.g., on Home or a Goals/Insights summary) showing how many of the user's actively-tracked metrics have moved past provisional status.
- **Why it matters:** Progress visualization is a well-established retention mechanic, and BADAN already computes every input needed (`Baseline.provisional` per metric) — this is a presentation gap, not a data gap.
- **Expected user impact:** Gives new users a concrete, encouraging sense of "getting there" during the otherwise invisible two-week calibration period.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Derivation/BaselineEngine.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Retention, baselines, home surface
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** New users have no visible sense of progress during the calibration window, which is exactly the period they're most likely to churn before seeing value.
- **Implementation notes:** A simple `X of Y metrics calibrated` count derived from existing per-metric `Baseline.provisional` flags across `keyMetrics` (or the FEAT-209-expanded set).

### FEAT-257 — Return-visit "since you were last here" summary card

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** Neither `HomeScreen` nor `InsightsScreen` distinguishes a same-day revisit from a return after several days away — there's no "here's what happened while you were away" framing anywhere, despite `AppEnvironment` already tracking `now()`/clock state that could support a last-opened comparison.
- **Recommendation:** Track last-opened timestamp (simple `UserDefaults` or profile field) and, when the gap exceeds a threshold (e.g., 3+ days), surface a short "welcome back" summary card highlighting what changed while away.
- **Why it matters:** This is a standard, low-cost re-engagement pattern that's currently entirely absent — the app treats every visit identically regardless of absence length.
- **Expected user impact:** Lapsed users get an easy on-ramp back into the app instead of facing the same undifferentiated Home screen as a daily user.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Retention, home surface
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Lapsed users returning after a break get no differentiated welcome-back experience to re-hook them.
- **Implementation notes:** Simplest version reuses the existing weekly-change computation (FEAT-210) scoped to the actual absence window instead of a fixed calendar week.

### FEAT-258 — In-app "reconnect a paused source" retention nudge (distinct from FEAT-219's insight card)

- **Affected systems:** Retention, source catalog
- **Suggested owner:** Design

### FEAT-259 — "Insight engagement" streak (days user opened Insights / gave feedback)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** There's no tracking anywhere of how consistently a user engages with the Insights tab or gives feedback — `InsightRepository.setFeedback` records individual feedback events but nothing aggregates them into an engagement pattern the user could see or be encouraged by.

### FEAT-260 — Recently-viewed metrics quick-access row (distinct from manual pinning)

- **Category:** New Feature

## CUSTOMIZATION (FEAT-263 – FEAT-282)

### FEAT-263 — Drag-to-reorder home module editor (the `order` field exists; only the UI is missing)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `HomeModule.order: Int` is a fully modeled, persisted field (`apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Customization.swift`) and `CustomizationProfile.visibleModulesOrdered` already sorts by it, but `SettingsScreen.modulesSection` only exposes visibility toggles (`SettingsToggleRow`) in a fixed list order — there is no drag handle, no reorder gesture, anywhere in `SettingsScreen.swift`.
- **Recommendation:** Replace the static `ForEach` in `modulesSection` with a `List`/`.onMove`-based reorderable list that writes back to `HomeModule.order` via `env.update`.
- **Why it matters:** This is a third instance (after Goals/pins) of a fully-modeled customization field with zero UI — the dashboard-layout-editor capability the brief specifically calls out already exists in the data model, only the editor is missing.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can actually customize their home layout order, not just which modules show/hide — completing the "custom dashboard layout" capability the domain model was clearly built for.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Customization.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Customization, home surface
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A third dead field/feature pairing sits in the codebase (module order is computed and used for rendering, but never user-editable).
- **Implementation notes:** SwiftUI's native `List { }.onMove(perform:)` maps directly onto reassigning `order` values in `env.profile.homeModules`.
- **First patch sketch:** Swap `modulesSection`'s `VStack`/`ForEach` for a `List` with `.onMove { from, to in ... }` reassigning `order` on the sorted `env.profile.homeModules` array, writing back through the existing `env.update { }` pattern already used by `setModuleVisible`.

### FEAT-264 — Per-metric unit override UI (the field and formatter already support it; only the picker is missing)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `CustomizationProfile.unitOverrides: [String: String]` (metricId → preferred unit) is a real, persisted field that `ValueFormatter.swift:16` already reads (`profile.unitOverrides[def.metricId] ?? def.primaryDisplayUnit`), but `SettingsScreen.unitsSection` only exposes the global `UnitProfileMode` (canonical vs. display) radio group — there is no per-metric unit picker anywhere in the app.
- **Recommendation:** Add a per-metric unit override list (e.g., accessible from `MetricDetailScreen` or a dedicated Units screen) letting a user pick, say, kilometers over miles for distance while keeping everything else at default — reading/writing the already-wired `unitOverrides` dictionary.
- **Why it matters:** This is a fourth instance of a fully-plumbed customization capability (data model + read-side consumer both exist) with no write-side UI — the exact "per-metric units overrides" gap the brief calls out by name.
- **Expected user impact:** Power users get the granular per-metric unit control the blueprint envisions ("units per metric" — `docs/BADAN_MASTER_BLUEPRINT_OLD_DONT_USE.md:1201`) instead of only a blunt global toggle.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/App/ValueFormatter.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Customization.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift` or `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Customization, units, value formatting
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None — the read path (`ValueFormatter`) already exists and works.
- **Risk if skipped:** A fully-working formatter code path (`unitOverrides[def.metricId]`) can never actually be populated by a real user, since nothing writes to that dictionary anywhere in the app.
- **Implementation notes:** `MetricDefinition.displayUnits` (from the registry) already enumerates the valid alternatives per metric — the picker is a straightforward per-metric enum choice writing into `env.update { $0.unitOverrides[metricId] = unit }`.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a "Preferred unit" row to `MetricDetailScreen` (power depth only) offering `data.def.displayUnits` as options, writing the selection into `env.profile.unitOverrides[data.def.metricId]` via `env.update`.

### FEAT-265 — Customizable baseline window (power users can't change the fixed 14-day window)

- **Category:** New Feature
- **Problem:** `BaselineEngine.windowDays` is a hardcoded `static let windowDays = 14` constant (`apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Derivation/BaselineEngine.swift:18`) — every user, casual or power, gets exactly the same 14-day rolling median/MAD window with zero way to widen it (e.g., 30 days for a more stable baseline) or narrow it (e.g., 7 days for faster adaptation after a lifestyle change).
- **Recommendation:** Make the window length a power-mode-only `CustomizationProfile` field (with sane min/max bounds and a clear default), threaded into `BaselineEngine.recomputeAll`.
- **Why it matters:** This is precisely the "custom baseline windows (power)" capability called out in the brief, and BADAN's baseline architecture already isolates the window as a single named constant, making this a contained, low-blast-radius change.
- **Expected user impact:** Power users recovering from a lifestyle change (new training block, recent illness) can get a faster-adapting baseline instead of waiting for a fixed 14-day rolling window to catch up.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Derivation/BaselineEngine.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Customization.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Customization, baselines
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** Needs care around the "provisional" honesty threshold, which is also currently tied to `windowDays`.
- **Risk if skipped:** All users, regardless of sophistication or need, are locked into one fixed calibration speed with no override.
- **Implementation notes:** `BaselineEngine.recompute` already parameterizes its query window off `Self.windowDays` in three places — converting that to an instance-level configurable value (still defaulting to 14) is a mechanical refactor plus a new Settings control.

- **Importance:** 2

- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Theme.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Customization.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Customization, design system
