### UIUX-068 — No cross-fade between splash, onboarding, and the tab shell

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `RootView.body`'s `Group { if !env.isReady { SplashView() } else if !env.onboardingComplete { OnboardingView() } else { MainTabView() } }` has no `.transition`/`.animation` anywhere — the app's three biggest top-level state changes (splash → onboarding → tab shell) all happen as instant jump cuts.
- **Recommendation:** Wrap the `Group` switch in `withAnimation`/`.transition(.opacity)` so these transitions cross-fade.
- **Why it matters:** This is the single most prominent, guaranteed-to-be-seen transition in the entire app (every user experiences it exactly once per install, and the splash→tabs transition on every cold launch), and it's currently the most abrupt one.
- **Expected user impact:** A calmer, more polished first impression on cold launch.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/App/RootView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS app launch flow
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The app's first impression stays the most jarring transition in the whole product.
- **Implementation notes:** `.animation(.easeInOut, value: env.isReady)` plus a matching value for `env.onboardingComplete` should cover both transitions without a full redesign.

### UIUX-069 — Splash screen's bare ProgressView gives no context for what's happening or how long it'll take

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SplashView` shows a plain `ProgressView()` beneath the heart icon and "BADAN" title with no label — during first run, `SeedController` seeds 90 days of demo data via `Task.detached`, which could take a perceptible moment, but the user has no idea the app is doing anything more than "starting up."
- **Recommendation:** Add a short, honest label under the spinner (e.g., "Setting up your repository…") that appears if the wait exceeds ~1 second.
- **Why it matters:** An unlabeled spinner during a potentially multi-second first-run wait offers no reassurance that anything meaningful is happening.
- **Expected user impact:** First-run users get a clearer sense of what the brief wait is for.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/App/RootView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS app launch, first-run seeding
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor first-run reassurance gap; low severity since seeding is likely brief in practice.
- **Implementation notes:** Keep the label calm/generic rather than technical ("Setting up," not "Seeding 90 days of synthetic HealthKit samples").

### UIUX-070 — Custom SwiftUI splash is visually disconnected from the native (blank) launch screen

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `project.yml` defines `UILaunchScreen: {}` (an empty/blank native launch screen), while `SplashView` shows a custom heart icon + "BADAN" wordmark + spinner immediately after — the OS-level blank launch screen and the SwiftUI splash are visually unrelated, so the instant the app becomes interactive, users see a visible flash/swap from blank white to the branded splash.
- **Recommendation:** Give the native launch screen matching branding (background color + centered icon) so the handoff to `SplashView` is seamless, per Apple's standard "match your launch screen to your first screen" guidance.
- **Why it matters:** This flash is the very first thing every user sees on every cold launch, and it's an easy, well-understood fix.
- **Expected user impact:** A seamless, professional-feeling cold launch instead of a visible blank-to-branded flash.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/project.yml`, `apps/ios/App/RootView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS app launch (Info.plist launch screen)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A visible, avoidable flash on every single cold launch.
- **Implementation notes:** `UILaunchScreen` supports a background color + centered image via Info.plist keys without needing a storyboard; match `BadanColor.background`'s light value and the heart glyph.

### UIUX-071 — Tab bar has no state/badge affordance for fresh content

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MainTabView`'s five `tabItem`s are static icon+label pairs with no badge or visual marker — a returning user landing on Today has no tab-level signal that, say, new insights have appeared since their last visit.
- **Recommendation:** Consider a minimal, non-intrusive badge (a small dot, not a number, to stay "calm") on the Insights tab when new content exists since last view.
- **Why it matters:** This is a genuine, currently-absent affordance opportunity for returning users, distinct from the empty-state/loading findings elsewhere.
- **Expected user impact:** Returning users are more likely to discover new insights without manually checking each tab.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/App/RootView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS tab shell
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor discoverability gap; low severity since Insights is already one of five always-visible tabs.
- **Implementation notes:** A calm dot badge (not a numeric count) fits the wellness-safe, non-alarming tone better than a red counter badge.

### UIUX-072 — No in-context way to preview the other language/RTL from any of the five read tabs

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** None of the reviewed screens (Home, Body, Sources, MetricDetail, Timeline, Insights) expose any language/RTL toggle — switching languages requires leaving to Settings (out of this review's scope) — and only Home has an Arabic screenshot in `docs/screenshots/` (`04-home-arabic-rtl.png`); Body, Sources, MetricDetail, Timeline, and Insights have no Arabic screenshot evidence anywhere in the repo.
- **Recommendation:** At minimum, capture and check in Arabic/RTL screenshots for the other five in-scope screens (cheap, high-signal), and consider a lightweight in-context language switch for faster QA/demo purposes.
- **Why it matters:** "Arabic/RTL readiness is a first-order concern" per the project's own guardrails, but the project's own screenshot evidence only actually demonstrates it on one of seven reviewed screens — several of this review's own RTL-related findings (UIUX-075, UIUX-082) could only be found by reading code, not by looking at a real rendered Arabic screenshot.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — improves the team's ability to catch real RTL regressions before users do.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `docs/screenshots/` (evidence gap), `apps/ios/App/RootView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS app-wide localization QA
- **Suggested owner:** QA
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** RTL regressions on Body/Sources/MetricDetail/Timeline/Insights remain undetectable by screenshot review alone.
- **Implementation notes:** Capturing the missing screenshots is a same-day task; a real in-context toggle is a larger, separate Ease-of-Use-category consideration.

### UIUX-073 — Every app font is a fixed point size, so Dynamic Type has zero effect on any text

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `BadanFont` (`Tokens.swift`) defines every type-ramp entry as `Font.system(size: N, weight:, design:)` with no `relativeTo:`/text-style basis (`heroNumeral` 44, `numeralM` 28, `sectionTitle` 20, `body` 16, `bodyCompact` 15, `chip`/`caption` 13); confirmed by grep that `dynamicTypeSize`/text-style-relative fonts are used nowhere in the reviewed scope — accessibility Dynamic Type sizes (which many low-vision users rely on) do not scale a single piece of text in the app.
- **Recommendation:** Rebuild `BadanFont` on `Font.system(.body, design:...)`-style text styles (or `.system(size:, weight:, design:).relativeTo(.body)` equivalents) so every font in the ramp scales with the user's chosen text size.
- **Why it matters:** This is the single highest-leverage accessibility fix in the whole design system — one component change benefits every screen and every text element in the app simultaneously.
- **Expected user impact:** Low-vision users who rely on larger system text sizes finally get a readable app instead of one frozen at a fixed size regardless of their accessibility settings.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system typography, every screen in the app
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** Will surface layout risks flagged elsewhere (UIUX-008, UIUX-010, UIUX-018, UIUX-026) that are currently latent because text doesn't scale yet.
- **Risk if skipped:** The app remains effectively unusable at accessibility text sizes for the population that most needs them, despite otherwise careful design-system work.
- **First patch sketch:** In `Tokens.swift`, change each `BadanFont` case to use `.system(size: N, weight: W, design: D).leading(...)` wrapped via a helper that applies `UIFontMetrics(forTextStyle: .body).scaledFont(for:)`, or simplest: swap fixed sizes for the nearest built-in text style (`.largeTitle`, `.title2`, `.body`, `.caption`) so scaling comes for free; then visually re-audit each screen since some layouts (grids, sparklines) will need reflow accommodations.
- **Implementation notes:** This is a foundational change — sequence it before UIUX-008/010/018/026, since those layout fixes are much easier to validate once text actually scales.

### UIUX-074 — StatusChip text fails WCAG AA contrast in light mode for both amber and green states

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Computing WCAG contrast for `StatusChip`'s 13pt `chip`-font text against its own `tint.opacity(0.14)`-over-`surface` background: light-mode amber (`#B97A14` text on its ~14%-tint background) computes to roughly **3.06:1**, and light-mode in-band green (`#2E9E63` on its tint) to roughly **2.9:1** — both well under WCAG AA's 4.5:1 minimum for normal-size text (dark mode fares much better, at roughly 6.3:1 for amber).
- **Recommendation:** Darken the light-mode `outOfBand`/`inBand` text colors specifically for on-tint use, or switch chip text to a solid (non-tinted) background with sufficient contrast, rather than semi-transparent tint fills.
- **Why it matters:** Contrast ratios of the amber/green status chips are explicitly called out as a review focus, and this is a directly computed, quantified failure on the component that carries the app's single most important piece of "how am I doing" information on nearly every screen.
- **Expected user impact:** Low-vision users in light mode can actually read the in-range/out-of-range status text that the app's whole "calm, honest" design language depends on.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatusChip.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, every screen that shows a status chip (Home, Body, MetricDetail, Insights)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The app's core "in range / out of range" signal is under-legible in light mode for exactly the users who most need clear text.
- **First patch sketch:** In `Tokens.swift`, either raise the tint-background opacity to ~22–25% (recomputes to a comfortably passing ratio) or introduce darker `-onTint` text-color variants for `inBand`/`outOfBand` used only inside `StatusChip`, then swap `StatusChip`'s `foregroundStyle(tint)` to use the new variant.
- **Implementation notes:** Re-verify both light and dark mode after the change — dark mode already passes, so avoid over-correcting and breaking it.

### UIUX-075 — StatusChip forces LTR on its entire chip, not just the directional arrow icon

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `StatusChip.body` applies `.environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight)` to the whole `HStack { icon; text }`, not just the `Image` — while the doc comment explains this is meant to keep the up/down arrow semantic (not mirrored), it also pins the icon-before-text internal ordering and disables the Arabic label's natural RTL flow inside the chip, unlike `PillLabel` (used for near-identical status pills elsewhere), which does not force LTR and mirrors correctly.
- **Recommendation:** Scope the `.leftToRight` override to just the `Image`, letting the `HStack` and its Arabic text follow the ambient layout direction normally.
- **Why it matters:** RTL mirroring quality is a named review theme; this is a concrete, code-verified case where more got pinned to LTR than the stated intent required.
- **Expected user impact:** Arabic-language status chips mirror correctly (text-then-icon in RTL) like every other pill in the app, while still protecting the arrow's semantic direction.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatusChip.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, Arabic/RTL layout
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** `StatusChip` remains the one pill component in the app whose internal element order doesn't respect RTL, unlike `PillLabel`.
- **Implementation notes:** Apply `.environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight)` directly on the `Image(systemName: iconName)` line instead of the outer `HStack`.

### UIUX-076 — StatusChip and PillLabel use different background opacities for the same visual "pill" shape

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `StatusChip` fills its background with `tint.opacity(0.14)` while `PillLabel` — visually the same rounded-rect icon+text pill shape, same `BadanRadius.chip` — uses `tint.opacity(0.12)`; two independently-defined components producing near-identical shapes with silently different numeric constants.
- **Recommendation:** Extract a shared `PillBackground` view modifier (opacity, radius, padding) that both `StatusChip` and `PillLabel` apply, so any future opacity/radius change is made once.
- **Why it matters:** Two visually-near-identical components maintained independently is exactly how small, hard-to-notice inconsistencies like this accumulate over time.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — prevents future visual drift between the app's two pill families.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatusChip.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/Pills.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-029
- **Risk if skipped:** The two pill families keep drifting independently as each gets touched separately over time.
- **Implementation notes:** A `.pillBackground(tint:)` `ViewModifier` in `Theme.swift` would be a natural home for the shared logic.

### UIUX-077 — BadanColor.critical is defined but has zero call sites, leaving no severity tier beyond one amber

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `Tokens.swift` defines `BadanColor.critical` with the comment "Reserved; near-never used so it keeps its power," but a repo-wide check finds it unused anywhere in the reviewed scope — every out-of-band reading, however far outside the personal band, renders with the exact same single amber `outOfBand` tint.
- **Recommendation:** Either keep it deliberately unused (and document that as an intentional, permanent design decision so future contributors don't "discover" and misuse it) or define the specific condition under which it should first appear.
- **Why it matters:** An unused-but-present token in the design system is a latent inconsistency risk — someone will eventually reach for it without a defined usage rule, especially once magnitude-aware status is considered (see UIUX-090's related magnitude point).
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — reduces the risk of an inconsistent one-off "critical" usage appearing later without a considered design rule.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Negligible in the short term; a documentation/governance nit more than a live bug.
- **Implementation notes:** A one-line doc-comment update clarifying the token's intended (non-)usage would resolve this without code changes.

### UIUX-078 — BadanCard's shadow is hardcoded inline instead of a reusable elevation token

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `BadanCard`'s `shadow(color: Color.black.opacity(0.05), radius: 12, x: 0, y: 6)` is written directly inside the component rather than exposed as a semantic `BadanShadow`/`.badanElevation()` token — any surface built without literally reusing `BadanCard` (e.g., `MetricDetailScreen`'s `anatomyButton`, see UIUX-036) silently loses the app's elevation language.
- **Recommendation:** Extract the shadow into a `View` extension (`.badanElevation()`) that both `BadanCard` and any card-adjacent custom surface can apply.
- **Why it matters:** This is the root cause behind UIUX-036's specific instance — fixing it here prevents the same flat-surface-next-to-a-card problem from recurring elsewhere.
- **Expected user impact:** Consistent elevation cues across every card-like surface in the app, present and future.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Theme.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-036
- **Risk if skipped:** Every future one-off custom card-like surface has to remember to hand-copy the exact shadow values.
- **Implementation notes:** A simple `extension View { func badanElevation() -> some View { shadow(...) } }` in `Theme.swift`.

### UIUX-079 — StatBox isn't consistently reused by every "value + unit + chip" surface

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `BodyPillarCard` and `MetricGridCell` (Home's power Snapshot grid) both hand-roll their own value/unit/chip layout at `BadanFont.numeralM` (28pt) with bespoke spacing, rather than using the `StatBox` component built specifically for this pattern (44pt `heroNumeral` + `space1` rhythm) — the app has one dedicated "stat block" component and two of its most natural use cases bypass it.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `size` parameter to `StatBox` (e.g., `.hero`/`.compact`) covering both the 44pt and 28pt use cases, then migrate `BodyPillarCard`/`MetricGridCell` onto it.
- **Why it matters:** A single well-tested, accessible (once UIUX-080 lands) component benefits every consumer at once instead of three independently-maintained near-duplicates.
- **Expected user impact:** More consistent spacing/typography rhythm for "stat block" content across Home and Body.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatBox.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, iOS Home/Body tabs
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-017, UIUX-080
- **Risk if skipped:** Three independently-maintained "stat block" layouts keep drifting apart in spacing/typography over time.
- **Implementation notes:** Sequence this after UIUX-080 (accessibility grouping) so the migration delivers both consistency and accessibility improvements at once.

### UIUX-080 — StatBox has no built-in VoiceOver grouping, so every consumer inherits the fragmentation

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `StatBox` (the shared "value + unit + label + chip" component used by Home and MetricDetail) renders its four pieces of content as independent `Text`/`View` nodes with no `accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` — every screen that uses it (see UIUX-007's Home-specific instance) inherits the same fragmented VoiceOver reading order.
- **Recommendation:** Fix the grouping once inside `StatBox` itself (as detailed in UIUX-007's patch sketch) rather than patching each call site separately.
- **Why it matters:** Root-causing this at the component level, rather than per-screen, guarantees every current and future `StatBox` consumer benefits automatically.
- **Expected user impact:** Every screen using `StatBox` gets a coherent single-phrase VoiceOver reading, not just Home.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatBox.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, VoiceOver / accessibility
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-007
- **Risk if skipped:** The fragmented VoiceOver experience persists on every screen using `StatBox`, not just Home.
- **First patch sketch:** Same fix as UIUX-007, applied directly inside `StatBox.body`: wrap in `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` with a synthesized `.accessibilityLabel`.
- **Implementation notes:** Do this once here instead of separately in UIUX-007 — the two items describe the same fix at two altitudes (symptom vs. root cause).

### UIUX-081 — ProvenanceRow has no lineLimit/truncation strategy on any of its three text elements

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ProvenanceRow` packs source name, ingestion-path label, and timestamp into one `HStack` with only a single `Spacer(minLength:)` between the middle group and the timestamp — none of `sourceName`, `ingestionPath.displayLabel`, or `timestampText` specify `.lineLimit`/`.truncationMode`, so long or arbitrary content (vendor-provided source names, longer Arabic ingestion-path labels) risks unpredictable wrapping or overflow.
- **Recommendation:** Add `.lineLimit(1)` with `.truncationMode(.tail)` to the source-name and ingestion-path `Text`s, since the row's whole design assumes a single tidy line.
- **Why it matters:** This is the one component whose entire job is a clean, single-row lineage list — without truncation safeguards, its core promise (a tidy row per record) isn't actually guaranteed by the code.
- **Expected user impact:** Provenance rows stay visually tidy regardless of how long a source or ingestion-path string happens to be.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/ProvenanceRow.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, MetricDetail lineage card
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A single unusually long source name (common with vendor/file-import sources) could visually break the lineage list layout.
- **Implementation notes:** Two-line change; verify against real vendor source names once available.

### UIUX-082 — ProvenanceRow and InsightsWhyDisclosure use two different conventions for rendering timestamps

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ProvenanceRow.timestampText` uses a fully locale-aware `DateFormatter` (mirrors direction/digits with the ambient language), while `InsightsWhyDisclosure.detailRow`'s conceptually similar "Generated" timestamp explicitly forces `.leftToRight` on just that value — two different rendering conventions for the same category of information (a record/generation timestamp) in two different components.
- **Recommendation:** Pick one convention (most likely: force LTR for all technical/provenance timestamps, matching `InsightsWhyDisclosure`'s more defensive choice) and apply it consistently to `ProvenanceRow` too.
- **Why it matters:** RTL mirroring quality should be a deliberate, consistent rule, not something that varies by which component happens to render a timestamp.
- **Expected user impact:** Predictable, consistent timestamp rendering wherever provenance/generation dates appear.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/ProvenanceRow.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Insights/InsightsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, RTL layout
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor but real inconsistency between two components handling the same kind of data.
- **Implementation notes:** Given `ProvenanceRow`'s numeric timestamp already reads fine either way, forcing LTR (matching `InsightsWhyDisclosure`) is the lower-risk direction to standardize on.

### UIUX-083 — EmptyStateView's action button has no button chrome, just tinted text

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `EmptyStateView`'s optional action button (currently only used by `TimelineScreen`'s "Clear filters") is `Text(actionTitle).foregroundStyle(BadanColor.primary)` inside a `Button` with no background, border, or shape — the sole interactive element inside an otherwise fully passive empty/error surface has no visual chrome distinguishing it as tappable beyond its color.
- **Recommendation:** Give the action a lightweight button treatment (e.g., a subtle bordered/tinted background) consistent with how other primary actions in the app are styled.
- **Why it matters:** In a screen state defined by having almost nothing else to look at, the one thing a user *can* do should be unmistakably actionable.
- **Expected user impact:** Users more readily notice and use the recovery action offered in empty/error states.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatefulContainer.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, every empty/error state in the app
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-014 (Home's empty-state CTA), UIUX-019 (Body/Sources empty-state context)
- **Risk if skipped:** The one actionable element in empty/error states stays visually understated.
- **Implementation notes:** A `.buttonStyle` with a light `BadanColor.primary.opacity(0.1)` background + `BadanRadius.control` would fit the existing token system without inventing new chrome.

### UIUX-084 — StatefulContainer's error state surfaces raw, untranslated Swift error descriptions to users

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Every ViewModel in scope (`HomeViewModel`, `MetricDetailViewModel`, `SourcesViewModel`, `TimelineViewModel`, `InsightsViewModel`) catches errors with `state = .error(String(describing: error))`, and `StatefulContainer`'s `.error` case renders that raw string directly as the screen's `EmptyStateView` title — meaning a technical, non-bilingual Swift error description (e.g., a raw `SQLiteError` case) can appear verbatim as user-facing copy.
- **Recommendation:** Replace `.error(String)` with `.error(LocalizedString)` carrying a calm, generic bilingual message (e.g., "Something went wrong loading this"), and log the raw technical string separately rather than displaying it.
- **Why it matters:** This directly breaks two named product guardrails at once — "everything user-facing is bilingual" and "wellness-safe language" — and it's a single shared root cause across every screen in scope, not a one-off.
- **Expected user impact:** Users never see cryptic technical error text; instead they see calm, bilingual, actionable messaging.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatefulContainer.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/SourcesScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Insights/InsightsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, every read screen's error handling
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Any unhandled storage/query error surfaces raw, English-only, technical text directly to end users on any screen, in any language.
- **First patch sketch:** Change `LoadState.error(String)` to `LoadState.error(LocalizedString)` in `StatefulContainer.swift`, add one generic `Loc.somethingWentWrong` bilingual string, and update each `catch { state = .error(...) }` site to use it while still logging `error` to console/telemetry for debugging.
- **Implementation notes:** Keep the raw error available for developer-facing logs (e.g., `print`/os_log) even though it's no longer shown to users.

### UIUX-085 — StatefulContainer's empty state always uses the same generic "tray" icon regardless of screen

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `StatefulContainer`'s `.empty` case always renders `EmptyStateView(icon: "tray", ...)` — only `TimelineScreen` and `InsightsScreen` bypass this by building their own custom `EmptyStateView` calls with context-specific icons; every other screen in scope (Home, Body, MetricDetail, Sources) shows the identical generic tray icon no matter what's actually missing.
- **Recommendation:** Extend `LoadState.empty` to optionally carry an icon name, defaulting to `"tray"` but letting each screen override it (Home → a heart/sparkle icon, Sources → antenna, etc.).
- **Why it matters:** This is the shared root cause behind UIUX-014 and UIUX-019 — fixing it once here means every screen's empty state can be made more specific with a one-line change instead of each screen having to bypass the shared container entirely.
- **Expected user impact:** Empty states across the app feel purpose-built rather than interchangeable.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatefulContainer.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, every read screen's empty state
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-014, UIUX-019
- **Risk if skipped:** Each screen has to independently bypass the shared component to get a contextual empty state, as Timeline/Insights already do, rather than the container supporting it directly.
- **Implementation notes:** `LoadState.empty(String, icon: String = "tray")` is a low-risk, additive API change.

### UIUX-086 — StatefulContainer's loading state is a bare, unlabeled spinner everywhere

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `StatefulContainer`'s `.loading` case is just a centered `ProgressView()` with no text — identical whether it's loading the entire Home dashboard, a single metric's 90-day history, or the Sources/permissions list; every screen already authors a contextual message for its *empty* state, but none carry that same contextual sensibility into loading.
- **Recommendation:** Extend `LoadState.loading` to optionally carry a label (or accept a per-screen skeleton view, per UIUX-013), so loading isn't the one state that stays fully generic across the whole app.
- **Why it matters:** "Skeleton/loading states vs bare ProgressView" is a named review theme, and this is its systemic root cause — every one of the six in-scope screens inherits the same generic spinner from this one component.
- **Expected user impact:** A more contextual, less generic loading moment on every screen.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatefulContainer.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, every read screen's loading state
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-013
- **Risk if skipped:** Loading remains the single least differentiated state across all six read screens.
- **Implementation notes:** Given how briefly loading is likely visible in practice (synchronous MainActor queries), a labeled spinner may be sufficient without needing full per-screen skeletons everywhere.

### UIUX-087 — MetricChart's baseline band has no stroke and no on-chart legend

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricChart`'s band `RectangleMark` is filled at a flat `BadanColor.inBand.opacity(0.10)` with no `strokeBorder`/outline and no accompanying `Text` anywhere in the component explaining what the shaded region represents.
- **Recommendation:** Add a thin border (e.g., `1pt` at slightly higher opacity) to define the band's edges more clearly, and expose a way for consumers to render an adjacent legend caption.
- **Why it matters:** This is the component-level root cause behind UIUX-043's screen-level instance — fixing legibility here benefits every current and future `MetricChart` consumer, not just `MetricDetailScreen`.
- **Expected user impact:** The single most meaningful visual layer on every metric chart (the personal range) becomes easier to see and understand everywhere it's used.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/MetricChart.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system charting
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-043
- **Risk if skipped:** The band stays faint and unexplained on every screen that uses `MetricChart`, not just MetricDetail.
- **Implementation notes:** Consider exposing a `bandLabel: LocalizedString?` parameter so consumers can opt into an inline legend without every consumer needing to hand-build one.

### UIUX-088 — MetricChart's line/bar rendering has no outlier clamping, so one extreme point can flatten the rest of the series

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricChart`'s `Chart` block sets no explicit `.chartYScale` domain — Swift Charts auto-scales the Y axis to the full min/max of the passed `points`, so a single erroneous or extreme outlier (e.g., one mis-recorded high step-count day) visually compresses the other 89 days of a 90-day series into a near-flat line near one edge of the plot.
- **Recommendation:** Consider a configurable Y-domain clamp (e.g., percentile-based) with a small "1 value out of range, not shown to scale" annotation, rather than always auto-fitting to the true min/max.
- **Why it matters:** This is a common, real charting legibility failure mode for personal health data specifically — sensor glitches and manual-entry typos are exactly the kind of outliers that would trigger it.
- **Expected user impact:** A single bad data point no longer silently destroys the readability of an otherwise informative 90-day trend.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/MetricChart.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system charting, MetricDetail
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Any single outlier reading (sensor glitch, manual-entry typo) can silently make a whole trend chart unreadable with no on-screen explanation.
- **Implementation notes:** A percentile-clamped domain (e.g., 1st–99th) with a small "±N values outside range" caption is a common, low-risk pattern for this.

### UIUX-089 — Neither chart primitive in the design system supports tap/drag inspection

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Confirmed by review of both `MetricChart` and `MetricSparkline` in `MetricChart.swift`: neither implements any gesture handling (`.chartOverlay`, `DragGesture`, or otherwise) anywhere in the file — this is the component-level root cause behind UIUX-032's `MetricDetailScreen`-specific instance, meaning tap-to-inspect is unavailable app-wide, not just on one screen.
- **Recommendation:** Build the crosshair/tooltip interaction once inside `MetricChart` (see UIUX-032's sketch) so every current and future chart consumer inherits it automatically.
- **Why it matters:** Fixing this at the component level, rather than screen-by-screen, means power users get consistent chart interaction everywhere a chart appears, present and future.
- **Expected user impact:** Every metric chart in the app becomes explorable, not just decorative.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/MetricChart.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system charting
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-032
- **Risk if skipped:** Tap-to-inspect stays absent from the design system's only two chart primitives indefinitely.
- **Implementation notes:** Should be built once here rather than duplicated per-screen; see UIUX-032 for the specific `MetricDetailScreen` integration point.

### UIUX-090 — MetricSparkline auto-scales to its own min/max, exaggerating trivial variance as dramatic zigzags

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricSparkline`'s `Chart` has no fixed Y-domain and no reference to the metric's baseline band — a metric with genuinely tiny day-to-day variance (e.g., resting heart rate hovering 52–55bpm) auto-scales to fill the full sparkline height exactly as dramatically as one with large true variance, since the rendered "shape of change" only reflects relative, not absolute, variation.
- **Recommendation:** Where a baseline band is available to the caller, pass it through so the sparkline can scale relative to the band width rather than its own local min/max — or accept a fixed default Y-range per metric family.
- **Why it matters:** Power users are meant to read sparkline shape as a fast signal of volatility; as built, the shape says nothing reliable about actual magnitude of change.
- **Expected user impact:** Sparkline shape becomes a trustworthy at-a-glance volatility signal instead of a visual illusion.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/MetricChart.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system charting, Home/Body sparkline consumers
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Sparklines keep visually overstating the significance of small, normal fluctuations.
- **Implementation notes:** Simplest version: accept an optional `band: (low: Double, high: Double)?` parameter and use it to set `.chartYScale(domain:)` when present.

### UIUX-091 — Chart's baseline band redraws at different widths as the period selector changes, with no continuity cue

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricChart`'s band `RectangleMark` spans only `xStart`/`xEnd` of whatever `points` array is currently passed in — when `MetricDetailScreen`'s period selector switches from 7 to 90 days, the exact same personal-range band redraws at a very different horizontal width with no visual continuity or explanation, which can read as if the range itself changed rather than just the viewing window.
- **Recommendation:** Keep the band's rendered width visually stable relative to the plot area regardless of point-array length, or add a brief crossfade animation when the period changes so the resize reads as "the same band, wider view" rather than a new shape.
- **Why it matters:** A user toggling the period selector shouldn't have to re-learn what the shaded region means each time its shape changes.
- **Expected user impact:** Switching time periods no longer visually implies the personal range itself is changing.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/MetricChart.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system charting, MetricDetail period selector
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A subtle but real "what changed" comprehension gap every time a power user adjusts the period selector.
- **Implementation notes:** Could be addressed largely by adding UIUX-003/UIUX-068-style `.animation` on the chart's data changes, giving the band a visible crossfade rather than an instant redraw.

### UIUX-092 — Chart axis labels bypass the app's own number-formatting/Arabic-digit pipeline

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricChart`'s `chartXAxis`/`chartYAxis` use Swift Charts' default `AxisValueLabel()` formatting, which is independent of the app's own `Numerals.format`/`ValueFormatter` pipeline (`ValueFormatter.swift`) — every other number in the app honors the user's `arabicDigits` preference via `env.format`, but chart axis numerals do not.
- **Recommendation:** Supply custom `AxisValueLabel { Text(Numerals.format(value, ...)) }` closures so axis numerals route through the same formatting pipeline as every other number in the app.
- **Why it matters:** A user who has enabled Arabic-Indic digits everywhere else in the app will see Western digits specifically on chart axes — a small but real inconsistency in a first-order localization feature.
- **Expected user impact:** Chart axis numerals honor the same digit preference as every other number the user sees.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/MetricChart.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system charting, localization
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-044 (unit suffix work touches the same axis label closures)
- **Risk if skipped:** Chart numerals stay the one place in the app where the Arabic-digit preference silently doesn't apply.
- **Implementation notes:** Since `MetricChart` doesn't currently have access to `AppEnvironment`/`ValueFormatter`, this requires threading a formatting closure or the relevant profile flags into the component.

### UIUX-093 — The app's smallest font size does double duty as both passive status text and primary link text

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `BadanFont.chip` (13pt medium) is used both for passive status-pill text (`StatusChip`, `PillLabel`) and for primary tappable link text throughout the app ("See all" in `HomeScreen`'s Snapshot/Timeline sections, "Why" on Insight cards, filter-chip labels in `TimelineScreen`) — the smallest, least-emphasized size in the type ramp is also carrying the app's interactive call-to-action text.
- **Recommendation:** Introduce a distinct, slightly larger link-text style (e.g., 14–15pt) for tappable text-only actions, reserving `chip` strictly for passive pill labels.
- **Why it matters:** Tappable text with no button chrome beyond color is already a weak affordance (see UIUX-012); giving it the smallest font size in the whole ramp compounds that weakness.
- **Expected user impact:** Interactive text links become easier to spot and tap, especially for users with lower vision.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system typography
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Interactive links across the app stay undersized relative to their importance.
- **Implementation notes:** A new `BadanFont.link` (e.g., 15pt medium) token, applied to the specific "See all"/"Why"/filter-chip-label call sites.

### UIUX-094 — DepthBadge, ProvisionalBadge, and technical citation pills share identical chrome despite different meanings

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `PillLabel`-based badges — `DepthBadge` (a mode-toggle status), `ProvisionalBadge` (a data-maturity caveat), and the ad hoc `"function"`-icon technical citation pill on Home's readiness card — all render with the exact same rounded-pill chrome, differing only in tint/icon/text, despite representing three fundamentally different kinds of information ("about you," "about the data," "about the algorithm").
- **Recommendation:** Establish a light visual grammar distinguishing these categories (e.g., a subtle shape or border-style difference for "about the algorithm" pills vs. status pills), even if all three keep the same base pill shape.
- **Why it matters:** As more pills accumulate across the app, an undifferentiated pill grammar makes it harder for users to build reliable expectations about what a given pill means just from its shape.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can start to infer a pill's category from its form, not just by reading its text every time.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/Pills.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-012
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor, slow-accumulating comprehension cost as more pill types are added over time.
- **Implementation notes:** Even a consistent outline-vs-filled rule (filled = status, outlined = meta/technical) would meaningfully differentiate the categories without a full redesign.

### UIUX-095 — BadanRadius.control (12pt) has no actual call sites in the reviewed scope

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `BadanRadius` defines four radii (`chip: 10`, `control: 12`, `card: 20`, `sheet: 24`), but nothing in the reviewed scope — segmented controls (`MetricDetailScreen`'s `periodSelector`), buttons, text fields — actually applies `control: 12`; every one of those relies on system-default corner radii instead.
- **Recommendation:** Either apply `BadanRadius.control` to the app's actual control surfaces (custom-styled buttons, if any exist elsewhere in the app) or remove it from the token set if it's genuinely unused everywhere, to avoid a design-system token nobody can find a live example of.
- **Why it matters:** A token with zero real usage in the reviewed scope isn't currently doing any consistency work — it's effectively decorative documentation of an intention rather than an enforced rule.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — a leaner, more trustworthy token set for future contributors to reason about.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Negligible; a minor token-hygiene nit.
- **Implementation notes:** Worth a quick grep across the full app (not just this review's scope) before removing, in case Settings/Onboarding/Export screens (out of this review's scope) do use it.

### UIUX-096 — RTL/component correctness for non-Home screens is unverified by the project's own screenshot evidence

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `docs/screenshots/` contains exactly one Arabic/RTL screenshot (`04-home-arabic-rtl.png`) across the entire iOS app; none of `MetricDetailScreen`'s segmented `Picker`, `MetricChart`'s axes, `SourcesScreen`'s multi-column detail rows, or `TimelineScreen`'s filter chips have ever been visually verified in Arabic by the project's own artifacts — several findings in this review (UIUX-075, UIUX-082) could only be identified by reading code, precisely because no rendered evidence exists to check against.
- **Recommendation:** Capture and check in at least one Arabic/RTL screenshot per in-scope screen, matching the coverage Home already has.
- **Why it matters:** "Arabic/RTL readiness is a first-order concern" per the project's own stated guardrails, but the project's own visual evidence doesn't yet back that claim for 6 of 7 reviewed screens.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — closes a real verification gap that could hide additional RTL issues beyond what static code review can catch (e.g., segmented-control mirroring, chart axis mirroring).
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `docs/screenshots/`
- **Affected systems:** QA process, iOS Body/Sources/MetricDetail/Timeline/Insights screens
- **Suggested owner:** QA
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** RTL regressions on 6 of 7 reviewed screens could ship undetected, since no visual evidence exists to catch them in review.
- **Implementation notes:** A one-time, low-effort screenshot pass with the simulator's language set to Arabic would close most of this gap immediately.

### UIUX-097 — SectionHeader takes a plain String, providing no compile-time bilingual guarantee

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SectionHeader`'s `init(_ title: String, ...)` accepts an already-resolved `String` rather than a `LocalizedString` — every call site must remember to call `env.s(...)` itself before passing a title in, unlike `LText`, which enforces bilingual coverage by construction (`LocalizedString` "cannot be constructed without both values," per its own doc comment).
- **Recommendation:** Consider an overload/variant of `SectionHeader` that accepts `LocalizedString` directly and resolves it internally, nudging future call sites toward the enforced-bilingual pattern.
- **Why it matters:** Section headers are one of the most-used building blocks in the app; being the one core component that doesn't structurally enforce bilingual coverage leaves a small but real opening for an English-only heading to ship unnoticed in a future screen.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — reduces the chance of a future English-only section title shipping to Arabic users.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Theme.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, localization
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A low-probability but plausible path for an English-only heading to slip through in future screens.
- **Implementation notes:** Add `init(_ title: LocalizedString, ...)` as a convenience overload rather than changing the existing `String`-based signature, to avoid a breaking change across every current call site.

### UIUX-098 — No design-system token exists for minimum spacing between adjacent touch targets

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `BadanSpace` defines a general 4pt scale (`space1`…`space8`) plus a single `touchMin` (44pt) for individual target size, but nothing captures "minimum gap between two adjacent tappable targets" — which is how Insights' thumbs-up/down buttons ended up only `space2` (8pt) apart (UIUX-060), a value nothing in the token layer would flag as too tight.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `BadanSpace.touchGap` (e.g., 16pt) token specifically for spacing between adjacent interactive controls, and apply it at the Insights feedback row (UIUX-060) and anywhere similar arises in the future.
- **Why it matters:** This is the systemic gap behind UIUX-060's specific instance — without a named token, nothing prevents the same under-spacing pattern from recurring in a future feature.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — reduces the likelihood of future mis-tap-prone adjacent-control layouts.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-060
- **Risk if skipped:** The specific under-spacing pattern that caused UIUX-060 has no token-level guard against recurring elsewhere.
- **Implementation notes:** A single new constant in `BadanSpace`; pair with the UIUX-060 fix so both land together.

### UIUX-099 — Cards get a visible 1px border everywhere; pills and the chart band never do, with no documented rule

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `BadanCard`'s `overlay(RoundedRectangle(...).strokeBorder(BadanColor.separator, lineWidth: 1))` gives every card a visible hairline outline, but `StatusChip`, `PillLabel`, and `MetricChart`'s baseline-band `RectangleMark` — all similarly "shaped, tinted regions" — never get a comparable border; there's no written rule anywhere in the design system for when a shape should or shouldn't have an outline.
- **Recommendation:** Document (in code comments on `Tokens.swift`/`Theme.swift`) an explicit rule for which shape categories get a `separator` stroke and which don't, so future components follow a stated convention rather than whatever the original author happened to do.
- **Why it matters:** Without a documented rule, this kind of "does this get a border" decision keeps getting made ad hoc per component, as the last several findings in this review demonstrate.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — more visually predictable shape language as new components are added.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Theme.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Negligible short-term; a documentation/governance nit.
- **Implementation notes:** A doc-comment addition is sufficient; no code change required unless the team also decides to actually add borders to pills/bands.

### UIUX-100 — No SwiftUI Previews exist for any DesignSystem component, and there are zero snapshot/UI tests

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** None of the eight `DesignSystem/Components` files (`MetricChart`, `Pills`, `ProvenanceRow`, `StatBox`, `StatefulContainer`, `StatusChip`) or `Tokens.swift`/`Theme.swift` include `#Preview` blocks; combined with the repo's confirmed lack of snapshot/UI tests (per repo facts: only `PipelineTests`/`SmokeTests`/`UnitTests`, no UI/snapshot coverage), there is no fast, low-effort way to visually check any shared component — light/dark, English/Arabic, casual/power — without running the full app.
- **Recommendation:** Add `#Preview` blocks to each design-system component covering at minimum light/dark and en/ar variants.
- **Why it matters:** Every one of the other 99 findings in this review would have been faster to verify, and future regressions of them faster to catch, with previews already in place — this is the meta-fix that makes the rest of this list cheaper to act on and keep fixed.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — faster, more reliable prevention of future visual regressions across the entire design system.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/MetricChart.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/Pills.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/ProvenanceRow.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatBox.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatefulContainer.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/StatusChip.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Tokens.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Theme.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, developer tooling
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every future design-system change (including fixes to the other 99 items here) stays harder to verify and easier to silently regress than it needs to be.
- **Implementation notes:** Start with `StatusChip`/`StatBox`/`MetricChart` (the components with the most findings above) since they'd catch regressions on UIUX-074/080/087 most directly.

## LogHub

### UIUX-101 — Quick-add tiles look identical whether they push or present a sheet

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `LogTile` renders the same card style for `logTypesSection` (NavigationLink pushes) and `quickAddSection` (Button presents a sheet) in `LogHubScreen.swift`, giving the user no visual cue which navigation pattern a tap will trigger.
- **Recommendation:** Give quick-add tiles a distinct visual treatment (e.g., a small sheet/chevron-vs-plus glyph or subtitle) so push vs. modal is predictable before tapping.
- **Why it matters:** Predictable navigation affordances reduce disorientation, especially for users toggling between casual/power modes who rely on consistent patterns.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer "where did I end up" moments; faster mental model of the Log tab.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Log tab
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor but persistent navigation-model confusion as more quick-add types are added.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a trailing small "sheet" indicator icon (e.g., `chevron.up` in a pill) to `LogTile` instances used inside `quickAddSection` only.

### UIUX-102 — Recent chips promise "log again" but open a blank capture form

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `LogHubViewModel.RecentItem` and `recentsSection`'s `destination(for:)` route to a brand-new `SymptomLogView()`/`WorkoutLogView()` with no pre-fill, even though the "Recents" label and history-style chip visually imply a one-tap re-log.
- **Recommendation:** Either rename/restyle the section to "Recent entries" (view-only) or actually pre-select the symptom/activity in the destination view via an initializer parameter.
- **Why it matters:** The affordance sets an expectation (2-tap re-log) the destination doesn't honor, which is a direct UX bait-and-switch on a screen meant to reduce logging friction.
- **Expected user impact:** Either faster real re-logging, or accurate expectations that avoid frustration.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Log tab, Symptom capture, Workout capture
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** SymptomLogView/WorkoutLogView need to accept an optional preselection parameter.
- **Risk if skipped:** Users abandon the "quick re-log" habit once they discover it isn't actually quick.
- **First patch sketch:** Add an optional `preselected:` init parameter to `SymptomLogView`/`WorkoutLogView` that sets `selection`/`activity` before first render, then pass the recent item's id from `LogHubScreen.destination(for:)`.

### UIUX-103 — Water quick-log sheet offers only two fixed amounts, no custom entry

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `WaterQuickSheet` in `LogHubScreen.swift` hardcodes `amounts: [250, 500]` with no way to enter a different volume, unlike `WeightQuickSheet` which accepts free text.
- **Recommendation:** Add a third row (or a small "custom" text entry) so any volume can be logged without leaving the sheet.
- **Why it matters:** Two presets is a narrow assumption about bottle/cup sizes; users with different containers can't log accurately.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer abandoned water logs for people whose typical serving isn't 250/500ml.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Log tab quick-add
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Persistent minor friction for non-average water containers.
- **Implementation notes:** Mirror `WeightQuickSheet`'s `TextField(.decimalPad)` + parsed-value pattern as a third row in `WaterQuickSheet`.

### UIUX-104 — Quick-log sheets use fixed pixel heights/minHeights instead of design tokens

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `LogHubScreen.swift` hardcodes `minHeight: 92` (LogTile), `minHeight: 60` (WaterQuickSheet/WeightQuickSheet rows), and `.presentationDetents([.height(260)])` rather than referencing `BadanSpace`/token values used elsewhere (`BadanSpace.touchMin`, `space*`).
- **Recommendation:** Replace raw literals with existing or new named tokens (e.g., `BadanSpace.rowCompact = 60`) so spacing stays centrally tunable.
- **Why it matters:** Repo guardrails treat the design system as a source of truth; raw numbers drift silently and complicate Dynamic Type/RTL audits.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — more consistent spacing over time, easier future polish passes.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS DesignSystem token usage
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Gradual token/spacing drift across the app as more screens copy the same hardcoded pattern.
- **Implementation notes:** Add `space*`-style constants to `Tokens.swift` for the 60/92/260 values found here, then substitute.

### UIUX-105 — Fixed 260pt sheet height risks clipping at large Dynamic Type sizes

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Both `WaterQuickSheet` and `WeightQuickSheet` use `.presentationDetents([.height(260)])`, a fixed pixel height that doesn't grow with the user's text size setting.
- **Recommendation:** Use `.presentationDetents([.medium, .height(260)])` or a `.fraction`-based detent, or wrap content so it can scroll within the fixed detent.
- **Why it matters:** At accessibility text sizes, "Log water"/"+500 ml" button labels and the weight field can wrap or clip within a non-scrolling 260pt sheet.
- **Expected user impact:** Reliable quick-log sheets for users with larger text sizes.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Log tab quick-add sheets, Dynamic Type support
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Broken/clipped quick-add sheets for accessibility-text-size users.

### UIUX-106 — Recent chips hide their time context from casual-mode users

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `RecentChip`'s `detail` (relative time via `relativeTime(item.date)`) is only passed `if env.depth.showsPowerDetail`, so casual users see undifferentiated chips with no way to tell "5 minutes ago" from "3 weeks ago" when duplicate activity types recur.
- **Recommendation:** Show relative time to all altitudes — it's orientation information, not raw/technical detail, and doesn't conflict with the casual/power split.
- **Why it matters:** Distinguishing near-duplicate recent entries (e.g., two "Run" chips) is a basic usability need, not a power-user affordance.
- **Expected user impact:** Casual users can correctly identify which recent chip is which before tapping.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Log tab
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Casual users occasionally tap the wrong recent chip.

### UIUX-107 — Log-types grid silently shrinks with no explanation when sensitive module is off

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `logTypesSection` only shows Symptom/Medication tiles `if env.profile.sensitiveModulesEnabled`, so the 2x2 grid becomes 1x2 with no label or hint explaining why two tiles disappeared.
- **Recommendation:** When sensitive modules are off, show a disabled/ghost tile or a one-line caption ("Turn on Sensitive records in Settings to log symptoms & medications") instead of silent omission.
- **Why it matters:** Users who expect four log types and see two may think the app is broken rather than realizing a Settings toggle is off.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer discoverability of the sensitive-records setting; fewer "where did this feature go" support questions.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Log tab, Settings sensitive-module toggle
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Confusing "missing feature" perception for users who toggled sensitive records off.

### UIUX-108 — No haptic or visible confirmation after a quick water/weight log

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `LogHubViewModel.logWater`/`logWeight` write silently and the sheet just calls `dismiss()`; there's no haptic tap, checkmark, or toast confirming the entry saved.
- **Recommendation:** Add a light haptic (`UINotificationFeedbackGenerator.success`) and a brief visual confirmation before dismiss.
- **Why it matters:** Quick-add is meant to be near-instant; without feedback, users can't be sure the tap registered versus the sheet just closing.

### UIUX-109 — Quick-add sheet titles don't distinguish themselves from the full capture flow

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `WaterQuickSheet`/`WeightQuickSheet` reuse `Loc.logWater`/`Loc.logWeight` verbatim as their `navigationTitle`, identical wording to the corresponding `LogTile` label, giving no "Quick" qualifier despite being a deliberately reduced flow.

### UIUX-110 — LazyVGrid tiles can end up uneven heights at large Dynamic Type

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `logTypesSection`/`quickAddSection` use `LazyVGrid` with `GridItem(.flexible())` columns; `LogTile` sets `minHeight: 92` but SwiftUI grids don't force row-mate heights to match when title text wraps differently between the two tiles in a row.
- **Recommendation:** Force equal row heights (e.g., wrap each row pair in an `HStack` with `.frame(maxHeight: .infinity)` on each tile, or use `alignment: .top` with a shared height read via `GeometryReader`/`.alignmentGuide`).
- **Why it matters:** At larger accessibility text sizes, mismatched tile heights within the same row look broken/unpolished.
- **Expected user impact:** Cleaner grid alignment for Dynamic Type users.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Log tab, Dynamic Type layout
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Visual roughness at larger text sizes only, low frequency.

### UIUX-111 — Weight quick-log gives no inline reason when Save stays disabled

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `WeightQuickSheet.parsedValue` silently returns `nil` for empty/zero/non-numeric text, disabling Save (`.disabled(parsedValue == nil)`) with no caption explaining why (e.g., "must be greater than 0").
- **Recommendation:** Show a small inline hint beneath the field when text is non-empty but invalid, similar to how other screens surface validation state.
- **Why it matters:** A disabled button with no explanation is a classic dead-end; users can't tell if it's a bug or their input.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer abandoned weight-log attempts from unexplained disabled buttons.

### UIUX-112 — Horizontal chip/pill scrollers give no cue that more content is offscreen

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Every horizontally scrolling chip row across the capture screens (`LogHubScreen.recentsSection`, `SymptomLogView`'s recents/category/trigger rows, `MedicationLogView`'s skip-reason/time chips, `WorkoutLogView.activityPill` row, `NutritionLogView.mealPill` row, `ExportCenterScreen`'s format cards are not scrolled but segmented controls are) uses `ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false)` with no trailing fade/gradient or partial-next-item peek, so a fully filled first screen looks final even when more chips exist.
- **Recommendation:** Add a subtle trailing fade mask (`.mask(LinearGradient(...))`) or ensure the last visible chip is always partially cut off to signal scrollability.
- **Why it matters:** `showsIndicators: false` removes the native scrollbar hint entirely, so without another cue, users may never discover additional symptoms/triggers/activities/reasons that are one swipe away.
- **Expected user impact:** Better discoverability of off-screen options across every capture screen in the app.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS capture-screen chip/pill rows (shared pattern)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** Best implemented once as a shared `HScrollFade` view modifier in DesignSystem, then applied everywhere.
- **Risk if skipped:** Silent feature/option discoverability gap repeated across five screens.

## Symptom

### UIUX-113 — Symptom save failure is silently swallowed with no error UI

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SymptomLogView.save(_:addAnother:)` does `catch { return }` when `env.logging.insertSymptom(entry)` throws — no error banner, no haptic, no retry affordance; the form just sits there looking unchanged.
- **Recommendation:** On catch, surface an inline error card (matching `ExportCenterScreen`'s `errorCard` pattern) with a wellness-safe message and keep the entered data intact for retry.
- **Why it matters:** For a sensitive, private health-logging flow, a save that silently fails erodes trust that anything was recorded — and the user has no way to know to retry.
- **Expected user impact:** Users are told when a symptom entry didn't save instead of assuming it did.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Symptom capture, sensitive-data storage
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users believe symptom history is complete when entries have silently failed to persist.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `@State private var saveError: String?` to `SymptomLogView`, set it in the `catch` block of `save(_:addAnother:)` instead of `return`, and render a small error `Text` above `saveButtons` when non-nil.

### UIUX-114 — Severity slider has no tick marks or positional landmarks

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `severityCard`'s `Slider(value: $severity, in: 0...10, step: 1)` shows only "Mild / Moderate / Severe" as endpoint+midpoint labels below the track with no visible ticks, so users can't see where the mild→moderate→severe boundaries actually fall while dragging.
- **Recommendation:** Add subtle tick marks (or a segmented background tint) at the 0–3 / 4–6 / 7–10 boundaries so the descriptor change isn't a surprise.
- **Why it matters:** A precise-feeling severity input should give visual landmarks; otherwise users guess at drag position and get an unexpected label flip.
- **Expected user impact:** More confident, faster severity selection.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Symptom capture
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor imprecision in a subjective input that's already inherently approximate.

### UIUX-115 — Adding a trigger doesn't dismiss/refocus the keyboard, and there's no dismiss affordance

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `commitTrigger()` clears `newTrigger` and calls `addTrigger`, but the `TextField` remains first responder with the keyboard up; there is no toolbar "Done" button or tap-to-dismiss anywhere in `captureForm`.
- **Recommendation:** Add a keyboard toolbar `Done` button (via `.toolbar { ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard) }`) or dismiss focus after `commitTrigger()`.
- **Why it matters:** With the keyboard covering roughly half the screen, users can't see the note/when/save cards below without manually scrolling behind the keyboard.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster path from "add trigger" to "save" without extra scroll/dismiss gestures.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Symptom capture, keyboard/focus management
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Persistent minor friction on every symptom log with a custom trigger.

### UIUX-116 — No sticky Save button; must scroll past every card to reach it

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `captureForm` stacks header → severity → triggers → note → when → (power) metadata → `saveButtons` in one plain `VStack` inside a `ScrollView`, so Save is always the last thing on screen, worse once the power-mode metadata card adds height.
- **Recommendation:** Pin Save/Save-and-add-another to a bottom bar outside the scroll content (safe-area-anchored), consistent with how `MedicationLogView`'s toolbar keeps "Add" always reachable.
- **Why it matters:** The screen's own doc comment promises "under-10-second symptom capture" — forcing a full scroll to save works against that goal, especially in power mode.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, one-thumb-reachable save on every symptom entry.

- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Symptom capture
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Slower capture flow than the screen's own "under 10 seconds" design goal.

### UIUX-117 — VoiceOver never hears the numeric severity value shown to power-mode sighted users

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `Slider(...).accessibilityValue(env.s(severityDescriptor(sev)))` only announces "Mild"/"Moderate"/"Severe" — it never includes the `sev/10` number that power-mode sighted users see next to the section header (line ~362).
- **Recommendation:** Include the numeric value in the accessibility value for power-depth users, e.g. `"\(descriptor), \(sev) of 10"`.
- **Why it matters:** VoiceOver users in power mode are denied information sighted power users get from the same screen — an accessibility parity gap tied directly to an existing depth-aware feature.
- **Expected user impact:** Equal information access for VoiceOver users at power depth.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Symptom capture, VoiceOver/accessibility
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Ongoing accessibility parity gap specific to power-mode users.

### UIUX-118 — Severity color jumps abruptly at the 7/10 threshold

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `severityTint(_:)` returns `BadanColor.outOfBand` at `value >= 7` and `BadanColor.primary` otherwise — a hard binary switch with no transition, even though the value comes from continuous slider dragging.
- **Recommendation:** Animate the tint change (`.animation(.easeInOut, value: sev)`) or introduce one intermediate step so the shift doesn't read as a sudden alarm state, consistent with the "calm amber, never alarming" guardrail.
- **Why it matters:** A snap color change at a single drag position can feel like a warning trigger, working against the wellness-safe, non-alarming intent this file's own comments describe.
- **Expected user impact:** Calmer, less startling severity feedback while dragging.

- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`

- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor tonal inconsistency with the app's explicit wellness-safe visual language.

### UIUX-122 — Backdating upper bound (`maxDate`) can go stale if the screen stays open

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `maxDate` is set once in `.task` (`maxDate = env.now()`) and never refreshed; if `SymptomLogView` remains open across a time boundary (e.g., left open in the background over midnight), the `DatePicker(... in: ...maxDate ...)` upper bound stops matching the real "now".
- **Recommendation:** Recompute `maxDate` on `scenePhase`/foreground return, or bind it live to `env.now()` instead of caching it.
- **Why it matters:** A backdating field that silently caps "now" at a stale timestamp can block users from logging the actual current time.
- **Expected user impact:** Reliable "cannot log future" constraint under all app lifecycle conditions.

- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Symptom capture
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Rare but confusing "can't pick current time" edge case.
