## Medication

### UIUX-126 — "Change your mind" flow for a resolved dose is dead code — `editingSlotId` is never assigned

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MedicationLogView` declares `@State private var editingSlotId: String?` and `dueSlotCard`'s `showActions` checks `editingSlotId == slot.id` to let a user revise a taken/skipped dose, but `editingSlotId` is only ever set to `nil` (lines ~329, ~450, ~493) — it is never set to an actual slot id anywhere, including on tapping a resolved `dueSlotCard`. The revise-a-choice flow the code (and the file's own doc comment "a slot always reflects the latest choice") implies is unreachable.
- **Recommendation:** Wire a tap gesture on resolved `dueSlotCard`s (taken/skipped) to set `editingSlotId = slot.id`, re-exposing `actionRow`/`skipReasonPicker` so users can actually correct a mistaken Take/Skip.
- **Why it matters:** The non-punitive "you can always change your mind" promise this screen is built around currently has no way to trigger it — a meaningful, already-half-built capability is invisible and unusable.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can correct an accidental Take/Skip tap without deleting/re-adding data.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Medication adherence logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users who mis-tap Take/Skip have no in-UI way to correct it, despite the state machine already supporting it.
- **First patch sketch:** In `dueSlotCard`, wrap the taken/skipped `statusTrailing` view (or the whole card) in a `Button`/`.onTapGesture` that sets `editingSlotId = slot.id` when `slot.status != .pending`, reusing the existing `showActions` branch.

### UIUX-127 — "Take all" can silently mark not-yet-due doses as taken

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `dueSection`'s "Take all" button calls `vm.takeAll(env:)`, which records `.taken` for every slot with `status == .pending` — including doses scheduled later today that aren't `isOverdue` yet — with no confirmation dialog, unlike the destructive-styled confirmations used elsewhere (`SettingsScreen`'s purge/reset).
- **Recommendation:** Either scope "Take all" to overdue-only pending slots, or add a lightweight confirmation ("Mark N doses as taken, including 1 not due until 8 PM?") before committing.
- **Why it matters:** A single tap can retroactively "take" a medication that hasn't actually been taken yet, corrupting adherence history with no undo path beyond the still-unreachable revise flow (see UIUX-126).
- **Expected user impact:** Adherence data stays accurate; fewer accidental bulk mis-logs.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Medication adherence logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Inaccurate adherence data that misrepresents whether/when medications were actually taken.
- **First patch sketch:** In `MedicationLogViewModel.takeAll(env:)`, filter `data.dueSlots` to `slot.status == .pending && slot.isOverdue` before recording, or gate the button behind a `confirmationDialog` when any pending slot is not overdue.

### UIUX-128 — Not-yet-due pending slots render no status marker, creating inconsistent card layout

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `statusTrailing(for:)` shows a "Still due" pill only when `slot.isOverdue`; otherwise pending slots render `EmptyView()` for their trailing status, so the "Due today" list mixes cards with a right-aligned marker and cards with none, and both still show the full Take/Skip `actionRow` regardless of whether the dose is actually due yet.
- **Recommendation:** Give not-yet-due pending slots a neutral "Upcoming · 8:00 PM" marker consistent with the overdue pill's visual slot, and/or defer showing the Take/Skip row until closer to the scheduled time (or clearly label it as early-logging).
- **Why it matters:** Visual rhythm breaks scanning the due list, and prominent Take/Skip buttons on a dose hours away invite premature/incorrect logging (compounds UIUX-127).
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer "what's actually due now vs. later today" list, less accidental early logging.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Medication adherence logging
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Continued visual inconsistency and premature-logging risk.

### UIUX-129 — 7-day adherence dots are hard to tell apart at a glance

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `AdherenceDot` renders four states as an 11pt circle differentiated only by fill/stroke/opacity — `.pending` is `textSecondary.opacity(0.22)` fill and `.none` is `separator.opacity(0.5)` fill, two faint, similarly-toned filled circles at a tiny size with no shape/pattern difference.
- **Recommendation:** Differentiate `.pending` vs `.none` with a shape or stroke-style change (e.g., a dashed outline for `.none`) rather than two close opacity values on the same fill color.
- **Why it matters:** The whole point of the 7-day strip is fast pattern recognition; two of its four states are currently difficult to distinguish, undermining that goal.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, more reliable at-a-glance adherence review.

- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Medication adherence strip
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Reduced legibility of the primary adherence-trend visualization.

### UIUX-130 — Add-medication Save button disables silently with no inline reason

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `AddMedicationSheet.canSave` disables Save when `name` is empty or (`mode == .daily && times.isEmpty`), but nothing in `scheduleSection`/`field` explains why — a user in Daily mode who hasn't added a time sees only a grayed-out Save with no "Add at least one time" hint.
- **Recommendation:** Show a small inline caption near the time-chip area when `mode == .daily && times.isEmpty` explaining the requirement.
- **Why it matters:** Disabled buttons with no explanation are dead ends; this is the only entry point for adding a medication at all.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer confused abandonments of the add-medication flow.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Medication regimen creation
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users abandon adding a medication without understanding why Save won't respond.

### UIUX-131 — Adding a schedule time is a two-step pick-then-tap instead of a single action

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `scheduleSection` requires picking a time on `DatePicker(displayedComponents:.hourAndMinute)` and then separately tapping "Add a time" (`addPickedTime()`); there's no direct feedback (toast/shake) if the picked time is already a duplicate — `addPickedTime()` just silently no-ops via `if !times.contains(key)`.
- **Recommendation:** Either auto-add on picker change (with an explicit "remove" affordance already present via `timeChip`), or add a brief inline message when a duplicate time is picked.
- **Why it matters:** The extra tap adds friction to a repetitive task (adding 2-4 daily times), and silent no-ops on duplicates look like the tap didn't register.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, less confusing multi-time schedule entry.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Medication regimen creation
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor repeated friction on a common multi-step task.

### UIUX-132 — Time chip text has no `.lineLimit`, unlike equivalent chips elsewhere in the app

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `timeChip(_:)`'s `Text(displayTime(time))` has no `.lineLimit(1)`, while the equivalent `chip(...)` helper in `SymptomLogView.swift` and pill helpers in `WorkoutLogView.swift`/`NutritionLogView.swift` all constrain chip text to one line.
- **Recommendation:** Add `.lineLimit(1)` to the time text in `timeChip`.
- **Why it matters:** Localized time strings (e.g., Arabic AM/PM markers) that are slightly longer than expected could wrap to two lines, breaking the capsule shape unlike every other chip in the app.
- **Expected user impact:** Consistent chip shape across languages/locales.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Medication regimen creation, RTL/localization
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Rare visual glitch for specific locale time formats.

### UIUX-133 — Daily/As-needed mode selection relies on a 0.5pt border difference as its main non-color cue

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `modeButton`'s selected vs. unselected states differ by fill opacity, text color, and `lineWidth: isSelected ? 1.5 : 1` — a half-point stroke difference that's hard to perceive, especially at accessibility zoom, with no checkmark or icon to reinforce selection the way `depthOption` (Onboarding) and `SettingsRadioGroup` do.
- **Recommendation:** Add a small checkmark or filled dot to the selected mode button, matching the selection vocabulary used elsewhere in the app.
- **Why it matters:** Selection state should be perceivable through more than a subtle stroke-width delta, especially for low-vision users.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer, more accessible selection state for Daily vs. As-needed.

- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`

- **Dependencies:** None

### UIUX-134 — Power-mode schedule detail duplicates info already shown, in a raw unlocalized format

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `regimenCard`'s power-mode line renders `scheduleDetail(regimen.schedule)`, producing strings like `"weekly(1,3,5; 09:00,21:00)"` (raw ISO weekday integers, unlabeled) right below `scheduleText(regimen.schedule)` which already shows a friendly "Weekly · 09:00, 21:00" — the same information twice, once nicely formatted and once as debug-style output.
- **Recommendation:** Either drop `scheduleDetail` in favor of `scheduleText`, or replace the raw weekday integers with localized weekday abbreviations if the power-mode line is meant to add real value (e.g., which specific weekdays).
- **Why it matters:** Power mode should add clarity/lineage, not raw programmer output that duplicates a friendlier line one row above it.
- **Expected user impact:** Less visual clutter and confusion for power-mode users reviewing their regimens.

### UIUX-135 — Strength field is unstructured free text with no numeric/unit handling

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `AddMedicationSheet`'s strength `TextField` (placeholder "e.g. 1000 IU") is a single plain text field with no `keyboardType`, unlike the app's `numberField` pattern used for kcal/distance/protein elsewhere, and doesn't participate in the `Loc.arabicDigits` formatting setting since it's raw stored text.
- **Recommendation:** Either keep it as free text but document that it's intentionally unstructured, or split into a numeric value + unit picker for consistency with the rest of the app's numeric-entry pattern.
- **Why it matters:** A user who typed digits in Arabic-Indic form (the app explicitly supports `arabicDigits` display) gets no formatting benefit here since the value is stored/displayed verbatim as entered.
- **Expected user impact:** More consistent, locale-aware strength entry.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Medication regimen creation
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor inconsistency; strength is inherently a mixed value+unit string in real-world use (e.g. "1000 IU", "50mg"), so full restructuring may not be worth the effort.

### UIUX-136 — No way to edit or deactivate an existing medication regimen from this screen

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `regimenCard` renders name/strength/schedule/adherence strip as a static, non-interactive `BadanCard` — there is no `NavigationLink`, swipe action, or context menu anywhere in `regimensSection` to revise a regimen's name, strength, or schedule, or to stop it once added.
- **Recommendation:** Add a tap target on `regimenCard` (or a context menu) that opens an edit form pre-filled from the existing `AddMedicationSheet`, reusing its fields.
- **Why it matters:** Medication schedules change often (dose adjustments, discontinuation); without an edit path, users must live with typos/mistakes made at creation time indefinitely.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can correct or update a regimen without deleting all history.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Medication regimen management
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** Reuse `AddMedicationSheet`'s form as an edit form via an optional `existing:` init parameter.
- **Risk if skipped:** Users stuck with a typo'd medication name or outdated schedule with no in-app fix.

### UIUX-137 — Boundary/disclaimer footer shows even on the empty state, adding noise before any data exists

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement

- **Why it matters:** Front-loading disclaimers before there's any content to disclaim about adds friction to the very first medication-add experience.

### UIUX-138 — `AddMedicationSheet`'s field wrapper hardcodes `minHeight: 52`, off the token scale

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** The private `field(label:content:)` helper sets `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 52, alignment: .leading)`, a raw literal that matches neither `BadanSpace.touchMin` (44) nor any other named token in `Tokens.swift`.
- **Recommendation:** Replace `52` with an existing or new named constant so the input-field height is centrally controlled.

- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — consistent field heights across screens over time.

- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`

### UIUX-139 — Add-medication toolbar button may truncate to icon-only for longer localized labels

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** The screen's `.toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) { Label(env.s(Loc.addMedication), systemImage: "plus") } }` relies on default iOS toolbar `Label` rendering, which commonly collapses to icon-only in the navigation bar — the Arabic label "إضافة دواء" (or similar) has no guaranteed visible text fallback communicated anywhere else on the empty toolbar-only screen state.
- **Recommendation:** Verify the toolbar renders with a visible title in both languages at standard and largest Dynamic Type sizes; if it collapses to icon-only, ensure `accessibilityLabel` still carries the full label (SwiftUI's `Label` should already forward it, but confirm the Arabic string does too).
- **Why it matters:** A plus-icon-only Add action with no text may be less discoverable for first-time users than a spelled-out "Add medication" button.
- **Expected user impact:** Confirmed discoverability of the add-medication action in both languages.

- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`

### UIUX-140 — Skip-reason chip grid can produce uneven row heights for longer localized labels

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `skipReasonPicker`'s `LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: 104), ...)])` sizes `SkipReason` chips with `frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: BadanSpace.touchMin)` and no `.lineLimit` on the reason text — longer Arabic skip-reason labels could wrap to two lines and grow that chip's height beyond its row-mates.
- **Recommendation:** Add `.lineLimit(2)` with a fixed/matched height, or increase `minimum` width so common localized labels fit on one line.

### UIUX-141 — No pull-to-refresh or staleness handling if the screen stays open across the day

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MedicationLogView.body` loads data once via `.task { vm.load(env) }`; if a user keeps this screen open (e.g., in a split view or backgrounded and foregrounded without a fresh push) as the day progresses, newly-due slots and updated overdue status never refresh unless a Take/Skip action happens to trigger `load(env)` as a side effect.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `.refreshable { vm.load(env) }` modifier, and/or refresh on `scenePhase` becoming active.
- **Why it matters:** A medication reminder screen that silently goes stale undermines the "Due today" section's core promise of showing what's actually due right now.
- **Expected user impact:** Always-current due/overdue status without needing to leave and re-enter the screen.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Medication due-today tracking
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Occasional stale "due" status if the screen is left open for an extended period.

### UIUX-142 — Save button has no disabled guard, unlike the sibling Nutrition screen

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `WorkoutLogView.saveButton` is always tappable with no `.disabled` condition, while `NutritionLogView.saveButton` explicitly gates on `canSave`. Rapid repeat taps on Workout's Save button will insert multiple duplicate workout entries with identical field values.
- **Recommendation:** Debounce the save action (disable briefly after tap, or track an `isSaving` flag) even though there's no "invalid" input state to gate on.
- **Why it matters:** Accidental double-taps are common on primary action buttons; without any guard, each one silently creates a duplicate record.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer accidental duplicate workout entries.

Two structurally identical slider+number patterns apply the casual/power split inconsistently.

### UIUX-146 — Distance entry hardcodes "km" and ignores the app's own display-unit system

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `optionalCard`'s distance `numberField` uses the literal string `WorkoutLogStrings.km` and `save()` does `distanceM: parseDecimal(distanceText).map { $0 * 1000 }`, assuming kilometers regardless of the user's configured display units — while `LogHubScreen.WeightQuickSheet` correctly reads `env.format.displayUnit(for:)` for weight.
- **Recommendation:** Read the metric's display unit from `env.format`/`env.registry` (as weight logging already does) and convert accordingly, or at minimum offer a km/mi toggle.
- **Why it matters:** Users with an imperial unit preference must manually convert miles to km before typing, an easy source of data-entry error.
- **Expected user impact:** Accurate, friction-free distance entry regardless of unit preference.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Workout capture, unit-conversion system
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** `Core/Units.swift`, `env.format`/`env.registry` unit APIs already used elsewhere.
- **Risk if skipped:** Silent unit-mismatch errors for imperial-preferring users (e.g. typing "5" meaning 5 miles, stored as 5km).

### UIUX-147 — "No workouts in the last two weeks" empty message is unreachable dead code

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `recentSection` does `if vm.recent.isEmpty { if vm.loggedToday { Text(noneYet) } }`, but `loggedToday` is computed from the same `all` array as `recent` (`loggedToday = all.contains { $0.startAt >= startOfToday }`); if `recent` (== `all`) is empty, `loggedToday` can never be true. The `noneYet` branch can never execute — a genuinely empty two-week workout history currently renders nothing at all below the recovery card.
- **Recommendation:** Fix the condition to `if vm.recent.isEmpty { Text(noneYet) }` (drop the impossible `loggedToday` guard), and give it icon/empty-state treatment consistent with `MedicationLogView`'s `EmptyStateView`.
- **Why it matters:** A brand-new user with zero workout history currently sees only the recovery card and then nothing — no explicit "no workouts yet" messaging ever appears, which is a real, verifiable logic bug hiding as a missing empty state.
- **Expected user impact:** New/inactive users get a clear, intentional empty state instead of a silently truncated list.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Workout capture, empty states
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Silent, uninformative blank space for any user with no workouts in the last two weeks.

## Nutrition

### UIUX-153 — Toggling "Quick calories" ON silently discards already-typed protein with no warning

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `NutritionLogView` swaps `optionalCard` (kcal + protein) for `quickEnergyCard` (kcal only) purely based on `quickCalories`; `proteinText` state persists but is unmounted from view, and `saveButton` explicitly passes `proteinG: quickCalories ? nil : parseDecimal(proteinText)` — meaning if the user types a protein value, then flips Quick Calories on, that value is silently discarded from the eventual save with zero warning.
- **Recommendation:** If `proteinText` is non-empty when the user enables Quick Calories, show a brief confirmation ("This will drop the protein value you entered") or keep protein saved regardless of the toggle.
- **Why it matters:** Silently discarding user-entered data based on an unrelated toggle is a real data-loss trap, especially since the field visually disappears rather than just becoming disabled/greyed.
- **Expected user impact:** No more silently lost protein entries.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Nutrition capture
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Recurrent, invisible loss of already-entered protein data.

### UIUX-154 — "Quick calories" toggle has no explanatory subtitle

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `quickToggleCard`'s `Toggle(isOn: $quickCalories) { Text(env.s(Loc.quickCalories)) }` has no subtitle/caption describing what flipping it actually does (hides the protein field, flags the entry as low-detail), unlike `SettingsToggleRow` elsewhere in the app which supports and regularly uses subtitles.
- **Recommendation:** Add a one-line caption beneath the toggle label, e.g. "Skip protein and mark this as a quick estimate."
- **Why it matters:** A first-time user has no way to know the consequence of this toggle before flipping it (including the data-loss risk in UIUX-153).
- **Expected user impact:** Informed, predictable use of the Quick Calories toggle.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Nutrition capture
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users flip a toggle they don't fully understand the effect of.

### UIUX-155 — kcal and protein detail chips apply inconsistent zero-value rules

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `detailChips(_:)` shows the kcal chip whenever `meal.energyKcal != nil` (even if the value is `0`), but only shows the protein chip `if protein > 0` — two structurally identical optional numeric fields on the same row follow different display rules with no visible rationale.
- **Recommendation:** Apply the same rule to both (e.g., only show a chip when the value is meaningfully non-zero, or always show both when present).
- **Why it matters:** Inconsistent rules on adjacent, visually similar chips reads as a bug rather than intentional design.
- **Expected user impact:** Predictable, consistent meal detail chips.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Nutrition capture, meal list
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor cosmetic inconsistency.

### UIUX-156 — Today's totals show "0 kcal / 0 g" with no distinction between "nothing logged" and "confirmed zero"

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `totalsSection`'s `StatBox`es always render `vm.kcalTotal`/`vm.proteinTotal` (defaulting to `0`) regardless of whether any meals have been logged yet — there's no em-dash/placeholder state distinguishing "you haven't logged anything today" from an actual zero.
- **Recommendation:** Show a dash or muted "—" placeholder in the totals row when `vm.meals.isEmpty`, reserving "0" for an actual logged-zero case.
- **Why it matters:** A prominent "0 kcal" reads as a factual statement about the day, not as "no data yet," which risks miscommunicating actual nutrition status for casual users only glancing at the summary.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer distinction between missing data and a genuine zero.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Nutrition capture, totals summary
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor risk of misreading an empty state as a confirmed-zero data point.

### UIUX-157 — Auto-selected meal type gives no visible cue that it was a suggestion, not a user choice

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `mealForHour(_:)` pre-selects a `mealType` pill based on the current hour in `.task`, but the selected pill looks identical whether the user tapped it or the app auto-picked it — no "suggested" badge or distinct initial styling.
- **Recommendation:** Add a subtle "suggested" indicator on the auto-selected pill until the user actively taps a (possibly different) one.
- **Why it matters:** Users may not realize the meal type was a guess and could save an entry under the wrong meal type without noticing.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer accidental wrong-meal-type saves.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Nutrition capture
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Occasional silently-wrong meal-type tagging.

### UIUX-158 — Today's meals list has no explicit sort, unlike LogHub's recents

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `NutritionLogViewModel.load(_:)` sets `meals = all` directly from `env.logging.nutrition(from:to:)` with no `.sorted` call, while `LogHubViewModel.load(_:)` explicitly sorts recents `{ $0.date > $1.date }`. The "Today's meals" list order depends entirely on unspecified repository return order.
- **Recommendation:** Add an explicit `.sorted { $0.occurredAt > $1.occurredAt }` (or ascending, whichever reads best) so the just-logged meal has a predictable position.
- **Why it matters:** Relying on implicit backend ordering is fragile and can silently change behavior if the repository's query changes; the just-saved meal may not appear where the user expects (e.g., at the top).
- **Expected user impact:** Predictable, stable ordering of today's meals, including right after saving a new one.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Nutrition capture, meal list ordering
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Meal order could appear to jump around unpredictably as the underlying data source changes.

### UIUX-159 — Description field has no `.autocorrectionDisabled()`, inconsistent with other named-entity fields

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `descriptionCard`'s `TextField(..., text: $descriptionText, axis: .vertical)` leaves autocorrection at its default, while `SymptomLogView`'s trigger field and `MedicationLogView`'s medication-name field both explicitly set `.autocorrectionDisabled()`.
- **Recommendation:** Decide deliberately whether free-text food descriptions should autocorrect (arguably yes, since it's prose) and document the choice; if not, disable it for consistency with sibling name-like fields.
- **Why it matters:** Small, inconsistent keyboard configuration choices across near-identical field types suggest the behavior wasn't a deliberate decision.
- **Expected user impact:** Predictable typing behavior consistent with the rest of the app's text fields.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Nutrition capture, keyboard configuration consistency
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Negligible; likely fine as-is since it's prose text, just undocumented.

### UIUX-160 — Quick Calories card swap has no animation, causing an abrupt layout jump

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** The `if !quickCalories { optionalCard } else { quickEnergyCard }` branch in `body` isn't wrapped in `withAnimation`, so toggling Quick Calories causes an instant, jarring height change, unlike `MedicationLogView`'s mode toggle or `SettingsScreen`'s theme/language changes which explicitly use `.easeInOut`.
- **Recommendation:** Wrap the toggle's effect (or at minimum the conditional view swap) in `withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.2))`.
- **Why it matters:** Consistent motion language matters for a "calm" product; this is one of the few remaining abrupt transitions among otherwise-animated toggles in the app.
- **Expected user impact:** Smoother, calmer visual feedback when switching Quick Calories.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Nutrition capture, motion consistency
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor motion-language inconsistency.

### UIUX-161 — Save button's disabled-state opacity (0.4) may leave white label text low-contrast

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `saveButton` applies `.opacity(canSave ? 1 : 0.4)` to the whole button including its white `.foregroundStyle(.white)` label over the primary-teal background — dimming both the fill and the text together to 40% can push the label below comfortable contrast against the (also dimmed) background, rather than dimming the fill only and keeping text legible-but-muted.
- **Recommendation:** Verify contrast at the 0.4 opacity state in both light/dark themes; consider dimming only the background fill or using a distinct "disabled" color pairing instead of blanket opacity.
- **Why it matters:** A disabled button should still be legible enough to read its label, especially for low-vision users trying to understand why it's inactive.
- **Expected user impact:** Legible disabled-state button text in all themes.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Nutrition capture, contrast/accessibility
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Possible contrast-accessibility shortfall on the disabled Save state.

### UIUX-162 — Empty meals state is text-only, inconsistent with Medication's illustrated empty state

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `mealsSection`'s empty state is a single caption line (`Text(env.s(NutritionLogStrings.noneYet))`), while `MedicationLogView.emptyState` uses a full `EmptyStateView` with icon, title, message, and an action button.
- **Recommendation:** Use the same `EmptyStateView` component here for visual consistency, at least for the "no meals logged today" case.
- **Why it matters:** Two logging screens in the same feature family (`WorkoutNutrition`) present empty states at very different visual weights with no clear reason.
- **Expected user impact:** More consistent, more inviting empty state across sibling logging screens.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Nutrition capture, empty-state consistency
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor visual inconsistency between sibling capture screens.

## Export

### UIUX-163 — Export progress indicator gives no size/duration cue or cancel option for large exports

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `runButton` swaps to a bare `ProgressView()` + "Preparing your export…" while `ExportCenterViewModel.run(scope:format:env:)` runs off the main actor specifically because "all time · raw+derived" exports can be large — yet the UI gives no progress percentage, row-count estimate, or way to cancel a long-running export once started.
- **Recommendation:** Add an indeterminate-with-context label (e.g., row count as it streams, if the exporter can report it) and/or a Cancel action that at least stops waiting on the UI side.
- **Why it matters:** A spinner with no bound on duration is a common source of "is this frozen?" anxiety, especially for the export path explicitly designed around potentially large jobs.
- **Expected user impact:** Reduced uncertainty during long export runs.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Export cockpit, `ExportRunner`
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** `ExportRunner` would need to report incremental progress for a true percentage; a row-count-so-far label is achievable without that.
- **Risk if skipped:** Users may force-quit or repeatedly re-tap "Run" believing a long export is stuck.

### UIUX-164 — Error card has no inline retry; user must scroll back up to re-run

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `errorCard(_:)` shows a message (and raw error text in power mode) but offers no "Try again" button — the only way to retry is to scroll back up to `runButton`, which may be off-screen after the error card renders below it.
- **Recommendation:** Add a "Try again" button directly inside `errorCard` that re-invokes `runExport()`.
- **Why it matters:** Recovery from a failed export should be one tap from the point of failure, not a scroll-and-relocate exercise.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster recovery from a failed export attempt.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Export cockpit
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor added friction recovering from an export failure.

### UIUX-165 — Several export detail strings use fixed 12pt monospaced fonts that ignore Dynamic Type

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `errorCard`'s raw message (`.font(.system(size: 12, design: .monospaced))`), `ExportSuccessCard`'s checksum rows, and `manifestDetail`'s id/count rows (lines using `size: 12, design: .monospaced`, four occurrences total) are fixed-size and don't scale with the user's chosen text size, unlike the rest of the screen which uses `BadanFont` tokens.
- **Recommendation:** Use a scalable monospaced style (`Font.system(.caption, design: .monospaced)` or a dedicated `BadanFont` monospaced token) instead of a fixed point size.
- **Why it matters:** Checksums, manifest IDs, and raw error text are exactly the content power users most need to actually read — fixed-size text defeats Dynamic Type for the most technical, high-stakes content on the screen.
- **Expected user impact:** Readable checksums/manifest detail at any text size setting.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Export cockpit, Dynamic Type support
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Dynamic-Type users can't enlarge exactly the content (checksums, error detail) they most need to read closely.

### UIUX-166 — Segmented range/unit labels rely on a thin 0.85 scale factor with no wrap fallback

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ExportSegmented`'s `Text(option.label).lineLimit(1).minimumScaleFactor(0.85)` allows only a 15% shrink before hard-clipping, for labels like "آخر ٩٠ يوماً" (Arabic "Last 90 days") sharing a third of the row's width with two other options.
- **Recommendation:** Increase the scale-factor headroom (e.g., to 0.7) or allow a two-line wrap for longer localized labels instead of clipping.
- **Why it matters:** Arabic numeral/word combinations are frequently longer than their English equivalents; a narrow scale-factor budget risks silent truncation specifically in the app's second first-class language.
- **Expected user impact:** Reliable, non-clipped segmented labels in both languages.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Export cockpit, RTL/localization
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Possible clipped/illegible date-range or unit labels in Arabic.

### UIUX-167 — Share sheet auto-presents the instant an export finishes, burying the success card

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `.onChange(of: vm.lastResult?.job.id)` auto-sets `showShare = true` as soon as a run completes, immediately covering the just-rendered `ExportSuccessCard` (row/file counts, checksums, manifest) with the system share sheet before the user has had a chance to read it.
- **Recommendation:** Don't auto-present the share sheet on completion; let the user read the success card and tap "Share" explicitly (the button already exists on `ExportSuccessCard`).
- **Why it matters:** The success card is deliberately built as a "trust cockpit" surface (checksums, manifest, row counts) — instantly hiding it behind a share sheet undermines that purpose for every single export run.
- **Expected user impact:** Users actually get to see/verify their export details before being pushed into sharing.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Export cockpit
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The carefully designed trust-building success card is functionally invisible on every completed export.
- **First patch sketch:** Remove the `.onChange(of: vm.lastResult?.job.id)` block that auto-sets `shareURLs`/`showShare`, leaving only the explicit `ExportSuccessCard`'s `onShare` closure and `ExportHistoryRow`'s share button to trigger `showShare`.

### UIUX-168 — ShareSheet has no completion handling or confirmation after AirDrop/Files/Mail

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ShareSheet` wraps `UIActivityViewController` with no `completionWithItemsHandler`, so there is no confirmation, toast, or state cleanup after the user actually shares (or cancels) a sensitive export file.
- **Recommendation:** Set `completionWithItemsHandler` and surface a brief "Shared" confirmation (or silently reset `shareURLs`) once the activity completes.
- **Why it matters:** For a privacy-sensitive export (potentially containing medications/symptoms), positive confirmation that a share genuinely completed (vs. was cancelled) is meaningful feedback that's currently entirely absent.
- **Expected user impact:** Clear confirmation after sharing a data export.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ShareSheet.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Export sharing
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** No feedback loop confirming a sensitive-data share actually completed.

### UIUX-169 — ShareSheet has no iPad popover anchor (latent gap given current iPhone-only target)

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ShareSheet.makeUIViewController` constructs `UIActivityViewController` with no `popoverPresentationController.sourceView`/`sourceItem` configured, which `UIActivityViewController` requires on iPad to avoid a silent failure/crash when presented as a popover.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `sourceView`/`sourceRect` (or `sourceItem` on iOS 16+) parameter to `ShareSheet` now, so it's ready if/when `TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY` expands beyond iPhone.
- **Why it matters:** Currently inert since the app targets iPhone only per project config, but it's a one-line latent crash risk that costs little to close off now versus rediscovering it during a future iPad expansion.
- **Expected user impact:** None today; prevents a future regression if iPad support is added.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ShareSheet.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Export sharing (iPad-readiness)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Only manifests if/when iPad support is added later.

### UIUX-170 — Sensitive-data note appears/disappears without animation, unlike the rest of the app's toggle transitions

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `scopeSection`'s `sensitiveNote` renders conditionally (`if scope.includeSensitive { sensitiveNote }`) with no `withAnimation` wrapper, causing an abrupt layout pop when the "Include sensitive" toggle flips, unlike Settings' theme/language changes or Medication's mode toggle which use `.easeInOut`.
- **Recommendation:** Wrap the toggle action (or the conditional view) in `withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.2))`.
- **Why it matters:** This is specifically the note warning about sensitive medication/symptom data leaving the device — an abrupt pop-in draws less deliberate attention than a smooth reveal would for a disclosure this important.
- **Expected user impact:** A calmer, more noticeable reveal of the sensitive-data disclosure.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Export cockpit, motion consistency
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor motion-language inconsistency on an otherwise-important disclosure.

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ExportFormatCard`'s `action` toggles `format` between `.csv`/`.json` with no haptic tap, unlike the light-touch feedback expected on a card-style single-select control.

### UIUX-172 — "On this device — no network" trust badge is only visible once, at the top of a long scroll

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** The offline-trust `PillLabel` in `introCard` is the screen's strongest reassurance signal, but it appears exactly once at the very top; by the time a cautious user scrolls past format, scope (including the "Include sensitive" toggle), date range, and reaches the actual "Run export" button, that reassurance is off-screen.

### UIUX-173 — Casual mode never sees which units an export will use

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `unitSection` (the display-vs-canonical unit choice) is gated `if env.depth.showsPowerDetail`, so casual users never see or choose which units their exported numbers will be in — `scope.unitProfile` silently keeps whatever its default/last-set value is.

- **Why it matters:** Units directly affect how exported numbers should be interpreted; hiding this entirely from casual users (rather than just hiding the *choice*) leaves a real gap in an otherwise transparency-focused export screen.
- **Expected user impact:** Casual users know what units to expect in their exported file without needing power mode.

- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Export cockpit
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Casual users may be surprised by unit values in an exported file they didn't realize they had a choice about.

### UIUX-174 — Past exports can be re-shared but never re-inspected for manifest/checksums

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ExportHistoryRow` only exposes a share icon button (via `availableFileURLs()`); there is no way to tap a history row to see the checksums/manifest detail that `ExportSuccessCard` shows for the most recent run — that detail view is tied exclusively to `vm.lastResult`, a single in-memory value.
- **Recommendation:** Make `ExportHistoryRow` tappable to reconstruct and show an `ExportSuccessCard`-style detail view from the persisted `ExportJob`/manifest, not just from the live in-memory result.
- **Why it matters:** The "trust cockpit" framing (checksums as evidence of integrity) is only available for the export you just ran, not for any of the history the screen otherwise takes care to persist and list.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can verify the integrity of any past export, not only the most recent one.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Export cockpit, export history
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** `ExportJob`/`ExportManifest` model already stores the needed data; requires a detail view decoupled from `vm.lastResult`.
- **Risk if skipped:** Trust/verification value of checksums is effectively limited to the single most recent export.

### UIUX-175 — Checksums list has zero explanatory copy for what a SHA-256 hash is or why it matters

- **Expected user impact:** Power users get to actually understand and use the trust signal the screen is trying to provide.

- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Export cockpit, power-mode detail
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor missed opportunity to reinforce the trust-building purpose of the screen.

### UIUX-176 — Two different single-select visual languages coexist on one screen (segmented pills vs. bordered cards)

- **Problem:** `formatSection` uses bordered `ExportFormatCard`s with a checkmark-circle icon for CSV/JSON selection, while `dateRangeSection`/`unitSection` use `ExportSegmented`'s pill-row style for conceptually identical single-select choices, all within the same screen.

## Settings

### UIUX-177 — "Reset demo data" row looks neutral despite triggering a destructive confirm

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `dataManagementSection`'s "Reset demo data" row uses `BadanColor.info` (informational blue) tint and a plain `arrow.counterclockwise` icon — visually indistinguishable from any harmless settings row — even though tapping it opens a `confirmationDialog` with `role: .destructive` warning it "restores the sample data set" (implying current data is discarded).
- **Recommendation:** Give the row a warning-toned icon/tint at rest (consistent with `sensitiveSection`'s persistent amber warning note above the purge toggle), so its destructive nature is visible before the confirmation dialog even appears.
- **Why it matters:** A row's resting visual weight should hint at its consequence; right now the only warning signal is the confirmation dialog itself, one tap too late for a user scanning the screen.
- **Expected user impact:** Users correctly judge the weight of "Reset demo data" before tapping it.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Settings, destructive-action styling
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users may tap "Reset demo data" without registering it as a meaningfully destructive action.

### UIUX-178 — Sensitive-off warning caption is shown even when sensitive records are already off

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `sensitiveSection`'s inline warning ("Turning this off removes all medication and symptom records from this device") renders unconditionally beneath the toggle, regardless of `env.profile.sensitiveModulesEnabled`'s current state — it's still shown even when the toggle is already off and the warning is no longer actionable.
- **Recommendation:** Only show the warning when the toggle is currently ON (i.e., turning it off is a live, relevant possibility).
- **Why it matters:** A persistent warning about an action that isn't currently available is just noise, and dilutes the warning's impact for when it actually matters.
- **Expected user impact:** Cleaner Settings screen when sensitive records are already disabled.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Settings
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor ongoing noise on an otherwise dense screen.

### UIUX-179 — Home-module toggle rows imply reorderability (a stored `order` field) with no way to actually reorder

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `modulesSection` sorts rows by `module.order` and only exposes a visibility `Toggle` per row — there's no drag handle, no "Edit"/reorder mode, and nothing communicating that the displayed order is fixed from this screen, even though the underlying `HomeModule` model clearly supports an `order` field.
- **Recommendation:** Either add drag-to-reorder (a common iOS pattern for a toggle-list like this) or add a small caption clarifying order isn't editable here (e.g. "Shown in Home screen order").
- **Why it matters:** A list of on/off rows with a visible fixed order is exactly the shape users expect to be drag-reorderable on iOS; the absence of any acknowledgment of that expectation reads as a missing/broken feature rather than a deliberate choice.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer expectations, or an actual reordering capability, for Home screen module layout.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Settings, Home screen module layout
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users attempt to long-press/drag module rows expecting reordering and get no response.

### UIUX-180 — Notification toggles have no explanatory subtitles and no permission-state awareness

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** All four rows in `notificationsSection` (`SettingsToggleRow(title: ..., subtitle: nil, ...)`) pass `subtitle: nil`, unlike sibling toggle rows on the same screen (`arabicDigitsHint`, `sensitiveSubtitle`) that explain themselves; additionally, none of the rows reflect the device's actual system notification-permission state.
- **Recommendation:** Add one-line subtitles describing each notification type, and check/display current OS notification authorization so a toggle that's ON here but blocked at the system level is visibly flagged.
- **Why it matters:** Unexplained toggles are a minor friction; a toggle that appears ON but can never actually deliver anything because iOS notifications are denied is a real trust gap (see UIUX-184 for the deeper version of this issue).
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer, more trustworthy notification settings.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Settings, notifications
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** `UNUserNotificationCenter` authorization status query.
- **Risk if skipped:** Users may believe notifications are configured correctly when the OS is silently blocking them.

### UIUX-181 — Nine flat, undifferentiated sections make Settings feel long with no higher-level grouping

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SettingsScreen.body` stacks `appearanceSection`, `languageSection`, `detailSection`, (power-only) `unitsSection`, `modulesSection`, `notificationsSection`, `sensitiveSection`, `privacySection`, and `dataManagementSection` as one continuous scroll with only plain `SectionHeader` text separating them — no grouping into higher-level categories the way iOS system Settings groups related items (e.g., "Appearance", "Data & Privacy", "Notifications").
- **Recommendation:** Introduce a lightweight visual/structural grouping (extra spacing + grouped headers, or split into "Appearance", "Data", "Privacy & Security" super-sections) to shorten perceived scroll length and aid scanning.
- **Why it matters:** As more settings accumulate (this screen already has 8-9 sections, growing to 9 in power mode), a flat list becomes progressively harder to scan and mentally map.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, less overwhelming navigation of a growing settings surface.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Settings information architecture
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Settings screen becomes progressively harder to scan as more sections are added over time.

### UIUX-182 — SectionHeaders provide no sticky/pinned scanning aid on a long page

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Every section on the Settings screen uses the same plain `SectionHeader` with no sticky/pinned behavior as the user scrolls, and there is no search field despite the screen spanning appearance, language, detail level, units, modules, notifications, sensitive records, privacy, and data management.
- **Recommendation:** Consider pinned section headers (`LazyVStack(pinnedViews: .sectionHeaders)`) so users always know which section they're scrolled into.
- **Why it matters:** On a long, flat settings page, losing track of which section you're in while scrolling makes returning to a specific control slower than necessary.
- **Expected user impact:** Easier orientation while scrolling a long Settings screen.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Settings
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** Related to UIUX-181's broader IA restructuring; best done together.
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor added scroll friction only on the longest configurations of this screen.

### UIUX-183 — `SettingsRadioGroup`'s subtitle support is used for Depth but not for Appearance/Language

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SettingsRadioGroup` accepts an optional `subtitle` closure; `detailSection` (Depth) supplies real explanatory text per option via `SettingsStrings.depthSubtitle(_:)`, but `appearanceSection` (Theme) and `languageSection` (Language) both pass `subtitle: nil` — the same reusable component is used with inconsistent depth of explanation across the same screen.
- **Recommendation:** Add a short subtitle to Theme options (e.g., what "System" does) for parity with how Depth options are explained.
- **Why it matters:** A user picking "System" for Appearance gets no explanation, while a user picking a Depth level gets a full descriptive sentence — an arbitrary difference in how much the app trusts users to already understand a choice.
- **Expected user impact:** More consistently helpful explanations across all radio-style settings choices.

### UIUX-184 — Notification toggles look fully functional despite no notification delivery being implemented

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `notificationsSection` presents four fully interactive, persisted toggles (morning summary, weekly digest, medication reminders, data-paused alerts) that read/write real `NotificationPreference` state via `env.update`, with no visual distinction from any other working toggle on the screen — while the repository has no notification scheduling, background delivery, or local-notification wiring implemented anywhere.
- **Recommendation:** Either wire these to actual scheduled local notifications, or clearly mark this section as "Coming soon" / disable the toggles with an explanatory caption until the underlying capability exists.
- **Why it matters:** Presenting fully-interactive controls for a capability that doesn't functionally exist yet is a trust-eroding pattern — a user who enables "Medication reminders" reasonably expects to receive one and won't.
- **Expected user impact:** Users are never misled into believing reminders/digests are active when they aren't.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Settings, notifications (currently unimplemented per repo)
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** Notification scheduling/delivery implementation, or an explicit product decision to defer/hide this section until it exists.
- **Risk if skipped:** Users believe they'll be reminded about medications or a weekly digest and silently never are — a real trust and (for medication reminders specifically) safety-adjacent expectation gap.

### UIUX-185 — Arabic-digits toggle stays visible and interactive even when it has no visible effect (language = English)

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** The `arabicDigits` `SettingsToggleRow` sits in its own card directly beneath the language radio group but is shown and enabled unconditionally, even when `env.language == .en`, where switching it produces no visible change anywhere in the app.

- **Expected user impact:** Clearer understanding of when/why the Arabic-digits setting applies.

### UIUX-186 — Unrecognized home-module IDs fall back to a non-Arabic label even in Arabic

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `homeModuleLabel(_:)`'s `default` case returns `LocalizedString(en: id.capitalized, ar: id)` — for any module id outside the hardcoded switch (`readiness`, `sleep`, `activity`, `heart`, `meds`, `nutrition`, `timeline`), the Arabic value is literally the raw, un-translated id string.
- **Recommendation:** At minimum use `id.capitalized` for both `en` and `ar` fallbacks (still imperfect, but not silently non-Arabic), and treat any reachable fallback case as a signal to add a real translation.

### UIUX-188 — Purge and Reset confirmations look identical despite very different blast radii

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Both `confirmationDialog`s (sensitive-data purge, demo-data reset) use the same title+destructive-button+cancel structure with no differentiation in visual weight — yet purging permanently deletes an entire on-device database namespace (per this file's own comment, "a real file deletion") while reset merely restores seeded demo data.
- **Recommendation:** Give the higher-consequence purge action a stronger confirmation pattern (e.g., require typing "delete" for purge, or at minimum a distinct icon/tone in the dialog) versus the lower-stakes reset.

- **Expected user impact:** Confirmation friction proportional to actual consequence.

- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None

## Onboarding

### UIUX-190 — Swipe gesture bypasses the "must choose a depth" gate

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `footer`'s "Next" button is `.disabled(step == 2 && selectedDepth == nil)` to force a depth choice before advancing, but the `TabView(selection: $step).tabViewStyle(.page(...))` lets the user physically swipe from the depth page directly to the connect page — swiping isn't gated by the same `disabled` condition, so the forced-choice step can be skipped entirely via a gesture the button-disable logic doesn't cover.
- **Recommendation:** Either disable swipe navigation on the depth step (e.g., via a custom paging control) or apply a default depth silently the moment the user swipes past without choosing, so the two navigation paths (button vs. swipe) enforce the same rule.
- **Why it matters:** The "forced choice" is only enforced on one of two ways to move between onboarding pages, making it a soft gate that a swipe defeats — undermining the deliberate depth-selection step the flow was designed around.
- **Expected user impact:** Consistent, gesture-independent enforcement of the depth-selection step.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding flow
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Some users reach the tab shell having never intentionally chosen casual vs. power depth.

### UIUX-191 — "Connect health data" and "Continue without connecting" are functionally identical buttons

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `connectPage`'s primary button (`Self.connectPrimary`, "Connect health data") and its secondary button (`Loc.continueWithoutConnecting`) both call the exact same `env.completeOnboarding()` — the primary CTA promising a connect action performs no different behavior than skipping it, and per repo facts, real HealthKit reads aren't wired into the iOS UI/sync flow at all yet.
- **Recommendation:** Either wire the primary button to an actual HealthKit permission prompt (via the existing `HealthKitAdapter` boundary) or relabel/restyle it so it doesn't visually promise an action it doesn't perform.
- **Why it matters:** A screen's most prominent, primary-styled button doing nothing different from its secondary "skip" option is a real trust/expectation mismatch on the very first flow a new user experiences.
- **Expected user impact:** Accurate first impression of what BADAN can do on day one; users aren't misled by a "Connect" button that can't actually connect anything.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding, HealthKit integration boundary
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** `Platform/Health/HealthKitAdapter.swift` (exists but per repo facts isn't wired into any UI flow).
- **Risk if skipped:** New users form an inaccurate first impression that health-source connection is available when it currently isn't reachable from onboarding.

### UIUX-192 — Progress dots are entirely hidden from VoiceOver, with no step-count substitute

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `progressDots` is marked `.accessibilityHidden(true)` with no alternative — VoiceOver users get zero "step 2 of 4" announcement anywhere in the onboarding header, unlike the visible capsule indicator sighted users rely on to gauge progress.
- **Recommendation:** Add an `accessibilityLabel`/`accessibilityValue` on the header (or a hidden `Text`) announcing current step and total, e.g. "Step 2 of 4."
- **Why it matters:** Progress orientation is a basic onboarding usability need; hiding it from VoiceOver users entirely, with nothing standing in for it, is a real accessibility gap on the very first screen every user sees.
- **Expected user impact:** VoiceOver users get the same progress orientation sighted users have.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding, VoiceOver/accessibility
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** VoiceOver users have no progress orientation through the entire onboarding flow.

### UIUX-193 — Skip on the depth step silently accepts a default without confirming intent

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Tapping "Skip" on step 2 (depth selection) calls `env.completeOnboarding()` immediately, leaving whatever default `env.depth` already holds (per the `onAppear` comment, likely `.balanced`) with no confirmation that skipping the depth choice was intentional, and no later nudge in Settings pointing out the choice was never made.
- **Recommendation:** Either disable Skip specifically on the depth step (forcing a real choice or an explicit "I'll decide later" acknowledgment), or leave Skip available but surface a one-time hint in Settings the first time a user visits `detailSection` having skipped this step.
- **Why it matters:** "Casual and power are one model, presented differently" is a core product guardrail; letting the very setting that controls this be silently skipped with no follow-up undercuts that design intent.
- **Expected user impact:** Users end up with a depth setting they actually chose (or knowingly deferred), not one silently defaulted.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding, casual/power depth system
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users may be on an unexamined default depth setting indefinitely with no prompt to revisit it.

### UIUX-194 — Welcome/Connect pages have no scroll escape hatch; Value/Depth pages do

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `valuePage` and `depthPage` wrap their content in a `ScrollView`, anticipating overflow, while `welcomePage` and `connectPage` use a fixed `VStack` with `Spacer()`s and no `ScrollView` at all.
- **Recommendation:** Wrap `welcomePage` and `connectPage` in `ScrollView` as well, for consistency and to guard against overflow at larger Dynamic Type sizes or smaller device heights.
- **Why it matters:** At larger accessibility text sizes or on smaller-screen devices, welcome/connect page content (title + subtitle + language toggle, or title + subtitle + two buttons) could overflow vertically with no way to reach content pushed off-screen.
- **Expected user impact:** No clipped/inaccessible content on the two pages currently missing scroll support.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding, Dynamic Type support
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Potential clipped onboarding content for large-text or small-screen users on 2 of the 4 steps.

### UIUX-195 — Hero icon sizes (84pt / 44pt) are hardcoded with no shared token, alongside a separately hardcoded 28pt title font

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `iconMark(_:tint:diameter:)` is called with hardcoded `84` (welcome/connect hero icons) and `44` (value/depth card icons) with no named constant in `Tokens.swift`, and `titleFont` is a locally hardcoded `Font.system(size: 28, ...)` — the file's own comment acknowledges "the token ramp tops out at sectionTitle (20pt)."
- **Recommendation:** Promote the 84/44 icon diameters and the 28pt onboarding title size to named tokens (even if onboarding-scoped) so future screens needing a similar "hero" treatment don't re-invent ad hoc values.
- **Why it matters:** Reinforces the design-system-over-magic-numbers discipline flagged elsewhere in this audit (LogHub, Medication); onboarding is the most visually bespoke screen in the app and currently the least token-governed.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — easier to keep future hero/marketing-style screens visually consistent.

- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS DesignSystem token usage
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile

### UIUX-198 — Back button and Skip button share the same visual weight as unrelated actions (back-navigation vs. flow-exit)

### UIUX-200 — Language toggle buttons rely on `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isSelected)` alone, with no VoiceOver hint of what selecting does

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `languageToggle`'s per-language `Button` adds `.isSelected` trait when active but has no `accessibilityHint` explaining the effect of selection (an immediate live RTL/LTR layout flip and full app re-render) — VoiceOver users get "English, selected, button" with no indication that switching will restructure the entire screen's layout direction.

- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding, VoiceOver/accessibility, RTL
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
