### UIUX-201 — No edge-to-edge / window-insets handling

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MainActivity.kt` never calls `enableEdgeToEdge()`/`WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows`, and no screen applies `WindowInsets` padding; with `targetSdk = 36` (build.gradle) edge-to-edge is enforced by the OS on Android 15+, so content can render under the status/nav bars unpredictably.
- **Recommendation:** Call `enableEdgeToEdge()` in `MainActivity.onCreate` and apply `WindowInsets.safeDrawing` padding at the `Scaffold`/root level in `RootScreen.kt` so every screen reserves space consistently.
- **Why it matters:** Unhandled edge-to-edge is the single most common Android 15 visual regression — top app bars and bottom nav can be obscured or overlapped by system bars.
- **Expected user impact:** Consistent, non-clipped content on all Android 15+ devices instead of device-dependent glitches.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/MainActivity.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/app/RootScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** App shell, all screens
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Visible clipping/overlap bugs on Android 15+ devices, especially the bottom `NavigationBar` and top `TopAppBar`s in detail screens.
- **Implementation notes:** Use `androidx.activity:activity-compose`'s `enableEdgeToEdge()`; add `Modifier.windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.safeDrawing)` around `Scaffold` content in `RootScreen.MainShell`.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `enableEdgeToEdge()` to `MainActivity.onCreate` before `setContent`, then wrap `MainShell`'s `Scaffold` padding to also consume `WindowInsets.safeDrawing`.

### UIUX-202 — No Android 12+ Splash Screen API; hand-rolled Compose splash likely double-flashes

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `RootScreen.kt`'s `SplashScreen()` composable (a `Box` with "BADAN" text + spinner) is the only splash; there is no `androidx.core:core-splashscreen` integration or `windowSplashScreenBackground` in `themes.xml`, so the OS shows its own default splash (icon-less white/black flash) before the Compose splash appears.
- **Recommendation:** Adopt `androidx.core:core-splashscreen`, set `Theme.SplashScreen` attributes in `themes.xml`/`values-night/themes.xml`, and call `installSplashScreen()` in `MainActivity` keyed to `env.isReady`.
- **Why it matters:** A stock system splash immediately followed by a custom Compose splash reads as two separate launches, undermining the calm/first-run polish the rest of the app invests in.
- **Expected user impact:** One seamless branded launch instead of a flash-then-swap.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/MainActivity.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml`, `apps/android/app/src/main/res/values-night/themes.xml`
- **Affected systems:** App launch
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Perceived janky/double launch, especially visible on slower devices.
- **Implementation notes:** `installSplashScreen().setKeepOnScreenCondition { !env.isReady }` removes the need for the manual Compose splash box entirely.
- **First patch sketch:** Add the `core-splashscreen` dependency, define `Theme.SplashScreen` in both theme files, and call `installSplashScreen()` before `setContent` in `MainActivity`.

### UIUX-203 — `themes.xml` still parents a legacy platform Material theme, not Material3

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `apps/android/app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml` and `values-night/themes.xml` parent `android:Theme.Material.Light.NoActionBar` / `android:Theme.Material.NoActionBar` — the pre-AndroidX platform theme, not `Theme.Material3.*` — even though the app is 100% Compose/Material3.
- **Recommendation:** Parent both theme files from a Material3 (or at minimum AppCompat/DayNight) base so window-level attributes (status bar contrast enforcement, `windowLightStatusBar`, edge-to-edge behavior) are consistent with the M3 components Compose renders.
- **Why it matters:** Mismatched theme ancestry can produce inconsistent system-bar icon contrast and ignores the automatic dark-mode status-bar-icon handling M3 themes provide.
- **Expected user impact:** Correct, theme-matched system bar icon color in both light and dark mode.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml`, `apps/android/app/src/main/res/values-night/themes.xml`
- **Affected systems:** App theming
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-201 (edge-to-edge)
- **Risk if skipped:** Status bar icons may not adapt correctly to `BadanColors.background` in one theme mode, producing low-contrast system chrome.
- **Implementation notes:** Switch parent to `Theme.MaterialComponents.DayNight.NoActionBar` or a proper `Theme.Material3.DayNight.NoActionBar` if the AndroidX Material3 XML artifact is added.

### UIUX-204 — System status/navigation bar color never synced to `BadanColors.background`

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Neither `MainActivity.kt` nor `themes.xml` sets the status/navigation bar color to track `BadanColors.background`/`surface`; combined with UIUX-201/203, the system bars can show a stock default color that doesn't match the app's dark-first palette (`Color(0xFF0C0E11)` dark / `Color(0xFFFAFAF8)` light).
- **Recommendation:** Once edge-to-edge is adopted, explicitly set `statusBarColor`/`navigationBarColor` (or transparent + scrim) to the current `BadanColors.background` inside `MainActivity`'s Compose tree via `SideEffect`.
- **Why it matters:** A visible color seam at the top/bottom of the screen breaks the otherwise carefully tuned dark/light palette.
- **Expected user impact:** Seamless full-bleed background matching the app's palette in both themes.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/MainActivity.kt`
- **Affected systems:** App theming
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-201
- **Risk if skipped:** Jarring color mismatch bar at the very edges of the screen in one or both themes.
- **Implementation notes:** Use `SideEffect { window.statusBarColor = colors.background.toArgb() }` scoped to the current `BadanTheme.colors`.

### UIUX-205 — No Material You / dynamic color opt-in

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `Theme.kt`'s `badanLightColors()`/`badanDarkColors()` are fully hardcoded; there is no `dynamicColorScheme`/`dynamicLightColorScheme(context)` path for Android 12+ users who expect wallpaper-derived theming in at least some apps.
- **Recommendation:** This is very likely an intentional brand decision (the mined hex palette is core to BADAN's calm identity) — recommend explicitly documenting the decision in `Theme.kt`'s doc comment rather than changing behavior, since silently deviating from Material You is a legitimate brand choice but should be a stated one for future maintainers/reviewers.
- **Why it matters:** Without a comment, future contributors may "fix" this as a bug, or reviewers may flag it as non-compliant with M3 guidance.
- **Expected user impact:** None directly; this is a maintainability/documentation safeguard for the existing design decision.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/Theme.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Theming
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low; mostly a documentation gap.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a doc comment noting BADAN intentionally uses a fixed brand palette instead of dynamic color to preserve visual identity and wellness-safe status colors.

### UIUX-206 — `NavigationBarItem` icon never swaps between selected/unselected states

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `RootScreen.kt`'s `MainShell` renders `Icon(tab.icon, ...)` with the exact same `ImageVector` regardless of `selected` (line ~87); Material3's expected tab-bar affordance (outlined→filled, or icon swap) is entirely absent, so the only "selected" cue is the label/indicator color.
- **Recommendation:** Provide a selected/unselected icon pair per tab (e.g., outlined vs filled variants of the same Material icon) and switch based on `detail == null && nav.selectedTab == index`.
- **Why it matters:** Icon-state swapping is a standard, expected Android tab-bar cue; its absence makes the bottom nav read as flatter/less polished than stock Android apps.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer, more familiar visual feedback for which tab is active.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/app/RootScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Navigation shell
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor but persistent polish gap on the most-used surface in the app.
- **Implementation notes:** Add an `outlinedIcon`/`filledIcon` pair to the private `Tab` data class in `RootScreen.kt` and select based on the existing `selected` boolean already computed per tab.

### UIUX-207 — Tab switches and detail push/pop render with zero transition

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MainShell`'s `when (nav.selectedTab)` and `DetailContent`'s `when (route)` (`RootScreen.kt`) are both plain, un-animated `when` blocks — every navigation (tab change, `nav.push`/`nav.pop`) hard-cuts the whole screen with no crossfade or slide.
- **Recommendation:** Wrap both `when` blocks in `AnimatedContent`/`Crossfade` with a calm fade or fade+slight-slide transition matching the app's "calm" design language.
- **Why it matters:** Every other piece of the design system (typography, spacing, motion-free but deliberate color language) signals restraint and polish; hard navigation cuts are the most visible remaining "unfinished" feel in the whole app.
- **Expected user impact:** Smoother, more premium-feeling navigation between all five tabs and every pushed detail screen.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/app/RootScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Navigation shell, all screens
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The whole app continues to feel visually static/abrupt during the single most frequent interaction (navigating).
- **Implementation notes:** `AnimatedContent(targetState = nav.selectedTab, transitionSpec = { fadeIn() togetherWith fadeOut() })` around the tab `when`; similarly for `detail` in `Box`.
- **First patch sketch:** Replace the two bare `when` blocks in `RootScreen.kt`'s `MainShell`/`DetailContent` with `AnimatedContent` using a simple `fadeIn()/fadeOut()` spec; verify predictive-back still pops correctly (UIUX-208).

### UIUX-208 — No predictive back gesture support on pushed detail routes

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MainShell`'s `BackHandler(enabled = true) { nav.pop() }` (`RootScreen.kt`) pops immediately on back-press with no interactive preview; Android 14+ (the app targets SDK 36) predictive back expects an in-progress swipe preview of the screen underneath before commit.
- **Recommendation:** Adopt `PredictiveBackHandler` (androidx.activity) to drive an interruptible pop animation/preview instead of the current all-or-nothing `BackHandler`.
- **Why it matters:** Predictive back is now a baseline user expectation on modern Android; its absence is conspicuous compared to any stock system app.
- **Expected user impact:** Users get the familiar "peek behind" back gesture instead of an abrupt pop.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/app/RootScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/app/Navigation.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Navigation shell
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-207
- **Risk if skipped:** Falls behind platform UX conventions as more OEMs enable predictive back by default.
- **Implementation notes:** `PredictiveBackHandler` requires collecting a `Flow<BackEventCompat>` and driving a custom transition; pair with the `AnimatedContent` from UIUX-207.

### UIUX-209 — Inconsistent bottom-sheet dismiss affordances across the app

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricAnatomySheet` (via `MetricDetailScreen.kt`) has an explicit header "Close" `TextButton`; `LogHubScreen.kt`'s Water/Weight quick-add sheets use a `SheetHeader` with "Cancel"; `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `AddMedicationSheetContent` also uses "Cancel" — three different label conventions ("Close" vs "Cancel") for functionally the same dismiss action across `ModalBottomSheet` instances.
- **Recommendation:** Standardize on one dismiss label/pattern (e.g., always "Cancel" for sheets that discard input, "Close" only for read-only sheets like the anatomy sheet) and document the rule.
- **Why it matters:** Inconsistent micro-copy for the same interaction pattern is a small but real coherence gap a careful user will notice across screens.
- **Expected user impact:** More predictable, learnable sheet interactions app-wide.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/metricdetail/MetricAnatomySheet.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/loghub/LogHubScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/medication/MedicationLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Sheets/modals
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor terminology inconsistency; low visibility but persistent.
- **Implementation notes:** The current usage is actually semantically correct (read-only sheet = "Close", input sheets = "Cancel") — worth confirming intent, then documenting rather than reflexively unifying it away.

### UIUX-210 — Stock Material dialogs/pickers visually break from the app's custom design language

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `AlertDialog`/`DatePickerDialog`/`TimePicker` (used in `SymptomLogScreen.kt`, `MedicationLogScreen.kt`, `SettingsScreen.kt`'s `ConfirmDialog`) render with stock Material3 dialog corner radius/elevation/typography, while every other surface in the app uses `BadanCard`'s 20dp-radius, soft-shadow, custom-bordered container — the two visual languages sit side by side whenever a dialog appears.
- **Recommendation:** Apply `shape = RoundedCornerShape(BadanRadius.sheet)` and BadanTheme-derived `containerColor`/`tonalElevation` overrides consistently to every `AlertDialog`/picker call site, or build a thin `BadanDialog` wrapper in the design system.
- **Why it matters:** Dialogs and pickers are moments of heightened user attention (confirmations, data entry) — a jarring style switch there undercuts trust/polish exactly when it matters most.
- **Expected user impact:** Dialogs and pickers feel like part of the same app instead of a bolted-on stock component.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/symptom/SymptomLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/medication/MedicationLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/settings/SettingsScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Dialogs, date/time pickers, settings
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Persistent, repeated "two design systems" feel every time a user confirms a destructive action or picks a date/time.
- **Implementation notes:** A single `BadanDialog(shape = RoundedCornerShape(BadanRadius.sheet), containerColor = BadanTheme.colors.surface) { ... }` wrapper in `designsystem/components/` would let every call site opt in with a one-line change.

### UIUX-211 — Custom `clickable` "buttons" lack Material button semantics for accessibility

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Many hand-rolled buttons (`AnatomyButton`/`MetricDetailScreen.kt`, `ModeButton`/`FilledPrimaryButton`/`MedicationLogScreen.kt`, `PrimaryButton`/`WorkoutLogScreen.kt` & `NutritionLogScreen.kt`, `RunButton`/`ShareButton`/`ExportScreen.kt`) are `Box(...).clickable{}` compositions rather than Material3 `Button`/`OutlinedButton`/`TextButton`, so they don't automatically get `Role.Button` semantics or announce a disabled state to TalkBack.
- **Recommendation:** Add `Modifier.semantics { role = Role.Button }` (and `.clickable(enabled=...)`'s built-in disabled semantics are already correct) to every hand-rolled button composable, or migrate the simplest ones to wrap Material3 `Button` with custom colors/shape.
- **Why it matters:** Screen-reader users currently hear these as generic tappable elements rather than buttons, which is a real accessibility regression across a large fraction of the app's primary actions.
- **Expected user impact:** Correct TalkBack announcements ("Save, button") instead of ambiguous generic-element announcements.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/metricdetail/MetricDetailScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/medication/MedicationLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/WorkoutLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/NutritionLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/export/ExportScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Accessibility, all logging/detail screens
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Ongoing accessibility gap for TalkBack users across most primary CTAs in the app.
- **Implementation notes:** Cheapest fix is a single reusable `Modifier.badanButtonSemantics(enabled: Boolean)` extension applied at each call site.

### UIUX-212 — `values-night/themes.xml` and `values/themes.xml` don't declare `windowLightStatusBar`/`windowLightNavigationBar`

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Neither theme file sets `android:windowLightStatusBar` or `android:windowLightNavigationBar`; combined with UIUX-201/204, system bar icon color (light vs dark icons) is left to OS defaults rather than tracking BADAN's light/dark palette.
- **Recommendation:** Once edge-to-edge (UIUX-201) lands, set these attributes per theme file (`true` in `values/themes.xml`, `false` in `values-night/themes.xml`) or drive icon contrast dynamically via `WindowCompat.getInsetsController`.
- **Why it matters:** Wrong-contrast system icons (e.g., dark icons on BADAN's dark background) are a visible, easily-missed bug that only appears in specific theme/device combinations.
- **Expected user impact:** System status/nav bar icons stay legible against BADAN's background in both themes.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml`, `apps/android/app/src/main/res/values-night/themes.xml`
- **Affected systems:** Theming
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-201
- **Risk if skipped:** Invisible or low-contrast system bar icons on some devices/themes.
- **Implementation notes:** Simple two-line XML addition once edge-to-edge insets are in place.

### UIUX-213 — `MetricChart` has no axis labels or gridlines

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricChart.kt`'s `Canvas` draws only the line/bar series and an optional band tint (lines ~72-121) — there is no time axis (dates) or value axis (scale) drawn anywhere on the chart itself.
- **Recommendation:** Add minimal axis labels (first/last date on the x-axis, min/max value on the y-axis) drawn with `drawText`/`Paint`, styled with `BadanType.caption`.
- **Why it matters:** A chart with no scale is decorative rather than informative — power users especially need to know what date range and value range they're looking at without leaving the chart to check the values table.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can read a metric's trend chart standalone, without cross-referencing the separate values table.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/MetricChart.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Metric detail chart, all metric charts app-wide
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The flagship data-visualization component in the app stays under-informative relative to its prominence.
- **Implementation notes:** Compose `Canvas` supports `drawText` via `drawContext.canvas.nativeCanvas` + `android.graphics.Paint`, or use `TextMeasurer` for a more idiomatic Compose-text approach.

### UIUX-214 — `MetricChart` has no tap/scrub interaction to inspect a value

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricChart.kt`'s `Canvas` has no `pointerInput`/drag-detection; the only way to see an exact value+date is to scroll down to `ValuesTableCard` in `MetricDetailScreen.kt`, which shows just the most recent 14 rows.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `detectTapGestures`/`detectDragGestures` handler that finds the nearest point to the touch x-position and shows a small floating value/date label + a highlighted marker.
- **Why it matters:** Direct manipulation of the chart (tap-to-inspect) is the expected interaction pattern for any health-trend chart and is currently entirely missing.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can inspect any point on the trend line directly, not just the last 14 table rows.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/MetricChart.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/metricdetail/MetricDetailScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Metric detail chart
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-213 (shared touch-target/label rendering work)
- **Risk if skipped:** Chart stays a passive illustration rather than an inspectable data surface, undercutting the app's "power" altitude promise.
- **Implementation notes:** Reuse the existing `xFor`/`yFor` closures in `MetricChart`; nearest-point lookup is a simple binary/linear search over `series`.

### UIUX-215 — Personal-band shading has no legend distinguishing it from the plotted series

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ChartCard` (`MetricDetailScreen.kt`) draws the personal band as a soft `colors.inBand.copy(alpha = 0.10f)` rectangle behind the line with zero labeling — a first-time user has no way to know the tinted region represents their personal typical range.
- **Recommendation:** Add a one-line caption under the chart (e.g., "Shaded area = your usual range") shown at least once, or a tiny inline legend swatch + label.
- **Why it matters:** The personal band is one of BADAN's core differentiators (a wellness-safe alternative to red/green scoring); if users don't know what the tint means, that design investment is wasted.
- **Expected user impact:** Users correctly interpret the shaded band as their personal range rather than an unexplained visual artifact.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/metricdetail/MetricDetailScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Metric detail chart
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A core wellness-safe design idea (the personal band) goes unexplained and easily misread as decoration.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a small `Text` caption below `MetricChart` in `ChartCard`, gated to show only when `data.baseline` is non-null and non-provisional.
- **First patch sketch:** In `MetricDetailScreen.kt`'s `ChartCard`, add a `Text(style = BadanType.caption)` line beneath the `MetricChart` call reading a localized "Shaded area = your usual range" string, visible whenever `data.baseline?.provisional == false`.

### UIUX-216 — `MetricChart`/`MetricSparkline` are fully inaccessible to screen readers

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Neither `Canvas` in `MetricChart.kt` has any `Modifier.semantics{}`/`contentDescription` — a TalkBack user focusing the chart region hears nothing describing the trend, range, or values.
- **Recommendation:** Add `Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "..." }` summarizing the series (e.g., "Resting heart rate, 30-day trend, from 58 to 64 bpm") computed from the already-available `series`/`band` data.
- **Why it matters:** Charts are one of the richest data surfaces in the app; leaving them silent for screen-reader users is a significant accessibility gap.
- **Expected user impact:** TalkBack users get a meaningful spoken summary of every chart and sparkline in the app.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/MetricChart.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Accessibility, all metric charts
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every chart in the app (Home cards, Body pillars, Metric detail) remains a screen-reader dead zone.
- **Implementation notes:** Compute a short summary string from `series.first()`/`series.last()`/`values.min()`/`values.max()` and attach via `semantics`.

### UIUX-217 — Empty-series `MetricChart` renders a silent blank Canvas

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricChart.kt` lines 43-46 early-return an empty, unlabeled `Canvas` when `series.isEmpty()` — if this happens while the surrounding `MetricDetailData` is otherwise non-empty (e.g., the selected 7/30/90-day period window has no points even though the metric has older history), the user sees a mysteriously blank rectangle with no explanation.
- **Recommendation:** Render a small "No data in this period" caption inside the chart's bounds when `series` is empty, rather than a bare blank Canvas.
- **Why it matters:** `MetricDetailScreen`'s outer `LoadState.Empty` only triggers when the *entire* metric has no data, not when just the selected period window is empty — this specific blank-chart case currently has no messaging at all.
- **Expected user impact:** Users understand immediately why the chart appears empty instead of assuming a bug.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/MetricChart.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Metric detail chart
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Confusing blank UI whenever a user picks a period (e.g., "7") shorter than the metric's actual data cadence.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a `Text`/`Box` fallback (or a `contentDescription`-only path) inside `MetricChart` gated on `series.isEmpty()`.
- **First patch sketch:** Replace the bare `Canvas(modifier = chartModifier) {}` early return in `MetricChart.kt` (lines 43-46) with a `Box(chartModifier, contentAlignment = Alignment.Center) { Text(...) }` showing a localized "No data in this period" caption.

### UIUX-218 — Bar-chart mode has no minimum bar width for long periods

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricChart.kt`'s `ChartStyle.Bar` branch computes `slot = w / series.size` and `barW = slot * 0.6f` with no floor — for a 90-day bar-style metric (`ChartHint.BAR`) this can produce sub-2px bars that are visually indistinguishable from each other or from empty space.
- **Recommendation:** Clamp `barW` to a sensible minimum (e.g., 2.dp in px) and, below that density, either aggregate bars (weekly rollup) or fall back to a line rendering.
- **Why it matters:** Bar-style metrics become unreadable exactly when there's the most data to show (the 90-day power view), the opposite of what a power user needs.
- **Expected user impact:** Bar charts stay legible across all supported period lengths.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/MetricChart.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Metric detail chart (bar-style metrics)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Bar-style metrics (e.g., step counts) look broken/empty at the 90-day period.
- **Implementation notes:** `val barW = (slot * 0.6f).coerceAtLeast(2.dp.toPx())`; consider period-aware downsampling for very long windows.

### UIUX-219 — Casual-mode chart window (30 days) is never disclosed to the user

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricDetailScreen.kt`'s `MetricDetailContent` hardcodes `val chartDays = if (power) periodDays else 30` — casual users never see the `PeriodSelector` (power-only) and have no other on-screen indication that the chart is scoped to "last 30 days."
- **Recommendation:** Show a small, always-visible caption (e.g., "Last 30 days") above or below the chart in casual mode too, reusing the existing `MetricDetailStrings.period`/day-count formatting.
- **Why it matters:** A trend chart without a stated time window is ambiguous — is this "recently," "all time," or something else? Casual users get no cue.
- **Expected user impact:** Casual users understand the chart's time scope without needing to switch to power mode.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/metricdetail/MetricDetailScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Metric detail (casual altitude)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Ambiguous chart context for the majority (casual) user base.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a small caption in `ChartCard`'s `SectionHeader` trailing slot when `!power`, mirroring the "Trend" title with a "· Last 30 days" suffix.
- **First patch sketch:** In `MetricDetailScreen.kt`'s `ChartCard`, add a trailing caption to the existing `SectionHeader(title = env.s(MetricDetailStrings.trend), ...)` reading a localized "Last 30 days" string whenever the caller is in casual mode.

### UIUX-220 — `ValuesTableCard` silently caps at 14 rows regardless of the selected period

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ValuesTableCard` in `MetricDetailScreen.kt` (`points.reversed().take(14)`) always shows at most 14 rows with no pagination, "see more," or count indicator — selecting a 90-day period in `PeriodSelector` still only ever surfaces the newest 14 entries in the table.
- **Recommendation:** Add a row count summary ("Showing 14 of 62") or paginate/expand the table so the selected period is actually browsable, not just chart-visible.
- **Why it matters:** Power users who explicitly select "90" days to see more history get a table that silently ignores 48 of those days.
- **Expected user impact:** The values table honestly reflects (or clearly caveats) the selected period.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/metricdetail/MetricDetailScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Metric detail (power altitude)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Power users may not realize the table is truncated and misread it as "there's only 14 days of data."
- **Implementation notes:** At minimum, add a `SectionHeader` trailing count like "14 of {points.size}"; a full fix would lazily page the list.

### UIUX-221 — `BadanCard`'s shadow is not dark-theme aware

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `Card.kt`'s `BadanCard` always applies `.shadow(elevation = 6.dp, shape = shape, clip = false)` regardless of `BadanTheme.colors.isDark`; Android's default drop-shadow rendering (a soft dark blur) reads as a faint, slightly muddy halo rather than a true shadow once the background is already near-black (`Color(0xFF0C0E11)`).
- **Recommendation:** In dark mode, replace or supplement the drop shadow with Material's tonal-elevation approach (a slightly lighter `surfaceElevated`-derived fill) rather than relying on a shadow that has almost nothing to contrast against.
- **Why it matters:** Material Design's own dark-theme guidance recommends tonal elevation over shadows for exactly this reason; the current approach can look like a rendering artifact rather than an intentional elevation cue.
- **Expected user impact:** Cards read as clearly "raised" in dark mode instead of having an ambiguous, low-contrast edge.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/Card.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Every card in the app (dark mode)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Subtly muddy card edges in dark mode across the entire app, the app's default/primary theme per Tokens.kt's "dark-first" doc comment.
- **Implementation notes:** Branch on `colors.isDark` inside `BadanCard` to use `colors.surfaceElevated` as the card background with little/no shadow, vs. `colors.surface` + shadow in light mode.

### UIUX-222 — Status pill/chip backgrounds use fixed low alpha that may not meet contrast minimums

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `StatusChip.kt`, `Pills.kt` (`PillLabel`), and their many call sites all use `tint.copy(alpha = 0.12f–0.14f)` as a background with the same full-opacity `tint` as the text/icon color — this pattern is repeated for every status chip, provisional badge, and label pill across the app, and has not been verified against WCAG contrast minimums for text-on-tinted-background in either theme.
- **Recommendation:** Audit the rendered text/background contrast ratio for each `BadanColors` tint (primary/inBand/outOfBand/info) at the standard 0.12–0.14 alpha in both light and dark mode, and raise the alpha or add a subtle border where ratios fall short of WCAG AA (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large/bold).
- **Why it matters:** This single pattern is reused dozens of times (every `StatusChip`, `PillLabel`, `DepthBadge`, `ProvisionalBadge` call site app-wide), so a contrast shortfall here has the widest possible blast radius of any single design-system fix.
- **Expected user impact:** Reliably legible status/label chips for low-vision users across the entire app.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/StatusChip.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/Pills.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Design system tokens, every screen using status chips/pills
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A single contrast defect silently propagates to the most-used status-communication pattern in the entire app.
- **Implementation notes:** Since text color is always the un-alpha'd `tint`, the actual risk is background-vs-surface contrast for chip *boundaries*, not text legibility (text sits at full opacity) — verify with a contrast checker against both `colors.surface`/`colors.background` per theme; consider this a verification/audit task, not a blind alpha bump.
- **First patch sketch:** Run each `BadanColors` tint at 0.12–0.14 alpha over both `badanLightColors().surface` and `badanDarkColors().surface` through a contrast checker; bump the alpha constants in `StatusChip.kt`/`Pills.kt` only where a ratio fails.

### UIUX-223 — "On-primary" text/icon color is independently re-derived in at least four places

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** There is no `BadanColors.onPrimary` token; instead, `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `ActionRow` computes `if (colors.isDark) colors.background else Color.White`, `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `FilledPrimaryButton` repeats the identical expression, `WorkoutLogScreen.kt`/`NutritionLogScreen.kt`'s `PrimaryButton` just hardcodes `Color.White` (no dark-mode branch), and `OnboardingScreen.kt`'s `PrimaryButton` uses yet a third bespoke value, `Color(0xFF08201D)`.
- **Recommendation:** Add a single `onPrimary: Color` field to `BadanColors` (computed once in `badanLightColors()`/`badanDarkColors()`) and replace all four ad-hoc derivations with it.
- **Why it matters:** `WorkoutLogScreen`/`NutritionLogScreen`'s hardcoded `Color.White` on primary in dark mode uses a *different* on-primary treatment than `MedicationLogScreen`'s dark-aware version, and neither matches Onboarding's bespoke hex — meaning the same "filled primary button" pattern can render with two or three different text-color behaviors depending on which screen you're on.
- **Expected user impact:** Consistent, correctly-contrasted button text everywhere the primary color is used as a fill.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/Tokens.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/medication/MedicationLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/WorkoutLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/NutritionLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/onboarding/OnboardingScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Design system tokens, all primary buttons
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** `WorkoutLogScreen`/`NutritionLogScreen`'s plain `Color.White` primary buttons likely have degraded contrast in dark mode against the lighter dark-mode `primary` teal (`0xFF5BC5BA`), unlike the other three call sites which already branch on `isDark`.
- **Implementation notes:** Add `onPrimary` to the `BadanColors` data class; light = `Color.White`, dark = a near-black tuned against `0xFF5BC5BA` (reuse Onboarding's already-tuned `0xFF08201D)`.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `val onPrimary: Color` to `BadanColors` in `Tokens.kt`, populate it in both palette factories, then replace the four independent `if (colors.isDark) ... else ...` expressions with `colors.onPrimary`.

### UIUX-224 — `AdherenceDot`'s "skipped" and "none" states are hard to distinguish at 11dp

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `AdherenceDot` renders `SKIPPED` as a bare 1.5dp `textSecondary` border with no fill and `NONE` as a `colors.separator.copy(alpha = 0.5f)` fill with no border — at an 11dp circle size, an unfilled outline vs. a very-low-alpha fill are difficult to tell apart at a glance, especially in dark mode where `separator` (`0xFF252A31`) is close to `background` (`0xFF0C0E11`).
- **Recommendation:** Increase the visual distinction — e.g., keep `SKIPPED` as an outline but with a stronger stroke color, and give `NONE` a fully transparent/no-render treatment (an empty slot) instead of a barely-visible fill.
- **Why it matters:** The 7-day adherence strip is the primary at-a-glance adherence summary in the whole medication feature; if two of its four states are visually confusable, the summary loses its point.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer at-a-glance read of the weekly adherence pattern.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/medication/MedicationLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Medication log
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users may misread "no dose scheduled that day" as "skipped," which is a meaningfully different (and more judgment-laden) state for a feature explicitly designed to be non-punitive.
- **Implementation notes:** Simplest fix: render `DotKind.NONE` as fully transparent (`Color.Transparent`) so it visually recedes rather than competing with `SKIPPED`'s outline.
- **First patch sketch:** In `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `AdherenceDot`, change the `DotKind.NONE` branch from `base.background(colors.separator.copy(alpha = 0.5f))` to `base.background(Color.Transparent)` (or a border-only treatment distinct from `SKIPPED`'s).

### UIUX-225 — `HealthConnectCard` distinguishes success/warning messages by color alone

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `HealthConnectCard.kt`'s `BodyText` renders both the informational "Connected — no data found yet" message and the softer-warning "Permission wasn't granted" message with identical `BadanType.bodyCompact` styling, differing only by `colors.textSecondary` vs. `colors.outOfBand` (lines ~132-138) — no icon differentiates the two message types the way `StatusChip` pairs every color with an icon+text.
- **Recommendation:** Apply the same icon+color pairing convention `StatusChip` already establishes elsewhere in the app (e.g., an info icon for neutral messages, a small amber icon for the denied-permission message) instead of relying on text color alone.
- **Why it matters:** The app is otherwise disciplined about never using color as the sole signal (see `StatusChip`'s doc comment); this card is an inconsistent exception to that stated principle.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer differentiation between "everything's fine, just no data yet" and "you need to take an action" states.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/HealthConnectCard.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Sources screen, Health Connect onboarding
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor color-blind accessibility gap and a small inconsistency with the app's own stated design principle.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a small leading `Icon` to `BodyText` calls that pass `colors.outOfBand`, reusing `Icons.Filled.Info`/`Icons.Filled.WarningAmber` already imported elsewhere in the codebase.

### UIUX-226 — `ProvenanceRow` has no overflow guard for long source names/labels

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `Provenance.kt`'s `ProvenanceRow` renders `sourceName` and `ingestionPath.displayLabel` as plain `Text` with no `maxLines`/`overflow` (lines ~53-63); a long device/source name (or a longer Arabic ingestion-path label) can wrap the fixed three-column row (icon, source, path, timestamp) onto multiple lines, breaking the row's intended single-line alignment.
- **Recommendation:** Add `maxLines = 1, overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis` to both `Text` calls, matching the ellipsis pattern already used elsewhere (`HomeScreen.kt`'s `TimelinePreviewCard`).
- **Why it matters:** Provenance rows appear throughout the power-altitude UI (`MetricDetailScreen`, `WorkoutLogScreen`) and are exactly the kind of place where Arabic strings tend to run longer than their English counterparts, making this a real RTL/localization robustness gap, not just a hypothetical one.
- **Expected user impact:** Provenance rows stay tidy single lines regardless of source-name length or language.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/Provenance.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Metric detail, Workout log (power altitude)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Layout breakage on long device/source names, more likely in Arabic.
- **Implementation notes:** Straightforward `Modifier`/parameter addition to the two `Text` calls in `ProvenanceRow`.
- **First patch sketch:** In `Provenance.kt`'s `ProvenanceRow`, add `maxLines = 1` and `overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis` to the `sourceName` and `ingestionPath.displayLabel` `Text` composables.

### UIUX-227 — Fixed 96dp Back/Skip tap zones in onboarding risk clipping longer translations

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `OnboardingScreen.kt`'s `OnboardingHeader` hardcodes `Modifier.size(width = 96.dp, height = BadanSpace.touchMin)` for both the Back and Skip controls (lines ~199-226); current EN/AR strings ("Back"/"رجوع", "Skip"/"تخطي") happen to fit, but the fixed width has no `wrapContentWidth` fallback if a string grows (e.g., a future retranslation or a different locale added later).
- **Recommendation:** Replace the fixed 96dp width with `Modifier.heightIn(min = BadanSpace.touchMin).wrapContentWidth()` plus a minimum-width floor only for touch-target purposes, not text containment.
- **Why it matters:** BADAN's stated Arabic/RTL-first-order priority means text-length fragility should be designed out proactively, not discovered after a string change ships.
- **Expected user impact:** Onboarding header controls remain robust to future copy changes in any language.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/onboarding/OnboardingScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Onboarding
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low today, but a latent localization-robustness bug that could clip text silently later.
- **Implementation notes:** Swap the `size(width = 96.dp, ...)` for `heightIn(min = BadanSpace.touchMin)` + `padding(horizontal = BadanSpace.s2)`, letting content size the width naturally.

### UIUX-228 — No RTL screenshot evidence for any logging/detail/settings screen

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `docs/screenshots/android/` contains exactly one Arabic/RTL screenshot (`02-home-arabic-rtl.png`) out of five total images; none of Metric Detail, Timeline, Symptom/Medication/Workout/Nutrition logging, Export, Insights, Onboarding, or Settings has ever been captured in Arabic/RTL, despite the project explicitly stating "Arabic/RTL readiness is a first-order concern" in `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Recommendation:** Capture RTL screenshots for at least Metric Detail (chart + values table), one logging form (e.g., Symptom), Export, and Settings, and add them to `docs/screenshots/android/`.
- **Why it matters:** Every RTL-specific bug found in this audit (e.g., UIUX-226, UIUX-227) was found by code reading, not by looking at an actual rendered RTL screen — the project has no visual evidence any of its power/logging screens actually mirror correctly.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — enables catching real RTL layout bugs before Arabic-speaking users do.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `docs/screenshots/android/` (new files), `docs/android-parity-status.md`
- **Affected systems:** QA/documentation
- **Suggested owner:** QA
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** RTL regressions in the majority of the app's screens go undetected until real Arabic-speaking users hit them.
- **Implementation notes:** Use the existing `badan_route` deep-link extras already wired in `MainActivity.kt` to jump directly to Sources/Export/Timeline for fast repeatable screenshot capture.

### UIUX-229 — Mixed Gregorian-weekday + digit direction in Timeline day headers is unverified under RTL

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `TimelineScreen.kt`'s `formattedDate` uses `android.text.format.DateFormat.getBestDateTimePattern(locale, "EEEEdMMM")` combined with `SimpleDateFormat` — this can interleave Arabic weekday/month names with Latin-script fragments and Arabic-Indic digits (if `arabicDigits` is on) in a single bidi run, which is exactly the kind of string that most often breaks visually under RTL without device testing.
- **Recommendation:** Verify actual rendering with an RTL + Arabic-digits screenshot (see UIUX-228) and, if broken, wrap the formatted string in explicit bidi isolation (`⁨...⁩`) or use `android.icu.text.DateFormat` which handles this more robustly than `java.text.SimpleDateFormat`.
- **Why it matters:** Date headers appear at the top of every Timeline day-group and are one of the most-read strings on the screen; a bidi rendering glitch there is highly visible.
- **Expected user impact:** Correctly-ordered, readable date headers in Arabic with Arabic-Indic digits enabled.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/timeline/TimelineScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Timeline (RTL + Arabic-digits combination)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-228 (screenshot evidence to confirm/deny)
- **Risk if skipped:** Potentially garbled date headers for Arabic users who also enable Arabic-Indic digits — an intersection of two first-class supported features that may not have been jointly tested.
- **Implementation notes:** This is a verify-then-fix item; the recommendation is contingent on what an actual RTL+Arabic-digits screenshot reveals.

### UIUX-230 — Per-screen number-field `unit`-after-value layout is unverified for RTL mirroring

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `WorkoutLogScreen.kt`'s and `NutritionLogScreen.kt`'s `NumberField` places the `unit` `Text` (e.g., "kcal", "km") as the last element in a `Row` after the input `Box`; Compose auto-mirrors `Row` layout direction under RTL, but this specific compound "icon → field → unit" pattern has no RTL screenshot to confirm the unit visually ends up on the correct (now-leading, in RTL) side without also mirroring the numerals themselves oddly.
- **Recommendation:** Capture Arabic screenshots of Workout and Nutrition logging screens (covered by UIUX-228) specifically checking this row.
- **Why it matters:** Numeric input rows combining LTR-biased numerals with RTL-mirrored layout are a classic source of subtle but jarring bugs (e.g., "kcal 450" reading backwards).
- **Expected user impact:** Confirms (or surfaces a fix for) correct numeral+unit presentation in Arabic.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/WorkoutLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/NutritionLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Workout/Nutrition logging (RTL)
- **Suggested owner:** QA
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-228
- **Risk if skipped:** Unknown until verified; low effort to check.
- **Implementation notes:** Verification-first item; no code change recommended until confirmed broken.

### UIUX-231 — `HomeHeader` greeting text has no overflow guard against long localized strings

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `HomeScreen.kt`'s `HomeHeader` renders `env.s(env.greeting)` with `BadanType.sectionTitle` and no `maxLines`/`overflow`, next to a fixed-size `DepthBadge` pinned via `Alignment.Top` in the same `Row` — a longer greeting string (a personalized or Arabic variant) has no truncation fallback and could push into or wrap awkwardly against the badge.
