- **Why it matters:** "Data-paused reminders" in particular is not self-explanatory from its label alone, and the fix is a same-file, same-pattern, low-effort addition.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer understanding of exactly what each notification toggle does before enabling it.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/settings/SettingsScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Settings
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor discoverability gap for less-obvious notification types.
- **Implementation notes:** Add four short bilingual `LocalizedString` subtitles to `SettingsStrings` and pass them into the existing `SettingsToggleRow` calls in `NotificationsSection`.
- **First patch sketch:** Add four new `LocalizedString` subtitle constants to `SettingsScreen.kt`'s `SettingsStrings` object and pass them as the `subtitle` argument to the four `SettingsToggleRow` calls inside `NotificationsSection`.

### UIUX-255 — Destructive "Reset demo data" row carries the same visual weight as informational rows

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SettingsScreen.kt`'s `DataManagementSection` renders "Reset demo data" as a plain `BadanCard` row with a neutral `colors.info`-tinted icon (`RestartAlt`) — visually identical in weight/prominence to the informational `PrivacySection` rows above it — even though tapping it opens a confirm dialog whose confirm button is tinted `colors.critical`, implicitly acknowledging the action is meaningfully destructive.
- **Recommendation:** Give the entry point itself a visual cue proportionate to its confirmed destructiveness (e.g., the same inline `WarningAmber` icon pattern the adjacent `SensitiveSection` already uses for its purge note), rather than only revealing the severity after the tap.
- **Why it matters:** The `SensitiveSection` right above it already demonstrates the correct pattern (an inline warning icon *before* the destructive toggle is even touched); `DataManagementSection` doesn't follow its own neighbor's precedent.
- **Expected user impact:** Users get a proportionate visual cue about an action's consequences before committing to open the confirm dialog.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/settings/SettingsScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Settings (data management)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor; the confirm dialog itself still gates the action, but the entry point undersells its consequence.
- **Implementation notes:** Reuse the exact inline warning-icon-plus-caption pattern already implemented two sections above in the same file's `SensitiveSection`.

### UIUX-256 — `MetricGrid`'s odd-row fallback leaves an empty half-width gap instead of matching the last card's width

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `HomeScreen.kt`'s `MetricGrid` chunks metrics into rows of 2 and, for a trailing single-item row, adds `Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))` (line ~371) to fill the other half — this produces a visually asymmetric card floating on one side rather than a balanced layout.
- **Recommendation:** Either let the last odd card span the full row width (`weight(2f)` or `fillMaxWidth()` for a lone trailing item) or switch to a proper `LazyVerticalGrid` with `Arrangement` that handles this natively.
- **Why it matters:** With exactly 4 candidate power metrics (`restingHeartRate, hrv, steps, activeEnergy`) in `loadMetrics`, an odd count is actually the *common* case whenever one metric has no recent data, not a rare edge case.
- **Expected user impact:** A more balanced, intentional-looking grid layout on the Home tab's power altitude.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/home/HomeScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Home tab (power altitude)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor cosmetic asymmetry that's actually reasonably likely to occur given the metric set size.
- **Implementation notes:** Simplest fix: when `row.size == 1`, render that lone `MetricGridCell` with `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` instead of half-width + spacer.
- **First patch sketch:** In `HomeScreen.kt`'s `MetricGrid`, change the `if (row.size == 1) Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))` branch to instead render the lone cell without the `Modifier.weight(1f)` Box wrapper, letting it span the full row width.

### UIUX-257 — `BodyAllMetricsBrowser` composes its full result list eagerly inside one `verticalScroll` Column

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `BodyScreen.kt`'s `BodyAllMetricsBrowser`, once expanded, renders every matching metric row (up to the full 44-metric registry per `packages/metric-ontology/registry.json`) directly inside the screen's single `verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())` `Column` rather than a `LazyColumn` — all rows compose and measure immediately regardless of visibility.
- **Recommendation:** Convert the expanded browser results into a `LazyColumn` (or nest it in a fixed-height scrollable region) so off-screen metric rows aren't composed until scrolled into view.
- **Why it matters:** This is a visible-jank concern as much as a raw performance one — expanding "All metrics" on a mid-range device can produce a visible frame hitch exactly at the moment a user taps to expand, undermining the calm feel the rest of the screen maintains.
- **Expected user impact:** Smoother expand/scroll interaction when browsing the full metric catalog.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/BodyScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Body screen (all-metrics browser)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A visible stutter on mid/low-end devices at the exact moment of the "browse everything" interaction, the feature explicitly designed to make the full raw catalog accessible (a stated product guardrail: "raw data is not paywalled").
- **Implementation notes:** Since the whole screen is already a single `verticalScroll` Column, converting just this nested section requires either `LazyColumn` inside a fixed-height container or restructuring the outer screen itself to be one `LazyColumn`.

### UIUX-258 — Log-hub tiles look identical whether they open a full-screen editor or a compact sheet

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `LogHubScreen.kt`'s `LogTile` composable is used identically for both the four `nav.push(...)`-based full-screen log editors (Symptom, Medication, Workout, Nutrition) and the two `activeSheet = LogSheet...`-based compact bottom sheets (Water, Weight) — there is no visual cue distinguishing "this opens a full screen" from "this opens a quick sheet."
- **Recommendation:** Add a small secondary visual cue (e.g., a tiny sheet-vs-chevron glyph, or grouping quick-add tiles with a subtly different tile treatment) so users can predict the weight of the interaction before tapping.
- **Why it matters:** The screen already visually separates these into two `SectionHeader`-grouped rows ("Log" vs. "Quick add"), which does most of the communicative work — this finding is a smaller polish layer on top of that existing (good) grouping.
- **Expected user impact:** Slightly better expectation-setting before tapping a tile.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/loghub/LogHubScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Log hub
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Very low; the existing section grouping already communicates most of this.
- **Implementation notes:** Lowest priority in this batch; the existing "Log" vs. "Quick add" section headers already largely solve the underlying problem.

### UIUX-259 — Medication Take/Skip button pair can become excessively wide on large-screen devices

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `ActionRow` gives both the "Take" and "Skip" buttons `Modifier.weight(1f)` with no `widthIn`/max-width cap — on a tablet or large-screen foldable, this stretches each button to potentially several hundred dp wide with the label centered in a mostly-empty pill.
- **Recommendation:** Cap button width (e.g., `widthIn(max = 220.dp)`) and center the pair within the available row width on larger screens, rather than always stretching to fill.
- **Why it matters:** While the app appears phone-first (no explicit tablet layouts found in scope), Android devices span a wide range of widths and a full-bleed-stretched button pair reads as unfinished on anything larger than a typical phone.
- **Expected user impact:** More proportionate button sizing on larger Android devices.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/medication/MedicationLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Cosmetic-only issue confined to large-screen/tablet form factors, which the app doesn't appear to specifically target yet.
- **Implementation notes:** A broader "does BADAN support large-screen Android layouts at all" question likely belongs in a separate, larger-scoped item — this one just notes the most visible instance of the underlying gap.

### UIUX-260 — `DueSlotCard`'s `SkipReasonPicker` collapses instantly with no exit transition

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `SkipReasonPicker` (revealed when `skippingSlotId == slot.id`) disappears the instant a reason chip is tapped (`onSkip` triggers a state reset that collapses `showActions`), with no `AnimatedVisibility`/fade-out — the whole reason-picker row and its chips vanish in a single frame.
- **Recommendation:** Wrap the picker's appearance/disappearance in `AnimatedVisibility` with a brief fade/expand-collapse, consistent with treating this as a considered, non-punitive interaction rather than an abrupt one.
- **Why it matters:** The skip flow is explicitly designed to feel calm and low-pressure ("No problem — pick a reason if you'd like"); an instant snap-away undercuts that tone at the exact moment the user completes the action.
- **Expected user impact:** A calmer, less jarring transition when completing a skip.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/medication/MedicationLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-207 (broader motion-polish effort)
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor tonal mismatch between the calm copy and the abrupt visual transition.
- **Implementation notes:** Wrap the `if (showActions) { ... }` block's `SkipReasonPicker`/`ActionRow` swap in `AnimatedContent` or `AnimatedVisibility`.

### UIUX-261 — Icons.kt's fallback glyph is visually identical to a real, meaningful icon elsewhere

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `Icons.kt`'s `iconForKey` falls back to `Icons.Filled.Circle` for any unmapped `symbolName` (line 74); separately, `SourcesScreen.kt`'s `deviceIcon` uses that exact same `Icons.Filled.Circle` to represent a real "ring"-type wearable device (line ~430) — a genuinely unmapped/mistyped icon key is now visually indistinguishable from a correctly-rendered ring-device icon.
- **Recommendation:** Reserve a distinct, obviously-neutral glyph for the fallback case (e.g., `Icons.Filled.HelpOutline` or `Icons.Filled.QuestionMark`) so an icon-mapping gap is visually diagnosable rather than silently masquerading as valid content.
- **Why it matters:** Icons.kt's own doc comment states "Unknown keys fall back to a neutral dot so nothing ever renders blank" — but "neutral" currently collides with a real, intentional use of the same glyph elsewhere in the app, defeating the fallback's own diagnostic value.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — helps developers/QA spot broken icon mappings during development rather than shipping a silently-wrong-looking icon.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/Icons.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/SourcesScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Icon mapping (design system)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Icon-mapping bugs (a typo'd `symbolName`) stay invisible because the fallback looks like valid content.
- **Implementation notes:** Swap the fallback in `iconForKey`'s `else` branch from `Icons.Filled.Circle` to a distinguishable placeholder glyph.
- **First patch sketch:** In `Icons.kt`'s `iconForKey`, change the `else -> Icons.Filled.Circle` fallback to `Icons.Filled.HelpOutline` (or similar), which is not used anywhere else in the icon map today.

### UIUX-262 — All app iconography uses the same `Filled` weight with no hierarchy

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Every icon import across the app (`Icons.kt`, and every screen's local icon imports) uses `androidx.compose.material.icons.filled.*` exclusively — there is no use of `Icons.Outlined.*`/`Icons.Rounded.*` anywhere, so primary actions, secondary/decorative icons, and navigation icons are all rendered at the same visual weight.
- **Recommendation:** Introduce outlined-vs-filled distinction at least for the one place it matters most for affordance clarity — tab bar selection state (see UIUX-206) — and consider it more broadly for primary vs. secondary icon usage in cards.
- **Why it matters:** Material Design's icon system deliberately uses weight variation to communicate state/hierarchy (this is exactly how stock Android apps signal "selected" in bottom nav); BADAN's single-weight approach forfeits that entire signal channel.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer visual hierarchy between primary and secondary icon usage app-wide.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/Icons.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/app/RootScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Iconography (design system-wide)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-206 (most concrete near-term application of this)
- **Risk if skipped:** A flatter overall visual hierarchy than a typical Material3 app; most acute in the bottom tab bar (UIUX-206).
- **Implementation notes:** This is a larger design-system investment; treat UIUX-206 (tab bar specifically) as the practical first slice rather than attempting an app-wide icon-weight pass at once.

### UIUX-263 — Three independently-defined "28sp bold" page-title styles instead of one shared token

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `LogHubScreen.kt` (`BadanType.sectionTitle.copy(fontSize = 28.sp)`), `SettingsScreen.kt` (identical `sectionTitle.copy(fontSize = 28.sp)`), and `OnboardingScreen.kt` (a wholly separate `private val titleFont = TextStyle(fontSize = 28.sp, fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold)`) each independently hand-roll the same "large page title" style rather than sharing one `BadanType` token — `BadanType.kt`'s ramp tops out at `heroNumeral` (44sp, for numerals only) and `sectionTitle` (20sp, for card headers), with no dedicated "page title" tier in between.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `BadanType.pageTitle` (28sp, Bold) token to `Tokens.kt` and replace all three ad-hoc definitions with it.
- **Why it matters:** Three independent definitions of the same visual style are three places that can silently drift (e.g., a future weight/size tweak applied to one and forgotten in the other two) — a single shared token eliminates that risk permanently.
- **Expected user impact:** Guaranteed-consistent page-title styling across Log, Settings, and Onboarding today, and any future screen that needs the same treatment.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/Tokens.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/loghub/LogHubScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/settings/SettingsScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/onboarding/OnboardingScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Typography (design system)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Silent visual drift between the three "page title" usages over time as the app evolves.
- **Implementation notes:** Add `val pageTitle = TextStyle(fontSize = 28.sp, fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold)` to `BadanType` in `Tokens.kt`; a pure find-and-replace at the three call sites.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `pageTitle` entry to `BadanType` in `Tokens.kt`, then replace the three independent 28sp-bold definitions in `LogHubScreen.kt`, `SettingsScreen.kt`, and `OnboardingScreen.kt` with `BadanType.pageTitle`.

### UIUX-264 — `StatBox`'s unit-baseline alignment uses padding approximation instead of true text-baseline alignment

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `StatBox.kt` aligns its `unit` `Text` to the hero `value` via `Row(verticalAlignment = Alignment.Bottom)` + a fixed `Modifier.padding(bottom = BadanSpace.s1)` approximation (lines ~42-48), whereas `BodyScreen.kt`'s `BodyPillarCard` achieves the same "value + unit" pairing using Compose's proper `Modifier.alignByBaseline()` on both `Text`s (lines ~270-278) — two different techniques for the same visual pattern can produce a subtly different vertical rhythm between `StatBox` (used on Home, Metric Detail, Nutrition) and the Body pillar cards.
- **Recommendation:** Standardize on `alignByBaseline()` in `StatBox` too, matching `BodyPillarCard`'s more precise technique.
- **Why it matters:** `StatBox` is the single most-reused "hero value" component in the app (Home, Metric Detail, Nutrition totals); getting its baseline alignment technique right once benefits every screen that uses it.
- **Expected user impact:** Marginally more precise, consistent vertical alignment between numerals and their units across the app.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/StatBox.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Design system (`StatBox`), all screens using it
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A very subtle, likely sub-pixel-to-a-few-pixels inconsistency; low visible impact but a real technique inconsistency worth fixing once at the source.
- **Implementation notes:** Replace `Row(verticalAlignment = Alignment.Bottom)` + manual bottom padding with a `Row` using `alignByBaseline()` on both the value and unit `Text` composables, as `BodyPillarCard` already demonstrates.

### UIUX-265 — Sleep duration hero text ("7h 12m") is a wider compound string with no width/scale safeguard

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SleepModuleCard` (`HomeScreen.kt`) renders `env.format.duration(sleep.seconds)` — a two-token string like "7h 12m" or Arabic "٧س ١٢د" — directly into `StatBox`'s `heroNumeral` style (44sp), which is otherwise used for simple single-number heroes ("72", "10,432"); there's no `autoSize`/scale-down guard if this compound string runs wider than a plain number on narrow devices.
- **Recommendation:** Verify rendering on a 360dp-width device/emulator and, if it's tight, either reduce the hero size specifically for compound-duration values or apply `Modifier.basicMarquee()`/auto-shrink as a safeguard.
- **Why it matters:** Sleep is one of the flagship casual-mode cards on Home; if its hero value clips or wraps on smaller/older Android devices (which the app's `minSdk = 26` suggests it still targets), it's a visible defect on the most prominent card in the app.
- **Expected user impact:** Confirms (or fixes) that the sleep hero value never clips on narrower devices.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/home/HomeScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/StatBox.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Home tab (sleep module)
- **Suggested owner:** QA
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Potential unverified clipping on narrow/small Android devices, a form factor `minSdk = 26` implies the app still supports.
- **Implementation notes:** A verify-first item; if confirmed tight, `StatBox` could accept an optional smaller hero style for compound-string values like durations.

### UIUX-266 — Timestamp phrasing is inconsistent: relative in Log hub, absolute everywhere else

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `LogHubScreen.kt`'s `relativeTime()` helper renders recent-item chips as "5 min ago"/"قبل ٥ د", while `ProvenanceRow` (`Provenance.kt`), `MetricDetailScreen.kt`'s `dateText`, `WorkoutLogScreen.kt`'s `dateTimeText`, and `NutritionLogScreen.kt`'s `timeText` all render absolute `DateFormat.MEDIUM/SHORT` timestamps ("Jan 12, 2:30 PM") for conceptually similar "when did this happen" values — the same kind of information is phrased two structurally different ways depending on which screen you're on.
- **Recommendation:** Decide one convention (relative-with-absolute-on-tap is the common pattern) and apply consistently, or explicitly reserve relative time for "just happened" contexts (Log hub recents) and absolute time for historical records (Metric Detail, Workout/Nutrition rows) — the current split may already reflect that reasonable distinction; if so, document it so it reads as intentional rather than incidental.
- **Why it matters:** Whether intentional or not, the inconsistency is currently undocumented, and a reader moving between the Log tab and a detail screen encounters two different time-phrasing conventions with no stated reasoning.
- **Expected user impact:** More predictable, learnable time-phrasing conventions across the app once the intent (documented or fixed) is clear.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/loghub/LogHubScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/Provenance.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/metricdetail/MetricDetailScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/WorkoutLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/NutritionLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Time/date formatting app-wide
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor, ongoing terminology-consistency debt.
- **Implementation notes:** At minimum, document the intended relative-vs-absolute rule (e.g., in `ValueFormatter`'s doc comment) so future screens follow a stated convention rather than reinventing it.

### UIUX-267 — Date/time formatting logic is independently reimplemented in five different files instead of centralized

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `HomeScreen.kt` (`longDate`, `eventTimeText`), `MetricDetailScreen.kt` (`dateText`), `SourcesScreen.kt` (`formatDateTime`), `WorkoutLogScreen.kt` (`dateTimeText`), `NutritionLogScreen.kt` (`timeText`), `TimelineScreen.kt` (`formattedDate`, `timeText`), `ExportScreen.kt` (`formatTimestamp`), and `SymptomLogScreen.kt` (`formatDate`, `formatTime`) each define their own private `DateFormat`/`SimpleDateFormat` helper functions — while `ValueFormatter.kt` already centralizes number/unit formatting for exactly this reason, no equivalent shared date/time formatter exists.
- **Recommendation:** Introduce a `DateTimeFormatter`-style companion to `ValueFormatter` (or extend it) providing shared `date()`, `time()`, `dateTime()`, `relative()` methods, and migrate the ~8 duplicated private helpers onto it.
- **Why it matters:** This duplication is exactly the kind of drift-risk `ValueFormatter` was built to prevent for numbers — eight independently-maintained date formatters is eight places a granularity/style inconsistency (like UIUX-266) can silently creep in.
- **Expected user impact:** Guaranteed-consistent date/time presentation everywhere in the app going forward.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/app/ValueFormatter.kt`, plus the ~8 screen files listed above
- **Affected systems:** Date/time formatting (app-wide)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-266
- **Risk if skipped:** Continued, compounding drift risk as more screens are added, each likely to reinvent its own date formatter yet again.
- **Implementation notes:** A meaningful refactor rather than a quick fix; best scheduled as a dedicated cleanup pass once the desired conventions (UIUX-266) are settled.

### UIUX-268 — `HomeScreen` casual mode shows unit-less numbers side-by-side for two different metrics

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricModuleCard`'s "secondary" slot (`HomeScreen.kt`, lines ~334-351) renders `secondary.heroValue` in `BadanType.numeralM` beside the primary `StatBox` with only a small caption label below it — for the steps+active-energy pairing this places two visually similar bare numbers (e.g., "8,432" and "312") side by side, differentiated only by a small caption underneath each.
- **Recommendation:** Consider surfacing the unit inline with the secondary value too (matching how the primary `StatBox` already does via its `unit` param), rather than relying solely on the caption label beneath to disambiguate.
- **Why it matters:** A first-time or quick-glancing casual user could misread which number is which at a glance, since both are large, bare numerals right next to each other.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, less error-prone at-a-glance reading of paired Home metrics.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/home/HomeScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Home tab (casual altitude)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor at-a-glance ambiguity; the caption label below does still resolve it on a closer look.
- **Implementation notes:** Add `secondary.unit` as a small trailing/inline label next to `secondary.heroValue`, matching the primary `StatBox`'s existing unit treatment.

### UIUX-269 — `WeeklyCard` on Insights carries full section-header visual weight for only ever 2 fixed rows

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `InsightsScreen.kt`'s `weeklyChanges()` hardcodes exactly two possible rows (sleep, resting heart rate — lines ~508-518) regardless of how many metrics a user actually tracks, yet `WeeklyCard` is styled with a full `SectionHeader` + `BadanCard` identical to the more open-ended `FeedCard` list below it, implying a broader "weekly summary" than the fixed two-metric content actually delivers.
- **Recommendation:** Either genuinely broaden `weeklyChanges()` to reflect more of the user's tracked metrics (a product decision) or adjust the visual framing (e.g., a lighter-weight inline treatment) to match the intentionally narrow, fixed scope.
- **Why it matters:** A user with 10+ actively-tracked metrics sees a "This week" section that only ever discusses two of them, which can read as an oversight rather than a deliberate curation choice, since nothing on screen explains why only these two are highlighted.
- **Expected user impact:** Either richer weekly context or a visual framing that doesn't overpromise.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/insights/InsightsScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Insights (weekly summary)
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A curated-but-unexplained weekly summary that some users may perceive as incomplete rather than deliberate.
- **Implementation notes:** Flagged for product sign-off since expanding scope touches the insight-generation logic itself, not just presentation; the presentation-only fix (visual re-framing) is a Design-owned, no-approval-needed alternative.

### UIUX-270 — Onboarding's disabled "Next" button on the Depth step gives no inline hint why it's disabled

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `OnboardingScreen.kt`'s footer `PrimaryButton` on the Depth step (`step == 2`) is disabled (`enabled = !disabled`) whenever `selectedDepth == null`, with no supporting text near the button explaining that a choice must be made first — the button simply renders at reduced opacity (`0.45f` alpha per `PrimaryButton`'s own implementation).
- **Recommendation:** Add a brief inline hint text ("Choose one to continue") beneath the two `DepthOption` cards when nothing is selected yet.
- **Why it matters:** A silently-disabled primary CTA during first-run onboarding — the single most consequence-sensitive moment for first impressions — risks users assuming the app is broken rather than realizing a selection is required.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer guidance during the most important early-app moment (onboarding).
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/onboarding/OnboardingScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Onboarding (depth-preset step)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A confusing dead-end moment during first-run onboarding specifically, the highest-stakes screen in the app for first impressions.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a conditionally-shown `Text` caption in `DepthPage` when `selected == null`.
- **First patch sketch:** In `OnboardingScreen.kt`'s `DepthPage`, add a `Text(style = BadanType.caption, color = colors.textSecondary)` reading a localized "Choose one to continue" string, shown only when `selected == null`, placed below the two `DepthOption` cards.

### UIUX-271 — Onboarding progress dots have no accessible step-count semantics

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `OnboardingScreen.kt`'s `OnboardingHeader` progress-dot row (`repeat(pageCount) { ... Box(...) }`, lines ~178-190) is built from plain, unlabeled `Box`es with no `Modifier.semantics{}` — a TalkBack user gets no spoken indication of which step they're on or how many total steps exist.
- **Recommendation:** Add `Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "Step ${step + 1} of $pageCount" }` to the progress-dot row (or the enclosing header) so screen readers announce onboarding progress.
- **Why it matters:** Onboarding is a linear, must-complete flow; a screen-reader user currently has no way to know how much of it remains without counting dots visually, which defeats the purpose of a progress indicator for exactly the users who benefit most from one.
- **Expected user impact:** Screen-reader users get spoken onboarding progress, matching sighted users' visual cue.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/onboarding/OnboardingScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Onboarding, accessibility
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A first-run accessibility gap for TalkBack users, at the very first screen they encounter.
- **Implementation notes:** One `semantics` modifier addition to the existing progress-dot `Row`.
- **First patch sketch:** In `OnboardingScreen.kt`'s `OnboardingHeader`, add `Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "Step ${step + 1} of $pageCount" }` (localized) to the progress-dot `Row`.

### UIUX-272 — Onboarding's "Connect health data" primary button performs the identical action as "Continue without connecting"

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `OnboardingScreen.kt`'s `ConnectPage` wires both the primary `PrimaryButton(label = s(connectPrimary), ...)` ("Connect health data") and the secondary text link ("Continue without connecting") to the exact same `onComplete` callback (lines ~537-556) — neither one actually triggers the Health Connect permission request flow that `HealthConnectCard.kt` implements elsewhere in the app; both buttons simply finish onboarding.
- **Recommendation:** Wire the primary "Connect health data" button to actually launch the Health Connect permission request (the same `HealthConnectAdapter.requestPermissionsContract()` flow already implemented in `HealthConnectCard.kt`), then complete onboarding on success/decline, so the button's label matches its behavior.
- **Why it matters:** This is a real affordance/behavior mismatch, not just a visual nit — a user who deliberately taps the more prominent, differently-styled "Connect health data" button (reasonably expecting a permission prompt) gets exactly the same outcome as if they'd tapped "skip," with no indication their intent to connect was ignored.
- **Expected user impact:** Users who choose to connect Health Connect during onboarding actually get prompted to do so, instead of silently landing in the same state as users who skipped.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/onboarding/OnboardingScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/HealthConnectCard.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Onboarding, Health Connect
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users intending to connect their health data during first-run get silently funneled into the "connect later, from Sources" path with no acknowledgment — a real drop-off risk for a core feature (Health Connect is described in the repo facts as more mature than iOS's equivalent).
- **Implementation notes:** `ConnectPage` would need access to the same `rememberLauncherForActivityResult(HealthConnectAdapter.requestPermissionsContract())` pattern `HealthConnectCard.kt` already implements; flagged for product approval since it changes onboarding's permission-request timing, one of the explicitly call-out-worthy categories (permissions) in this audit's own scoring rules.
- **First patch sketch:** In `OnboardingScreen.kt`'s `ConnectPage`, replace the primary button's `onClick = onComplete` with a Health Connect permission launcher (mirroring `HealthConnectCard.kt`'s `rememberLauncherForActivityResult` setup) that calls `onComplete` only after the permission flow resolves.

### UIUX-273 — Onboarding's `IconMark` decorative icons carry no `contentDescription`, correctly, but page titles aren't linked via semantics heading

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** None of the four onboarding pages mark their title `Text` (`WelcomePage`, `ValuePage`, `DepthPage`, `ConnectPage`) with `Modifier.semantics { heading() }`, so TalkBack's heading-navigation gesture (swipe to jump between headings) can't be used to skip between onboarding page titles.
- **Recommendation:** Add `Modifier.semantics { heading() }` to each page's title `Text`.
- **Why it matters:** Small, low-effort addition that materially improves TalkBack navigation efficiency through a multi-page flow.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster TalkBack navigation through onboarding via heading gestures.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/onboarding/OnboardingScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Onboarding, accessibility
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor TalkBack navigation-efficiency gap.
- **Implementation notes:** Add `.semantics { heading() }` to the four `titleFont`-styled `Text` composables.

### UIUX-274 — `ConfirmDialog`'s critical/destructive tint appears only on the confirm button text, not the dialog chrome

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SettingsScreen.kt`'s shared `ConfirmDialog` (used for both the sensitive-data purge and demo-data reset — both explicitly irreversible per their own doc comment) tints only the confirm `TextButton`'s text with `colors.critical`; the dialog's icon, title, and body text all use the same neutral styling as any non-destructive dialog would.
- **Recommendation:** Add a small warning icon to the dialog title row, or tint the title text itself with `colors.critical`, so the dialog's overall visual weight better signals irreversibility before the user reads all the way to the (correctly-tinted) confirm button.
- **Why it matters:** The dialog's own doc comment states the confirm-button tint exists specifically "because both call sites... are destructive" — but that intent only manifests in one small text element, easy to miss on a fast confirm-dialog skim.
- **Expected user impact:** A more immediately legible "this is serious" cue for the app's two genuinely irreversible actions.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/settings/SettingsScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Settings (destructive confirmations)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A subtle but real risk that a user fast-tapping through a confirm dialog underweights the consequence of purge/reset actions.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a small `Icons.Filled.WarningAmber` icon (tinted `colors.critical`) beside the `AlertDialog`'s `title` composable in `ConfirmDialog`.
- **First patch sketch:** In `SettingsScreen.kt`'s `ConfirmDialog`, change the `title` lambda to a `Row` pairing a small `Icon(Icons.Filled.WarningAmber, tint = colors.critical)` with the existing `Text(title, ...)`.

### UIUX-275 — `LabeledField`/`NumberField` placeholders use a fixed 0.6 alpha that may read too faint in bright ambient light

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `LabeledField`, `WorkoutLogScreen.kt`/`NutritionLogScreen.kt`'s `NumberField`, and `LogHubScreen.kt`'s `WeightQuickSheet` all render placeholder text as `colors.textSecondary.copy(alpha = 0.6f)` — an extra alpha reduction stacked on top of `textSecondary`, which is already a muted tone relative to `textPrimary`.
- **Recommendation:** Verify this compound-alpha placeholder still meets a reasonable contrast minimum against `colors.surface` in both themes (it's plausible it does, but it's a double-dimming stack worth a quick contrast check rather than an assumption).
- **Why it matters:** Placeholder legibility directly affects how easily a user can tell what a field expects before typing, especially for less-common fields (strength, distance) where the placeholder is the only hint.
- **Expected user impact:** Confirms (or improves) placeholder legibility across every custom text field in the app.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/medication/MedicationLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/WorkoutLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/NutritionLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/loghub/LogHubScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Form fields (all logging screens)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-232/UIUX-240 (ideally consolidated into one shared field component)
- **Risk if skipped:** Low-to-moderate; a verify-first item likely to require only a minor alpha adjustment if it fails a contrast check.
- **Implementation notes:** Best fixed once at the source if/when a shared `BadanTextField` (UIUX-232) is introduced, rather than patched at four independent call sites.

### UIUX-276 — Home's flagship "Readiness" score is a plain number, not a glanceable ring/gauge

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ReadinessHeroCard` (`HomeScreen.kt`) renders the readiness score purely as `StatBox(value = "72", unit = "/ 100")` text — the app's single most prominent, flagship metric has no graphical (ring/arc/gauge) representation anywhere on Android, only a text fraction.
- **Recommendation:** Investigate whether iOS's `ReadinessHeroCard` equivalent uses a graphical ring (a very common pattern for "readiness"/"score out of 100" concepts) and, if so, treat this as a cross-platform product-truth gap worth closing on Android rather than a from-scratch design decision.
- **Why it matters:** This is exactly the "where Android should match iOS product truth" question called out as in-scope for this audit — a flagship score rendered as plain text vs. a graphical gauge is a meaningfully different product experience, not just a style choice.
- **Expected user impact:** A more glanceable, visually engaging flagship metric matching the weight of its role in the app.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/home/HomeScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/StatBox.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Home tab (flagship readiness card)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** If iOS does present readiness graphically, Android's flagship first-glance experience under-delivers relative to its own sibling platform on the single most important screen in the app.
- **Implementation notes:** Flagged for product/design approval since this changes the visual identity of the app's primary metric, not just an internal implementation detail; would likely reuse `MetricChart.kt`'s `Canvas` infrastructure for a new ring-gauge component.

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `HomeScreen.kt`'s `MetricGridCell` renders its `MetricSparkline` at `Modifier.height(28.dp)` while `SleepModuleCard` (same file) renders its sparkline at `Modifier.height(36.dp)` — both are "recent trend at a glance" sparklines on the same screen, sized differently with no documented rationale (grid density is a plausible reason, but it's not stated anywhere).

- **Expected user impact:** Marginal; mostly a code-maintainability/consistency signal.

- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/home/HomeScreen.kt`

### UIUX-278 — No design-system-level minimum-height/sizing tokens; many one-off literal `dp` values

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Across the scoped screens, numerous one-off literal `dp` sizes bypass `BadanSpace`/`BadanRadius` tokens: `LogHubScreen.kt`'s `LogTile` uses `heightIn(min = 92.dp)`, `ExportScreen.kt`'s `ExportFormatCard` uses `heightIn(min = 116.dp)`, `LogHubScreen.kt`'s water/weight sheet rows use `heightIn(min = 60.dp)`, `OnboardingScreen.kt`'s `IconMark` diameters vary (`84.dp`, `44.dp`) with no shared "icon mark size" token, and `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `RegimenCard` icon box reuses `BadanSpace.touchMin` (48dp) for an icon container rather than a dedicated icon-container token.
- **Recommendation:** Extend `BadanSpace`/a new `BadanSize` object with named tokens for the recurring patterns found (tile min-height, format-card min-height, icon-mark diameters, sheet-row min-height) and migrate these call sites onto them.
- **Why it matters:** This is a systemic pattern across nearly every screen in scope, not a single-file issue — centralizing these sizes is what prevents visual drift as the app grows and makes intentional resizing (a future design refresh) a one-line change instead of a grep-and-replace across a dozen files.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — reduces the risk of visual inconsistency creeping in over time as new screens are added.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/Tokens.kt`, plus the several feature files cited above
- **Affected systems:** Design system tokens (app-wide)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Slow, compounding visual-consistency drift across the app as more one-off sizes accumulate.
- **Implementation notes:** A larger design-system consolidation effort; best scheduled as a dedicated pass rather than attempted piecemeal alongside unrelated feature work.

### UIUX-279 — `ExportFormatCard`'s CSV/JSON choice offers no illustrative preview of the actual output difference

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ExportScreen.kt`'s two `ExportFormatCard`s differ only by icon (`TableChart` vs `DataObject`), title, and a one-sentence subtitle — for a fairly technical, consequential choice (spreadsheet-friendly multi-file CSV vs. one structured JSON bundle), there's no visual preview (e.g., a tiny mock file-tree or snippet) helping a less-technical casual user understand what they're actually choosing between.
- **Recommendation:** Consider adding a minimal illustrative element (e.g., a small mock "raw.csv / derived.csv / manifest.json" file-chip row for CSV vs. a single "bundle.json" chip for JSON) reusing information already present in `availableFiles()`'s naming logic.
- **Why it matters:** Export is explicitly a casual-and-power-both surface (per the screen's own doc comment: "Casual keeps it calm... power exposes..."), yet the format choice — arguably the most consequential single decision on the whole screen — is presented with no illustrative aid for the casual audience.
- **Expected user impact:** More confident, better-informed format selection for less-technical users.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/export/ExportScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Export
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor; the existing subtitle text already conveys the essential difference reasonably well.
- **Implementation notes:** Lowest-effort version: add 1-2 small `PillLabel`-style file-name chips inside each `ExportFormatCard` reusing the naming already defined in `availableFiles()`.

### UIUX-280 — `ScopeToggleRow`'s icon column uses a fixed 26dp width while `SettingsNavRow`'s icon uses natural sizing

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ExportScreen.kt`'s `ScopeToggleRow` wraps its leading icon in `Box(modifier = Modifier.width(26.dp), contentAlignment = Alignment.Center)` (line ~616) to align icons of varying intrinsic width, while `SettingsScreen.kt`'s otherwise near-identical `SettingsNavRow` pattern (icon + label + trailing chevron) doesn't use this fixed-width wrapper at all — the same "icon-led settings row" pattern is implemented two different ways in two different files.

- **Why it matters:** At least four files (`ExportScreen`, `SettingsScreen`, `BodyScreen`, `SourcesScreen`) each reimplement a near-identical "icon + label + trailing" row pattern independently, meaning any future consistency fix (like this one) must currently be applied four separate times.
- **Expected user impact:** Perfectly consistent icon-column alignment across every settings/list-style row in the app.

- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/export/ExportScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/settings/SettingsScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/BodyScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/SourcesScreen.kt`

- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None

### UIUX-281 — `RecentChip`'s detail line (relative time) only appears in power depth, unlike its icon/label which are always shown

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `LogHubScreen.kt`'s `RecentChip` passes `detail = if (env.depth.showsPowerDetail) relativeTime(env, item.date) else null` — casual users see a "log again" chip with no time context at all, so two visually identical "Headache" chips (one from this morning, one from three weeks ago) are indistinguishable to a casual user.
- **Recommendation:** Consider surfacing at least a coarse relative-time cue to casual users too (e.g., "today"/"this week" rather than the precise power-depth granularity), since knowing roughly how recent a "log again" suggestion is seems useful regardless of altitude.
- **Why it matters:** The recents feature's entire value proposition is fast re-logging of *recent* items — without any time context, a casual user can't tell whether a suggested chip reflects something from today or a month ago.
- **Expected user impact:** More trustworthy "recent" suggestions for casual users.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/loghub/LogHubScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Log hub (recents)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Casual users may re-log outdated/stale suggested items believing them to be genuinely recent.
- **Implementation notes:** A coarse relative label ("today"/"this week"/"earlier") could be shown at all altitudes, reserving the precise "5 min ago" granularity for power depth only.

### UIUX-282 — `PillLabel`'s `tint` parameter defaults to `textSecondary`, making most pills visually indistinguishable from plain captions at a glance

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `Pills.kt`'s `PillLabel` defaults `tint` to `colors.textSecondary` when not explicitly passed — many call sites (e.g., `ExportHistoryRow`'s record-count pill in `ExportScreen.kt`, un-tinted `PillLabel` calls in `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `TimeChip`-adjacent usages) end up rendering a barely-tinted, low-contrast pill background (`textSecondary.copy(alpha=0.12f)`) that's easy to visually miss as "a pill" versus plain text with a very faint box behind it.
- **Recommendation:** Reserve `PillLabel` for genuinely tinted/semantic pills and use a plainer, un-pilled `Text` for count-only labels like `ExportHistoryRow`'s "N records," or give the default tint slightly more presence (e.g., `colors.surfaceElevated`-backed with a border) so untin ted pills still read clearly as pills.
- **Why it matters:** When a component's "default" styling is nearly invisible, it undermines the pill pattern's whole purpose (visually chunking metadata) at every call site that doesn't bother to pass an explicit tint.
- **Expected user impact:** More visually legible metadata pills across Export, Medication, and other screens using the untinted default.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/Pills.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Design system (`PillLabel`), Export/Medication/Workout/Nutrition screens
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low-contrast default pill styling continues to under-communicate at every call site that relies on the default tint.
- **Implementation notes:** Small, self-contained change to `PillLabel`'s default `tint` value or its alpha constant.

### UIUX-283 — `WorkoutLogScreen`/`NutritionLogScreen` `PrimaryButton` duplicated verbatim in two files instead of shared

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `WorkoutLogScreen.kt` and `NutritionLogScreen.kt` each define their own private `PrimaryButton` composable with byte-for-byte identical implementations (same shape, same alpha-based disabled treatment, same `Color.White` text) — a change to one (e.g., fixing the on-primary contrast gap noted in UIUX-223) must be manually mirrored in the other or they silently diverge.
- **Recommendation:** Extract one shared `BadanPrimaryButton` into `designsystem/components/` and have both screens (and ideally `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s near-identical `FilledPrimaryButton`) consume it.
- **Why it matters:** This is the exact mechanism by which UIUX-223's on-primary color inconsistency happened in the first place — duplicated component logic across files with no single source of truth.
- **Expected user impact:** Guaranteed-consistent primary-button behavior across Workout, Nutrition, and Medication logging screens.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/WorkoutLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/NutritionLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/medication/MedicationLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Design system, all logging screens
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-223 (share the same fix)
- **Risk if skipped:** Continued risk of the three near-identical button implementations silently diverging over time.
- **Implementation notes:** Extract into `designsystem/components/` alongside the existing `BadanCard`/`PillLabel` components; do this in the same pass as UIUX-223's `onPrimary` token addition since both touch the same code.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `BadanPrimaryButton(label, enabled, onClick)` composable to `designsystem/components/`, reusing `colors.onPrimary` from UIUX-223, then replace the three near-duplicate `PrimaryButton`/`FilledPrimaryButton` definitions in Workout/Nutrition/Medication with it.

### UIUX-284 — `SymptomChip`'s `selected` parameter is defined but never actually used by any call site

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SymptomLogScreen.kt`'s `SymptomChip` composable accepts a `selected: Boolean = false` parameter and fully implements selected-state styling (filled background, white text — lines ~813-838), but every call site in the file (`Picker`'s recents/category chips, `WhenCard`'s date/time chips) always uses the default `false`, meaning the selected-state styling code is entirely dead/unreachable in practice.
- **Recommendation:** Either use `selected` where it would genuinely help (e.g., highlighting a symptom the user has hovered/hesitated over is unlikely to apply, but this is worth a quick audit for any place a selected-chip visual was intended but never wired up), or remove the unused parameter and dead styling branch to reduce component surface area.
- **Why it matters:** Dead, never-exercised UI-state code is a maintenance liability — it can silently break (e.g., during a refactor) without anyone noticing since no test or screen ever renders it.
- **Expected user impact:** None directly; a code-health item with no user-facing behavior change either way.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/symptom/SymptomLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Negligible; purely a code-cleanliness note included here because it directly affects the interaction design surface reviewed for this audit.
- **Implementation notes:** Quick audit-then-decide: either wire `selected` up somewhere meaningful or delete the dead branch.

### UIUX-285 — `WhyDisclosure`'s expand/collapse chevron flips with no rotation animation

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `InsightsScreen.kt`'s `WhyDisclosure` swaps `Icons.Filled.ExpandLess`/`ExpandMore` outright based on `expanded` state (lines ~369-374) rather than rotating a single chevron icon with `animateFloatAsState` — a common, low-cost Material pattern for expand/collapse affordances that's absent here (and in `BodyScreen.kt`'s nearly identical `ExpandLess`/`ExpandMore` swap for "All metrics").
- **Recommendation:** Replace the icon-swap with a single chevron `Icon` rotated via `Modifier.rotate(if (expanded) 180f else 0f)` animated with `animateFloatAsState`, applied consistently to both `InsightsScreen.kt` and `BodyScreen.kt`'s equivalent disclosure triangles.
- **Why it matters:** This is a two-site, low-effort motion-polish fix that makes both of the app's expand/collapse disclosures feel more considered, aligning with the broader motion gaps noted in UIUX-207.
- **Expected user impact:** A smoother, more tactile expand/collapse interaction on both the Insights "Why am I seeing this?" and Body "All metrics" disclosures.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/insights/InsightsScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/BodyScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Insights, Body screen
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-207 (same motion-polish theme)
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor; a small missed polish opportunity in two places.
- **Implementation notes:** `Modifier.rotate(animateFloatAsState(if (expanded) 180f else 0f).value)` on a single `Icons.Filled.ExpandMore` icon replaces the two-icon swap at both sites.
- **First patch sketch:** In `InsightsScreen.kt`'s `WhyDisclosure` and `BodyScreen.kt`'s equivalent toggle icon, replace the `if (expanded) Icons.Filled.ExpandLess else Icons.Filled.ExpandMore` swap with a single rotated `Icons.Filled.ExpandMore` driven by `animateFloatAsState`.

### UIUX-286 — `MetricAnatomySheet`'s dedup "Kept"/"Suppressed duplicate" pills read as a fixed pair with no visual link to which record is which

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricAnatomySheet.kt`'s `DedupCard` renders a `Row` of two `PillLabel`s ("Kept" + "Suppressed duplicate") per dedup decision (lines ~217-227) with no source/device identification on either pill — a user with two wearables can't tell *which* device's reading was kept vs. suppressed from this view alone, only that a dedup happened.
- **Recommendation:** Add the source/device name to each pill's label (e.g., "Kept · Apple Watch" / "Suppressed · iPhone") using data already available via `ReconciliationDecision`.
- **Why it matters:** This screen exists specifically to make "how this was worked out" transparent and trustworthy (the anatomy sheet's whole purpose per its doc comment); omitting exactly which source won the tie-break undercuts that transparency goal for the one piece of information a curious power user most wants to know.
- **Expected user impact:** Fuller, more genuinely transparent explanation of the dedup decision for power users who open this sheet.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/metricdetail/MetricAnatomySheet.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Metric detail (anatomy sheet, power altitude)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The anatomy sheet's core transparency promise is only partially delivered for the dedup case specifically.
- **Implementation notes:** Check whether `ReconciliationDecision` (used to populate `data.recentDedup`) already carries source identifiers; if so this is primarily a presentation change.

### UIUX-287 — `MetricAnatomySheet`'s `RecordsCard` has no maximum height inside an already-tall bottom sheet

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MetricAnatomySheet.kt`'s overall `Column` is `verticalScroll`-wrapped, but for composite metrics with many contributing inputs, `RecordsCard`'s `InfoRow` list has no independent height cap — combined with `BaselineCard`, `MethodCard`, and potentially `DedupCard` all stacked above/below it, a metric with a long input list can push the sheet's total content well past one screen height with the "Close" action only reachable at the very top.
- **Recommendation:** Consider a sticky header (keep "How this was worked out" + Close pinned) or cap `RecordsCard`'s own height with an internal scroll + "show all" affordance for unusually long input lists.
- **Why it matters:** For the rare but real case of a composite metric with many inputs, the sheet becomes a long scroll with the only dismiss action requiring a scroll back to the top (swipe-to-dismiss on the sheet itself is the actual escape hatch, but it's not obviously discoverable from inside a long scrolled list).
- **Expected user impact:** Easier dismissal/navigation for anatomy sheets with unusually long contributing-record lists.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/metricdetail/MetricAnatomySheet.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Metric detail (anatomy sheet)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Edge-case friction only affecting composite metrics with unusually many contributing inputs.
- **Implementation notes:** `ModalBottomSheet`'s own drag handle already provides a dismiss path regardless of scroll position, which partially mitigates this — worth verifying that's sufficiently discoverable before investing in a sticky header.

### UIUX-288 — `MedicationLogScreen`'s `BoundaryFooter` disclaimer text sits with no distinct visual treatment from ordinary captions

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `BoundaryFooter` (rendering `Loc.medsBoundary`, presumably a "BADAN records, it never prescribes" style disclaimer per the file's own doc comment) is styled identically to any other `BadanType.caption` secondary text on the screen, with no framing (icon, border, background tint) distinguishing it as an important scope-of-service disclaimer.
- **Recommendation:** Give this specific disclaimer a lightweight distinguishing treatment (e.g., a small info icon prefix, matching the pattern already used for `ExportCopy.sensitiveNote`/`ExportScreen.kt`'s `SensitiveNote`) so it reads as a deliberate boundary statement rather than blending into ordinary footer text.
- **Why it matters:** A disclaimer that blends into ordinary caption text is easy to skim past unnoticed, undermining its purpose of clearly communicating the app's non-prescriptive scope for a health-adjacent feature.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer communication of the app's scope-of-service boundary on the medication screen.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/medication/MedicationLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor; the text is still present and readable, just under-emphasized relative to its importance.
- **Implementation notes:** Reuse the `SensitiveNote`-style icon+tinted-caption pattern already established in `ExportScreen.kt`.

### UIUX-289 — `NutritionLogScreen`'s "quick calories" toggle changes which card layout appears with an abrupt swap, not a transition

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `NutritionLogScreen.kt`'s `if (!quickCalories) { BadanCard {...} } else { BadanCard {...} }` (lines ~279-324) swaps between the full "Optional details" card (calories + protein fields) and the compact quick-calories card the instant the `Switch` is toggled, with no `AnimatedContent`/crossfade — the whole card's height and content changes in a single frame.
- **Recommendation:** Wrap the conditional card swap in `AnimatedContent`/`animateContentSize()` for a smoother height/content transition.
- **Why it matters:** This toggle sits directly above the swapped content, so the abrupt layout jump is maximally visible right where the user's attention already is.
- **Expected user impact:** A smoother, less jarring transition when toggling "quick calories."
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/NutritionLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile

- **Risk if skipped:** Minor visual jump directly beneath the toggle the user just interacted with.
- **Implementation notes:** Simplest fix: apply `Modifier.animateContentSize()` to the parent `Column` wrapping the conditional cards.
- **First patch sketch:** In `NutritionLogScreen.kt`, add `Modifier.animateContentSize()` to the `Column` (or `BadanCard`) that swaps between the full and quick-calories layouts based on `quickCalories`.

### UIUX-290 — `SourcesScreen`'s "How duplicates are settled" power-only note appears without any lead-in from the source cards above it

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SourcesScreen.kt`'s `SourcesPriorityNote` (power-only, at the very bottom of the screen) is the only place explaining source-priority tie-breaking, but nothing on the `SourcesSourceCard`s above it (which do show a `SourceStatusPill` but no priority-rank indicator) visually connects "here's a list of sources" to "here's how conflicts between them are resolved" — a power user has to scroll all the way to the bottom to learn a rule that would be more useful understood while looking at the actual list of sources.
- **Recommendation:** Consider surfacing a source's priority rank directly on `SourcesSourceCard` (e.g., a small "#1 priority" pill) so the explanatory note at the bottom has something concrete to point back to, or move a short version of the explanation nearer the source list itself.
- **Why it matters:** The underlying mechanism (source-priority tie-breaking) is a meaningful piece of "how the numbers you see were decided," directly tied to this audit's provenance-transparency theme — currently it's documented but not visually connected to the data it explains.
- **Expected user impact:** Better-connected understanding of why one source's data appears over another's when duplicates occur.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/SourcesScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Sources screen (power altitude)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The priority-note content remains correct but somewhat disconnected from the source list it describes.
- **Implementation notes:** Would require exposing a priority-rank field already presumably present in the `Source`/`SourcesSourceInfo` model, just not currently surfaced in `SourcesSourceCard`.

### UIUX-291 — `DeviceRow`'s "last seen" column only appears in power depth, leaving casual users with no recency signal for devices

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SourcesScreen.kt`'s `DeviceRow` gates its entire "Last seen" `Column` (lines ~279-296) behind `env.depth.showsPowerDetail` — casual users see a device name only, with no indication of whether a listed device is still actively delivering data or hasn't reported in months.
- **Recommendation:** Surface at least a coarse recency cue to casual users too (e.g., a small "active" vs. "inactive" `StatusChip`-style badge derived from `device.lastSeen` vs. some staleness threshold), reserving the precise timestamp for power depth.
- **Why it matters:** Knowing whether a connected device is still actually delivering data seems like baseline information relevant to any user, not just power users — the current gating may be over-applying the casual/power split to information that isn't really "detail," it's core status.
- **Expected user impact:** Casual users get a basic sense of which connected devices are actively contributing data.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/SourcesScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Sources screen (casual altitude)
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Casual users can't tell a stale/disconnected device from an actively-syncing one without switching to power mode.
- **Implementation notes:** A coarse `StatusChip`-style "active"/"inactive" badge computed from `device.lastSeen` age could be shown at all altitudes, with the precise absolute timestamp reserved for power depth as it is today.

### UIUX-292 — `WorkoutRow`/`MealRow`'s power-only provenance details push chip rows and provenance text into a tall, unbroken column

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `WorkoutLogScreen.kt`'s `WorkoutRow` and `NutritionLogScreen.kt`'s `MealRow`, in power depth, stack: title row → chip row (effort/energy/distance) → date/time caption → raw-values caption → full `ProvenanceRow` (Workout only), all within one `BadanCard` with no internal separator distinguishing "user-facing summary" from "technical/provenance detail" — the two categories of information visually blend together.
- **Recommendation:** Add a subtle `HorizontalDivider`/spacing break (matching the pattern `SourcesSourceCard` already uses between its main content and its device list) between the summary chips and the power-only technical detail lines.
- **Why it matters:** As power users scan a list of many recent workouts/meals, a clear visual break between "what I logged" and "how it's stored" would make each card easier to scan at a glance rather than reading as one undifferentiated block of text.
- **Expected user impact:** Easier scanning of recent workout/meal history in power mode.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/WorkoutLogScreen.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/NutritionLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Workout/Nutrition logging (power altitude)
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor scanability friction in power-mode history lists.
- **Implementation notes:** A single `Box(...).height(1.dp).background(colors.separator)` divider (the same pattern used throughout the codebase) inserted before the power-only detail lines in both `WorkoutRow` and `MealRow`.

### UIUX-293 — Symptom "recents" and "trigger suggestions" chip rows use the same `SymptomChip` visual style with no differentiation between "pick a symptom" and "add a trigger" semantics

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `SymptomLogScreen.kt` uses the identical `SymptomChip` composable for the top-level symptom picker (`Picker`'s recents/category rows) and for trigger suggestions (`TriggersCard`'s suggestion row) — the two chip rows appear back-to-back within the same capture flow (once a symptom is picked, `TriggersCard` shows suggestion chips styled identically to the symptom-selection chips the user just interacted with).
- **Recommendation:** Give trigger-suggestion chips a visually distinct (e.g., outlined-only, no icon) treatment from the primary symptom-selection chips, so it's immediately clear the interaction model has shifted from "pick one" to "add optional tags."
- **Why it matters:** Reusing identical chip styling across two different interaction semantics (single-select navigation vs. multi-add tagging) within the same continuous flow risks a user expecting trigger chips to behave like symptom chips (e.g., expecting selection state/highlighting) when they instead immediately add and disappear from the suggestion row.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer signal that trigger suggestions behave differently (additive tags) than the symptom picker that preceded them.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/symptom/SymptomLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor interaction-model ambiguity within a single continuous flow.
- **Implementation notes:** The `SymptomChip`'s existing `icon` param already differentiates trigger suggestions (`Icons.Filled.Add`) from symptom chips visually to a degree — this finding suggests going further with the container styling itself, not just the icon.

### UIUX-294 — `ExportSuccessCard`'s checksum list has no copy-to-clipboard affordance for the truncated hashes

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ExportScreen.kt`'s `ExportSuccessCard` shows each file's SHA-256 checksum truncated to 12 characters (`shortHash`, line ~998) with no way to view or copy the full hash — a power user wanting to actually verify export integrity (the entire stated purpose of showing checksums at all) can't get the full value from the UI.
- **Recommendation:** Add a tap-to-copy affordance (or a long-press context menu) on each checksum row that copies the full hash to the clipboard, with a brief confirmation.
- **Why it matters:** Showing a checksum that can't be copied or viewed in full defeats its own stated purpose — verifiable export integrity, one of the "trust cockpit" screen's core promises per its own doc comment.
- **Expected user impact:** Power users can actually use the displayed checksums to verify export integrity against an external tool.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/export/ExportScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Export (power altitude)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The checksum display currently functions as a trust signal without functioning as an actually-usable verification tool.
- **Implementation notes:** `ClipboardManager` (`LocalClipboardManager.current`) + a `clickable` modifier on each checksum `Text` row is a minimal, self-contained fix.
- **First patch sketch:** In `ExportScreen.kt`'s `ExportSuccessCard`, wrap each checksum `Row` in `Modifier.clickable { clipboardManager.setText(AnnotatedString(fullHash)) }` using `LocalClipboardManager.current`, and show a brief `Snackbar`/toast confirmation.

### UIUX-295 — `ManifestDetail`'s "Export ID" is truncated to 10 characters with no way to view/copy the full ID

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `ExportScreen.kt`'s `ManifestDetail` shows `manifest.exportId.take(10)` (line ~840) with no copy affordance or full-value disclosure — similar to UIUX-294, a power user who needs the full export ID (e.g., to reference it when reporting an issue, or to cross-check against the manifest file itself) can't retrieve it from the UI.

- **Expected user impact:** Power users can retrieve the full export ID when needed (e.g., support requests).
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/export/ExportScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Export (power altitude)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-294 (same fix pattern, could be done together)
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor; low-frequency need (support/debugging scenarios).
