### UIUX-296 — `MetricDetailStrings`/`AnatomyStrings`/`InsightsStrings`/`SettingsStrings`/etc. — every screen defines its own private bilingual-string object instead of a shared catalog entry point

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Nearly every feature file in scope defines its own file-local `private object XStrings { val ... = LocalizedString(...) }` (at least 8 distinct such objects found: `MetricDetailStrings`, `AnatomyStrings`, `InsightsStrings`, `SettingsStrings`, `SymptomLogStrings`, plus loose top-level `private val`s in `HomeScreen.kt`, `LogHubScreen.kt`, `MedicationLogScreen.kt`, `WorkoutLogScreen.kt`/`NutritionLogScreen.kt`, `ExportScreen.kt`, `OnboardingScreen.kt`) rather than all living in the shared `Loc` catalog (`core/Localization/Strings.swift`'s Android counterpart) that already exists precisely for this purpose.
- **Recommendation:** This is a deliberate, documented pattern per each file's own comments ("Shared vocabulary comes from `Loc`; these fill the gaps") — the finding here is that with ~8+ independent string objects now existing, there's a real risk of near-duplicate strings drifting slightly apart across files (e.g., two screens independently writing near-identical "saved manually" copy with slightly different wording) with no single place to check for existing equivalents before adding a new one.
- **Why it matters:** As the string surface grows, screen-local string objects make it progressively harder for any single contributor to know whether a phrase they're about to add already exists elsewhere with different wording, risking exactly the kind of terminology drift (UIUX-266) already found in this audit.
- **Expected user impact:** More consistent terminology across the app as it continues to grow.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** All feature screen files in scope (see list above)
- **Affected systems:** Localization architecture
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Slow-building terminology drift as more screen-local string objects accumulate independently.
- **Implementation notes:** Not a "fix the pattern" recommendation (the file-local pattern is intentional and documented) — rather, recommend a lightweight process safeguard, e.g. a periodic grep-based audit for near-duplicate English phrases across all `*Strings` objects before each release.

### UIUX-297 — `Icons.kt`'s `iconForKey` is invoked with plain strings everywhere, with no compile-time exhaustiveness check against the domain enums it's meant to cover

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `iconForKey(key: String)` (`Icons.kt`) is called with `.symbolName` string properties from `MetricFamily`, `MealType`, `TimelineEventType`, and various hardcoded string literals (`"healing"`, `"medication"`, `"directions_run"`, etc. scattered through `LogHubScreen.kt`) — since the function's input is a bare `String`, adding a new `MetricFamily`/`MealType`/`TimelineEventType` case with a new `symbolName` produces no compiler warning if `iconForKey` isn't updated to match, silently falling back to the ambiguous default glyph (see UIUX-261).
- **Recommendation:** Where feasible, convert the highest-value mappings (`MetricFamily`, `TimelineEventType`) to `when` expressions directly over the enum type rather than its string `symbolName`, so the Kotlin compiler enforces exhaustiveness and flags any future unmapped case at compile time.
- **Why it matters:** This closes the loop on UIUX-261 at its root cause — a string-keyed lookup can never be compiler-verified, while an enum-keyed one can, converting a silent runtime fallback into a compile-time guarantee.
- **Expected user impact:** Indirect — prevents future icon-mapping gaps from ever shipping silently.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/components/Icons.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Icon mapping (design system)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** UIUX-261, UIUX-085 (same theme)
- **Risk if skipped:** Continued reliance on manual vigilance (rather than the compiler) to keep icon mappings complete as new domain enum cases are added.
- **Implementation notes:** A larger refactor than UIUX-261's quick fallback-glyph swap; best scheduled as a deliberate follow-up once the fallback-glyph fix (UIUX-261) ships first for the immediate mitigation.

### UIUX-298 — `SkippedPill`'s outline-only treatment visually under-communicates compared to `StatusChip`'s consistently filled-tint pattern used everywhere else

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `MedicationLogScreen.kt`'s `SkippedPill` (a bespoke composable, not reusing `StatusChip`/`PillLabel`) renders with only a 1dp `colors.separator` border and no background fill (lines ~534-549), breaking from every other status indicator in the app (`StatusChip`, `PillLabel`, `DepthBadge`, `ProvisionalBadge`) which all use a tinted-fill + matching text/icon color pattern.
- **Recommendation:** Reuse `PillLabel` (with a `textSecondary` or dedicated "skipped" tint) instead of the bespoke border-only `SkippedPill`, for visual consistency with every other status indicator in the app.
- **Why it matters:** This is the one status-communication element in the whole app that doesn't follow the established fill+tint convention, making it look unintentionally unstyled next to its sibling `StatusChip`s (Taken, Still due) on the very same screen.
- **Expected user impact:** Visually consistent status indicators within the medication screen itself.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/medication/MedicationLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A single visually-inconsistent status pill on an otherwise consistent screen.
- **Implementation notes:** Replace the custom `Row` in `SkippedPill` with a `PillLabel(text = ..., icon = Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.Redo, tint = colors.textSecondary)` call, matching the app's established pattern.
- **First patch sketch:** In `MedicationLogScreen.kt`, replace `SkippedPill`'s bespoke `Row(...)` implementation with a direct call to the existing `PillLabel` composable, passing the same icon/text/tint already computed.

### UIUX-299 — `LogTile`'s icon-box background tint (`primary.copy(alpha = 0.12f)`) is visually near-identical across all tile types, giving no color-coded categorization

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** `LogHubScreen.kt`'s `LogTile` uses the same `colors.primary.copy(alpha = 0.12f)` icon-box background for every log type (Symptom, Medication, Workout, Nutrition, Water, Weight) — the only differentiator between tiles is the icon glyph itself and the label text, with no color-coding to help users build spatial/color memory for frequently-used log types.
- **Recommendation:** This is a legitimate design decision either way (uniform tinting keeps the grid calm and non-hierarchical, matching the wellness-safe "no moralizing colors" principle) — worth confirming as intentional rather than a missed opportunity, since some users do benefit from color-coded categorization for fast recognition.
- **Why it matters:** Given the app's explicit "wellness-safe, no moralizing color" design principle, uniform tinting here is plausibly deliberate rather than an oversight — flagging for confirmation rather than recommending a change outright.
- **Expected user impact:** None if already intentional; potentially faster tile recognition if color-coding is later deemed worthwhile.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/loghub/LogHubScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Log hub
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** None if the uniform treatment is confirmed intentional (likely).
- **Implementation notes:** Lowest-priority item in this batch; primarily a "confirm intent" note rather than a concrete recommendation.

### UIUX-300 — No consolidated design-system component inventory/reference screen for the Android app

- **Category:** UI/UX Improvement
- **Problem:** Unlike some design systems that ship an internal "component gallery" debug screen, BADAN's Android `designsystem/` package (`Theme.kt`, `Tokens.kt`, `components/*.kt`) has no equivalent — every component (`BadanCard`, `StatusChip`, `PillLabel`, `MetricChart`, etc.) can only be visually inspected in the context of whichever real screen happens to use it, making many of this audit's findings (e.g., UIUX-222's contrast audit, UIUX-223's on-primary consolidation) harder to verify holistically than they'd be with a single reference screen showing every token/component/state side by side.
- **Recommendation:** Add a lightweight, debug-build-only "Design System" screen (reachable via a hidden Settings tap-sequence or a debug-only nav entry) rendering every `BadanColors`/`BadanType`/component variant in one place.
- **Why it matters:** Nearly a dozen findings in this audit (theme contrast, token duplication, dark-mode-specific issues) would have been faster to verify — and future regressions faster to catch — with one screen showing every design-system primitive at once instead of hunting through a dozen feature files.
- **Expected user impact:** None directly for end users (a developer/QA tool); indirectly improves the pace and confidence of every future design-system change.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** New file under `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/designsystem/` (e.g., `DesignSystemGalleryScreen.kt`)
- **Affected systems:** Developer tooling, design system
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Continued reliance on scattered, screen-by-screen visual verification for design-system-wide changes.
- **Implementation notes:** Debug-build-gated (e.g., `BuildConfig.DEBUG`) so it never ships to production; could be wired behind a long-press on the Settings title as a low-friction developer entry point.

All items grounded in the actual repo at `/Users/binjamshid/Desktop/badan`.

## LogHub entry hierarchy

### EASE-001 — Recents strip only covers 2 of 6 loggable types

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `LogHubViewModel.RecentItem.Kind` (`LogHubScreen.swift:17`) only has `.symptom` and `.workout` cases, and `load()` (lines 28-50) only ever queries `env.logging.symptoms` and `env.logging.workouts`. Medication doses, water, weight, and nutrition entries never appear in the "Recents" row.
- **Recommendation:** Extend `RecentItem.Kind` with `.medication`, `.water`, `.weight`, `.nutrition` cases and populate them from the same repositories already used elsewhere in this file (`env.logging.nutrition`, `env.logging.adherence`, `env.measurements` for weight).
- **Why it matters:** The four excluded types are among the most frequently repeated daily logs (a daily med, a glass of water, a morning weigh-in), yet they get none of the 2-tap re-log benefit the recents row exists to provide.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster repeat-logging for the majority of daily entries, not just symptoms/workouts.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** LogHub view model, Logging/Measurement repositories
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users keep re-navigating full forms for the most repetitive log types.
- **Implementation notes:** Merge four additional query results into the same sorted `recents` array; cap total to a small number (e.g. 6) to keep the horizontal strip scannable.
- **First patch sketch:** Add cases to `RecentItem.Kind`, extend `load()` in `LogHubScreen.swift:28-50` to also pull last adherence/nutrition/weight records, and extend `destination(for:)` (line 227) accordingly.

### EASE-002 — Recent chip re-opens a blank form instead of repeating the entry

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `recentsSection` (`LogHubScreen.swift:203-224`) wraps each recent item in a `NavigationLink` to `destination(for:)` (lines 226-232), which pushes a fresh `SymptomLogView()`/`WorkoutLogView()` with no pre-filled values from the tapped item — the "recent" tap doesn't actually repeat anything.
- **Recommendation:** Add a true one-tap "log again" action that writes a new record with the same field values (symptom/activity/duration/etc.) immediately, with an undo affordance, instead of only navigating to an empty capture form.
- **Why it matters:** The UI implies a shortcut ("Recents") but delivers the same tap count as starting from scratch once the destination screen's own picker/fields are filled in.
- **Expected user impact:** True 1-tap repeat logging for the most common recurring entries.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** LogHub, Symptom/Workout logging repositories
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** "Recents" remains a misleading label for what is really just a filtered navigation shortcut.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a `logAgain(_:)` method to `LogHubViewModel` that inserts a record cloned from the recent item (new id/timestamp), then show a brief undo toast.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `logAgain` to `LogHubViewModel` calling `env.logging.insertSymptom`/`upsertWorkout` with today's timestamp, wire a secondary tap target on `RecentChip` (line 208-219) distinct from the existing NavigationLink.

### EASE-003 — Water quick sheet only offers two fixed amounts

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `WaterQuickSheet.amounts` is hardcoded to `[250, 500]` (`LogHubScreen.swift:309`) with no custom-amount entry and no memory of the user's usual amount.
- **Recommendation:** Add a "custom" option (numeric field) and default the top chip to the user's own most-frequently-logged amount instead of a fixed 250 ml.
- **Why it matters:** Many common serving sizes (330 ml can, 750 ml bottle, 1 L) aren't reachable without leaving the quick sheet.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer users falling back to the slower Nutrition flow just to log water.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** LogHub quick-add sheet
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users with non-250/500 ml habits get worse UX than one-off manual entry would give them.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a decimal text field row below the two chips, matching `WeightQuickSheet`'s input pattern already in the same file.

### EASE-004 — Weight quick sheet never pre-fills the last known value

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `WeightQuickSheet` (`LogHubScreen.swift:359-436`) starts `text` at `""` every time (line 364), forcing a full manual retype even though weight changes minimally day to day and the last value is already in the database.
- **Recommendation:** Pre-fill `text` with the most recent weight sample (formatted in the user's display unit) so a same-value re-log is a single tap on Save, and adjustment is a small edit rather than a full retype.
- **Why it matters:** Daily weigh-ins are one of the most repetitive logs in the app; retyping ~5 digits every day is avoidable friction.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster daily weight logging, especially for casual users doing simple confirmatory taps.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** LogHub, Measurement repository
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Small daily friction compounds across the app's most frequent manual metric.
- **Implementation notes:** Fetch `env.measurements` latest raw sample for `MetricID.weight` in `.task`/`onAppear` and seed `text` before the sheet renders.
- **First patch sketch:** In `WeightQuickSheet` (`LogHubScreen.swift:359-436`), add a `.task` that loads the latest weight sample via `env.measurements` and sets `text` to its formatted display value.

### EASE-005 — No confirmation after a quick water/weight log

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** Both `WaterQuickSheet.onLog` and `WeightQuickSheet.onLog` (lines 132-135, 407-415) call `dismiss()` immediately after saving with no toast, checkmark, or other feedback that the entry was recorded.
- **Recommendation:** Show a brief inline confirmation (checkmark animation or toast) before/as the sheet dismisses.
- **Why it matters:** Users have no positive signal the tap worked, which can lead to re-tapping "just in case" and creating duplicate entries.
- **Expected user impact:** More confidence per log, fewer accidental duplicate quick-logs.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** LogHub quick-add sheets
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Continued uncertainty-driven duplicate taps.
- **Implementation notes:** A simple `.overlay` checkmark with a short delay before `dismiss()` is enough; no new infra needed.

### EASE-006 — Log-type grid reflows tile positions when sensitive modules are off

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `logTypesSection` (`LogHubScreen.swift:142-180`) conditionally omits Symptom/Medication tiles entirely when `env.profile.sensitiveModulesEnabled` is false, and Nutrition when `env.profile.nutritionEnabled` is false — the grid silently goes from 4 tiles to 2, shifting every tile's position.
- **Recommendation:** Keep a stable tile count/order and grey out or hide via a settings link rather than removing tiles, or at minimum keep positions stable across the two most common configurations.

- **Importance:** 2

### EASE-007 — Log-type and quick-add sections use a fixed, non-usage-based order

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `logTypesSection` and `quickAddSection` (`LogHubScreen.swift:142-201`) hardcode tile order (Symptom, Medication, Workout, Nutrition, then Water, Weight) regardless of which types a given user actually logs most.
- **Recommendation:** Order tiles by the user's own logging frequency (derivable from the same repositories already queried in `load()`), falling back to the current fixed order for new users.

### EASE-008 — Recent-item time context hidden in casual mode

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `RecentChip`'s `detail` parameter is only populated `if env.depth.showsPowerDetail` (`LogHubScreen.swift:213-217`); casual-mode users see a label with no indication of when the recent item happened.

### EASE-009 — 30-day recents window drops infrequent loggers back to a blank state

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `LogHubViewModel.load()` (`LogHubScreen.swift:28-50`) queries `from: now.addingTimeInterval(-30 * 86_400)`; anyone who logs a chronic symptom or activity less than monthly gets an empty Recents row and loses the 2-tap shortcut entirely.
- **Recommendation:** Fall back to "last N entries regardless of date" when the 30-day window returns nothing, so infrequent loggers still get a shortcut to their own history.
- **Why it matters:** The users who benefit most from a shortcut (people who log rarely and don't remember exact dictionary terms) are the ones most likely to fall outside a 30-day cutoff.
- **Expected user impact:** Recents shortcut stays useful for low-frequency logging patterns.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** LogHub view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Recents silently stops working for exactly the users it would help most.
- **Implementation notes:** Change the repository call to `limit`-based rather than purely date-window-based, or widen the window and rely on `prefix(3)` for capping.

### EASE-010 — Quick-add sheets have no edit/undo path for the entry just logged

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `WaterQuickSheet`/`WeightQuickSheet` dismiss immediately on save (`LogHubScreen.swift:315-318`, `407-415`) with no way to reopen and correct the just-entered value from within the same interaction.
- **Recommendation:** Keep the sheet open briefly with an inline "Edit" / "Undo" action after save, mirroring the confirmation added in EASE-005.
- **Why it matters:** A fat-fingered decimal (e.g. 750 instead of 75.0 kg) currently requires navigating elsewhere to find and manually correct the record — there's no repository update method for raw samples either, compounding the gap.
- **Expected user impact:** Immediate, low-friction correction of the most common mistake in quick-entry flows.
- **ROI:** 3

- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** LogHub, Measurement/Logging repositories

- **Implementation notes:** Pair with the broader edit/delete work tracked in the Timeline correction items; the quick sheet only needs a thin "undo the entry I just made" affordance.

## Symptom log flow

### EASE-011 — Symptom picker orders "recents" by recency, not frequency

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `SymptomLogViewModel.load()` (`SymptomLogView.swift:88-114`) builds `recents` from the most recent 30 days of entries, deduplicated by first-seen order — a symptom logged 20 times last month but not since ranks below one logged once yesterday.
- **Recommendation:** Rank the recents row by logged-frequency (with recency as a tiebreaker) so the symptom a user actually logs most often is consistently first, as the assignment brief's "most-frequent symptom first" default implies.
- **Why it matters:** Chronic-symptom users (the primary beneficiaries of a fast picker) get an unstable, recency-biased ordering instead of a predictable one.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, more predictable symptom selection for repeat/chronic loggers.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The picker's "recents" shortcut under-serves exactly the users who log symptoms repeatedly.
- **Implementation notes:** Count occurrences per `symptomId` across the same 30-day query already run in `load()`, then sort by count desc before deduping.
- **First patch sketch:** In `load()` (`SymptomLogView.swift:88-114`), replace the first-seen dedup loop with a frequency count keyed by `symptomId`, sort by count, and rebuild `recents` from the top entries.

### EASE-012 — Severity always resets to a hardcoded default regardless of the symptom's own history

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `severity` starts at `3` (`SymptomLogView.swift:130`) and `resetForm()` resets it back to `3` (line 623) for every symptom, ignoring that a given symptom (e.g. a recurring migraine) may consistently be logged around a very different severity.
- **Recommendation:** Pre-set the slider to the user's own last-logged severity for that specific symptom when selecting from recents/search, keeping `3` only as the true cold-start default for symptoms never logged before.
- **Why it matters:** For a symptom that's reliably severe, starting the slider at "mild" (3) means an extra drag every single time before the entry reflects reality.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer slider adjustments for recurring symptoms; more accurate first-glance severity for new ones.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Recurring-symptom loggers keep re-doing the same slider adjustment on every entry.
- **Implementation notes:** When `select(_:)` is called with a `.known` choice, look up that symptom's most recent severity from `SymptomLogData`/a fresh query and seed `severity` from it.
- **First patch sketch:** In `select(_:)` (`SymptomLogView.swift:571-574`), for `.known(def)` look up the matching entry from the already-loaded recents/history and set `severity` before showing `captureForm`.

### EASE-017 — Severity is settable only via an imprecise slider

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `severityCard` (`SymptomLogView.swift:355-384`) exposes only a `Slider(value: $severity, in: 0...10, step: 1)`; there's no direct tap-to-select numeric control for users who know exactly which of the 11 values they want.
- **Recommendation:** Add a compact row of tappable 0–10 numeric buttons (or a segmented control) as an alternative/adjunct to the slider.
- **Why it matters:** Sliders are comparatively imprecise and slower to hit an exact value than a direct tap, and are harder to use for anyone with reduced fine-motor precision.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, more precise severity entry for users who already know their number.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging capture form
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Slower/less precise entry, particularly for accessibility-sensitive users.
- **Implementation notes:** Keep the slider for the "feel out a value" case; add a secondary compact digit row bound to the same `$severity` state.

### EASE-018 — "Save & add another" always returns to the picker root, losing search/category context

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `resetForm()` (`SymptomLogView.swift:620-629`) clears `selection` and `searchText` entirely, so logging a second related symptom (e.g. after "Nausea", logging "Headache" from the same "head"/"digestive" scroll position) starts the picker completely fresh.
- **Recommendation:** Preserve the last-used search text or expanded category context across a "Save & add another" cycle so a cluster of related symptoms can be logged without re-searching each time.
- **Why it matters:** Symptom clusters (e.g. migraine + nausea + light sensitivity) are commonly logged together in one sitting.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer repeated searches when logging multiple related symptoms back to back.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging capture form
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor added friction specifically for multi-symptom logging sessions.
- **Implementation notes:** Only clear `selection`, not `searchText`, in the `addAnother` branch of `save(_:addAnother:)` (line 612-614).

### EASE-019 — "Change" button silently discards severity/triggers/note with no confirmation

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `selectedHeader(_:)`'s "Change" button (`SymptomLogView.swift:343-350`) sets `selection = nil`, which per `body` (lines 139-160) routes back to `picker(data)` — but `severity`, `triggers`, `note`, and `occurredAt` are not reset, so switching symptom choice mid-entry silently discards whatever context was already valid, with no undo.
- **Recommendation:** Either preserve the already-entered severity/triggers/note when just swapping the symptom identity, or show a lightweight confirmation before discarding a partially-filled form.
- **Why it matters:** A mis-tap on "Change" after carefully setting severity and adding two triggers currently loses that work with no warning.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer accidental full-form resets from a single mis-tap.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging capture form
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Occasional lost partial entries from an easy-to-mis-tap control.
- **Implementation notes:** Simplest fix: don't reset `severity`/`triggers`/`note` when only `selection` changes; only `resetForm()` (the explicit post-save path) should clear everything.

### EASE-020 — 47-symptom dictionary is only browsable via per-category horizontal scroll

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `categorySections(_:)` (`SymptomLogView.swift:294-312`) renders each of the 8 categories as its own horizontally-scrolling chip row; browsing without search means scrolling right within each of up to 8 separate rows to see everything.
- **Recommendation:** Offer a consolidated, vertically-scrolling full list/grid view (e.g. behind a "Browse all" toggle) as an alternative to the current per-category horizontal rows.
- **Why it matters:** Finding an unfamiliar symptom by browsing (rather than by knowing the exact search term) currently requires up to 8 separate horizontal scroll gestures.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster browse-based discovery for symptoms the user doesn't know the exact name for.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging picker
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users default to typing guesses into search rather than browsing, or give up and use a generic custom label.
- **Implementation notes:** A single `LazyVGrid` of all 47 symptoms grouped by category header, reusing the existing `chip(title:...)` helper.

### EASE-021 — Category order is fixed dictionary order, never personalized

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `categorySections(_:)` iterates `data.categories` in the order returned by `env.symptoms.categories` (`SymptomLogView.swift:103-105`), which is the dictionary's static declaration order, not the user's own usage pattern.
- **Recommendation:** Order category sections by the user's own historical logging frequency per category, falling back to dictionary order for new users.
- **Why it matters:** A user who only ever logs digestive/sleep symptoms still scrolls past General/Head/Respiratory every time.
- **Expected user impact:** Shorter scroll to the relevant category for established users.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Persistent low-grade scroll friction for users with concentrated symptom categories.
- **Implementation notes:** Compute category frequency from the same history used for recents, sort `categories` accordingly in `load()`.

### EASE-022 — The documented "2-tap re-log" from recents actually requires the full capture form + Save

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** The file's own doc comment (`SymptomLogView.swift:119`) claims recents are a "2 taps" re-log path, but `select(.known(def))` (line 571-574, triggered from `recentsSection`) only sets `selection`, which routes into the full `captureForm` (severity slider, triggers, note, when, then Save) — genuinely completing a re-log takes at least 3 taps (chip, Save, and often a slider touch since severity resets per EASE-012).
- **Recommendation:** Either make the recents chip a true one-tap "log again with same values + undo" action (see EASE-002 for the LogHub equivalent), or update the comment/UX to intentionally support a fast-but-reviewable 2-step flow (chip → confirm) instead of the full form.
- **Why it matters:** The gap between the intended and actual tap count is exactly the kind of friction this audit is meant to surface.
- **Expected user impact:** A genuinely fast recents path for the highest-frequency use case (re-logging a known, recurring symptom).
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging picker/capture flow
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-012 (severity memory), EASE-002 (LogHub equivalent pattern)
- **Risk if skipped:** The app's own "under 10 seconds" framing (see the type's doc comment) remains aspirational rather than actual for the common recents case.
- **Implementation notes:** A "Log again" quick-confirm sheet showing the last values with a single Save button, falling through to the full form only if the user taps "Edit details."
- **First patch sketch:** Add a lightweight confirm sheet triggered from `recentsSection` (`SymptomLogView.swift:278-292`) that pre-fills severity/triggers/time from the matched history entry and saves directly on confirm.

### EASE-023 — No way to pin/favorite a chronic symptom independent of recency

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** The only "fast access" mechanism is `recentsSection` (`SymptomLogView.swift:278-292`), which is purely recency-driven (even after the EASE-011 frequency fix, it's still derived from actual logging history, not an explicit user choice).
- **Recommendation:** Let users explicitly pin one or more chronic symptoms (e.g. long-press a dictionary chip) so they always appear first regardless of recent logging gaps.
- **Why it matters:** A chronic-condition user managing a symptom that flares intermittently (e.g. monthly) wants a stable, explicit shortcut rather than one that depends on recent activity.
- **Expected user impact:** Predictable, user-controlled fast access for known chronic symptoms.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2

- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Symptom logging, CustomizationProfile (for storing pins)
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Chronic-condition users get a less predictable shortcut than a one-off logger.
- **Implementation notes:** Persist pinned symptom IDs in the profile/preferences store and merge them into the top of `SymptomLogData.recents`.

## Medication log flow

### EASE-027 — Resolved medication slots (Taken/Skipped) have no working correction path — the code for it is dead

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `MedicationLogView` declares `@State private var editingSlotId: String?` (`MedicationLogView.swift:283`) with a comment describing it as the "Resolved slot the user re-opened to change their choice," and `showActions` (line 371) is gated on `editingSlotId == slot.id`. But `editingSlotId` is only ever *reset to nil* (lines 329, 450, 493) — nothing in the file ever sets it to a slot's id. Compounding this, `statusTrailing(for:)` (lines 408-423) renders `.taken`/`.skipped` slots as a plain `StatusChip`/`skippedPill` with no `Button`/tap gesture at all. The two facts combine into a complete dead end: there is no way, anywhere in the UI, to tap an already-resolved dose and change it.
- **Recommendation:** Wrap the resolved-slot trailing view in a tappable control that sets `editingSlotId = slot.id`, re-showing `actionRow`/`skipReasonPicker` so Take↔Skip can be corrected after the fact.
- **Why it matters:** This is the single largest correction-flow gap in the logging surfaces: a mis-tap on Take vs Skip for a medication (a sensitive, adherence-tracked record) is currently unfixable from within the app.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can correct medication logging mistakes without needing to understand raw data export/inspection.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging view/view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A wrong tap on a sensitive adherence record is permanently unfixable through the app UI.
- **Implementation notes:** `insertAdherence` already uses a deterministic id (`"adh-\(regimenId)-\(dayKey)-\(time)"`, line 214) so re-recording the same slot with a different `kind` cleanly replaces the row — the data layer already supports this, only the tap target and state wiring are missing.
- **First patch sketch:** Wrap `statusTrailing(for:)`'s content (`MedicationLogView.swift:408-423`) in a `Button` that sets `editingSlotId = slot.id`; `showActions` (line 371) already reacts to that state correctly once it's actually set.

### EASE-028 — No undo window after Take / Skip / Take All

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `record(...)` (`MedicationLogView.swift:208-226`) commits `insertAdherence` immediately with no confirmation delay or undo affordance, and `takeAll(env:)` (lines 199-206) bulk-commits every pending slot the same way.
- **Recommendation:** Add a brief undo toast ("Marked taken · Undo") after any Take/Skip/Take-all action, giving a low-friction correction window that doesn't require the full editing flow from EASE-027.
- **Why it matters:** Most mis-taps are noticed within a second or two; a toast-based undo is far lower friction than reopening a resolved slot.
- **Expected user impact:** Immediate, near-zero-effort correction for the most common "oops, wrong button" case.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging view/view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users rely entirely on the heavier EASE-027 correction flow even for instantly-noticed mistakes.
- **Implementation notes:** A shared lightweight toast component would also serve EASE-094 (no undo pattern anywhere in the app).
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `@State private var lastAction: (slotId: String, previousStatus: SlotStatus)?` in `MedicationLogView`, set it in `take(_:)`/`skip(_:reason:)` callers, and show a toast with an undo button that re-records the previous status.

### EASE-029 — Building a daily schedule requires adding every dose time one at a time with no common presets

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `AddMedicationSheet.scheduleSection` (`MedicationLogView.swift:729-770`) only offers a `DatePicker` + "Add a time" button (lines 754-767); creating a common "twice daily" schedule requires operating the wheel picker and tapping "Add a time" twice, with no shortcut for round, common patterns (once/twice/three-times daily, morning+evening, etc.).
- **Recommendation:** Add quick-preset chips (e.g. "Once daily," "Twice daily," "3× daily") that populate sensible default times in one tap, with the existing picker still available for customization.
- **Why it matters:** Most real-world medication schedules fall into a handful of common patterns; the current flow treats every schedule as fully custom.
- **Expected user impact:** Adding a new medication with a standard schedule drops from ~4-6 interactions to 1-2.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** `AddMedicationSheet`
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Regimen creation stays disproportionately slow relative to how often it's a simple, common pattern.
- **Implementation notes:** Preset chips would each populate the `times` array directly (e.g. `["08:00", "20:00"]` for twice daily) rather than requiring per-time manual entry.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a preset chip row above the existing time-chip list in `scheduleSection` (`MedicationLogView.swift:729-770`) that sets `times` directly for the 2-3 most common patterns.

### EASE-030 — Strength field has no unit quick-picker

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `field(label: Loc.strength) { TextField(...) }` (`MedicationLogView.swift:702-706`) is a fully free-text field with only a placeholder hint ("e.g. 1000 IU," line 24) — every strength/unit combination is typed manually even though most fall into a handful of common units (mg, mcg, IU, mL, g).
- **Recommendation:** Add a small unit suffix picker (segmented control or menu) next to a numeric-only strength field, composing the two into the stored string.
- **Why it matters:** Reduces typing and unit-formatting inconsistency (e.g. "1000IU" vs "1000 IU" vs "1,000 IU") across a user's regimen list.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, more consistent strength entry.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** `AddMedicationSheet`
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor, cosmetic-adjacent friction.
- **Implementation notes:** Keep the free-text field as a fallback for unusual units; the picker only needs to cover the common cases.

### EASE-031 — "Take all" bulk-resolves every pending dose with zero review step

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `dueSection(_:)`'s "Take all" button (`MedicationLogView.swift:325-339`) calls `vm.takeAll(env:)`, which immediately marks every pending slot as taken (lines 199-206) with no list-review or per-item confirmation — a single tap can resolve four unrelated medications at once.
- **Recommendation:** Show a brief one-tap confirmation (or the undo toast from EASE-028) specifically for the bulk action, since it affects multiple records at once rather than one.
- **Why it matters:** A single mis-tap on "Take all" silently marks medications as taken that weren't actually taken, which is a meaningfully larger mistake than a single-slot mis-tap.
- **Expected user impact:** Safer bulk actions without adding friction to the common single-slot case.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-028 (shared undo mechanism covers this)
- **Risk if skipped:** A destructive-adjacent bulk action has the least protection of any action in the flow.
- **Implementation notes:** The undo toast from EASE-028 can double as the confirmation mechanism here — "4 doses marked taken · Undo" — without adding a blocking dialog.

### EASE-032 — Skip flow forces a reason despite copy implying it's optional

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `MedStrings.skipPrompt` reads "No problem — pick a reason if you'd like" (`MedicationLogView.swift:14-15`), but `skip(_:reason:)`'s signature requires a non-optional `SkipReason` (line 194-197), and `skipReasonPicker(for:)` (lines 481-521) offers no "skip without a reason" option — only `Cancel`, which aborts the skip entirely rather than completing it reason-less.
- **Recommendation:** Either add a "No reason" chip to the picker so skipping truly can be reason-less as the copy promises, or change the copy to reflect that a reason is required.
- **Why it matters:** The current mismatch between reassuring copy and enforced behavior undermines the wellness-safe, non-punitive tone the flow is explicitly designed around.
- **Expected user impact:** Skipping a dose becomes genuinely as low-friction as the copy already claims.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging capture flow
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A visible contradiction between wellness-safe copy and actual required behavior.
- **Implementation notes:** Add a `SkipReason`-independent "just skip" path (nil reason) alongside the existing chips, or make `skip(_:reason:)` accept `SkipReason?`.
- **First patch sketch:** Change `skip(_:reason:)` (`MedicationLogView.swift:194-197`) to accept `SkipReason?`, and add a "No reason" chip in `skipReasonPicker(for:)` (lines 481-521) that calls it with `nil`.

### EASE-035 — No UI to delete or discontinue a medication regimen, despite the repository already supporting it

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `LoggingRepository.deleteRegimen(id:at:)` (`LoggingRepository.swift:38-40`) already exists and soft-deletes a regimen, but `MedicationLogView.swift` never calls it — there is no delete, archive, or "end" button anywhere in `regimenCard(_:data:)` (lines 536-576) or elsewhere in the screen.

- **Dependencies:** None

- **Implementation notes:** `upsertRegimen` (`LoggingRepository.swift:17-25`) is already an `INSERT OR REPLACE` keyed by id, so editing in place is a small UI change, not a data-layer one.
- **First patch sketch:** Add an `editingRegimen: MedicationRegimen?` state to `MedicationLogView`, reuse `AddMedicationSheet` with pre-filled `@State` when non-nil, and call `vm.addRegimen` (renamed/overloaded to preserve the existing id).

### EASE-038 — Skip-reason grid is never ordered by the user's own most-common reason

- **Recommendation:** Sort the chips by the user's historical skip-reason frequency (from `env.logging.adherence`), keeping declaration order as the cold-start default.

### EASE-039 — No one-tap way to explicitly log a dose as "taken late," despite the data model supporting it

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `AdherenceKind.late` is a real case used by `TimelineAssembler.kindLabel` (`TimelineAssembler.swift:146-149`, rendering "Taken late"), but `MedicationLogView`'s `take(_:)` (lines 189-192) always records `kind: .taken` — there is no UI path that ever produces `.late`, making that Timeline label currently unreachable from the app's own logging flow.
- **Recommendation:** When a slot `isOverdue` (line 130, already computed), offer the Take button as "Take (late)" or otherwise record `.late` instead of `.taken` for overdue slots.
- **Why it matters:** The distinction already exists in the domain model and is already displayed elsewhere, but the logging flow that should produce it doesn't.
- **Expected user impact:** More accurate adherence records without any extra taps — this only requires branching on state already computed.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A modeled, displayed adherence state stays permanently unreachable from the app's own UI.
- **Implementation notes:** In `take(_:env:)` (line 189-192), branch `kind: slot.isOverdue ? .late : .taken` — no new UI control needed, just correct use of existing state.

### EASE-040 — New regimens always start "now," with no way to backdate when a medication actually began

### EASE-041 — No "duplicate this regimen" shortcut for a similar new medication

### EASE-042 — Take/Skip are equal-weight tap targets with no swipe shortcut for the majority action

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `actionRow(for:)` (`MedicationLogView.swift:446-479`) renders Take and Skip as identically-sized side-by-side buttons, and there is no swipe gesture anywhere in the file (or app-wide — confirmed no `.swipeActions`/`onLongPressGesture` usage) as a faster one-handed alternative to precisely tapping a button.

### EASE-043 — "Take" always records the current moment, with no "log for the scheduled time" option

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `take(_:env:)` (`MedicationLogView.swift:189-192`) always passes `occurredAt: now` into `record(...)`, even though `scheduledFor` (the slot's actual due time) is already available and distinct in the data model.
- **Recommendation:** When a user opens the app and takes a dose noticeably after actually swallowing it, allow recording against the scheduled time rather than forcing "now" as the only option — or at minimum expose the distinction if it matters to adherence accuracy.
- **Why it matters:** For a user who checks the app 20 minutes after actually taking a pill, the record's timestamp is subtly inaccurate with no way to correct it.
- **Expected user impact:** More accurate adherence timestamps without adding friction to the common "check app right after taking" case.

- **Importance:** 2

- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Medication logging view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor timestamp inaccuracy in adherence records; low visibility to most users.
- **Implementation notes:** Could be as simple as a long-press on Take offering "Log for [scheduled time]" as an alternate action.

### EASE-044 — Weekly schedules are modeled but not creatable through the UI

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `MedicationSchedule.weekly` is a real case handled by `scheduleText`/`scheduleDetail` (`MedicationLogView.swift:624-642`) and `dueTimes(onWeekday:)` elsewhere in the domain, but `AddMedicationSheet.scheduleSection` (lines 729-770) only exposes `Mode.daily`/`Mode.asNeeded` — there is no UI path to create a weekly (e.g. "Mondays and Thursdays") regimen at all.

- **Suggested owner:** Mobile

- **Implementation notes:** No domain/schema changes needed — `MedicationSchedule.weekly(days:times:)` and its rendering already exist; this is purely a missing UI mode.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `case weekly` to `AddMedicationSheet.Mode` (`MedicationLogView.swift:683`), a weekday picker row in `scheduleSection`, and branch `save()` (lines 848-857) to construct `.weekly(days:times:)`.

## Workout log flow

### EASE-049 — No date/time control at all; workouts can never be backdated

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `WorkoutLogViewModel.save(...)` (`WorkoutLogView.swift:92-109`) always computes `startAt: now.addingTimeInterval(-Double(minutes) * 60)` and `endAt: now` — there is no `DatePicker` or any state variable for a custom start time anywhere in `WorkoutLogView`, unlike `SymptomLogView`'s `whenCard`.
- **Recommendation:** Add a "When" control (defaulting to now, matching `SymptomLogView`'s pattern) so a workout done earlier today or yesterday can be logged accurately.
- **Why it matters:** Workouts are very commonly logged after the fact (post-shower, end of day); today the only way to log one is to pretend it just ended, corrupting the actual time-of-day record.
- **Expected user impact:** Accurate workout timestamps for the common after-the-fact logging case.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Workout logging view/view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Workout timing data is systematically inaccurate for any non-immediate logging, undermining anything downstream that reasons about time of day.
- **Implementation notes:** Add an `occurredAt`/end-time `DatePicker` mirroring `SymptomLogView.whenCard` (`SymptomLogView.swift:448-463`), then derive `startAt` from it minus `minutes` as today.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `@State private var endAt: Date = Date()` to `WorkoutLogView`, a `DatePicker` card similar to `whenCard`, and thread `endAt` through `vm.save(...)` in place of the hardcoded `now` in `WorkoutLogViewModel.save` (line 95-106).

### EASE-050 — Duration stepper alone requires many taps to reach common durations

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `durationCard` (`WorkoutLogView.swift:192-215`) only offers a `Stepper(value: $minutes, in: 1...360, step: 5)`; reaching a common 60-minute session from the default 30 requires 6 individual taps.
- **Recommendation:** Add quick-duration preset chips (15/30/45/60/90 min) above or beside the stepper, which remains for fine adjustment.
- **Why it matters:** Duration is set on every single workout log; a multi-tap stepper is the slowest part of an otherwise fast flow.
- **Expected user impact:** Duration entry for common session lengths drops to a single tap.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Workout logging capture form
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Duration entry remains the slowest step of an otherwise sub-10-second flow.
- **Implementation notes:** A row of chips setting `$minutes` directly, alongside the existing `Stepper`.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a chip row above the `Stepper` in `durationCard` (`WorkoutLogView.swift:192-215`) with fixed values that set `minutes` directly.

### EASE-051 — "Other" activity has no free-text sub-label, unlike Symptom's custom-label pattern

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `WorkoutActivity.other` (`WorkoutLogView.swift:37`) always stores the literal string `"Other"` on the record (via `activity.rawValue`, line 97) with no companion text field to specify what it actually was — contrast with `SymptomLogView`'s `.custom(String)` case, which captures a real label.
- **Recommendation:** When "Other" is selected, reveal a short free-text field (e.g. "What kind of activity?") and store it, similar to symptom's custom label handling.
- **Why it matters:** Every "Other" workout is currently indistinguishable from every other "Other" workout in Recent/Timeline views, permanently losing information the user actually typed nowhere.
- **Expected user impact:** "Other" workouts become individually identifiable instead of a generic bucket.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Workout logging capture form, `WorkoutEntry` model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** "Other" activity data stays permanently generic and unsearchable.

### EASE-055 — No save confirmation, and an inconsistent partial form reset after save

### EASE-059 — Activity pill order is fixed, never adapted to the user's actual usage

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `activityCard` (`WorkoutLogView.swift:151-165`) always renders `WorkoutActivity.allCases` in declaration order (Run, Walk, Strength, Cycle, Other) regardless of which activities a given user actually logs most.
- **Recommendation:** Order the pill row by the user's own historical activity frequency, falling back to the current fixed order for new users.
- **Why it matters:** A cyclist must scroll/tap past Run, Walk, and Strength on every single entry.

- **Affected systems:** Workout logging view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile

- **Risk if skipped:** Minor persistent scan friction for users with a strong activity preference.

### EASE-060 — Recovery-day messaging can't reflect a workout that hasn't been logged yet due to the backdating gap

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `recoveryCard` (`WorkoutLogView.swift:317-339`) shows "Nothing logged today — rest is part of movement too" whenever `!vm.loggedToday`; combined with EASE-049 (no backdating), a workout genuinely completed earlier today but not yet logged has no way to be entered with the correct time, so the recovery framing and the actual activity stay out of sync until EASE-049 ships.
- **Recommendation:** Ship alongside EASE-049; once backdating exists, `loggedToday` will correctly reflect same-day entries logged after the fact.
- **Why it matters:** The calm, non-judgmental recovery framing is undermined if it's showing "nothing logged" purely because of a UI gap rather than an actual rest day.
- **Expected user impact:** Recovery-day messaging becomes trustworthy once paired with real backdating support.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Workout logging view
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-049
- **Risk if skipped:** A minor but avoidable trust gap in an otherwise carefully-worded wellness-safe message.
- **Implementation notes:** No standalone work needed beyond EASE-049 — flagged here to ensure it's verified as resolved once that item ships.

### EASE-061 — Form state silently persists stale values across tab revisits with no staleness indicator

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `WorkoutLogView.body`'s `.task { vm.load(env) }` (line 146) has no `id:` parameter and `@State` fields (`activity`, `minutes`, `rpe`, `kcalText`, `distanceText`) aren't reset on reappearance — starting an entry, switching tabs, and returning later leaves the half-filled form exactly as it was, with no visual cue that it's stale.
- **Recommendation:** Either reset the form when the view reappears after a meaningful time gap, or add a subtle "resuming a draft" indicator so the user knows the values aren't fresh defaults.
- **Why it matters:** Under time pressure, a user could save with several-minutes-old leftover field values without realizing they never actually re-checked them.
- **Expected user impact:** Reduced risk of accidentally saving stale form values.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Workout logging view
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low-frequency but confusing edge case for interrupted logging sessions.
- **Implementation notes:** Track a `lastOpenedAt` and reset fields if the gap exceeds a threshold (e.g. 10 minutes) in `.task`.

### EASE-062 — No swipe/long-press "log again" shortcut on a recent workout row

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `workoutRow(_:)` (`WorkoutLogView.swift:341-380`) displays prior workouts directly below the entry form with no gesture to repeat one — a daily identical session (e.g. the same walk) requires refilling activity, duration, and RPE even though the exact prior values are rendered right there.
- **Recommendation:** Add a swipe or long-press "Log again" action on `workoutRow` that pre-fills (or directly re-saves with today's date, per EASE-002's pattern) the form from that entry.
- **Why it matters:** Directly implements the brief's "swipe/long-press shortcuts" and "one-tap repeat-last-entry" themes for the workout flow's own recent list.
- **Expected user impact:** Near-instant repeat logging for routine, identical daily activities.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Workout logging view/view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-049 (so the repeat can be dated correctly rather than always "now")
- **Risk if skipped:** Routine, repetitive workout logging stays as slow as logging a brand-new activity type every time.
- **Implementation notes:** Reuse the "log again + undo" pattern proposed in EASE-002 rather than building a separate mechanism.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `.swipeActions` (or `onLongPressGesture`) to `workoutRow(_:)` (`WorkoutLogView.swift:341-380`) that calls `vm.save(activity: w.activityType..., ...)` using the tapped entry's own field values.

## Nutrition log flow

### EASE-063 — No date/time control at all; meals can never be backdated

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `NutritionLogViewModel.save(...)` (`NutritionLogView.swift:42-58`) always sets `occurredAt: now`, and `NutritionLogView` has no `DatePicker`/time state anywhere — a meal eaten an hour ago (very common — few people log while actively eating) can only ever be recorded with the wrong timestamp.
- **Recommendation:** Add a "When" control defaulting to now, matching the pattern proposed for Workout (EASE-049) and already present in Symptom logging.
- **Why it matters:** Meal logging is disproportionately after-the-fact compared to other log types, making this gap especially costly here.
- **Expected user impact:** Accurate meal timestamps for realistic after-the-fact logging.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging view/view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Meal-timing data (used for "today's totals" and meal-type-by-hour defaults) is systematically inaccurate for anyone logging even slightly after eating.
- **Implementation notes:** Mirror the `whenCard` pattern from `SymptomLogView.swift:448-463`, capped at "now" like the symptom flow.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `@State private var occurredAt: Date = Date()` to `NutritionLogView`, a compact `DatePicker` row, and pass it into `vm.save(...)` in place of the hardcoded `now` in `NutritionLogViewModel.save` (line 42-58).

### EASE-064 — No recent-meal quick-repeat list; every description is retyped from scratch

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `descriptionCard` (`NutritionLogView.swift:116-123`) is a free-text field with no suggestions; `mealsSection` (lines 274-287) only shows *today's* already-logged meals for reference, not a tappable history to repeat from — a daily-repeated item (coffee, a standard lunch) is fully retyped every time.
- **Recommendation:** Add a "recent meals" quick-repeat row (similar to Symptom's recents) surfacing the user's own frequently-logged descriptions as one-tap chips that pre-fill (or directly log, per EASE-002's pattern) description/mealType/kcal/protein.
- **Why it matters:** Repeated identical meals are extremely common and currently get zero benefit from the app's own logging history.
- **Expected user impact:** Large reduction in typing for the most repetitive food-logging pattern.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging view/view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Nutrition logging remains disproportionately high-friction relative to how repetitive real diets actually are.
- **Implementation notes:** Aggregate distinct `description` values (with their most recent kcal/protein/mealType) from `env.logging.nutrition` history, ranked by frequency.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `recentMeals: [NutritionEntry]` (deduped by description) computed in `NutritionLogViewModel.load()` (`NutritionLogView.swift:32-39`), and render as a chip row above `descriptionCard` that pre-fills the form fields on tap.

### EASE-065 — Meal-type default is only computed once per screen visit, not re-evaluated for a second meal in the same session

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `didSetInitialMeal` (`NutritionLogView.swift:76, 105-109`) guards `mealForHour(...)` to run exactly once per view lifecycle; logging breakfast, then returning a few hours later within the same navigation session to log lunch, keeps `mealType` stuck on the earlier guess instead of re-deriving it from the new current hour.
- **Recommendation:** Re-evaluate the hour-based default meal type after each successful save (or whenever the form is "fresh," i.e. `descriptionText` is empty), not just on first appearance.
- **Why it matters:** The whole point of the time-based default is to save a tap — leaving it stale after the first save defeats that purpose for same-session repeat use.
- **Expected user impact:** The meal-type default stays useful for realistic multi-meal-per-visit sessions.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging capture form
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A well-intentioned smart default silently stops working after the first entry in a session.
- **Implementation notes:** In `saveButton`'s action (`NutritionLogView.swift:226-233`), after clearing `descriptionText`, also re-run `Self.mealForHour(...)` against the current hour.

### EASE-066 — "Quick calories" preference isn't remembered across sessions

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `quickCalories` always initializes to `false` (`NutritionLogView.swift:75`) — a user who consistently prefers the low-detail quick-entry mode must re-toggle it every single visit.
- **Recommendation:** Persist the user's last-used toggle state (e.g. via the profile/preferences store) and restore it as the default.
- **Why it matters:** For users who've deliberately chosen the lower-friction quick-calorie mode as their standard habit, the app resets that choice every time.
- **Expected user impact:** One fewer toggle tap per meal for users with a consistent logging style.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging capture form, preferences storage
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-099 (shared last-used-value memory mechanism)
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor but repeated toggle friction for quick-calorie users.
- **Implementation notes:** Fold into the shared "remember last-used values" work proposed in EASE-099 rather than a one-off flag.

### EASE-067 — No portion-size shortcuts; every kcal/protein value is manual decimal-pad typing

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `numberField(icon:placeholder:text:unit:)` (`NutritionLogView.swift:208-223`) is the only input mechanism for both `kcalText` and `proteinText` — there's no small/medium/large or common-serving quick-fill, so a tiny snack takes exactly as much typing as a full meal.
- **Recommendation:** Add optional portion-size quick-fill chips (e.g. "Small," "Medium," "Large" or common preset kcal values) above the numeric fields.
- **Why it matters:** Reduces typing for the (very common) case of a rough, "good enough" quick-calorie estimate rather than a precise figure.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster entry for approximate/quick logging, which is already the app's own stated intent for the `lowDetail` mode.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes

- **Suggested owner:** Mobile

### EASE-068 — Disabled Save only dims via opacity, giving no explanation for a silent no-op tap

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `saveButton` (`NutritionLogView.swift:225-246`) sets `.background(BadanColor.primary.opacity(canSave ? 1 : 0.4), ...)` and `.disabled(!canSave)` (line 242, 245) — tapping it while `descriptionText` is empty produces no error message, just a subtle opacity difference that's easy to miss.
- **Recommendation:** Add a brief inline hint ("Add a description to save") when Save is tapped while disabled, or make the disabled state more visually explicit.
- **Why it matters:** A user who taps a dimmed-but-not-obviously-disabled button gets no feedback at all about why nothing happened.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer feedback loop when Save doesn't work as expected.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`

- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None

### EASE-069 — No guard against duplicate-save on rapid double-tap

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `saveButton`'s action (`NutritionLogView.swift:226-235`) calls `vm.save(...)` directly with no in-flight/disabled state beyond the `canSave` description check; `upsertNutrition` always inserts a fresh `ULID`-keyed row (`NutritionLogViewModel.save`, lines 42-58), so a fast double-tap while `canSave` is true creates two meal entries.
- **Recommendation:** Disable Save for the duration of the save call, matching EASE-016/EASE-056.
- **Why it matters:** Silent duplicate meal entries would double-count kcal/protein in `totalsSection`.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer accidental duplicate meal records and more trustworthy daily totals.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`

- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Silent data-quality erosion directly visible in the day's own totals bar.
- **Implementation notes:** Same `isSaving` flag pattern as EASE-016/EASE-056.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `@State private var isSaving = false` to `NutritionLogView`, set it around the `vm.save(...)` call in `saveButton` (lines 226-235), and combine with the existing `.disabled(!canSave)`.

### EASE-070 — No way to edit or delete a logged meal from within the app

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `mealRow(_:)` (`NutritionLogView.swift:289-326`) renders each meal as a static `BadanCard` with no tap target, swipe action, or context menu; `LoggingRepository` has no `deleteNutrition`/`updateNutrition` method (confirmed — only `upsertNutrition`/`nutrition(from:to:)` exist, `LoggingRepository.swift:132-147`).
- **Recommendation:** Add repository delete/update methods for nutrition entries (mirroring the existing soft-delete pattern) and wire a swipe-to-delete / tap-to-edit affordance on `mealRow`.
- **Why it matters:** A mistyped description or wrong kcal/protein value — including any duplicate created by EASE-069's gap — can never be corrected or removed once saved.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can fix mistakes in their nutrition history without raw data access, and daily totals stay trustworthy.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/LoggingRepository.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging view, LoggingRepository
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** A wrong meal entry permanently and silently skews "Today's totals" with no recovery path.
- **Implementation notes:** `nutrition_entries` already has a `deleted_at` column used in the existing `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` query, so a soft-delete method follows the exact existing pattern.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `deleteNutrition(id:at:)` to `LoggingRepository.swift` (mirroring `deleteSymptom`, lines 84-86), and add `.swipeActions` on `mealRow(_:)` (`NutritionLogView.swift:289-326`) calling it through a new `NutritionLogViewModel.delete(_:env:)`.

### EASE-071 — Today's totals only recompute via a full reload, giving no fast way to spot an accidental double-count

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `kcalTotal`/`proteinTotal` are only recalculated inside `load(env)` (`NutritionLogView.swift:32-39`), called after every save — an accidental duplicate entry (EASE-069) silently inflates the totals bar with no per-entry breakdown or warning shown alongside `totalsSection`.

- **Expected user impact:** Faster detection of a mis-logged or duplicate entry.

- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Nutrition logging view
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-070
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor; mostly relevant once duplicate-detection matters more (i.e. after EASE-069/070 land).

## Home logging entry points

### EASE-077 — MedsModuleCard always full-navigates; no direct Take/Skip from Home

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `MedsModuleCard` (`HomeScreen.swift:338-381`) wraps its entire content in a single `NavigationLink { MedicationLogView() }` — even though the card already shows "N due" (line 359-364), tapping it always requires a second full screen navigation and then visually locating the right slot before a dose can be marked.
- **Recommendation:** Add a direct "Take" quick-action (e.g. a small button within the card, distinct from the card's own navigation tap) for the single-next-due dose when there's exactly one or a small number due.
