## Timeline & correction flows

### EASE-085 — TimelineEvent's `deletable` flag is dead: no delete UI exists anywhere on the unified feed

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `TimelineEvent` (`apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Timeline.swift:46-56`) defines a `deletable: Bool` explicitly set `true` for medication, meal, and note events in `TimelineAssembler.swift` (lines 102, 112, 120), but `TimelineScreen.swift`'s `eventRow(_:)` (lines 88-134) has no swipe action, context menu, or any interaction at all. The domain model already knows which rows should be deletable; the view simply never asks.
- **Recommendation:** Add `.swipeActions` (or a context menu) to `eventRow`, gated on `event.deletable`, wired to per-type delete methods (see EASE-087 for the missing repository methods this depends on).
- **Why it matters:** Timeline is the app's single unified view across all log types — it's the most natural place for a correction affordance, and it already tracks exactly which rows should support one.
- **Expected user impact:** A single, consistent place to delete a wrong log entry regardless of which screen originally created it.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Timeline.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Timeline view, LoggingRepository
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-087 (repository delete methods for the 4 event types that currently lack them)
- **Risk if skipped:** The app's own domain model has been tracking "is this row correctable" since it was written, with the corresponding UI never built.
- **Implementation notes:** `eventRow` is a plain `HStack`, not a `List` row, so `.swipeActions` requires wrapping the day's events in a `List` or implementing a custom swipe gesture.

### EASE-086 — Timeline rows have no tap target to view or reach the source record at all

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `eventRow(_:)` (`TimelineScreen.swift:88-134`) has zero tap handling — sleep, workout, medication, symptom, meal, and note rows are all purely informational. A user spotting an entry they want to investigate or fix has to remember which screen it came from and navigate there manually (and even then, most of those screens have no edit affordance either, per EASE-035/057/070).
- **Recommendation:** Add a tap gesture on `eventRow` that navigates to (or opens a detail sheet for) the originating record.
- **Why it matters:** Timeline is explicitly described in its own code comments as the "anti-fragmentation spine" (`TimelineAssembler.swift:3-8`), but currently fragments the correction workflow worse than the individual log screens do, since it offers no path back to the source at all.
- **Expected user impact:** Timeline becomes a genuine hub for reviewing and acting on past entries, not just a read-only feed.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Timeline view
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Timeline stays a dead-end summary rather than the correction/review hub its own design intent implies.
- **Implementation notes:** Minimal version: a detail sheet showing the full record's fields (reusing existing row-rendering logic from each log screen) even before per-type edit support exists.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `.onTapGesture` to `eventRow(_:)` (`TimelineScreen.swift:88-134`) presenting a simple read-only detail sheet keyed by `event.sourceRecordId`/`event.type`, as a first step before full edit support.

### EASE-087 — LoggingRepository has no delete method for workouts, nutrition, or notes

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `LoggingRepository.swift` has `deleteRegimen(id:at:)` (lines 38-40) and `deleteSymptom(id:at:)` (lines 84-86), but no `deleteWorkout`, `deleteNutrition`, or `deleteNote`/`updateNote` — even though `workout_entries`, `nutrition_entries`, and `note_entries` all already have a `deleted_at` column used in their existing `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` read queries (lines 126, 145, 158).
- **Recommendation:** Add the three missing soft-delete methods following the exact existing pattern, as a prerequisite for any Timeline or per-screen delete UI (EASE-057, EASE-070, EASE-085).
- **Why it matters:** This is the single blocking piece of foundational work behind essentially every correction-flow item in this section — the schema already supports it, only the repository methods are missing.
- **Expected user impact:** Unblocks delete UI across Workout, Nutrition, and Timeline.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Storage/Repositories/LoggingRepository.swift`
- **Affected systems:** LoggingRepository
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** No downstream delete UI (Workout, Nutrition, Timeline) can be built without this.
- **Implementation notes:** Three near-identical one-line SQL `UPDATE ... SET deleted_at = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?` methods, copy-pasted from `deleteSymptom`'s pattern (line 84-86) against `workout_entries`, `nutrition_entries`, and `note_entries` respectively.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `deleteWorkout(id:at:)`, `deleteNutrition(id:at:)`, and `deleteNote(id:at:)` to `LoggingRepository.swift`, mirroring `deleteSymptom` (lines 84-86) exactly against the other three tables.

### EASE-088 — No update/edit repository method exists for any structured log type

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** Every `upsert*` method in `LoggingRepository.swift` (`upsertRegimen`, `insertSymptom`, `upsertWorkout`, `upsertNutrition`, `upsertNote`) is an `INSERT OR REPLACE` keyed by a caller-supplied id, and none of the four primary capture screens (Symptom, Medication regimen, Workout, Nutrition) ever load an existing record's values back into their form for editing — every "edit" would currently have to be a delete-and-fully-retype.
- **Recommendation:** Standardize an "open for edit" pattern across the four capture screens: load an existing record's fields into the same `@State` variables the create flow already uses, then save via the existing `upsert*` method (which already supports replace-by-id).
- **Why it matters:** This is the shared missing piece behind EASE-036 (medication), and the natural next step after EASE-057/070/087 add delete support — delete without edit only lets users remove mistakes, not correct them.
- **Expected user impact:** Genuine in-place correction of any log entry, not just delete-and-redo.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** All four logging capture screens, LoggingRepository
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-087
- **Risk if skipped:** Every correction across the app's four primary logging surfaces remains delete-and-retype at best, or entirely impossible at worst.
- **Implementation notes:** No data-layer changes needed beyond EASE-087 — `upsert*` methods already support id-based replace; this is purely "add a `editing: T?` parameter to each capture view and pre-fill `@State` from it."

- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`

### EASE-091 — Timeline doesn't reliably refresh after logging something in a different tab

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `TimelineViewModel.load(env:)` is only triggered via `.task(id: env.profile)` (`TimelineScreen.swift:41`) — it reloads on profile/presentation changes, not after returning from a logging screen. Since Timeline and LogHub are separate tabs (separate `NavigationStack`s per `RootView.swift:29-44`), a user who logs a symptom via the Log tab and then switches to Timeline may see a stale feed until some other trigger causes a reload.
- **Recommendation:** Reload Timeline data whenever the tab becomes visible again (e.g. via `.onAppear` in addition to the existing `.task(id:)`), not only on profile changes.
- **Why it matters:** Undermines confidence that Timeline reflects what was "just logged," which matters most exactly when a user wants to immediately verify or correct an entry.
- **Expected user impact:** Timeline reliably shows the latest state after any logging action, regardless of tab-switch order.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** Timeline view model
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users may believe a log didn't save because Timeline hasn't caught up, prompting unnecessary duplicate re-logging.
- **Implementation notes:** Add `.onAppear { vm.load(env) }` alongside the existing `.task(id: env.profile)` modifier (`TimelineScreen.swift:33-42`).
- **First patch sketch:** Add `.onAppear { vm.load(env) }` to `TimelineScreen.body` (`TimelineScreen.swift:33-42`), keeping the existing `.task(id:)` for profile-driven reloads.

- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** All row-rendering logging views
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Each correction-flow item risks a separate, inconsistent custom-gesture implementation instead of one shared pattern.
- **Implementation notes:** Converting `BadanCard`-in-`VStack` row rendering to `List`-backed rows has styling implications (default `List` chrome vs. the app's custom card styling) that need a small design pass alongside the engineering work.

### EASE-094 — No undo pattern exists anywhere in the app for any committed logging action

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** Every logging action across Symptom, Medication (Take/Skip/Take All), Workout, and Nutrition commits immediately via a repository call with no confirmation delay, toast, or undo mechanism (confirmed across all four files) — once a record is written, the only way to fix a mistake is a compensating manual correction, and for most types (workouts, meals, notes — see EASE-057/070/085) there isn't even that.
- **Recommendation:** Build one shared, reusable "undo toast" component (a lightweight snackbar with a timed undo action) and adopt it across Take/Skip/Take-all (EASE-028), and any future delete actions (EASE-085).
- **Why it matters:** This is the single most impactful shared pattern for correction-flow friction across the entire logging surface — one component, reused everywhere, rather than five bespoke fixes.
- **Expected user impact:** A consistent, low-effort recovery path for the most common mistake (an immediately-noticed mis-tap) across every logging screen.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/`
- **Affected systems:** DesignSystem (new shared component), all logging views
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every individual undo/correction item in this section (EASE-010, 028) gets built as a one-off instead of sharing infrastructure.
- **Implementation notes:** A single `UndoToast` DesignSystem component (overlay + timer + action closure) added once, then referenced from each save/take/skip call site.

## Cross-cutting

### EASE-095 — No logging form dismisses the keyboard on scroll

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** A repo-wide search confirms zero uses of `.scrollDismissesKeyboard` in `Features/Symptom`, `Features/Medication`, `Features/WorkoutNutrition`, or `Features/LogHub` — after tapping any text field (note, name, strength, description, custom symptom, trigger), the keyboard can obscure the Save button with no way to dismiss it except tapping precisely on empty space.
- **Recommendation:** Add `.scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively)` to the `ScrollView` in each of the four capture screens.
- **Why it matters:** This is a single-line fix that improves save-button reachability across every text-entry point in the logging surface at once.
- **Expected user impact:** The keyboard no longer traps users away from the Save button on any logging screen.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** All logging capture screens
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Continued avoidable keyboard-obscures-Save friction on every text field in the app.
- **Implementation notes:** One modifier per top-level `ScrollView` (e.g. `SymptomLogView.swift:140`, `WorkoutLogView.swift:132`, `NutritionLogView.swift:86`, `MedicationLogView.swift:287`, `AddMedicationSheet` at `MedicationLogView.swift:693`).
- **First patch sketch:** Add `.scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively)` to each `ScrollView` listed above — a mechanical, low-risk change with no behavior beyond keyboard dismissal.

### EASE-096 — Decimal-pad fields have no keyboard "Done" toolbar button

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** Every numeric `TextField` across the logging screens (`kcalText`/`distanceText` in Workout, `kcalText`/`proteinText` in Nutrition, `WeightQuickSheet.text` in LogHub) uses `.keyboardType(.decimalPad)`, which has no built-in Return/Done key on iOS — the only dismissal is tapping outside the field.
- **Recommendation:** Add a shared `ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard)` with a "Done" button to each of these fields.
- **Why it matters:** Decimal-pad is the one keyboard type on iOS that structurally lacks a dismiss key, making this a real (not cosmetic) gap rather than redundant with EASE-095's scroll-dismiss fix — a stationary form (no scroll needed) still has no way to close the keyboard without EASE-096.
- **Expected user impact:** A reliable, discoverable way to close the numeric keyboard on every decimal field in the app.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** All numeric-entry logging fields
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Decimal-pad fields remain the one input type with no first-class dismissal affordance.
- **Implementation notes:** A small reusable `View` extension (`.decimalPadDoneButton()`) applied to `numberField(...)` in both Workout and Nutrition, and to `WeightQuickSheet`'s field.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard)` with a "Done" button (using `@FocusState`) to `numberField(...)` in `WorkoutLogView.swift:259-274` and `NutritionLogView.swift:208-223`, and to `WeightQuickSheet` (`LogHubScreen.swift:359-436`).

### EASE-097 — No shared in-flight save state; duplicate-save guard is missing consistently across all four forms

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** As detailed individually in EASE-016 (Symptom), EASE-056 (Workout), and EASE-069 (Nutrition), none of the four primary capture screens disable Save while a write is in flight, and each `upsert*`/`insert*` call creates a fresh id-keyed row — rapid double-tapping is a real, reproducible way to create duplicate entries anywhere in the logging surface.
- **Recommendation:** Rather than patching each screen individually, add one small shared `@State`/view-modifier pattern (or a reusable "debounced save button" component) and apply it consistently across all four forms in one pass.
- **Why it matters:** The same bug exists independently in three (and effectively four, since Medication's `take`/`skip` share the same fire-and-forget pattern) separate places — fixing it once, consistently, is both cheaper and more reliable than three or four bespoke patches.
- **Expected user impact:** Elimination of an entire class of silent duplicate-entry bugs across the app.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** All logging capture screens
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The duplicate-save bug keeps getting independently rediscovered and independently patched (or missed) screen by screen.
- **Implementation notes:** A small `SavingButton`/`isSaving` helper in DesignSystem, adopted by all four screens' Save actions and Medication's `take`/`skip` calls in one coordinated change.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a tiny `@Observable` `SaveGuard` helper (or simple `isSaving` `@State` convention) and apply it to the four Save button actions identified in EASE-016/056/069, plus `MedicationLogView`'s `take`/`skip` call sites.

### EASE-098 — No logging form persists an in-progress draft across backgrounding

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** None of the four primary capture screens (Symptom, Workout, Nutrition, `AddMedicationSheet`) persist their `@State` form values anywhere beyond in-memory view state — a low-memory tab switch, a phone call, or simply backgrounding the app mid-entry loses all typed values with no restoration on return.
- **Recommendation:** Persist in-progress form state for at least the highest-friction forms (Symptom capture, `AddMedicationSheet`) to a lightweight local draft store, restored on next open and cleared on successful save.
- **Why it matters:** Losing a partially-completed symptom or medication entry to an interruption (a phone call is a very plausible interruption mid-log) means redoing several taps of work from scratch.
- **Expected user impact:** Interrupted logging sessions can be resumed instead of restarted.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 4
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** All logging capture screens, local draft persistence
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Interrupted logging sessions lose all progress, discouraging the very "log it in the moment" behavior the app is designed to encourage.
- **Implementation notes:** A small `UserDefaults`-backed draft codable struct per form type, saved on `scenePhase` change to `.background` and cleared after successful save.

### EASE-099 — No last-used-value memory anywhere; every "smart default" is a hardcoded constant

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** A repo-wide search confirms zero uses of `UserDefaults`/`@AppStorage` in `Features/Symptom`, `Features/Medication`, `Features/WorkoutNutrition`, or `Features/LogHub` — every default called out elsewhere in this section (severity=3, RPE=5, minutes=30, activity=.run, mealType-by-hour, quickCalories=false) is a fixed constant in code, not a learned preference. The app never gets faster to use the more a specific person actually uses it.
- **Recommendation:** Introduce one small shared "last-used values" preference layer (per log type) that each capture screen reads for its initial `@State` and writes to on successful save.
- **Why it matters:** This is the foundational piece behind roughly a dozen individual items in this section (EASE-012, 052, 053, 059, 066, and others) — building it once as shared infrastructure is far more efficient than a dozen separate ad hoc persistence mechanisms.
- **Expected user impact:** The app's defaults converge toward each user's actual habits over time instead of staying static forever.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/LogHubScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** All logging capture screens, new lightweight preferences layer
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Every individual "remember the last value" item in this section keeps being proposed and built independently instead of sharing one mechanism.
- **Implementation notes:** A small `@AppStorage`-backed or `CustomizationProfile`-integrated key-value store, namespaced per log type, read in each screen's `.task`/`init` and written in each `save(...)` call.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a small `LastUsedDefaults` helper (`@AppStorage`-backed, one key per field-per-log-type) and wire it into `WorkoutLogView`'s `activity`/`rpe` initial state (`WorkoutLogView.swift:122-124`) as the first concrete adoption, since it's the simplest of the four screens to retrofit.

### EASE-100 — Save-button reachability is inconsistent across the four logging forms

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `SymptomLogView` and `MedicationLogView`'s `AddMedicationSheet` place Save at the bottom of a variable-height card stack (below trigger chips / a growing time-chip list, `SymptomLogView.swift:480-506`, `MedicationLogView.swift:715-723` toolbar-based) while `WorkoutLogView`/`NutritionLogView` place an inline Save button above their respective "recent" lists (`WorkoutLogView.swift:276-293`, `NutritionLogView.swift:225-246`) — the two pairs use structurally different reachability strategies (scroll-to-bottom vs. toolbar vs. inline-above-list) with no shared convention.
- **Recommendation:** Converge on one consistent Save-reachability pattern across all four forms — either a persistent bottom action bar for all of them, or the toolbar-confirmation-action pattern already used successfully in `AddMedicationSheet`.
- **Why it matters:** The number of scroll gestures needed to reach Save currently varies unpredictably screen to screen for no functional reason, adding inconsistent friction depending on which log type a user happens to be using.
- **Expected user impact:** Predictable, consistently-reachable Save action regardless of which log type is being used or how long the form has grown.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Symptom/SymptomLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Medication/MedicationLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/WorkoutLogView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/WorkoutNutrition/NutritionLogView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** All logging capture screens
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Continued unpredictable, screen-dependent Save-button reachability across the app's core logging surfaces.
- **Implementation notes:** The toolbar-confirmation pattern already proven in `AddMedicationSheet` (`MedicationLogView.swift:719-722`) is the lowest-risk convention to standardize on, since it keeps Save reachable regardless of scroll position without a new sticky-bar component.

Scope: Onboarding, Permissions, Discoverability, Terminology, Interpretation on iOS.

### EASE-101 — Onboarding asks for depth (casual/power) before showing any real data

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `OnboardingView.depthPage` (apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift:212-236) forces a "Keep it simple" vs "Show me detail" choice on step 3, before the user has seen a single real screen or metric. `footer` even disables Next until a choice is made (`let disabled = (step == 2 && selectedDepth == nil)`, line 314), so a first-time user with no context must commit to an abstraction they cannot yet evaluate.
- **Recommendation:** Default silently to `.balanced` (already the app default) and move the explicit depth choice into Settings-on-first-visit or a contextual prompt shown after the user has seen the Home screen once, rather than gating onboarding progress on it.
- **Why it matters:** Asking users to self-classify their own data literacy before they've seen the product is a well-known onboarding anti-pattern — it adds a decision with no information to decide from.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer stalled onboarding sessions at step 3; users reach real data one screen sooner.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** New users bounce or guess at step 3 rather than making an informed choice.
- **Implementation notes:** Remove the `disabled` gate on step 2's Next button; keep the depth cards but make choosing optional (skippable), defaulting to `.balanced`.
- **First patch sketch:** In `OnboardingView.swift`, delete the `disabled(disabled)`/`opacity` lines in `footer` (312-324) so Next always advances on step 2; leave `selectedDepth` write-through unchanged.

### EASE-102 — "Connect health data" primary CTA does not request HealthKit authorization

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `connectPage` (OnboardingView.swift:277-308) wires its primary button to `{ env.completeOnboarding() }` — identical to the secondary "Continue without connecting" button. `HealthKitAdapter.requestAuthorization` (apps/ios/Sources/Platform/Health/HealthKitAdapter.swift:24-34) exists but is never called from anywhere in the app (verified via repo-wide search). Tapping "Connect health data" produces no system permission sheet and silently behaves exactly like skipping.
- **Recommendation:** Call `env.healthStore.requestAuthorization` (or equivalent) from the primary button's action before completing onboarding, and only fall through to `completeOnboarding()` once the callback returns.
- **Why it matters:** This is the single highest-impact comprehension bug in the onboarding flow — the CTA makes an explicit promise ("Connect health data") the code does not keep, and the user has no way to discover this short of noticing HealthKit's system dialog never appeared.
- **Expected user impact:** Users who intend to connect Apple Health currently believe they have when they have not; fixing this closes that gap entirely.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Platform/Health/HealthKitAdapter.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/App/AppEnvironment.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding, Health source abstraction
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** HealthKit entitlement wiring (real reads are still stubbed in `HealthKitAdapter.readSamples/readIntervals/readSessions`).
- **Risk if skipped:** Users make a real trust decision ("connect my health data") that the app never honors; discovered later this reads as a privacy/trust violation, not just a bug.
- **Implementation notes:** Even a partial fix — actually presenting the system permission sheet, even if reads stay stubbed post-MVP — closes the comprehension gap; the read-mapping TODOs can land separately.
- **First patch sketch:** In `connectPage`'s primary button closure, call `HealthKitAdapter().requestAuthorization { granted, _ in DispatchQueue.main.async { env.completeOnboarding() } }` instead of completing immediately.

### EASE-103 — Onboarding never discloses that seeded demo data will appear regardless of the connect choice

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** Neither `connectPage` nor any earlier onboarding step (OnboardingView.swift) mentions that `SeedController.seedIfNeeded` (apps/ios/Sources/App/SeedController.swift:28-31) will populate 90 days of synthetic data the moment onboarding completes, independent of whether the user connected a source or tapped "Continue without connecting."
- **Recommendation:** Add one sentence to `connectPage`'s subtitle or a follow-up first-Home-visit callout: "We've filled BADAN with sample data so you can explore — replace it any time in Settings."
- **Why it matters:** A user who chooses "Continue without connecting" and then sees a full readiness score, sleep history and HRV trend on Home has no way to know it isn't theirs.
- **Expected user impact:** Removes a first-run trust/comprehension gap that otherwise persists until the user stumbles onto Settings → "Reset demo data."
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/App/SeedController.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding, Seed data
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** New users mistake synthetic data for a working real integration, then lose trust when they realize (e.g., during a demo or app-store review) it was fake all along.
- **Implementation notes:** Wellness-safe, low-alarm phrasing; keep it to one sentence per the product's calm tone.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `Text` line under `connectSubtitle` in `connectPage` (OnboardingView.swift:283-291) with a new `LocalizedString` disclosing sample data.

### EASE-104 — Four onboarding steps mix orientation, values, configuration and action with no differentiation of importance

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `OnboardingView.body` (lines 22-45) treats "Welcome", "Why BADAN", "How much detail?" and "Connect" as four equally-weighted, equally-paced pages behind identical Next/Back controls, even though only the last step has consequence and the middle two are pure reading.
- **Recommendation:** Collapse the "Why BADAN" value cards (valuePage, lines 168-208) into the welcome page as three short bullet icons rather than a separate swipe, cutting total steps from 4 to 3.
- **Why it matters:** Fewer, denser steps reduce the perceived length of setup without losing content — the three value cards are read-only and add no branching.
- **Expected user impact:** ~25% fewer swipes/taps to reach the working app on first launch.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor; onboarding remains slightly longer than necessary.
- **Implementation notes:** Update `lastStep`/`pageCount` and `progressDots` accordingly if merged.
- **First patch sketch:** Merge `valueCard` calls from `valuePage` into `welcomePage`'s VStack; remove the `valuePage` case and decrement `lastStep` to 2.

### EASE-105 — Skip button abandons the depth choice silently, leaving users on an unexplained "Balanced" default

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** Tapping "Skip" at any step before the last (`header`, OnboardingView.swift:72-83) calls `env.completeOnboarding()` directly, bypassing `depthPage` entirely. Because `CustomizationProfile.depthPolicy` defaults to `.balanced` (Domain/Customization.swift:96), skip-path users land on a depth level that was never presented as a choice anywhere in onboarding — only "Simple" and "Show me detail" were ever shown as options (depthPage, lines 227-230).
- **Recommendation:** Either surface "Balanced" as a visible third onboarding option (matching Settings' three-way `DepthPolicy.allCases`), or explicitly state in the skip confirmation / first Home visit which mode the user landed in and how to change it.
- **Why it matters:** The onboarding depth picker and Settings' depth picker present inconsistent option sets (2 vs 3), so a skip-path user's actual state ("Balanced") is not discoverable from the flow that supposedly explains it.
- **Expected user impact:** Removes a silent mismatch between what onboarding promises and what state the user actually ends up in.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Customization.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding, Customization profile
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low-severity but persistent terminology mismatch between onboarding and Settings.
- **Implementation notes:** Simplest fix is to make `depthPage` present exactly the two options users can reach either way, and document that skip = same as "Keep it simple" (i.e. change the default to `.casual` rather than `.balanced`).

### EASE-106 — Depth-page copy doesn't say the choice is changeable until the user has already chosen

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `depthSubtitle` ("Two views over the same data. Switch anytime in Settings.", OnboardingView.swift:385-387) is the only place onboarding tells users the depth choice is reversible, and it's a single small caption above two large tappable cards — easy to skip past while scanning the bigger card titles.
- **Recommendation:** Repeat the "you can change this anytime" reassurance as a persistent footnote near the Next button on this step, not just the page subtitle.
- **Why it matters:** Users facing a binary, disabled-until-chosen decision (see EASE-101) are more likely to freeze if they don't register that it's reversible; the reassurance is currently easy to miss.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster step-3 completion, especially for hesitant users.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor increased hesitation at step 3.
- **Implementation notes:** Small caption addition; no logic change.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `Text` under the `depthOption` VStack in `depthPage` (lines 212-236) reiterating reversibility, styled as `BadanFont.caption`.

### EASE-107 — Two nearly-identical "get started" strings exist in the catalog, only one of which is used

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change

Two overlapping "start using the app" strings live in the codebase with no clear owner of which is canonical.

### EASE-108 — Language toggle on step 1 previews only the toggle itself, not the RTL flip of the rest of onboarding

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `languageToggle` (OnboardingView.swift:137-164) lets a user switch to Arabic on the welcome page, and `env.update { $0.language = lang }` does re-render the whole app RTL — but the change is easy to miss because the same welcome page content re-renders in place with no transition cue calling out that layout direction just flipped.
- **Recommendation:** Add a brief animated layout-direction cue (or at minimum ensure `withAnimation` wraps the RTL-affecting frame changes) so switching language visibly demonstrates the RTL support the product prides itself on.
- **Why it matters:** Arabic/RTL readiness is a first-order product guardrail; onboarding is the one place where showing off correct RTL behavior builds early trust with Arabic-speaking users.
- **Expected user impact:** Reinforces confidence that Arabic is a first-class experience, not an afterthought.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding, Localization
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor missed opportunity to showcase RTL quality early.
- **Implementation notes:** Existing `withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.2))` around the language write (line 142) already animates some properties; verify layout-direction-dependent frames animate too.

### EASE-109 — Progress dots carry no accessible label for VoiceOver users

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `progressDots` (OnboardingView.swift:90-100) is marked `.accessibilityHidden(true)`, so a VoiceOver user gets no "step 2 of 4" announcement anywhere in the header — the only progress cue is purely visual.

- **Why it matters:** Onboarding is the first accessibility impression of the app; silently dropping progress context for screen-reader users is an easy, cheap fix.
- **Expected user impact:** VoiceOver users can track onboarding progress instead of navigating blind.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding, Accessibility
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Screen-reader users lack progress orientation during setup.

- **First patch sketch:** In `header` (lines 49-88), replace `progressDots`'s `.accessibilityHidden(true)` with a computed label on the parent `ZStack`.

### EASE-110 — "Why BADAN" page repeats the welcome subtitle's message without adding new decision-relevant information

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `welcomeSubtitle` ("Your private health repository.", Strings.swift:148) and `valuePrivateBody`/`valueOfflineBody` (OnboardingView.swift:370-382) all restate "private" and "offline" in slightly different words across two consecutive onboarding pages.

### EASE-111 — "Skip" and "Back" controls share the same 44pt hit target sizing but very different consequences, with no distinguishing weight

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** In `header` (OnboardingView.swift:49-88), "Back" (safe, reversible) and "Skip" (jumps straight past all remaining setup into the live app) are both plain-style `Text` buttons in `BadanFont.bodyCompact`/`textSecondary`, visually identical in weight — nothing signals that Skip is the more consequential action.
- **Recommendation:** Keep Skip visually quieter (e.g., smaller/lighter) than Back, or require a single confirmation tap only on Skip from step 0 (before any context has been given) since it discards the whole flow's remaining information.
- **Why it matters:** A first-time user can accidentally skip past onboarding entirely from step 0 without realizing how much they bypassed (value prop, depth choice, connect).
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer accidental full-skips before the user has seen anything.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Onboarding
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor; some users skip onboarding without meaning to lose the value/connect context.
- **Implementation notes:** A visual-weight change is enough; avoid adding friction via a modal confirmation, which would fight the "calm" tone.

### EASE-117 — SourcesScreen shows seeded "Apple Watch"/"iPhone" sources as "Active · Apple Health" even though no real HealthKit permission was ever granted

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `FakeHealthStore.sourceDescriptors()` (apps/ios/Sources/Platform/Health/FakeHealthStore.swift:173-179) declares its synthetic sources with `type: .healthkit`, `displayName: "Apple Watch"` / `"iPhone"`. `SourcesScreen` (apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/SourcesScreen.swift:261-279, `sourceIcon`/`sourceTypeLabel`) renders these with the real Apple Health icon and label and an "Active" green-ish status pill (`sourceStatus`, lines 281-287), with zero visual distinction from a genuine HealthKit connection.
- **Recommendation:** Give seed-originated sources a distinct badge (e.g. "Sample data") in `SourcesSourceCard`, or gate `type: .healthkit` in `FakeHealthStore` behind a separate `.manual`/`.demo` `SourceType` so the UI can render it honestly.
- **Why it matters:** Combined with EASE-102 (the connect button being a no-op), this is the second half of why users cannot currently tell demo data from a real Apple Health connection anywhere in the app — Sources is the one screen whose entire purpose is "where does my data come from," and it currently answers that question incorrectly for every first-run user.
- **Expected user impact:** Restores trust in the one screen designed to show data provenance.
- **ROI:** 5
- **Importance:** 5
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Platform/Health/FakeHealthStore.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/SourcesScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Sources screen, Health seam
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Sources screen actively misinforms about provenance, undermining the "preserve provenance" product guardrail.
- **Implementation notes:** A minimal fix: prefix `FakeHealthStore`'s `displayName`s with "Sample" or add a `isSynthetic` flag threaded through `SourceDescriptor` → `Source` → `SourcesSourceCard`.
- **First patch sketch:** Add `isSynthetic: Bool` to `SourceDescriptor` (HealthStorePort.swift:19-35), set `true` in `FakeHealthStore.sourceDescriptors()`, and render a small "Sample data" `PillLabel` in `SourcesSourceCard` when set.

### EASE-118 — Info.plist `NSHealthShareUsageDescription` promises a capability the app doesn't yet exercise

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `apps/ios/project.yml:52` sets `NSHealthShareUsageDescription: "BADAN reads your health data on your device to build your personal, private health repository. Nothing leaves your phone."` — accurate for intent, but since `HealthKitAdapter.readSamples/readIntervals/readSessions` are stub no-ops returning `[]` (HealthKitAdapter.swift:36-46) and `requestAuthorization` is never called (EASE-102), this permission string would currently never even be shown to a user, and if it were, granting it would read zero data.
- **Recommendation:** No text change needed once EASE-102 ships and authorization is actually requested; until then, treat this as a reminder that the permission string and the underlying capability are currently out of sync.
- **Why it matters:** Permission strings are a contract with the user and with App Review; an unused, never-triggered usage string sitting in the manifest is a smell that the permission flow was never finished, not deliberately deferred.
- **Expected user impact:** None until EASE-102 ships, at which point this string becomes load-bearing and should be re-reviewed for accuracy against what `HealthKitAdapter` actually reads (currently: nothing).
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/project.yml`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Info.plist / permission strings
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-102
- **Risk if skipped:** Low now; becomes a real App Review risk once authorization is actually requested against still-stubbed reads.
- **Implementation notes:** Revisit wording once `readSamples`/`readIntervals`/`readSessions` are implemented so the string accurately reflects which data types are read.

### EASE-119 — No in-app messaging for what happens after a user denies the HealthKit prompt

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `HealthKitAdapter.requestAuthorization` (HealthKitAdapter.swift:24-34) surfaces `granted`/`error` via a completion handler, but nothing in `SourcesScreen` or onboarding currently handles a `granted == false` outcome — there's no denied-permission state, recovery copy, or Settings deep link anywhere in the reviewed files.

- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Platform/Health/HealthKitAdapter.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/SourcesScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Permissions, Sources

### EASE-120 — `Loc.dataPaused` ("Your data has been paused for a while — let's reconnect.") is defined but never shown anywhere

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `Loc.dataPaused` (Core/Localization/Strings.swift:39-40) and `Loc.backToToday` (line 38) exist in the shared string catalog but a repo-wide search finds zero call sites rendering them in any screen — there is no stale-source/paused-sync detection or messaging anywhere in Home, Sources, or Settings.
- **Recommendation:** Either wire a simple staleness check (e.g., "no new samples from any active source in N days" against `Source.lastDeliveryAt`, already tracked in `SourcesSourceCard`, SourcesScreen.swift:126-131) to actually show this message on Home, or remove the dead strings.
- **Why it matters:** This is exactly the kind of comprehension gap permission-timing audits look for: a source can silently stop delivering (revoked permission, uninstalled companion app) and BADAN has copy ready for that moment but never triggers it.
- **Expected user impact:** Users learn promptly when a connected source has gone quiet, instead of noticing only when a metric looks "stuck."
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Core/Localization/Strings.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/SourcesScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Home, Sources, staleness detection
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Stale-source situations remain invisible to the user until they investigate manually.
- **Implementation notes:** `Source.lastDeliveryAt` (SourcesScreen.swift:129) already carries the timestamp needed for a simple threshold check.

### EASE-121 — Permission list in Sources humanizes unknown platform type tokens instead of using the metric ontology's real names

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `permissionTypeLabel` (SourcesScreen.swift:318-334) hand-maintains a ten-entry switch of platform-type strings to bilingual labels, then falls back to `SourcesDateText.humanize(platformType)` — a naive camelCase splitter — for anything not in that list, producing raw, unlocalized, technical labels (e.g. an un-mapped HealthKit identifier would render as "Vo2 Max" in both English and Arabic).
- **Recommendation:** Route permission-type labels through `MetricRegistry.definitionOrFallback` (which already carries bilingual `nameEn`/`nameAr` for all 44 ontology metrics) instead of maintaining a second, partial, hand-written mapping.
- **Why it matters:** Any HealthKit type outside the current 10-entry switch silently loses Arabic localization and gets a mechanically humanized English label — a direct violation of the "no screen ships English-only" rule stated in `Strings.swift`'s own header comment.
- **Expected user impact:** Consistent, correctly localized permission names for every data type, not just the ten hand-picked ones.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/SourcesScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Ontology/MetricRegistry.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Sources, Localization
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Non-mapped permission types silently break the app's Arabic-parity guarantee.
- **Implementation notes:** Requires a platform-type → metricId lookup, which likely already exists in the ingestion mapping layer and could be reused here.

### EASE-128 — Only "Reset demo data" in Settings hints that the app is running on synthetic data — nothing on Home says so

### EASE-129 — "Reset demo data" confirmation doesn't explain what "demo data" currently means to the user (that it's everything they see)

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** The `showResetConfirm` dialog (SettingsScreen.swift:49-60) presents `SettingsStrings.resetConfirmMessage` without the reviewed excerpt showing its exact wording, but the action button is simply "Reset demo data" — a user who has been logging their own real meds, symptoms, and workouts since seeding has no way to tell from this dialog whether their own manually-entered data will also be wiped alongside the seeded rows.
- **Recommendation:** State explicitly in the confirmation copy whether reset removes only the original seed rows or the user's own subsequent entries too (per `SeedController.seed`, all data — seeded and later manual entries — lives in the same tables, so a reset almost certainly wipes everything).
- **Why it matters:** A destructive action ("Reset") with ambiguous scope is a classic error-correction/comprehension failure — users need to know exactly what they're about to lose.
- **Expected user impact:** Prevents accidental loss of real logged data that a user believed was separate from "demo data."
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes

- **Risk if skipped:** Users could lose real personal logs (meds adherence, symptoms, workouts) believing only "demo" rows would be removed.

### EASE-130 — Seeded medication regimen names ("Vitamin D", "Magnesium") are indistinguishable from a real user's own future entries once mixed together

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `SeedController.seedMedications` (SeedController.swift:62-88) inserts two `MedicationRegimen` rows with ordinary names and no `isSeeded`/`isSample` flag anywhere in the `MedicationRegimen` model (as constructed here). If a user adds their own real medication after first launch, the medication list mixes real and sample entries with no way to tell which is which.
- **Recommendation:** Either flag seed-originated rows so they can be visually distinguished (and cleanly removed independent of user data on reset), or make onboarding/first-Home messaging (EASE-128) clear that *all* data — including these two medications — is sample content to be replaced.
- **Why it matters:** A user who genuinely takes Vitamin D and Magnesium might reasonably assume these are entries they created, compounding the "is this data real" confusion from EASE-128.
- **Expected user impact:** Clearer separation between sample and real logged data everywhere it's displayed (Home meds module, Log, Timeline).
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/App/SeedController.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Seed data, Medication logging
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-128
- **Risk if skipped:** Real and sample medication/symptom/workout entries become indistinguishable and hard to clean up selectively.
- **Implementation notes:** This is a data-model change (a boolean or provenance tag), so treat as a medium-effort follow-on to the higher-priority disclosure items above.

### EASE-131 — No explanation anywhere of how to replace demo data with a real connection once the user notices it's fake

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** Even after a user works out (via Settings → "Reset demo data") that the app was showing sample data, the reset flow (`env.resetDemoData()`, called from SettingsScreen.swift:55) only wipes and presumably re-seeds — there is no visible path from that screen into actually connecting a real HealthKit source (`SourcesScreen`) as the natural next step.
- **Recommendation:** Chain the reset flow to prompt "Connect a real source now?" immediately after wiping demo data, linking directly into `SourcesScreen`.
- **Why it matters:** "Reset demo data" without a next step just produces an empty app (or freshly re-seeded fake data, depending on `resetDemoData`'s implementation) rather than progress toward the user's actual goal of using their own data.
- **Expected user impact:** Converts demo-data awareness into an actual real-data connection instead of a dead end.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/SourcesScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Settings, Sources
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** EASE-102 (real connect action), EASE-128
- **Risk if skipped:** Users who discover the demo-data issue have no guided path to resolve it.
- **Implementation notes:** A simple post-reset navigation push to `SourcesScreen` covers this.

### EASE-132 — First-run seed data spans exactly 90 days, but nothing tells the user why history "starts" at a fixed point

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `SeedController.seed` ingests `historyDays: 90` (SeedController.swift:35-36) via `FakeHealthStore`, and `TimelineScreen`'s `historyStartFooter` ("Your record begins here", Loc.historyStart, TimelineScreen.swift:201-210) will eventually show a boundary — but a first-run user has no way to know this 90-day boundary is a seed-data artifact rather than "how far back the app can ever look."
- **Recommendation:** Once EASE-128's demo-data disclosure exists, extend it to clarify that the visible history length is a property of the sample dataset, not a hard app limitation.
- **Why it matters:** Prevents users from concluding BADAN "only keeps 90 days of history" when that's purely a seed-data characteristic.
- **Expected user impact:** Avoids a false product-capability belief formed during the demo period.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/App/SeedController.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Seed data, Timeline
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** EASE-128
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor misconception about the app's actual history-retention capability.
- **Implementation notes:** Simple copy addition once the broader demo-data messaging (EASE-128) is in place.

### EASE-133 — Seeded symptom entries appear in Timeline/Log recents identically to entries the user will log themselves, with no severity-scale primer

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `SeedController.seedSymptoms` (SeedController.swift:90-100) inserts five symptoms with severities 3-6 on a presumably 1-10 (or similar) scale, but nothing in `LogHubScreen`'s recents chips (RecentChip, LogHubScreen.swift:272-300) or `SymptomLogView` (not in this scope, but its output surfaces here) explains what the severity numbers mean the first time a user encounters a seeded symptom entry.

- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No

### EASE-134 — SeedController's insight generation runs for exactly 4 days back, so Insights can look sparse or empty despite 90 days of underlying seed data

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `SeedController.seed` calls `insightEngine.generate(forDay:tz:)` only `for dayOffset in 0..<4` (SeedController.swift:55-57), meaning the Insights feed a first-run user sees is generated from just the last 4 of the 90 seeded days, while `InsightsScreen`'s empty-feed message (`InsightsLoc.emptyMessage`, InsightsScreen.swift:419-421) implies insights simply haven't "built up" yet.
- **Recommendation:** Either extend seed-time insight generation to cover more of the 90-day history, or make the empty/sparse-feed copy accurate to the fact that this is a seed-data characteristic, not organic new-user behavior.
- **Why it matters:** A first-run user comparing 90 days of rich metric history against a nearly empty Insights tab may reasonably conclude the Insights feature itself is broken or under-populated, when it's actually just a seed-time limitation.
- **Expected user impact:** Insights feed better reflects the depth of the (synthetic) history already present.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/App/SeedController.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Seed data, Insights
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Insights looks under-populated relative to the rest of the seeded demo experience.
- **Implementation notes:** Bounded by `InsightEngine.generate`'s performance characteristics for a larger day range; verify cost before widening the loop.

### EASE-135 — SplashView gives no indication of what's happening during first-run seeding, which is the slowest cold start in the app

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `SplashView` (App/RootView.swift:48-62) shows a static heart icon, "BADAN" wordmark and a bare `ProgressView()` with no label — identical whether the app is doing a fast normal launch or a first-run `SeedController.seed` pass that ingests 90 days of data across multiple tables (SeedController.swift:33-58, described elsewhere in the repo as `Task.detached`).
- **Recommendation:** On first run specifically, show a short label under the spinner ("Setting up your sample data…") so the (likely longer) wait has an explanation.
- **Why it matters:** An unexplained longer-than-usual spinner on the very first launch risks users force-quitting mid-seed, which given `seedIfNeeded`'s presence-check gate (`if try catalog.sources().isEmpty == false { return }`, SeedController.swift:29) could leave the app in a partially-seeded state.
- **Expected user impact:** Reduces first-launch abandonment during the one-time seed operation.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/App/RootView.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/App/SeedController.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Splash, Seed data
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Users may force-quit during an unexplained long first launch.
- **Implementation notes:** `SplashView` would need a way to know a seed is in progress (e.g., an `env.isSeeding` published flag) to conditionally show the label only on first run.

### EASE-137 — Readiness "/100" score gives no explanation of what inputs produce it or what a good/typical score looks like

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `ReadinessHeroCard` (HomeScreen.swift:156-197) renders `readiness.value` as a bare integer over "/ 100" via `StatBox`, with only a one-sentence mood narrative (`narrative(for:sleep:)`, lines 703-716) beneath it — nothing on the casual path explains that readiness derives from sleep and resting heart rate (per `BaselineEngine`'s `composite.readiness_score`), or what ranges typically mean.
- **Recommendation:** Add a lightweight "based on your sleep and resting heart rate" caption under the score at casual depth, without requiring a trip to the (power-only) anatomy sheet.
- **Why it matters:** "72/100" is a number that invites the question "72 out of what, based on what?" — casual users get no answer unless they switch to power mode and open `MetricAnatomySheet`, which doesn't even apply to composite readiness the same way (see EASE-165).
- **Expected user impact:** Casual users understand what moves their readiness score without needing power mode.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Home
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** The single most prominent number in the app remains unexplained to its primary (casual) audience.
- **Implementation notes:** A one-line static caption naming the two inputs is enough; avoid exposing algorithm IDs at casual depth.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `Text` caption under the `StatBox` in `ReadinessHeroCard` (HomeScreen.swift:163-179) reading e.g. "Based on your sleep and resting heart rate," gated to `!env.depth.showsPowerDetail`.

### EASE-138 — Readiness narrative sentence is one of only three fixed strings regardless of which underlying metric actually drove the score

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `HomeViewModel.narrative(for:sleep:)` (HomeScreen.swift:703-716) buckets the readiness value into three ranges (66+, 45-65, <45) and returns one of exactly three static sentences ("You're rested and steady today" / "You're in a balanced place today" / "A gentler pace may suit you today"), ignoring the `sleep` parameter it's passed and never naming which input (sleep vs. resting heart rate) actually changed.
- **Recommendation:** Use the passed-in `sleep` summary (already computed and available) to make the narrative reference the specific driver, e.g. "You slept well and your resting heart rate was typical" vs. a generic score-bucket sentence.
- **Why it matters:** A "why am I at 58 today" question is exactly what the narrative sentence should answer, but three fixed sentences convey mood, not cause — undermining the "why" affordance the product otherwise cares about (see the Insights "why" disclosure elsewhere).
- **Expected user impact:** Narrative becomes genuinely informative rather than decorative.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Home
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Narrative stays generic and doesn't build user understanding of their own patterns.
- **Implementation notes:** The `sleep` parameter is already unused in the function body (line 703's signature includes it, but only `readiness.value` is read) — this is a straightforward parameter-utilization gap.

### EASE-139 — "Still learning your baseline" gives no sense of how much longer until it's ready

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** When `data.readiness == nil`, `ReadinessHeroCard`'s fallback (HomeScreen.swift:186-193) shows only `Loc.stillLearning` ("Still learning your baseline") with no count of days remaining, even though `BaselineEngine.minPointsForConfident = 7` (BaselineEngine.swift:19) is a known, fixed threshold the app could report progress against (e.g., "3 of 7 days").
- **Recommendation:** Surface a simple day-count ("3 of 7 days needed") wherever "Still learning" appears, using each baseline's `nPoints` (already stored on `Baseline`, referenced in `MetricAnatomySheet`'s `daysUsed` row, MetricAnatomySheet.swift:72) against the fixed `minPointsForConfident` threshold.
- **Why it matters:** "Still learning" with no ETA is an open-ended wait state; a progress count converts uncertainty into a concrete, motivating countdown.
- **Expected user impact:** Users understand exactly how much longer before readiness/baselines become available, encouraging continued source connection.
- **ROI:** 4
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Derivation/BaselineEngine.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricAnatomySheet.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Home, MetricDetail, Baseline engine
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** "Still learning" remains a dead-end status with no actionable timeframe.
- **Implementation notes:** `MetricAnatomySheet.baselineCard` already has the `nPoints` value (line 72) available for a similar "X of 7" treatment.
- **First patch sketch:** In `MetricAnatomySheet.baselineCard` (lines 62-81), append "(\(b.nPoints) of \(BaselineEngine.minPointsForConfident) days)" to the existing `daysUsed` row when `b.provisional`.

### EASE-140 — "In your usual range" phrasing doesn't say what the range actually is without a second tap into Metric Detail

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `Loc.inYourRange`/`aboveYourRange`/`belowYourRange` (Strings.swift:49-51) appear as `StatusChip` labels throughout Home, Body and Timeline (e.g. `MetricModuleCard`, HomeScreen.swift:269-271; `BodyPillarCard`, BodyScreen.swift:179-181) with no accompanying numeric band — a user must tap through to `MetricDetailScreen`/`MetricAnatomySheet` to see the actual low-high values behind "your usual range."

- **Why it matters:** "In your usual range" is reassuring but unfalsifiable without evidence; showing the actual band once (not on every chip, to avoid clutter) builds trust in the claim.
- **Expected user impact:** Users can sanity-check status chips against real numbers without extra navigation.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2

### EASE-141 — DepthBadge sits in the Home header looking like a control but performs no action when tapped

- **Problem:** `HomeHeader` places `DepthBadge(env.depth, language: env.language)` (HomeScreen.swift:53) as a bare view with no `Button`/`NavigationLink`/tap gesture wrapper. Visually it's a pill with an icon and text — the same `PillLabel` shape used elsewhere for genuinely interactive elements — but tapping it does nothing; the only way to change depth is via Settings → Detail level.
- **Recommendation:** Either make the Home header's `DepthBadge` tappable (opening a quick depth switcher, e.g. a small action sheet or direct navigation to Settings' detail section), or visually de-emphasize it so it doesn't imply interactivity it lacks.

- **Importance:** 4
- **Effort:** 2

- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/Pills.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Home, Settings, Design system
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile

- **Implementation notes:** Simplest safe fix: wrap the badge in a `NavigationLink`/`Button` pushing straight to `SettingsScreen`'s `detailSection`, reusing the existing three-way `SettingsRadioGroup`.

### EASE-143 — "Balanced" depth is functionally identical to "Simple" everywhere except its display label, but Settings presents it as a distinct third choice

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** Every `env.depth.showsPowerDetail` check in the codebase (e.g. HomeScreen.swift:18, MetricDetailScreen.swift:142, BodyScreen.swift, TimelineScreen.swift:51) evaluates `self == .power` (`Customization.swift:17`) — meaning `.balanced` produces pixel-identical UI to `.casual` everywhere reviewed. Yet `SettingsRadioGroup` in `detailSection` (SettingsScreen.swift:113-122) presents Simple/Balanced/Detailed as three seemingly-different options.
- **Recommendation:** Either implement a genuine visual/content difference for `.balanced` (e.g., showing delta text but not the full method/lineage detail), or collapse the picker to the two options that actually behave differently (Simple/Detailed) and keep `.balanced` purely as an internal default alias for `.casual`.
- **Why it matters:** Presenting three named choices where two behave identically is a direct terminology/comprehension gap — a user who deliberately picks "Balanced" expecting an in-between experience gets exactly the "Simple" experience with no way to tell.
- **Expected user impact:** Removes a false-choice: users get what the UI promises, or the UI stops promising something it doesn't deliver.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Customization.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Customization, Settings
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** "Balanced" remains a decoy option that misleads users about what they're choosing.
- **Implementation notes:** Cheapest fix is collapsing the picker to two options; a "real" balanced tier is a larger design effort better tracked separately from this ease-of-use pass.

### EASE-144 — Provisional badge ("Still learning") uses the same wording for two different underlying situations: no baseline yet vs. a thin/uncertain baseline

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `ProvisionalBadge` (Pills.swift:63-79) and its text `Loc.stillLearning` are shown both when `data.readiness == nil` (no computed value at all, HomeScreen.swift:186-193) and when a `Baseline.provisional == true` (a baseline exists but has fewer than 7 days of data, per `BaselineEngine.swift:60`) — e.g. in `MetricAnatomySheet.baselineCard` (line 66) and `MetricDetailScreen.statusChip` (lines 345-347). Both states render identical copy despite being meaningfully different ("nothing yet" vs. "something, but not confident yet").

- **Why it matters:** A user with 1 day of data and a user with 6 days of data both see identical "still learning" messaging with no sense of relative progress, which compounds EASE-139's missing day-count.
- **Expected user impact:** More accurate signal of how close a metric is to a confident baseline.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/Pills.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Core/Localization/Strings.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Home, MetricDetail, Design system
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** EASE-139
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor; the two states remain conflated in copy.
- **Implementation notes:** Pairs naturally with EASE-139's day-count addition — once `nPoints`/threshold are surfaced, the wording distinction becomes almost free.

### EASE-145 — `dateText`/`timeText` allocate a fresh `DateFormatter` on every render across Home, adding avoidable per-frame cost that also risks locale/RTL formatting drift between call sites

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `HomeHeader.dateText` (HomeScreen.swift:57-63) and `TimelinePreviewCard.timeText` (HomeScreen.swift:467-472) each construct a new `DateFormatter` per render with slightly different setup (`dateStyle`/`timeStyle` vs. `setLocalizedDateFormatFromTemplate`), and similarly ad hoc formatter code is repeated in `SourcesScreen.SourcesDateText`, `MetricDetailScreen.dateText`, `TimelineScreen.timeText/formattedDate`. Beyond the (separately flagged) performance cost, this duplication risks each call site drifting in exact date/time formatting conventions, which is a comprehension consistency issue for a bilingual, RTL-aware app.
- **Recommendation:** Centralize date/time formatting in one shared helper (e.g. extend `env.format` the way numeric formatting already is centralized) so every screen presents dates and times identically in both languages.
- **Why it matters:** Inconsistent date formatting between Home's header, Timeline's day labels, and Metric Detail's value dates undermines the sense of one coherent app, especially in Arabic where digit style (`arabicDigits` setting) also needs to apply uniformly.
- **Expected user impact:** Visually and semantically consistent date/time presentation everywhere.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Home/HomeScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/SourcesScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Timeline/TimelineScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Home, Sources, MetricDetail, Timeline, Localization
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Slow accumulation of subtly inconsistent date/time formatting across screens.
- **Implementation notes:** This is primarily a code-reuse item with a comprehension side-effect; coordinate with any Performance-track item addressing the same per-render `DateFormatter` allocation.

### EASE-150 — Home's "hasAny" empty-state gate can hide a screen that actually has useful content because one check fails silently

### EASE-154 — HomeCasualBody's module visibility check silently defaults to visible for unknown module IDs, so a broken/removed module id fails open rather than closed

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change

- **Expected user impact:** Prevents a hidden module from silently reappearing after an id change.

- **Affected systems:** iOS Home, Customization
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Low today; a latent risk for future module-id changes.
- **Implementation notes:** Flip the `?? true` default to `?? false` only if paired with a migration that seeds all current module ids into existing profiles, to avoid the opposite regression (modules disappearing for existing users).

### EASE-164 — MetricDetail's period selector (7/30/90 days) is power-only, but casual users viewing a fixed 30-day chart have no way to know that window is fixed rather than "all history"

### EASE-166 — Settings literally promises "Balanced" gives "A little more context" than Simple, but no code path delivers any difference

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `SettingsStrings.depthSubtitle(.balanced)` (SettingsScreen.swift:476) reads "A little more context." as the subtitle shown next to the Balanced radio option in `detailSection` (lines 108-124) — but as established in EASE-143, every `showsPowerDetail` check in the app treats `.balanced` identically to `.casual` (`Customization.swift:17`, `self == .power`). This is a directly falsifiable, user-facing claim in shipped copy that the code does not honor.
- **Recommendation:** Fix the underlying behavior gap (implement some genuine "a little more context" tier for Balanced) or change the subtitle to accurately describe what Balanced currently does (nothing different from Simple) — do not ship a promise the picker doesn't keep.
- **Why it matters:** This is the clearest, most quotable proof point that the three-way depth picker currently sells a distinction it doesn't have — exactly the kind of terminology/interpretation gap this audit slice is meant to catch.
- **Expected user impact:** Removes a directly disprovable claim from Settings copy.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 3
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`, `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Customization.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Settings, Customization
- **Suggested owner:** Product
- **Dependencies:** EASE-143
- **Risk if skipped:** A user who deliberately picks "Balanced" for its promised extra context gets nothing different and has no way to know the setting is a no-op.
- **Implementation notes:** Cheapest correct fix: change the copy to match reality (identical to Simple) until/unless product decides to build a real middle tier.

### EASE-167 — DepthBadge's icon for "Balanced" (`circle.lefthalf.filled`) doesn't visually relate to either "leaf" (Simple) or "slider.horizontal.3" (Detailed), breaking the implied spectrum

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `DepthBadge.iconName` (Pills.swift:52-58) maps casual→"leaf", balanced→"circle.lefthalf.filled", power→"slider.horizontal.3" — three visually unrelated SF Symbols with no shared visual language suggesting "these are three points on one spectrum," which is exactly the mental model the depth concept is trying to convey.
- **Recommendation:** Use a coherent icon family that visually communicates a progression, e.g. a fill-level metaphor (empty circle → half-filled circle → full circle, or a 1-bar/2-bar/3-bar signal-strength style icon).
- **Why it matters:** Icons are a discoverability aid; three unrelated glyphs (a leaf, a half-filled circle, a slider) do nothing to help a user intuit "these are levels of the same thing" at a glance.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster intuitive grasp of the depth concept as a single spectrum rather than three unrelated modes.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/Pills.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Design system
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor; icon choice doesn't reinforce the spectrum concept but doesn't actively mislead either.
- **Implementation notes:** SF Symbols like `"dial.low.fill"`/`"dial.medium.fill"`/`"dial.high.fill"` would communicate a progression more directly than the current unrelated set.

### EASE-169 — Changing depth in Settings animates the Settings screen but gives no preview of how Home/Body will look before navigating there
