## (e) Cross-cutting remembered preferences — last tab, last metric range, collapsed sections

### EASE-286 — Neither platform remembers the last-viewed tab across app launches

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** iOS's `TabView` (`RootView.swift` lines 29–45) has no `selection` binding at all, and Android's `Navigator.selectedTab` (`Navigation.kt` line 41) initializes to `0` with no persistence — both apps always cold-launch onto the "Today" tab regardless of which tab the user was last using.
- **Recommendation:** Persist the last-selected tab index (e.g., in `UserDefaults`/`SharedPreferences`, or as a new field on `CustomizationProfile`) and restore it on launch.
- **Why it matters:** A user who lives mostly on the Log or Insights tab is forced back to Today every single cold launch.
- **Expected user impact:** The app reopens where the user left it, reducing one habitual re-navigation per session.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/App/RootView.swift`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/app/Navigation.kt`
- **Affected systems:** iOS App shell, Android Navigation
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-300 (a dedicated persistence field would make this and the following items easier to implement consistently)
- **Risk if skipped:** Users re-navigate to their preferred tab on every single app open, indefinitely.

### EASE-287 — Depth-gated screens re-fetch and reset scroll position every time a tab is re-visited

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** Every tab's root screen re-runs its full load on re-entry (`.task` on iOS, `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` on Android — e.g., `BodyScreen.swift` line 144, `LogHubScreen.kt` line 113) with no cached "last loaded" state or scroll-position memory, so returning to a previously-scrolled list (Body's pillars, Export's history) always snaps back to the top with a fresh loading spinner.
- **Recommendation:** Cache the last-loaded state per tab in the composition-root environment and restore scroll position on re-entry, only re-fetching in the background if data may be stale.
- **Why it matters:** Every tab switch pays a full reload + scroll-reset cost even when nothing has changed since the user was last there seconds ago.
- **Expected user impact:** Snappier, less jarring tab switching.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/loghub/LogHubScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android App shell
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Continued jarring reload-and-reset on every tab revisit.

### EASE-288 — Metric Detail's period selection (7/30/90 days) resets on every visit

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `periodDays` is `@State`/`remember`-scoped to the screen instance on both platforms (`MetricDetailScreen.swift` line 112, `MetricDetailScreen.kt` line 191) and hardcoded to `30` — navigating away and back to the same metric (or to a different one and back) always resets the period, discarding a power user's preferred longer window every single visit.
- **Recommendation:** Persist the last-chosen period (globally, or per-metric) in `CustomizationProfile` and initialize `periodDays` from it.
- **Why it matters:** A power user who always wants to see 90 days of a given metric must re-select "90" on every single visit to every metric.
- **Expected user impact:** Metric detail opens at the window size the user actually prefers, not a fixed default.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/MetricDetail/MetricDetailScreen.swift`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/metricdetail/MetricDetailScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android Metric Detail
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-300
- **Risk if skipped:** Power users re-select their preferred period every single time they open any metric.

### EASE-289 — Export screen's chosen format/range reset to hardcoded defaults on every visit

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** Both `ExportCenterScreen.swift` (`@State private var format: ExportFormat = .csv`, `range: ExportRange = .last30`, lines 136–137) and `ExportScreen.kt` (`format by remember { mutableStateOf(ExportFormat.CSV) }`, `range by remember { mutableStateOf(ExportRange.LAST30) }`, lines 222–223) reset to CSV/Last-30-days every time the screen is reopened, with no memory of the user's last-used configuration.
- **Recommendation:** Persist the last-used format/range/scope (or at minimum format + range) and initialize the screen's state from it.
- **Why it matters:** A user who always exports "All time · JSON" for a specific recurring purpose must reselect both every single visit.
- **Expected user impact:** Export opens pre-configured to the user's habitual choice.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/export/ExportScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android Export
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-300
- **Risk if skipped:** Recurring exporters reconfigure the same two-to-three controls on every single export.

### EASE-290 — No section can be collapsed anywhere, so there's no "remembered collapse state" to lose — but also no way to shorten repeat-visit scanning

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** None of the multi-section screens (Settings on both platforms, Export, Sources) support collapsing a section at all; a returning user who has already internalized, say, the Notifications section's four toggles still scrolls past the fully-expanded section every visit.
- **Recommendation:** Add optional section collapsing (with the collapse state itself persisted) to the longest screens — Settings first.
- **Why it matters:** This is the structural gap that makes items like EASE-296 impossible today; without any collapse mechanism, there's nothing for a "remembered preference" to apply to.
- **Expected user impact:** Shorter, more scannable repeat visits to long settings/list screens.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 3
- **Approval needed:** Yes
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Settings/SettingsScreen.swift`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/settings/SettingsScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android Settings
- **Suggested owner:** Design
- **Dependencies:** EASE-300
- **Risk if skipped:** Long screens stay uniformly fully-expanded for every visit, forever.

### EASE-291 — Quick-add sheets never pre-fill the user's most recent or most common value

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `LogHubScreen`'s Water and Weight quick-add sheets (`WaterQuickSheet`/`WeightQuickSheet`, lines 313–431) always reset to a blank/default state on each open (`text = ""` for Weight; no memory of the last-logged water amount), even for a user who logs the same value repeatedly.
- **Recommendation:** Pre-fill the text field with the user's most recently logged value for that quick-add type.
- **Why it matters:** Users with a highly repetitive logging pattern (same body weight, same water serving) get no benefit from that repetition — every quick-add starts from scratch.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster repeat logging for the app's most habitual use case.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 1
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/loghub/LogHubScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Android Log hub
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** "Quick add" stays no faster than typing from scratch for repeat entries.

### EASE-292 — Symptom severity slider always resets to the hardcoded midpoint, never recalling a per-symptom pattern

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `SymptomLogScreen`'s `severity` state (line 198: `mutableStateOf(3f)`) always starts at 3 for every new capture — even for a symptom the same user has logged at severity 7–8 several times in a row — despite `recents` already being loaded and available to the screen at capture time.
- **Recommendation:** When the chosen symptom matches a recently-logged one, pre-fill severity with that symptom's last-recorded value instead of the fixed midpoint.
- **Why it matters:** For a recurring, consistently-severe symptom, the user must drag the slider away from an inaccurate default on every single log.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster, more accurate default severity for recurring symptoms.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/symptom/SymptomLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Android Symptom log
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Recurring, severity-consistent symptoms get logged with an inaccurate default every time.

### EASE-293 — Workout duration/effort reset to hardcoded defaults on every fresh screen open

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `WorkoutLogScreen`'s `minutes` (line 171: `mutableStateOf(30)`) and `rpe` (line 172: `mutableStateOf(5f)`) reset to fixed defaults every time the screen is freshly opened (they do persist across consecutive same-session saves, but not across a nav-away-and-back or a fresh launch), with no memory of the user's typical duration/effort for their most-logged activity type.
- **Recommendation:** Pre-fill `minutes`/`rpe` from the user's most recent entry for the currently-selected activity type on fresh screen entry.
- **Why it matters:** A user who always logs ~45-minute runs at RPE 6 has to manually re-adjust both sliders from the generic 30/5 defaults on every fresh visit.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster logging for a user's habitual workout pattern.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/WorkoutLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Android Workout log
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor repeated slider adjustment for users with a consistent workout routine.

### EASE-294 — Nutrition meal type is always guessed fresh from the current hour, never recalling the user's last explicit choice

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `NutritionLogScreen`'s `initialMeal` (line 147: `mealForHour(...)`) is recomputed from the current hour every time the screen is freshly opened, with no memory of the user's last explicitly-picked meal type from a previous visit.
- **Recommendation:** If the user manually overrode the meal type on their last entry (rather than accepting the hour-based guess), prefer that as the starting point for a similar time-of-day next time.
- **Why it matters:** A user who regularly eats lunch at 3pm (landing near the LUNCH/DINNER hour-bucket boundary) has to manually correct the auto-picked meal type on every single visit rather than the app learning the pattern.
- **Expected user impact:** Fewer manual meal-type corrections for users with atypical (but consistent) meal timing.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/workoutnutrition/NutritionLogScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** Android Nutrition log
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor, recurring meal-type correction for users with atypical meal timing.

### EASE-295 — Screen-local power features never inherit the one global preference built for exactly their purpose

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** As documented specifically for Export in EASE-204, screen-local power-only controls (Export's unit-profile segmented control) maintain their own separate, non-inherited default rather than reading `CustomizationProfile.unitProfile`, which already exists globally for exactly this decision.
- **Recommendation:** Audit every screen-local power control for the same pattern (initializing from a hardcoded default instead of the matching global `CustomizationProfile` field) and fix them together as one pass.
- **Why it matters:** This is a repeatable pattern, not a one-off bug — any future screen that adds its own unit/format/depth-adjacent control risks the same mismatch unless the pattern itself is fixed.
- **Expected user impact:** Global preferences reliably propagate to every screen that has an equivalent local control, instead of requiring a per-screen fix each time.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Export/ExportCenterScreen.swift`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/export/ExportScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android Export, Settings
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-204
- **Risk if skipped:** Every new screen-local power control repeats the same default-mismatch bug independently.

### EASE-296 — Sources screen has no "collapse permissions I've already reviewed" mechanism

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `SourcesPermissionCard` (iOS `SourcesScreen.swift` lines 193–229; Android `SourcesScreen.kt` lines 301–342) shows every permission row every visit with no way to mark or hide previously-reviewed, already-granted permissions.
- **Recommendation:** Once EASE-290's collapse mechanism exists, let users collapse a "Granted — reviewed" group, remembering that collapse state across visits.
- **Why it matters:** A returning power user with many long-granted permissions re-scans the same fully-granted list on every visit with no way to reduce it to just what's new or actionable.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster repeat visits to Sources for users who've already confirmed their permission set.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/SourcesScreen.swift`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/SourcesScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android Sources
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-290
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor, growing scan cost for long-term users with many granted permissions.

### EASE-297 — All-metrics browser search query is cleared every time the screen is reopened

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `BodyAllMetricsBrowser`'s `query` (`BodyScreen.swift` line 293: `@State private var query = ""`) resets to empty every time the browser is dismissed and reopened, with no recent-search memory or pinning of frequently-visited metrics.
- **Recommendation:** Remember the last few search queries (or, better, track frequently-opened metrics directly) and surface them as quick suggestions when the search field is empty.
- **Why it matters:** A power user who regularly jumps to the same handful of niche metrics via search must retype the same query on every single visit.
- **Expected user impact:** Faster repeat access to a user's regularly-checked niche metrics.
- **ROI:** 2
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift`
- **Affected systems:** iOS Body
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Continued retyping of the same search query for a small set of habitually-checked metrics.

### EASE-298 — LogHub recents are recency-only, never frequency-weighted

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `loadRecents` (`LogHubScreen.kt` lines 472–488, mirrored on iOS) orders purely by most-recent `occurredAt`/`startAt`, so a symptom or workout the user logs consistently but not most-recently can be crowded out of the "recents" row by one-off entries logged more recently.
- **Recommendation:** Blend recency with frequency (e.g., a simple recency-weighted count) when selecting which items appear as quick "log again" chips.
- **Why it matters:** The whole point of a "recents" quick-log row is to surface what the user is likely to log again; pure recency is a weaker signal than "this is a pattern for this user."
- **Expected user impact:** Recents chips better predict what the user is about to log next.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/loghub/LogHubScreen.kt`, `apps/ios/Sources/Features/LogHub/`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android Log hub
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Minor; recents remain useful but suboptimal for consistent-but-not-recent patterns.

### EASE-299 — Tab re-selection always re-fetches and resets scroll position, discarding both in one motion

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** Combining EASE-287's re-fetch behavior with the total absence of scroll-position memory anywhere in the app, returning to any previously-scrolled tab (Body's pillar list, Export's history, Sources' device list) always snaps back to the very top and re-shows a loading state, even for data that hasn't changed.
- **Recommendation:** Cache the last scroll offset per tab/screen instance (e.g., via `ScrollState` restoration keyed by route) independent of whether the underlying data is re-fetched.
- **Why it matters:** Scroll-position loss compounds with reload-on-every-visit (EASE-287) to make tab switching feel like re-opening a fresh screen every time, never "coming back."
- **Expected user impact:** Returning to a tab feels like resuming, not restarting.
- **ROI:** 1
- **Importance:** 1
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Features/Body/BodyScreen.swift`, `apps/android/app/src/main/java/net/albayyan/badan/features/body/SourcesScreen.kt`
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android App shell
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** EASE-287
- **Risk if skipped:** Continued "always starts over" feeling on every tab revisit.

### EASE-300 — `CustomizationProfile` has no persistence seam for session/navigation memory at all

- **Category:** Ease-of-Use Change
- **Problem:** `CustomizationProfile` (`Customization.swift` lines 84–122) models layout/preference state thoroughly (`homeModules`, `unitOverrides`, `unitProfile`, `theme`, `notifications`) but has no field at all for "last active tab," "last viewed metric ID," "last export format/range," or any other session-navigation memory — there's no schema seam for any of EASE-286/288/289 to write into.
- **Recommendation:** Add a small, explicitly-non-critical "session preferences" struct to `CustomizationProfile` (or a separate lightweight store) purpose-built for exactly this class of remembered-but-not-precious state.
- **Why it matters:** Every "remember the last X" fix in this section currently requires inventing its own ad-hoc persistence mechanism instead of plugging into an existing, well-understood one — this is the root cause enabling EASE-286, 288, and 289.
- **Expected user impact:** None directly, but it's the prerequisite that makes every other remembered-preference fix in this list cheap and consistent to implement.
- **ROI:** 3
- **Importance:** 2
- **Effort:** 2
- **Approval needed:** No
- **Affected files:** `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/Customization.swift`, Android equivalent domain model
- **Affected systems:** iOS/Android Domain, App shell
- **Suggested owner:** Mobile
- **Dependencies:** None
- **Risk if skipped:** Each future "remember the last X" fix reinvents its own persistence mechanism instead of sharing one.
- **First patch sketch:** Add a `public var sessionPreferences: SessionPreferences = .init()` field to `CustomizationProfile` with `lastActiveTab: Int?`, `lastMetricPeriodDays: [String: Int]`, and `lastExportFormat`/`lastExportRange` — mirrored in the Android `CustomizationProfile` equivalent.

## 9. Major themes and risks

### 9.1 Recurring architectural smell patterns

1. **The half-shipped seam.** The repo's defining smell: infrastructure built to a high standard, then never connected to a producer or consumer. `HealthKitAdapter` reads return `[]`; `read_anchors`/`import_batches`/`sync_cursors` tables exist with zero writers; `Goal` has a table, entity, and repository but no screen; `metric_pins` likewise; `NoteEntry` and `Condition` have full backends and zero UI; `unitOverrides` is read but never written; 6+ of 13 insight templates are never selected; `deletable`/`sourceRecordId` on `TimelineEvent` are populated and never consumed; `editingSlotId` is declared and never set; dedup "reversal" has a journal but no reversal path. Each instance is individually defensible ("sync-ready, not sync-dependent" — ADR-0003); collectively they mean the *hard* half of nearly every feature was deferred while the schema-shaped half shipped.
2. **`try?` as an error-handling strategy.** Write failures are swallowed silently in every logging flow (symptom, medication adherence, workout, nutrition, quick-add), in `bootstrap()`, `resetDemoData()`, purge, and profile persistence. Where errors *do* surface, they surface as `String(describing: error)` — raw Swift error dumps in a bilingual wellness product (`LoadState.error`, 5+ screens, both platforms). For an app whose brand is trustworthiness about health data, silent data loss is the single most brand-corrosive failure mode possible.
3. **Main-actor synchronous SQL everywhere.** Every view model queries the lock-serialized `SQLiteConnection` synchronously on the `@MainActor` (`HomeViewModel.load` ~16 queries, `BodyViewModel` worst fan-out, `TimelineAssembler` 7 sequential full-window queries, `ExportRunner` ~88+). Invisible at 90 seeded days; a guaranteed jank cliff the day real multi-year HealthKit history lands — i.e., exactly when the flagship feature ships.
4. **Duplication instead of shared primitives.** `DateFormatter` allocation at 15+ render sites; `parseDecimal` in 3 files; status-chip position→label mapping in 4; `methodString` in 2; manual-record `Provenance`/ULID boilerplate in 4 view models; kcal formatting in 2; Android date formatting in 8 files; per-platform template-selection logic with no shared fixture. Each duplicate is small; together they guarantee drift, and drift in a "one model, two altitudes, two languages, two platforms" product is user-visible inconsistency.
5. **Parity by assertion, not by fixture.** `docs/android-parity-status.md` claims "same numbers as iOS" but no cross-platform conformance fixtures exist or run in CI; decoders already diverge (`casualLabel` fallback timing); CI has no Android job and checks only iOS asset mirrors; the three representations of the 24-column CSV contract are never machine-compared. The architecture doc promises fixtures (§8); the promise is unfunded.
6. **Config/infra drift.** `docs/data-model.md` still claims Room; EXECUTION_PLAN describes a 4-tab IA; GRDB/Room references linger in 5 places; two blueprint copies; stale `scripts/tree.txt`; `project.yml` declares iPad orientations for an iPhone-only target; `proguard-rules.pro` referenced but missing.

### 9.2 Recurring UX smell patterns

1. **The demo-data masquerade.** Seeded fake data is presented as a real, "Active" Apple Health source, onboarding never discloses it, the "Connect health data" CTA silently does nothing, and no screen carries a sample-data indicator. A first-run user is being *shown a lie*, however well-intentioned — the inverse of the product's trust thesis, and the most urgent UX fix in the repo.
2. **No way back.** No undo, no edit, and (for 3 of 6 log types) no delete anywhere: a mis-tapped medication dose, a typo'd weight that skews the baseline for weeks (no plausibility bounds), a duplicate save from a double-tap (no guard on 3+ forms) — all permanent. Correction flows are the largest coherent ease-of-use gap.
3. **Honesty gates applied inconsistently.** Home shows confident chips on provisional baselines that Body/MetricDetail gate; charts shade provisional bands as reliable; "no baseline yet" and "thin baseline" share one badge; MAD=0 produces false "outside your range" flags. The product's differentiator — statistical honesty — is unevenly enforced.
4. **Power-mode as a dumping ground.** Raw algorithm IDs, IANA timezones, checksums, and reconciliation-rule tokens are shown verbatim to power users instead of being *explained more deeply* — power depth currently means "less filtered," not "more insightful." Meanwhile casual users lose load-bearing context (device last-seen, dedup notes, relative timestamps) that isn't actually "power" information.
5. **Dead-end states.** Empty and error states are generic, identical to each other, and action-less across both platforms (`StatefulContainer`/`EmptyStateView` support actions; almost no screen passes one). The highest-traffic dead end is Home's own empty state.
6. **Static accessibility.** Fixed-size fonts (zero Dynamic Type), measured WCAG AA contrast failures on the core `StatusChip` amber and dark-mode filter chips, chart components with no VoiceOver/TalkBack story, hidden onboarding progress for screen readers, no reduce-motion checks, no haptics. Accessibility was designed (44pt touch minimums, `accessibilityHidden` on decorative icons) but not finished.
7. **Arabic parity is structural, not substantive.** RTL layout genuinely works, but: explainers fall back to metric names, search folds English only, unit labels miss BMI/VO2max Arabic, two greetings share one Arabic string, workout activity labels are untranslated on Android, insight text splices Latin values with no bidi isolates. Arabic users get the layout of a first-class experience and the content of a partial one.

### 9.3 Product scope risks

1. **Risk: shipping breadth before the spine.** 300 new-feature candidates exist, but the app's spine — real data in (HealthKit), trust in what's shown (demo disclosure, error surfacing), and the ability to fix mistakes (edit/undo/delete) — is incomplete. Any roadmap that adds surface area before closing those three multiplies the cost of closing them later.
2. **Risk: the ontology outgrowing the UI.** 44 metrics, 8 families — but Home hardcodes 4 metrics, insights cover 3, and 10+ registry metrics have no logging or ingestion path at all ("dead registry entries"). Either the registry is the roadmap (fine — say so) or it's inventory rot.
3. **Risk: local-first without backup = data-loss product.** No backup/restore on either platform, `allowBackup="false"` on Android, exports that nothing can re-import, a silent temp-dir DB fallback on iOS, and export files in purgeable cache dirs. For a "your health repository for life" product this is the loudest strategic contradiction in the repo.
4. **Risk: notification-shaped promises.** Settings shows notification toggles wired to nothing; medication schedules exist with no reminders. Users forgive absent features; they do not forgive inert switches.
5. **Risk: parity tax compounding.** Every iOS feature now implicitly costs 2× (Android mirror, by hand, no fixtures). Without conformance fixtures + shared contract validation in CI, parity will silently rot precisely as velocity increases.
6. **Risk: the sensitive namespace's guarantees are ahead of its UX.** File-deletion purge is genuinely strong engineering, but the UI can show "off" while files persist (ordering bug), re-enable implies restoration that never happens, and there's no app lock despite a dedicated sensitive DB. Privacy features that mislead are worse than absent ones.

## 10. Final implementation guidance

**The one-sentence read:** BADAN's domain model and product philosophy are genuinely excellent; its risk is concentrated in the unglamorous connective tissue — real ingestion, error truth-telling, correction flows, backup, and cross-platform enforcement — and nearly all of the 1,500 items above are downstream of those five.

**Recommended sequencing (90-day shape):**

1. **Weeks 1–2 — Stop the lies (mostly Effort 1–2).** Fix `SourcesScreen` never loading (OPT-023); label demo data everywhere + honest onboarding CTA (EASE-102/103/117/128); replace raw error strings with localized wellness-safe copy + retry (OPT-092, EASE-193/194, UIUX-084/249); fix the Arabic explainer substitution (OPT-032/UIUX-031); guard MAD=0 bands (OPT-175); fix purge ordering (OPT-153); add double-save guards (EASE-016/056/069); exclude DBs from iCloud backup after making the backup decision consciously (PERF-120).
2. **Weeks 2–5 — Land the spine: real HealthKit reads (FEAT-001…010).** Wire `HealthKitAdapter` query mapping for the 4 already-authorized types, connect it to `IngestionPipeline` behind the existing seam, make onboarding's CTA real, add a Sync Now to Sources. Wrap ingest/seed in transactions first (PERF-152/149/185) so first real sync isn't 1,500 commits.
3. **Weeks 4–8 — Correction & trust flows.** Edit/delete/undo for all six log types (repo methods + UI + swipe actions: EASE-085…099, OPT-107/115/117/130); export files to Documents not tmp (OPT-140); import/restore for BADAN's own export (FEAT-182 — the backup story's cheapest first half).
4. **Weeks 6–10 — Enforcement infrastructure (parallel, Infra-owned).** Android CI job + Android asset mirror check + pinned toolchains (OPT-276/277/279); shared conformance fixtures both platforms run (OPT-293); SwiftLint/ktlint with a wellness-language lint (OPT-299/265); prepared-statement cache + async repository façade before data volumes grow (PERF-101/103).
5. **Weeks 8–12 — Casual polish + power depth, from the existing backlog's 4/1 and 4/2 items.** Dynamic Type migration (UIUX-073), contrast fixes (UIUX-074/047), Home provisional gating (UIUX-001), quick-repeat logging (EASE-002/004), Goals UI (FEAT-251) and reorderable modules (FEAT-263) as the first *new* surface area — only after 1–4 are underway.

**What NOT to do yet** (expanded in §8.7): widgets/watch/Wear, BLE vendor integrations, LLM insights, multi-profile, menstrual-cycle family, PDF reports, correlation lab, theme packs — each is legitimate, none survives prioritization against a product whose iOS build has never ingested a real heartbeat.

**Owner split suggestion:** Mobile owns waves 1–3 and 5; Infra/QA owns wave 4; Product owns the ~40 approval-gated decisions this audit flags as blocking those waves (demo-data policy, backup policy, permission timing, notification scope, correction-flow semantics, iCloud exclusion). Design owns a one-week token pass (Dynamic Type scale, contrast-fixed palette, on-primary token) that unblocks ~30 UIUX items mechanically.
